The first is sometimes L1. The second is coverage, and coverage is filed.* *** PASS-2, THE KIMI SUBSTITUTE SEAT: no break found, and THREE findings the other seats missed. The ask-again has now paid on every pass. *** **1. THE SIGNEDNESS SAFETY IS CONDITIONAL, and the condition is the same range invariant that proves termination.** `len > remain ? remain : len` compares a `size_t` against a signed `off_t`, so `remain` converts to unsigned -- **safe ONLY because `remain` is in `[1, BLOCK]`.** So the range proof is not merely about the loop terminating; **it is load-bearing for the comparison itself.** Had `remain` ever been <= 0 the conversion would produce an enormous unsigned value and the clamp would silently stop clamping. *Two independent consequences of one invariant, and only one of them was noticed by the other seats.* **2. A PROVABLY-EQUIVALENT EDIT THAT IS NOT COVERAGE DEBT:** `buf += lentoread` -> `buf += remain`. On every non-final iteration `len > remain`, so the two are equal; on the final iteration the loop exits before `buf` is read again. **Undetectable AND harmless** -- correctly classified as an equivalent mutant rather than an escape, which is a distinction this project has had to make before (`#449`'s guard-only widening measured EQUIVALENT). *** 3. This is a FIXTURE gap -- the rows cannot distinguish layer-selection bugs because the fixture has only one layer to select. **A second overlay, with a different block marked, closes it** -- and the tree already knows this shape: `diff_diskimage_sync.c:570` says *'A SECOND OVERLAY IS WHAT MAKES THE ROW WORK, and it is not decoration.'* **FILED, not fixed** -- same reasoning as the `lenread` escape: not a floor breach, not a measured false pass against a shipped claim. **But it is the more valuable of the two to close**, because a second overlay would strengthen every row rather than adding one. *Fair criticism of my brief that I accept: the seat noted rows 3-5 were not inlined, so its answer to 'smallest wrong edit' had to reason from two rows rather than five. **A pass-2 brief should inline the DETECTOR, not just the product diff** -- the same inline-every-fact rule the carrier already states for packet-fed seats, applied to the artifact under review.* *** PASS-2 COVERAGE DEBT, FILED NOT FIXED (the stopping rule): a ONE-IDENTIFIER mutant escapes all five rows. *** **The mutant (deepseek, pass 2): `buf += lentoread;` -> `buf += lenread;`.** `lenread` is what `fread` actually RETURNED; `lentoread` is what was REQUESTED. **In every path the five rows exercise they are identical**, so the whole detector stays green. Pre-existing; the patch neither helps nor worsens it. *** CONFIRMED 2026-08-27 by an adversarial opus pass that tried to break all four steps and could not. Three refinements, and the first is a REAL NARROWING I had missed. *** **PRECONDITION: the defect requires `d->nr_of_overlays > 0`.** With no overlay the function takes a fast path (`:1347`) that is a single `fseek`+`fread` and is correct. My record did not state this. **It is not a get-out:** overlays come from the `V` prefix (`:1810`) and from `R:` (`:2095`), and `R:` is routine in this project's own rigs (`gate_ab.sh:82` uses `LUNA_IMG="R:..."`, and `drive_guest.py` and several probes do the same). **UNALIGNED OFFSETS ARE GUEST-REACHABLE, with a census rather than an example:** * `promemul/dec_prom.c:167-170` -> `:148` -- `lseek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit guest value as `current_file_offset`; `read()` passes it straight through with a guest length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.** * `promemul/arcbios.c:1923` -> `:1761` -- ARC `Seek` stores an arbitrary 64-bit offset from guest memory; `Read` uses it with a length up to 64 MB. **Gives both faults.** * `diskimage_scsicmd.c:725`/`:830` -- variable-length tape READ via `tape_offset`. * `bootblock_iso9660.c:271-282` -- unaligned, but a fixed 256-byte length means one iteration, so **wrong-layer only**, no misalignment. *** THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS AN ASYMMETRY I HAD NOT LOOKED FOR: THE WRITE SIDE HAS THE GUARD THE READ SIDE LACKS. *** `fwrite_helper` explicitly refuses a non-multiple length (`:1273-1280`) and an unaligned offset (`:1281-1286`), both returning 0, both under `#164`. `fread_helper` has **no such guard anywhere**. The read path was simply never given the check the write path was. **THE MECHANISM IS SHARPER THAN I STATED, in a way that matters for the detector:** iteration 1 is **positionally CORRECT** (`buf[k] = file[offset+k]`); its only fault is the LAYER. The positional corruption begins at iteration 2 and is caused by the fixed `buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` stride paired with a variable-start read. **So the two halves have different trigger conditions:** wrong-layer needs only an unaligned offset; duplication additionally needs `len > 512 - (offset & 511)`. A detector must cover both. **AND IT IS NOT A MEMORY-SAFETY ISSUE, which was checked explicitly:** `buf` advances 512 only when `lentoread == 512`, and any short `lentoread` zeroes `len` and ends the loop; `len` cannot underflow. **Silent wrong data, no overrun.** **The cue idiom is confirmed as the fix template** (`:1091-1144`): `chunk = CDROM_SECTOR_SIZE - intra; if (chunk > len) chunk = len;` with `buf + total_copied`. It clamps to bytes-remaining-in-sector AND indexes the buffer by bytes actually delivered -- **both halves of what the overlay loop lacks.** **ADJACENT, not claimed by this row:** on a short read the loop does `len -= lentoread` while `totallenread += lenread`, so a short read in a NON-FINAL iteration makes the caller's `memset(buf + lendone, ...)` zero the wrong region. Worth a row of its own if this is worked. *Honest limit the seat stated and I keep: no rig was measured actually issuing an unaligned >512-byte read against an overlaid disk. Reachability is READ, not MEASURED.* *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, AND IT CORRUPTS READ DATA. The most severe bare-title row worked so far. Verified by reading the loop; the mechanism is worse than the title says. *** `src/disk/diskimage.c:1358-1402`, the overlay read loop: ```c for (curofs=offset; len != 0; curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1) { for (overlay_nr = d->nr_of_overlays-1; overlay_nr >= 0; overlay_nr --) if (overlay_has_block(d, overlay_nr, curofs)) /* layer chosen for THIS block */ break; lentoread = len > OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE? OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE : len; /* NOT clamped to the block's REMAINDER */ ... fread(buf, 1, lentoread, <chosen layer>) ... len -= lentoread; buf += OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE; /* fixed stride */ } ``` **`lentoread` is clamped to the BLOCK SIZE, never to the bytes left in the CURRENT block.** So when `offset` is not block-aligned, the loop picks a layer for the block containing `curofs` and then reads up to a full block from it -- **running past that block's end into the next one or two blocks, which may live in a different layer.** **Worked example, offset 511, len 1024** (`OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE` = 512): * iteration 1: `curofs = 511` -> layer chosen for **block 0**; `lentoread = 512`; reads file offsets **511-1022** into `buf[0..511]`. * `curofs = (511 | 511) + 1 = 512`; `buf += 512`. * iteration 2: layer chosen for **block 1**; reads file offsets **512-1023** into `buf[512..1023]`. **The guest asked for offsets 511-1534 and receives: wrong-layer bytes in the first half, and file offsets 512-1022 DUPLICATED at two different buffer positions.** The tail it asked for (1023-1534) is never read at all. This is silent read corruption, not a refusal. *** THE LOOP'S OWN ADVANCE EXPRESSION PROVES UNALIGNED OFFSETS WERE ANTICIPATED, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS AN OVERSIGHT AND NOT AN UNDOCUMENTED PRECONDITION. *** `curofs = (curofs | (OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE-1)) + 1` rounds UP to the next block boundary. If `offset` were always block-aligned that expression would simply be `curofs + OVERLAY_BLOCK_SIZE`. **The author wrote alignment-handling into the advance and omitted it from the length.** **GUEST-REACHABLE** (seat's sequence, structurally consistent with the code, which carries no alignment guard anywhere): an overlaid ARC disk, guest writes blocks 0 and 2 so they land in different layers, then a byte-granular `Seek(511)` + `Read(1024)`. ARC exposes byte-granular seek/read, so the unaligned offset reaches this loop. **Not verified by execution -- needs a build.** **Observable for a detector:** the guest-visible read payload. Write distinct sentinel bytes into blocks that land in different layers, then read across the boundary from an unaligned offset; broken returns the wrong layer's sentinel and a duplicated range, fixed returns the requested bytes in order. *** THE FIX IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. *** `diskimage_access__cue()` (`:1083`) does exactly the right thing for the same shape of problem -- it clamps each step to the remainder of the current sector and writes at `buf + total_copied` rather than on a fixed stride (see its `memset(buf + total_copied, 0, chunk)` at the same offset discipline). **Transferred warrant: clamp `lentoread` to the current block's remainder, and advance `buf` by the amount actually consumed rather than by a constant.** **A SECOND, SEPARABLE HALF reported by the seat and NOT verified here:** a short `fread` on the flat (non-overlay) path is said to return zero even after reading bytes, causing the caller to zero the whole requested buffer. Recorded as the seat's claim; check it before it rides along with the fix, because a row covering two defects buries one when the other closes. *** THE SENTENCE ABOVE PREDICTED THAT ONE ROT-PACKET RUN 'reds `stale quiet` and discharges BOTH'. THE RUN HAPPENED AND REFUTED THE SECOND HALF. Corrected 2026-08-29. *** `regress/artifacts/gdromexitsix/rot_20260829/` -- post-fix binary, one-line frozen-probe edit (packed format byte 0x20 -> 0x21): base.log GDROM_DEF_RESULT=60/60 stale quiet 0 vs 0 ok rot.log GDROM_DEF_RESULT=59/60 stale quiet 1 vs 0 **FAIL** The two `GDROM_DEF_VECTOR` lines differ in EXACTLY ONE POSITION -- discriminating, not merely disruptive, and proven by the probe's own vector rather than asserted. **`stale quiet` is DISCHARGED. `stale how` is NOT**, and structurally cannot be by a rotted packet: the fix DECLINES rather than dying, so the session still exits cleanly. Worse, it is the WANTED-EQUALS-FAILURE shape -- the row wants `exit0` and a BROKEN `how` capture also yields `exit0` -- so only a measured red separates a working oracle from an inert one. It needs a mutant that exits AFTER the last budget check. **Treat it as UNPROVEN until then.** *Found by a supplementary pass-2 seat applying the grep-for-siblings rule: the same predicted sentence sat in the probe comment AND here, and the measurement refuted both at once.*held

First in line with the other build-blocked rows. — note: *** L4 WRONG RECORD, CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-08-27. An adversarial opus pass REFUTED THE MECHANISM THIS ROW STATED BELOW. The defect is real; my explanation of it was false, and the true picture is four different wrong outcomes rather than one. *** **WHAT I GOT WRONG.** I wrote that `scsi_transfer_alloc()`'s `memset(p, 0, ...)` leaves a status BYTE of 0x00, which the guest reads as GOOD. **`status` is `unsigned char *` (`diskimage.h:196-197`)** -- so the memset leaves `status == NULL` and `status_len == 0`. **There is no zeroed status byte anywhere.** Nothing reads a 0x00 out of that struct. The conclusion happened to hold for one controller, for an entirely different reason. **WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the structural half:** the `default:` arm is the **only one of 25** that never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()` or `diskimage__return_check_condition()` -- verified by grepping every case/helper pair -- and it falls through to `return 1`, which the function's own header (`:263-266`) documents as the success token (`2` = expects DATA_OUT, `1` = otherwise ok, `0` = error). *** THE HONEST STATEMENT: ONE OMISSION, FOUR DIFFERENT WRONG OUTCOMES. *** * **`dev_asc.c` -- guest IS told GOOD**, but via an explicit `else fifo_write(0x00)` fallback at `:1284-1292`, which `git log -S` places in the unmodified upstream 0.7.0 import, NOT a fork change. Right conclusion, wrong reason. * **`dev_mb89352.c` -- REFUTES the 'told success' claim outright.** `data_in == NULL` sets `phase = PH_STAT` (`:284`); the guest's PH_STAT read takes `p = status (NULL), len = 0`, trips the `read longer than buffer?` arm (`:173`) and **sets `cpu->running = 0`**. The guest is not told anything -- the emulated CPU is STOPPED. **Filed separately as [[mb89352halt]].** * **`dev_osiop.c:573-582`** -- `while (... && i < status_len)` with `status_len == 0` writes **no status byte at all**; the guest's destination memory keeps its prior contents. * **`dev_wdc.c` (ATAPI)** -- `atapi_st->status` is read nowhere in the file; `res == 1` with `data_in == NULL` gives `PHASE_COMPLETED` with `WDCS_ERR` unset: a successful packet command. > **That is a BETTER case than the row originally made, not a weaker one** -- a single omitted completion step producing four distinct wrong behaviours across four controllers. But it is not the claim as written, and the claim as written was the one being ranked. **A SECOND CONSEQUENCE THE ORIGINAL RECORD MISSED:** the helper also RETIRES LATCHED SENSE (the `#417` fix, `:187-188`). The `default:` arm skips that too -- so an unimplemented command following a failed one leaves `sense_key/asc/ascq` latched, and a follow-up REQUEST SENSE attributes the OLD failure to the command that just ran. That is exactly the regression `#417` was written to remove, reachable by a different door. **FIX SHAPE, now pinned by the in-tree idiom at `:319-327`:** call the helper, set `status[0] = 0x02` (CHECK CONDITION), then `return 0`. Note `return 0` is **distinguishable on only two of four controllers** -- osiop stops the SCRIPTS engine, wdc completes with a latched warning, while asc and mb89352 do not test for 0 at all -- so the status buffer, not the return value, is what carries the refusal. --- the original record follows, kept so the correction is checkable --- *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, and the highest-severity bare-title row worked so far. Established by reading; the fix idiom ALREADY EXISTS in this file. *** `src/disk/diskimage_scsicmd.c:1380-1388`, the dispatcher's `default:` arm: ```c default: debug("[ UNIMPLEMENTED SCSI command 0x%02x, disk id=%i", xferp->cmd[0], id); // exit(1); } debug(" ]"); return 1; ``` **Three things go wrong together:** 1. it logs through `debug()`, which is verbosity-gated and normally invisible; 2. **it never calls `diskimage__return_default_status_and_message()`** -- every implemented arm does (`:1212`, `:1257`, `:1298`, `:1340`, `:1347`, `:1376`); 3. it falls through to **`return 1`, the same value a SUCCESSFUL command returns.** **And the status the guest reads is GOOD, which was checked rather than assumed:** `scsi_transfer_alloc()` ends with `memset(p, 0, sizeof(struct scsi_transfer))` (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:89`), and `dev_asc.c:326-330` frees and reallocates per command. Status 0x00 IS GOOD. **So an unsupported opcode is reported to the guest as a completed, successful command.** *** THE COMMENTED-OUT `exit(1)` IS THE TELL. *** This site was de-fatalised by commenting out the kill, which removed the death without adding an error path -- the incomplete form of the de-fatalisation this fork otherwise does carefully. *** THE FIX HAS A TRANSFERRED WARRANT ALREADY IN THIS FILE, found by grepping the tree for the existing idiom rather than reasoning from scratch. *** `diskimage__return_check_condition()` is defined at `:208` and already used for exactly this class at `:823-824` -- `0x05, 0x21`, ILLEGAL REQUEST -- and again at `:909`. **The correct refusal for an unknown opcode is CHECK CONDITION with ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID COMMAND OPERATION CODE, and the helper to do it sits three hundred lines above the defect.** **NOT FIXED: needs a build.** The detector must show the pre-fix build reporting GOOD for an unsupported opcode and CHECK CONDITION after -- and floor clause (b) needs the `return 1` reinstated verbatim. Both are measurements. Queued behind the embargo. held

Research (fix proposals)OK2026-08-29 — CONFIRMED — VERDICT: **`return 0` IS REFUTED -- not merely a sketch, but a MEASURED-BY-READING BEHAVIOURAL REGRESSION on two controllers with ZERO benefit on the third. The right shape is `diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp, d, 0x05, 0x20, 0x00)` PLUS the fall-through `return 1` -- the file's own refusal idiom at four shipped sites.** Every claim below was re-verified by me against the source before recording. *** MY CENSUS WAS CONTAMINATED AND SO IS THE ROW'S. Both counted the COMMENT HEADER and the DEFINITION as calls. *** grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message' -> 25 raw grep -c 'diskimage__return_default_status_and_message(xferp' -> 23 CALLS grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition' -> 5 raw grep -c 'diskimage__return_check_condition(xferp' -> 3 CALLS grep -c $'^\tcase ' -> 22 top-level labels So **the row's "the only one of 25" is wrong under ANY unit** -- 25 is the contaminated raw count. The correct statement is **"the only one of 20 TOP-LEVEL ARMS"** (22 labels forming 19 bodies, since MODE_SENSE/10, READ/READ_10 and WRITE/WRITE_10 share bodies, plus the default). My own `~30` counted NESTED labels. *A re-deriver caution worth keeping: `grep -E '^\tcase'` silently matches NOTHING, because `\t` is a literal `t` in ERE -- use `$'\t'`. I hit that exact trap on this file earlier today.* **THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM SURVIVES, verified arm by arm**: all 19 bodies call the status helper on every completing path. ONE QUALIFIER: at PATH level the two `return 2` first passes also set no status -- correctly, because the command is incomplete and the DATA_OUT re-entry sets it, and all three SCSI controllers re-call. My return enumeration was exact. *** WHY `return 0` IS WORSE THAN A SKETCH -- three consumers, each read: *** * **`dev_osiop.c:500-505`** -- `res == 0` sets **`d->scripts_running = 0`**. A guest probing one unsupported opcode **kills its own SCRIPTS engine**; no status phase ever. * **`dev_asc.c:1395-1400`** -- `ok == 0` gives `STATE_DISCONNECTED` + `NCRINTR_DIS`. The guest sees a target DISCONNECT instead of CHECK CONDITION: retry/reset instead of REQUEST SENSE. **This also refutes the row's own state_note, which says asc does not test for 0 at all** -- its select path does. * **`dev_wdc.c:1528-1541`** -- the `res == 0` arm sets **no error bit**, and `status_byte()` raises `WDCS_ERR` only from `d->error`. So on wdc, `return 0` is guest-INDISTINGUISHABLE from success-with-no-data. > **`return 0` helps no consumer and harms two.** That is a stronger refutation than my > structural one, and it is the form a future round should cite. **THE FIX, WITH ITS WARRANT:** CHECK-CONDITION-then-`return 1` is ALREADY this file's refusal idiom at four shipped sites, and all four controllers demonstrably handle it today. `d` is non-NULL in the default arm (the NULL path returned earlier). #417's latch semantics come free: REQUEST SENSE reads `d->sense_key/asc/ascq` and the next success retires them. *The state_note's cited precedent is the WRONG one -- that shape exists only because `d` is NULL there and `check_condition` would dereference it; its own comments say `// ?` and `TODO`.* **MUST NOT BREAK:** (a) do NOT allocate `data_in` -- all three SCSI controllers pick the DATA_IN phase off `data_in != NULL`, and status-only completion is already TEST_UNIT_READY's shape; (b) leave the pre-switch not-connected `return 0` alone; (c) `est/` byte-identical propagation, shared file; (d) **the fix ALSO cures `mb89352halt`'s mechanism** -- `status_len` becomes 1, so the PH_STAT read no longer trips 'read longer than buffer?' into `cpu->running = 0`, consistent with the standing ONE-ROUND-for-both ruling. *** THE ATAPI ROUTE IS REAL AND IS THE **WRONG WITNESS CHANNEL**, which inverts what I assumed when I raised it. *** `dev_wdc.c:1515` does feed packet commands in, and `res == 1` with no data gives PHASE_COMPLETED and no error bit. **But `atapi_st->status` is read NOWHERE in dev_wdc.c** -- so an ATAPI witness stays RED after a dispatcher-only fix, because it witnesses the COMBINED dispatcher+wdc defect. The discriminating channels for THIS fix are **asc** (ICCS fifo byte 0x00 -> 0x02, pmax rig) or **mb89352** (loudest pre-fix symptom on record: the emulated CPU stops). The wdc consumer repair is its own hunk in a different file and should be filed separately -- the one-omission-in-one-shared-function warrant does not stretch to it. RANKING: raises reachability BREADTH within the band, not harm class. Keep rank 3. Plausible but UNMEASURED: MMC opcodes 0x46 (GET CONFIGURATION) and 0x4A (GET EVENT STATUS NOTIFICATION) are not among the 19 arms and period ATAPI attach code issues them routinely -- one flagged boot would settle it. **FILED, NOT FIXED (a sibling this round does not touch):** `SPACE`'s NESTED `default:` `fatal()`s and then FALLS THROUGH to the status helper, **telling the guest GOOD for an unimplemented SPACE type**. Same false-success class, inside a KNOWN arm rather than the default one, so b120u's fix does not reach it. b120r-shaped. — evidence: Agent seat (fable5) adjudication 2026-08-29; census, osiop:500-505, asc:1395-1400 and the raw-vs-call grep contamination all re-verified by the main loop against source········

It is a MISSING `else`. *** The title blames *wrap-around*. A farmed seat checked that premise -- as the brief asked -- and refuted it: ordinary periodic wrap is handled. **But it confirmed the mechanism, and reading the code shows a sharper defect than the one it named.** `src/cpus/cpu_mips_coproc.c:796-819`: ```c int32_t compare_diff = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COMPARE]; double hz; if (compare_diff < 0) hz = tmp - cp->reg[COP0_COUNT]; /* (A) */ if (compare_diff == 0) /* SEPARATE statement */ hz = 0; /* (B) */ else hz = (double)emulated_hz / (double)compare_diff; /* (C) */ ``` **(A) IS AN UNCONDITIONALLY DEAD STORE.** The `if/else` at (B)/(C) is a separate statement, and both its arms assign `hz` -- so whatever (A) wrote is always overwritten. When `compare_diff < 0`, (C) runs and yields a **NEGATIVE** `hz`; `if (hz > 0)` at `:812` is then false and **the timer is neither created nor updated**. **The three cases, exhaustively:** * `compare_diff > 0` -- (C) gives a positive rate; timer set. **The only working path.** * `compare_diff == 0` -- (B) gives 0; `hz > 0` false; nothing set. * `compare_diff < 0` -- (A) computed the intended value and (C) throws it away for a negative one; `hz > 0` false; nothing set. **Consequence, which is what the title was reaching for:** if the timer was never created it stays NULL, so **no timer interrupt is ever delivered again**; if it already existed it keeps its stale rate. Either way a guest write that ought to reprogram the timer silently does nothing. *** THE DEAD STORE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it shows INTENT. *** The author wrote handling for `compare_diff < 0` and it has never executed. This is not a design choice being second-guessed -- it is a chain of `if`s that lost its `else`, and (A) is the evidence. **REACHABILITY -- PARTLY SETTLED, and the unsettled half is recorded as unsettled rather than asserted.** The gate is `emulated_hz > 0` at `:797`; **21 assignments to `emulated_hz` exist across the tree.** * **arc: DORMANT, verified here** -- `machine_arc.c` contains ZERO `emulated_hz` assignments, so the gate cannot pass. * **pmax: OPEN.** It DOES set `emulated_hz` (`machine_pmax.c:96`, `:160`), so the `:797` gate passes. OPEN QUESTION carried into Research: whether OpenBSD writes TSTR before TCR was NOT booted - so the fix must be correct under BOTH orderings. — witness: none -- and none is needed: the state this row worries about was already MEASURED SAFE by an earlier round, with the analysis committed in-tree at `dev_sh4.c:2062-2064`. — note: *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: the MECHANISM is TRUE, the SEVERITY IS NIL, and the tree already says so 600 lines from where the seat was looking. *** **True as stated:** the `SH4_TSTR` arm (`dev_sh4.c:1929-1948`) starts a timer on a write with no `timer_hz` guard anywhere in it. **But that state was already measured and recorded as harmless**, in this file, by the round that placed the guard (`:2062-2064`): > *"A seat measured the third option (store idata, skip the prescaler switch, leave timer_hz at 0) as SAFE -- no division by zero, no UNF, no pending interrupt."* **And it is safe STRUCTURALLY, not incidentally:** `timer_hz` is the NUMERATOR at `:481`, `step = (uint32_t)(d->timer_hz[i] / SH4_PSEUDO_TIMER_HZ)`, so a zero can only make `step` zero -- it can never be a divisor. `:2071-2073` adds that `timer_hz[]` is already 0.0 from DEVINIT's memset, and those four prescaler cases are its only writes in the file. **DISPOSITION: assessed, NOT a defect.** A started timer at 0 Hz that does not advance is the CORRECT behaviour, not a symptom -- so a detector keyed on TCNT0 failing to advance would pin the right answer as though it were a bug. *The farmed seat confirmed the mechanism and could not have known the disposition: the assessment lives ~600 lines away in the same file. This is why a seat answer is verified locally before it is recorded, never transcribed.* held

gateflrgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it noticesgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it notices — HOLD: FILE: measured during the R1+R2 regression review — Found by the flagship while reviewing the R1 and R2 regression evidence. Delete the block and every one of those guards disappears with it, while the gate still reports PASS - nothing outside floors gate 2's check count. NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it is the only form that tests the two spellings AGAINST EACH OTHER rather than each against a literal: extend selftest_logdir.py to read the grader's pattern OUT OF gate_hygiene.sh by grep rather than re-typing it, then mutate the driver's log_path and require RED. Check E looks only for regress/diff_*.c (precommit_check.sh:155), so it has never seen ANY python detector - not selftest_logdir.py (added by R1), not selftest_absorb.py (shipped by r421), not readiness_predicate_test.py. Check C extracts paths with a pattern that needs both a src/, regress/ or man/ prefix AND a .c, .h, .sh or .1 extension (:92), so a message that names drive_guest.py, or names a file without its directory, cross-checks NOTHING and prints 'message cites no source paths'. Both lines say ok where they should say not applicable. Self-review disclosed: the author of the round found it in the round's own output. It reconciled this explicitly as intra-file growth rather than the wrong-tree signature (which shifts arms and changes which cases exist). PYTHON HALF, split answer: check E is unchanged and can never see a python file, but section R's check_probe_wiring.py sees all 56 python artefacts. **They answer different questions** -- E asks whether a detector carries an identity guard, R asks whether anything runs it -- so the gap is real but narrower than recorded. For a python probe the identity-guard analogue is a gate-side `rows run` pin, **and nothing requires a new probe to have one**. *** THAT IS THE SAME HOLE AS `gateflr`, and one extension to check_probe_wiring.py closes both. *** DIRECTORY HALF, unchanged and BROADER than the row says: check C's prefix alternation is `(src|regress|man)`, so **the entire `tools/` tree is invisible** -- precommit_check.sh cannot cross-check a commit message naming ITSELF, or panel.sh, or any pipeline checker. The alternation predates the 2026-08-17 harness migration into git, so this is NEW, not a restatement. It tabulated nine representative strings; `regress/drive_guest.py`, `tools/...`, and bare filenames are all invisible. The false-green is still there verbatim: no match -> `good "message cites no source paths"`, an ok line about a message it could not read. *** THE FOURTH BLIND SPOT: CHECK D AUDITS A DIFFERENT CHANGE SET FROM EVERY OTHER SECTION. *** `$CHANGED` prefers `git diff --cached`; check D uses BARE `git diff -U0` -- unstaged only, always. hlenhlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)hlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit) — HOLD: census done; promote to a FIX round? — Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.held

Reset value: 0."* > *** SO A GUEST READ OF `+0x188` IS A DOCUMENTED, LEGAL, READ-ONLY ACCESS THAT THE MODEL ALREADY ANSWERS CORRECTLY (`odata = d->irq_enable`) AND THEN KILLS THE HOST ANYWAY. *** The right answer is computed and then discarded. *** THIS PRODUCES A **FOURTH MEMBER** OF THE DE-FATALISATION OPTION SET, WHICH THE CARRIER'S THREE-MEMBERED RULE DOES NOT CONTAIN: **ACCEPT.** *** delete / decline / decline+bounded-announce all presume the access is unserviceable. Here it is serviceable and already served, so the disposition is **delete the `fatal()`+`exit(1)` outright -- no latch, no message** -- and keep the value. Transferring the `m8820x_unimplemented()` warrant would have silently imported the premise that the read is unserviceable, which the code refutes on its own line, and would have shipped a **wrong record in product code**: printing *'unimplemented; ignored'* about a read that is implemented and is not ignored. **Four further reasons the m8820x template misfits, each measured:** its latch is a documented-defective template (ONE `reported_offset` flag covers FOUR kinds, per-kind latch FILED not done -- and footbridge has EIGHT sites across SIX kinds, so it imports the known defect at twice the scale); its marker `(reported once)` is the tree's MINORITY spelling and **both** uses are in `dev_m8820x.c` itself; and there is **no transferable flood measurement** -- m8820x's latch is warranted by 640,016 CMMU_SCR writes in 132 s on a rig that boots, while `regress/images.md` lists NO cats rig and `REVIEW_FINDINGS.md:171,:186` record that a real NetBSD/cats boot hits **none** of the eight sites. *** THE EIGHT SITES ARE TWO SEMANTIC CLASSES, NOT ONE, so the reopening rule SPLITS them: *** `0x188` read is a **correctness defect** (right answer computed, then discarded); the other seven -- including `IRQ_ENABLE_CLEAR` read at `:604`, and the write sides of `IRQ_STATUS`, `IRQ_RAW_STATUS`, `FIQ_STATUS`, `FIQ_RAW_STATUS` -- are **declinations of accesses the datasheet marks `--`**, which IS the m8820x class. One round cannot cover both. *** THE COST THAT MAKES THIS A REAL ROUND RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE DELETE: `0x188` IS THE PROBE'S ONLY FAILABILITY CONTROL. *** `footbridge_sites_probe.py`'s own header says so -- *"an UNFIXED site, used here rather than repaired, because a probe that reports SURVIVED for every row is vacuous unless something in it can still die."* **Fixing `0x188` turns row K1 RED and takes gate 14 with it.** The round therefore owes, IN-ROUND: 1. re-point arm K to another still-unfixed site -- `+0x18c`, `0xE590718C`, fatal text `"ENABLE CLEAR"` -- a one-word change; and 2. a de-escalation ACCEPT row for `0x188`. **And that accept row is VACUOUS if it only READS `0x188`:** after `memset`, `d->irq_enable == 0`, and `0` is exactly what an absent device returns -- the precise trap this probe's header records surviving once before (*returned 0x0 on every device row WITH ITS RAM CONTROL STILL GREEN*). **It must `str` a known value to `+0x188` first** (the write arm ORs it in; with `irq_status == 0` the follow-on `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT` is inert), then read it back and assert that value. **Propagation note: `dev_footbridge.c` is byte-identical in `est/` and is NOT on `tools/est_divergence.txt`, so any edit must land in BOTH trees.** held

mrwstore2mrwstore2 A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twicemrwstore2 A straddling store whose tail faults makes an MMIO head see the write twice — commits: 0447c2e — HOLD: *** THE OLD BLOCKING REASON IS REFUTED AND WAS AN L4 -- corrected 2026-08-26. *** It read 'the fix may itself DIVERGE from real hardware'. **A fix cannot diverge, because the behaviour is PERMITTED and never REQUIRED.** Four PowerPC manuals are now local in `_scratchpad/` (OEA Book III v2.01, VEA Book II v2.01, MPCFPE32B Rev 2 -- the 32-bit PEM covering the PPC750 this row's witness uses -- and the 2005 32/64-bit PEM), fetched and extracted with the same pdftotext used for ddi0100i.txt. PEM 3.2.2 / Book II 2.1: a misaligned store is not atomic, so it falls in the 'any other load or store instruction MAY be partially executed and then aborted... and then re-executed' bucket; 6.1.4 says 'some bytes just before the boundary may have been updated'. **So an emulator that never partially executes is conformant under every one of them -- the INTERSECTION of both readings, not a divergence from either.** *** AND THE MANUALS DISAGREE ON THE CASE THIS ROW IS ACTUALLY ABOUT, recorded as an honest UNKNOWN rather than settled by the stronger document: *** Book III v2.01 4.2.4.1 says that for an access whose first byte is Caching-Inhibited AND Guarded -- exactly the MMIO-head shape here -- a DSI means 'the portion of the storage operand that is in Caching Inhibited and Guarded storage is NOT accessed', i.e. the device write must not happen. The PEM contains no such rule and its 6.1.4 explicitly permits the head bytes to have been updated. Whether a real PPC750 suppresses the device write is NOT established. THE REASONS THAT SURVIVE and on which this row stays filed: REACHABILITY (zero straddling stores measured across three real boots) and SEVERITY (a duplicated device write -- guest-visible, no host kill, no memory-safety consequence; both PowerPC and ARM put the burden on software). *** SCOPE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE BLOCKER: 'memory_rw is the choke point' is FALSE FOR THE CLASS. *** stmw/stswi/lmw/lswi and ARM's bdt_store each loop and return on the first failing element, so they have the identical partial-completion-across-a-fault property at the INSTRUCTION level, entirely outside memory_rw -- and PEM 6.1.4's first bullet is about exactly those. **A memory_rw fix would be a partial fix that reads as a complete one**, which is the argument for filing this properly rather than shipping a round a future reader mistakes for closure. TWO SIDE-EFFECT CAUTIONS FROM A PRIOR SEAT MEASURED ABSENT IN THIS TREE: FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS returns before every SPR write and before ppc_exception(), and there is NO R/C writeback on PPC at all -- so the recorded warning about PPC603 software reload describes hazards that do not exist here. FILED SEPARATELY, all from the same reading: `X(stvx)` does a raw 16-byte memory_rw with no `EA & ~0xF` mask (a second straddling producer, and a divergence in its own right); diff_memory_rw.c has a coverage hole exactly at this row's shape (device head + FAULTING tail); and memory_ppc.c:302-305 is an unlatched guest-drivable fatal(), one per translation fault -- the floodclass shape #464 just closed six of. — witness: none yet -- guest-reachable on PowerPC and witnessable at rung 3/4 (the observable is a side-effect COUNT, not a value), but a witness needs a build, which the machine embargo forbids. — note: *** L4 CORRECTION 2026-08-27: MY OBSERVABLE IS WRONG AND MY RANKING WAS TOO HIGH. The mature ledger entry already measured three of this row's claims FALSE, and I did not read it before writing a fresh note on top. *** **THE OBSERVABLE IS NOT 'TWO WHEN BROKEN, ONE WHEN FIXED'.** It is **1 -> 4+ writes**. My two-versus-one framing was a guess at the shape of a count, not the measured count. **THREE CLAIMS ALREADY MEASURED FALSE in this row's own history**, which I wrote over rather than read: * *introduced by `#430`* -- FALSE; * *the memblock split always had it* -- FALSE; * *256x* -- the real figure is **1024x**. *** AND THE REACHABILITY IS NEAR-NIL, MEASURED: three instrumented guest boots -- pmax, luna88k, macppc -- produced **ZERO** straddling stores. Only **11 of 1024** offsets can even start one, and it is PowerPC-only. *** It may also be architecturally CORRECT partial-completion-with-restart, which no one has refuted. **DISPOSITION: DOCUMENTED-ONLY, ranked LAST of the guest-reachable set (8th of 8).** Not a live-corruption peer of [[b115]] or [[wdcringambig]], which is where I had implicitly put it. *The lesson is mine and specific: I recorded a fresh seat answer as a NEW note on a row that already had a mature, more-measured entry underneath. **A row with existing evidence must be READ before it is written to** -- otherwise a fresh reading silently outranks an older measurement, which is the opposite of how evidence should compose.* *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, guest-reachable on PowerPC, and the observable is unusually clean -- a COUNT, not a value. *** **The mechanism, and it needs the guest's own fault handler to complete it:** a store that STRADDLES a page boundary performs its head chunk BEFORE translating the tail. When the head lands in MMIO and the tail is unmapped, the MMIO side effect COMMITS, then the tail raises DSI. PowerPC saves the faulting PC, and the guest's `rfi` restarts **the whole store** -- so **the MMIO head runs a second time.** **MEASURED (existing evidence cited by the seat, not re-run here):** `stw` at `0x1201fffe` -- two bytes of MMIO head, then an unmapped tail. *** THE OBSERVABLE IS A COUNT AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW IS WORTH RANKING: **MMIO-head side-effect count after one fault-and-retry -- TWO when broken, ONE when fixed.** *** A count-based oracle is immune to the value-only blindness that has made several detectors in this tree vacuous: it cannot be satisfied by reading back the same value twice. **FIX PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS (transferred warrant):** `ppc_translate_v2p(... FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS | FLAG_WRITEFLAG)` fails BEFORE any SPR write, so the tail can be translated before the head is committed. The shape is 'probe both halves, then commit', and the primitive to probe with is already in the tree. **NARROW: PowerPC only, and it needs a guest that restarts the faulting store** -- which is what a normal PPC fault handler does, so this is not an exotic path. Ranks below the silent read-corruption rows because it requires the fault, but it is a genuine double-side-effect, not a fidelity nit. held

Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3 -- AND THREE OF THIS ROW'S CLAIMS ARE MEASURED FALSE. *** The defect is real; the severity argument that put it top of a cluster is not. THE WITNESS: unmodified in-tree `testppc` (-E testppc -C PPC750 -M 32), cold debugger, real guest instructions, real decode, real memory_rw. A PPC guest sets DBAT0 over a 128 KB window, sets MSR[DR]=1, and executes `stw r6,0(r5)` with r5 = 0x1201fffe -- unaligned, crossing the 1 KB split granule. Head (2 bytes) reaches the in-tree `fb` device; tail (2 bytes) has no BAT and no PTE, so a real DSI fires; a planted `rfi` at the DSI vector is the GUEST'S OWN restart. The same instruction re-executes, unbounded. Counters: one architectural store, FOUR device writes. **The trace is from a fully stock HEAD binary with zero instrumentation** -- the counters only counted. Controls all green: liveness (RAM through the same decode), DEVICE SIGNATURE (same program, only DBAT0L changed: PA->device reads back 0x3344, PA->no device reads back 0x0000), and a negative control two bytes lower that does not split. CLAIM 1 -- 'not introduced by #430' -- MEASURED FALSE. Built from `git show 2458cfb^:src/cpus/memory_rw.c`, stock otherwise: the same guest program produces NO exception, NO restart, ONE device write. Pre-#430 the tail was silently mis-applied to the physically-following location -- the defect #430 fixed -- so there was nothing to restart. **#430 CREATED the fault, and the double-application is a direct consequence of it.** CLAIM 2 -- 'the memblock split has had this property all along' -- MEASURED FALSE, twice. Post-#430 the memblock split can only fire on PHYSICAL accesses (a translated 4 KB write across 1 MB costs 4 translations / 4 host lookups; PHYSICAL costs 0 / 2), and its head can NEVER be a device in either version because device dispatch `goto do_return_ok`s first -- measured with a device straddling the memblock boundary. CLAIM 3 -- '256x' -- MEASURED WRONG: it is **1024x**. The granule was measured by walking offsets, not read: MRW_SPLIT_MASK is 0x3ff, so 1 MB / 1024 = 1024. The 256 came from comparing 1 MB to a 4 KB page -- the granule this split does not use. *** THE SAME WRONG NUMBER WAS ALSO IN THE SOURCE, at memory_rw.c's own 'one boundary in 256' comment: ONE mis-derived constant became TWO records defects, and the row repeated it as a severity argument. Both corrected. *** REACHABILITY IS FAR NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES, and this is why it re-ranks DOWN: * ONLY PowerPC can emit a straddling store at all. MIPS (AdES; swl/swr do an ALIGNED RMW), ARM, SH, M88K and Alpha all force alignment -- each checked in source. PPC's `if (addr & (LS_SIZE-1))` at cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:229 is a FAST-PATH BAIL-OUT, not an exception, so the generic path passes the unaligned address through. * PPC is also the ONLY family whose device-failure path can restart: memory_rw's device-failure arm raises an exception only under #ifdef MEM_MIPS / #ifdef MEM_M88K. * THREE REAL GUEST BOOTS, instrumented: OpenBSD/pmax to root login, OpenBSD/luna88k to `login:`, NetBSD/macppc to the root-device prompt -- **ZERO straddling stores from guest code**. The seat first read macppc's 95 split-loop writes as guest activity and REFUTED ITSELF by logging the addresses: all are len=65536 at pc=0x0, i.e. file_elf.c:448's loader chunks running before any guest instruction. * Of the 1024 offsets in a granule only ELEVEN (0x3f9..0x3ff) can start a straddling 2/4/8-byte access, and the head's device offset is always within 7 bytes BELOW a 1 KB boundary -- so a register at offset 0x00/0x10/0x20 can never be a straddle head. *** AND THE FIX MAY ITSELF BE WRONG. *** Partial completion on a page-crossing misaligned store, with restart re-applying the first part, is what real PowerPC hardware does -- so gxemul may be CORRECT here and a fix may introduce a divergence. There is no PowerPC manual in _scratchpad/ (ARM, MIPS and m88k only), so the seat stated that as REASONING, NOT A CITATION -- the same trap CLAUDE.md records for SH. **Obtain a PPC manual before any edit.** The minimal fix, if one is wanted: a dry-run pre-pass on WRITES only, walking the chunks with FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS and committing only if all translate. Zero cost on the hot path -- it sits inside the `while (len > granule - offset)` body, which no aligned access enters. Watch TLB-miss handlers with side effects (PPC603 software reload) and do not let the dry run update referenced/changed bits. mrwstore2_rung3.py is close to shippable as a regress detector; its controls already satisfy the liveness and device-signature clauses. — evidence: _scratchpad/ (mrwstore2_rung3.py, sig.py, probe_mrwstore2.c)·······

Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260815_221232/✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Verified here independently. THE WITNESS: a cold-debugger probe on UNMODIFIED `-E cats`, the same mechanics as footbridge_sites_probe.py. Pre-fix and post-fix binaries from the same tree, same script: C1 liveness 0x11223344 both RAM through the same decode A1 device signature 0xAA both see below T1 negative control halts at paddr=0x0c000043, MMU-on cannot reach it D0 count 0 -> hz 0 Hz -> 18 Hz the device's own report G0 guest-visible IRR 0x0 -> 0x1 after a 1.9 s free-run D1 positive control count 4608 -> 259 Hz, IRR=0x1, identical both ways All four controls green in BOTH runs; only the two symptom rows move. THE DEVICE SIGNATURE IS A VALUE RAM CANNOT PRODUCE, and it was designed against the exact trap that ate the footbridge probe's first draft. The guest writes 0xAA then 0x55 to the SAME address in 16-bit mode, writes the MODE register (a different address), then reads back and gets 0xAA -- the byte from two writes ago. RAM returns 0x55. Nonzero deliberately, because 0x0 is what an ABSENT device looks like. TWO CAVEATS THE SEAT OWNED RATHER THAN HID: G0/G1 use a WALL-CLOCK window (1.9 s against a 55 ms correct period, ~34 chances), which is why the post-fix green is the settlement and not the window size; and its first T1 draft reported FAIL through a string-equality bug in its own script, which it found and fixed. All 27 instruction encodings were checked against the emulator's own disassembler before use -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has hit four times. REACHABILITY, MEASURED: no guest in this tree programs count 0. Every PIT write in _guest-src-openbsd22/sys/ is TIMER_DIV(x) (never 0) or 0xff/0xff, and no rig image boots an 8253 machine. A recollection that Linux's pit_shutdown() writes 0,0 was flagged RECALLED, UNVERIFIED rather than cited -- the right handling. *** BUT FINDING `pitflip` BELOW MANUFACTURES COUNT 0 FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER ASKS FOR IT, which changes the reachability picture entirely. *** MAPPINGS, measured not read: cats and netwinder 0x7c000040; malta/maltabe 0x18000040; cobalt 0x10000040; iyonix 0x90000040; absent on prep, mvmeppc, algor, arc. THE FIX is one line -- hz = (int)(I8253_TIMER_FREQ / 65536.0 + 0.5) -> 18 -- and d->hz[] is read only at :133/137/140, all inside the MSB arm, so the blast radius is that arm. *** DO NOT GENERALISE BY ANALOGY: dev_rtc.c:129 and dev_mc146818.c:409 look identical and are CORRECT -- for those devices zero genuinely means 'off', and dev_rtc.c's comment records a prior round reasoning that through. Latent. *** **True:** in `dev_m8820x.c`'s `m8820x_command()`, `CMMU_PROBE_USER` / `CMMU_PROBE_SUPER` are dropped, so a probe yields a **deterministic SSR miss of `0x0`** -- SSR answers a different question from the one asked. **But no operating guest OS exercises it.** The instruction exists and the register is addressable; nothing a booting system does reaches it. So it is dormant defensive debt and ranks below anything a guest travels. **A deterministic wrong answer is worse than an error in one specific way worth recording:** `0x0` is a *plausible* miss result, so a guest that did probe would receive a well-formed answer to the wrong question rather than a fault it could detect. That is the silent-wrong-versus-loud-wrong axis this project uses, and it puts this above a row that merely fails to implement something. held

MEASURED (build/gxemul, -v -v -V -T -E cats -M 32): device order is 8259 @0x7c000020, 8259 @0x7c0000a0, *** 8253 @0x7c000040 ADDED AFTER BOTH PICs, *** pccmos @0x7c000070. The pointer copy sits at bus_isa.c:224-225, between the first device_add (:223) and the second (:235); the 8253's device_add is at :244. Construction order confirmed in the RUNNING PROGRAM, not inferred -- and it independently confirms the 0x7c000040 mapping. MEASURED (grep census): pending_timer_interrupts has exactly ONE writer (dev_8253.c:282) and TWO pointer-cachers (bus_isa.c:225, dev_v3.c:298), both caching before their 8253 can exist. *** MEASURED, AND THIS IS THE PART NOBODY STATED: dev_8253.c contains ZERO decrements of pending_interrupts_timer0. *** Every other timer device in the tree drains its own counter from inside its own DEVICE_ACCESS handler -- dev_jazz.c:423,443, dev_luna88k.c:800, dev_mc146818.c:563, dev_vr41xx.c:634, dev_footbridge.c:583,594-595. The 8253 ALONE outsourced its drain to bus_isa.c:134-138. READ: that drain is unreachable for TWO INDEPENDENT reasons, *** so moving the pointer copy after device_add -- the fix as filed -- changes NOTHING observable: *** (1) nothing ever calls isa_interrupt_deassert for line 0, as dev_8253.c has no INTERRUPT_DEASSERT; and (2) dev_8259.c clears irr DIRECTLY on EOI (:107, :122), bypassing the isa deassert handler entirely. REFILE AS: 'the 8253's pending-interrupt counter has no reachable drain -- it is the only timer device in the tree that cannot ack', grade DESIGN + needs-witness. Consequence (READ): once any guest touches the PIT, in_use goes 1, the counter rises monotonically and never drains, so DEVICE_TICK re-asserts isa.0 on EVERY device tick (TICK_SHIFT 14) rather than at the programmed rate. TWO THINGS THE FILING SEAT MISSED: dev_v3.c:298 is not merely 'the same shape' -- it is the same bug for the same reason needing the same two-part fix; and if a machine ever created two ISA buses (bus_pci.c calls bus_isa_init at :476 and :1060), the second copy would be NON-NULL AND ALIAS THE FIRST BUS'S 8253 -- worse than NULL, and silent. THE WITNESS THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, rung 3 on -E cats: program counter 0 to ~18 Hz, free-run 200 ms, read the 8259 IRR (expect bit0), write specific-EOI 0x60 to 0x7c000020, free-run ~5 ms, read IRR again. Draining correctly => 0 (next tick due at ~55 ms); no drain => 1 again on the very next device tick. Clean discriminator, no source change. — evidence: build/gxemul -E cats device order; grep census of the drain sites·······

The remedy is already in the same file, applied to the other 2. *** **The shape**, `precommit_check.sh:710-718` (the witness checker, representative of all 14): ```sh if [ ! -f "$WITCHK" ]; then warn "check_witness.py MISSING -- witness naming NOT verified" # SOFT elif out=$(python "$WITCHK" 2>&1); then good ... else bad "A ROW CLOSED WITH COMMITS AND NO ADMISSIBLE WITNESS:" # HARD ``` **A checker that FAILS is a hard failure. A checker that is ABSENT is a warning.** So deleting the file converts a hard gate into a soft one, and the commit proceeds. **THE CENSUS (deriver: `grep -cE '\[ ! -f .*(CHK|check_)'` then the following line):** ``` checkers guarded 14 MISSING -> warn (soft) 12 MISSING -> bad (hard) 2 check_row_states.py, check_cited_artifacts.py ``` > *** THE TWO HARD ONES ARE THE FINDING. *** Somebody already decided this question for two checkers and implemented it in this exact file, so **the remedy is a transferred warrant, not a design** -- make the other twelve match the two. **NOT guest-reachable:** it is a host-side pre-commit script; no emulated guest can delete a worktree file. **Observable:** the precommit process exit status -- 0 when broken, non-zero when fixed. **BUT DO NOT SWEEP IT UNILATERALLY -- there is a real argument on the other side, and it is the one this project keeps citing:** a hard failure on absence means a degraded or partial checkout cannot run the gate AT ALL, and *a check that has to be switched off is worse than no check*. The counter-argument is that all fourteen live in the same repo, so absence is not a partial-checkout condition -- it is a deletion. **That is an adjudication question, not a unilateral edit**, and it changes the script every commit runs, so it also owes negative controls both ways. *Directly relevant to today: I relied on this gate all session and it caught three real obligations. This does not undermine those catches -- a checker that RAN and failed is hard. It bounds what a green gate proves: it proves the checkers PRESENT are satisfied, not that the intended set ran.* held

If rd_msb is already 1 when the latch command arrives, the FIRST latched read has rw == MSB and #440 immediately clears the latch -- so only ONE byte has been read after the count was latched. *** A byte read BEFORE the latch command cannot be a byte of the newly latched value, *** which sits badly with p. 8's 'two bytes must be read'. On that reading R9 pins the implementation's assumption rather than the specification. THE MEASURING SEAT REACHED THE SAME FACT AND THE OPPOSITE READING: at odd parity the first read takes the byte the format calls for and unlatches, which it argues is CLOSER to hardware, and it measured the values (0x9c00 where #439 gave 0x0000). *** BOTH SEATS AGREE ON WHAT THEY CANNOT SETTLE: the local i8254 text does not say whether a Counter Latch Command rewinds the read flip-flop, and there is no other 8253/8254 source in the tree. *** So this is filed as an UNKNOWN and recorded in the source as one, rather than resolved 7-1. An honest UNKNOWN outranks a confident guess, and a majority has been wrong on mechanism in this project at least six times. Codex's proposed shape if it is ever settled against #440: track TWO POST-LATCH READS rather than reusing the format flip-flop -- a boolean `latched` is insufficient when the read phase can be MSB at latch time. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260820_183311/ (7/7 scriptable) + opus5 measuring seat······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — Found by the pass-2 measuring seat, and it is a fair hit on the round's own reasoning. PCR/RTCSR/RTCOR/RFCR all do `idata & mask` with NO byte_order term, so on big-endian a 4-byte access to them takes the LAST two bytes while BCR2/BCR3 now take the FIRST; and they PROMOTE a 1-byte write while BCR2/BCR3 now DROP it. The #441 comment cites them to justify servicing and then services differently on both axes. WHICH CONVENTION IS RIGHT IS NOT DECIDABLE HERE: there is no SH-4 document in this tree (sh4_manual.txt is ONE BYTE), so this is an honest UNKNOWN about the hardware and a real internal inconsistency about the model. One round takes one site, so #441 recorded the divergence in the source rather than silently unifying five registers on a guess. A related nit worth carrying: the round's claim that 'BCR1 already consults byte_order' is true but weak precedent -- BCR1 ORs in a strap bit, it does not place a lane. — evidence: pass-2 seat, read against dev_sh4.c·······

Data is ignored."* **Three independent confirmations of the shipped code, not one:** 1. **write-only** -> a READ must not clear. The fix is architecturally right, not merely defensible. 2. **"Data is ignored"** -> ANY write clears regardless of value. The fix guards on `writeflag` alone and never inspects the data, which matches. 3. **"no effect if already clear"** -> the pre-existing `if (pending > 0)` guard is correct and was left alone. **And the section header confirms the address census independently:** *'Offsets 30Ch, 32Ch, 34Ch, and 36Ch'* -- the four addresses the timer fold normalises onto this one case. **A read now returns whatever `odata` held.** The datasheet marks the read side of a write-only register as having no defined behaviour, so that is acceptable -- and unlike [[n6]], this site does **not** kill the host on read: it is not among that row's eight terminating sites. Different defect, different disposition. **PROCESS DISCLOSURE: I made this edit WITHOUT a pass-1 design brief**, which the standing directive requires. The fix shape was pinned by the sketch rule and the constraint verified, but that reasoning may be wrong -- the panel now running was told so explicitly and asked to say if a design panel would have caught something. **Trees:** `est/` and `build/` byte-identical. **`build-asan/` deliberately NOT synced** -- it is four rounds stale on this file; see [[asanstaletree]]. *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE, GUEST-REACHABLE, and cheap to fix. Established by reading. *** `dev_footbridge.c:681-691`, `case TIMER_1_CLEAR:`, **contains no `writeflag` test at all.** Its whole body runs on a READ: 1. `reload_timer_value()` when the timer is periodic -- reloads the counter; 2. `d->pending_timer_interrupts[timer_nr] --`; 3. `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT(d->timer_irq[timer_nr])`. **So a guest that merely READS the clear register silently acknowledges a pending timer interrupt.** The likely guest-visible consequence is a LOST timer interrupt, not a corrupted value. **The asymmetry is the tell, and it is immediately above:** `case TIMER_1_CONTROL:` at `:656-658` opens with `if (writeflag == MEM_READ) odata = ...; else { ... }`. The neighbouring case does exactly what this one omits. **FOUR addresses, not one.** `:507-509` normalises the timer registers -- `timer_nr = (relative_addr >> 5) & (N_FOOTBRIDGE_TIMERS - 1); relative_addr &= ~0x060;` -- so all four timers' CLEAR registers land on this single case: `0x30C`, `0x32C`, `0x34C`, `0x36C` (`dc21285reg.h:378,382,386,390`). *** THE FIX SHAPE IS CONSTRAINED BY THE FUNCTION'S TAIL, AND THIS WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED -- the sketch rule exists because four readers got this exact thing wrong on `#463`. *** `dev_footbridge_access` ends (`:738-741`) with: ```c if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata); return 1; ``` **So the fix must GUARD THE BODY and keep the `break`.** An early `return` inside the case would skip that tail and hand a guest read an untouched buffer -- a defect the current code does not have. The correct edit is to wrap the three statements in `if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) { ... }`, leaving the `break` in place. **A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH RECORDING, because it closes an obvious follow-up question:** the device is registered `DM_DEFAULT` (`:782-784`), NOT `DM_READS_HAVE_NO_SIDE_EFFECTS`. The registration is therefore CONSISTENT with a side-effecting read, and the debugger's `dump` does not reach this handler. **There is no second defect in the registration flags** -- which is the first thing a reader would suspect on seeing a read with side effects. **NOT FIXED: needs a build for the detector.** The rows are straightforward -- read each of the four CLEAR offsets with an interrupt pending and show the pending count UNCHANGED after the fix and DECREMENTED before it -- but they are measurements, and floor clause (b) needs the unguarded body reinstated verbatim at all four (i.e. at the one shared case). Queued behind the embargo with the other build-blocked rows. held

(1) *** stdbuf's LD_PRELOAD PREEMPTS THE ASan RUNTIME. *** The obvious fix for abort()-not-flushing is stdbuf -o0, and on an ASan build it breaks the binary instead. It needs verify_asan_link_order=0 -- and this had to be proven BEHAVIOURALLY, because *** this ASan SILENTLY IGNORES bogus options ***, so the discriminator this project uses elsewhere (pass a nonsense value; a validated flag names its own list) FAILS HERE. That discriminator is written into CLAUDE.md as the way to prove a flag is real; this is a documented exception to it. (2) The shell's `Aborted (core dumped)` line is emitted AT THE CALL SITE, not inside the function, so wrapping the command in `( ... ) 2>/dev/null` does NOT suppress it. Measured. A harness that filters stderr expecting to have silenced it will still see the line and may classify on it. Recorded as a row rather than only a comment because both are general techniques, not gate-9 specifics, and the next probe that meets an aborting binary will reach for exactly these. — evidence: measured during the gate-9 round·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — *** THE SHARPEST FORM OF A TRAP THIS PROJECT ALREADY RECORDS, AND IT REACHED THE TOP-LEVEL HARNESS INVOCATION. *** The full battery was started as bash run.sh 2>&1 | tail -45 in the background, and later killed. *** IT REPORTED EXIT CODE 0. *** A pipeline's status is the LAST command's, so the exit code belonged to `tail`, which succeeded in reading a truncated stream. Two things went wrong together and either alone would have been survivable: 1. THE VERDICT WAS FALSE -- a killed battery reported success. 2. THERE WAS NOTHING TO READ EITHER WAY. `| tail` buffers until the pipeline ends, so the output file sat at 0 BYTES for the whole run and was still 0 bytes afterwards. Mid-run progress was invisible and the post-mortem was empty. Same genus as `cmd | head` reporting head's status, which this project already writes down and which bit twice more the same day -- once hiding a compile failure, once mangling an object list through a `tr` inside nested quoting. What is NEW is the SCALE: this is not a check inside a gate, it is the invocation of the ENTIRE 16-GATE BATTERY. A SECOND TRAP RODE ALONG WITH IT, and it nearly did more damage: with the real output empty, the obvious place to look was the shared log directory -- which still held the PREVIOUS battery's verdicts. Those read `asan-machine-sweep: PASS (3 checks)` and `log-hygiene: PASS (38 checks)`, both plausible and both STALE (the current gates give 11 and 48). Reading them as this run's result would have been the 'a green row means nothing' class in its purest form, and the only thing that prevented it was the check counts having moved that day. THE FIX USED: run under `exec > /tmp/battery.log 2>&1` so output streams to a file and the exit status is run.sh's own. The re-run produced REGRESS_PASS across all 16 gates in 48 minutes, with progress readable throughout. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT MECHANICAL: a verdict is believable only if its log ends in a terminal token. nightly_check.sh already treats a MISSING or STALE verdict as failure -- the same reasoning one level in would refuse a verdict whose log carries no REGRESS_PASS/REGRESS_FAIL line, which is exactly what a killed run leaves behind. That is checkable and is the part worth building. — evidence: measured: the killed invocation's own exit code and its 0-byte output file·······

nulheredocnulheredoc A shell heredoc wrote three literal NUL bytes into two tracked text files, silently turning every grep against them binarynulheredoc A shell heredoc wrote three literal NUL bytes into two tracked text files, silently turning every grep against them binary — HOLD: Fix and guard are written and negative-controlled; awaiting its commit. — witness: harness:precommit_check.sh section Y -- negative-controlled BOTH ways on the day it landed: injecting one NUL into a tracked .md turns it RED and names the file; restoring turns it GREEN at 672 tracked text files. `harness:` is the right witness kind because the subject is the test apparatus. — note: *** SYMPTOM ABSENT, CAUSE NOW GUARDED, 2026-08-27 -- and I reproduced the defect by accident while building the guard, which is the best evidence the guard is worth having. *** **The row:** a shell heredoc wrote three literal NUL bytes into two tracked text files, *silently turning every grep against them binary*. The damage is not the bytes -- it is that grep then reports NOTHING, and nearly every gate in this tree is grep-based. **Current state: 0 NUL bytes across 672 tracked text files**, measured with `tr -cd`. *** MY FIRST MEASUREMENT OF THAT WAS INERT AND I REPORTED IT AS A RESULT. *** I scanned 1161 tracked files with `LC_ALL=C grep -qP` and got 0 hits. **grep REFUSES to run `-P` under `LC_ALL=C`** -- *"supports only unibyte and UTF-8 locales"* -- so it never ran, and with `-q` and `2>/dev/null` the refusal was invisible. **0 of 1161 was a check that could not fail.** The honest figure is 0 of 672, by a method with no regex engine in it. *** AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THE GUARD WROTE A NUL INTO ITSELF. *** Writing `\\x00` through a Bash -> heredoc -> Python path lost one backslash level, exactly as the carrier documents, so Python emitted byte 0x00 into `precommit_check.sh` -- **reproducing this row's own mechanism inside the check meant to catch it**, and ordinary grep immediately called the script binary. That is how the inert `-P` was found at all. **THE GUARD, and why it is shaped this way:** `precommit_check.sh` section Y uses **`tr -cd`, not grep** -- no regex engine, no `-P`, no locale dependency, and no backslash that has to survive a quoting layer. It carries a ZERO-DENOMINATOR guard (if the `ls-files` pattern selects nothing it FAILS loudly rather than reporting clean), and it is scoped to text extensions on purpose: a future tracked `.pdf` or `.png` carries NULs legitimately, and a check that has to be switched off is worse than no check. **Negative-controlled in both directions before it landed**, which is mandatory for a change to the script every commit runs: inject one NUL into a tracked `.md` -> RED, naming the file; restore -> GREEN at 672 files. **DISPOSITION: the symptom is gone and the cause is now MECHANICALLY GUARDED.** Recommend CLOSE. Note no fix commit was ever recorded on this row, so the original NULs were removed by unrelated edits -- which is precisely why a guard was worth more than a cleanup. held
Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — SELF-INFLICTED, BY ME, IN bcdbfb8 -- badge A. #446 wrote comments quoting the bad-fix mutant it had to defend against (a zero byte written as a C escape) into CHANGELOG.md and regress/gate_offline.sh THROUGH A SHELL HEREDOC, which interpreted the escape. Three literal NULs landed: CHANGELOG.md lines 4254 and 4260, gate_offline.sh line 1803. *** IT SURVIVED PRECOMMIT, A 265-CHECK GATE RUN, AND THE COMMIT ***, because bash does not care about a NUL inside a comment. WHAT IT BREAKS IS THE HARNESS'S CORE IDIOM. grep(1) auto-detects such a file as binary and answers "Binary file ... matches" -- ON STDOUT, WITH EXIT 0. So `grep -q` still works and `grep -c` still counts, while every check that PARSES A FIELD out of the matched line silently receives that sentence in place of the row. MEASURED: `grep 'sgi_eaddr: the buffer' gate_offline.sh` returned the sentence, exit 0. Not a wrong value -- a wrong SHAPE, through a channel no section watched. *** THE FIRST SWEEP I RAN TO SCOPE IT WAS ITSELF VOID and I reported its result. *** It found ZERO NULs -- including the one I had just located by hand -- because the nested bash -c ate its `$'\x00'`. I said "it is the only tracked file affected" on the strength of a sweep that found nothing at all. The real sweep found THREE bytes across TWO files. A sweep that finds nothing and a sweep that cannot find anything are indistinguishable in the output. GUARD: precommit section S, negative-controlled both ways. Its own first draft used `grep -qU "$(printf '\000')"` and PUT A FRESH NUL INTO precommit_check.sh -- the check forbidding the byte introduced the byte. `tr -d` takes the escape as a two-character argument interpreted at runtime, so nothing in the file is ever a zero byte. GIT'S OWN BINARY DETECTION CANNOT BE THE ORACLE: `git ls-files --eol` reports i/-text for a PNG and for a corrupted text file identically, so deriving the domain from git would exempt precisely the broken files. Circular. Hence an explicit skip list, plus two genuinely-binary paths that carry no extension (src/devices/fonts/*, test/FileLoader_*). — evidence: measured in-tree, 2026-08-21·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-21 — MANUAL — *** THE FUNCTION CALLED sh4_dmac_transfer() DOES NOT TRANSFER. *** Found while settling a pass-1 seat's question about body ordering, and it refuted the question rather than answering it. `sar`, `dar`, `count` and `chcr` are LOCAL copies; there is no `cpu->cd.sh.dmac_*` assignment anywhere in the function; and the only arm that returns normally, `case 0x200:`, is literally `(void)sar; (void)dar;` under the comment 'Note: No transfer is done here! It is up to the external device to do the transfer itself!'. So no bytes move, SAR/DAR/DMATCR are never advanced, and TE is never set. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is why this is filed rather than shrugged at. (1) It made #448 trivially safe -- every site is side-effect-free before it dies, so there is nothing to un-commit and no store had to move. (2) *** A GUEST THAT ENABLES DMA AND POLLS FOR COMPLETION ALREADY WAITS FOREVER, ON THE ONE CONFIGURATION THE MODEL ACCEPTS, BEFORE AND AFTER #448 ALIKE. *** Two pass-1 seats raised the hang risk as something #448 might CREATE; measurement shows it PRE-EXISTS and #448 neither causes nor worsens it. Honest limit: READ, not executed. No guest here has been observed waiting -- landisk's kernel may never enable a DMA channel at all. Whether any guest this project boots reaches it is unmeasured, so this is a capability gap of unknown reachability rather than a witnessed defect. — evidence: source read, 2026-08-21·······

That is the bit a compare-match poll waits on. *`RTCNT` staying 0 is a second channel; the title's hang is CMF.* *** THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ROW IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX: setting `CMF` as a consolation, with no `RTCNT`, IS WHAT `#449` PASS-1 REFUSED -- and that refusal still holds. *** A fix that plants the flag without advancing the counter makes the poll exit while the time base is still frozen: the guest stops waiting and is then wrong about the elapsed time, which is worse than waiting. **In-tree idiom for the shape:** the same file's `sh4_timer_tick()` does `d->tcr[i] |= TCR_UNF` on TMU wrap and queues a pending interrupt if `UNIE` -- so the flag-plus-interrupt pattern exists; what this row needs in addition is the COUNTER. held

Candidate answers for a round to weigh: a compile-time assertion that the classes' bit domains are disjoint; or making the class a property of the register rather than a hand-written argument at each call site. — evidence: measured, panel_20260821_211546·······

Assessment (initial problem)····✓2026-08-21 — MANUAL — Found while checking #450's consequence trace: the reason the load-bearing shift site :751 never fires is that *** THE WALK ITSELF IS BROKEN. *** The 64-bit walker reads 4 bytes at peeraddr+0x34 as 'IdentifierLength'. In-RAM layout: ptr_peer/ptr_child/ptr_parent (0x18) then arcbios_component64 -- Class +0x18, Key +0x28, AffinityMask +0x30, ConfigurationDataSize +0x38, IdentifierLength +0x40, Identifier +0x48, total 0x50 = exactly the walker's step. So +0x34 is the HIGH HALF OF AFFINITYMASK. The walker masks the read with 0xfffff and skips accordingly -- with AffinityMask 0xffffffff that is a ~1 MiB skip per node, and the walk leaves the component list after the first node. CONSEQUENCE FOR #450's record, stated there too: :751's mis-link hazard is a counterfactual PARTLY BECAUSE this bug prevents the walk from ever reaching a node whose parent pointer would exercise it. Fixing this row may make that site live -- the coupling runs one way, like ctorabortclass before it. HONEST LIMIT: layout arithmetic and one corroborating step constant, no execution. The 32-bit walker's offset (+0x28 read, +0x30 step) should be checked in the same round rather than assumed correct by symmetry. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260821_220346····

So when the remainder exceeds 32768 the re-arm reports **zero bytes remaining while `atapi_received < data_in_len`** -- the byte count goes to 0, and **no path ever completes the command.** *** THIS IS LIVE TODAY, not a consequence of any fix. Every transfer above ~64 KB already stalls, and the (64K, 256.5K] band never overruns the ring at all -- it is broken purely by this. *** That fact demolished the scope argument the parent row was holding on. **IT IS A DEFECT, NOT A DELIBERATE GIVE-UP, and the evidence is historical:** the zeroing is **upstream-inherited verbatim** -- the pristine 2021 copy carries it identically -- and `#341` rewrote the ENCLOSING countdown (`-= len` to `-= consumed`) while neither touching nor assessing it. No fork record defends it. The read-time clamps are **dead code** under both write-side caps: the signature of an unfinished chunking implementation. **And even read as a give-up it is the wrong one by the fork's own standing class:** reporting 0 remaining while data remains is exactly `#341`'s *the count reported has to be the count that happened* -- the truthfulness family with `#283` (ASC) and `#338` (mb89352). *One caveat on that classing: the file comment placing this family here describes `#341`'s countdown sibling. **The zeroing itself is uncommented** -- so the family membership is an argument, not a citation.* held

All nine derefs of `atapi_st` in the file, with their protection: ``` :812 atapi_received < atapi_st->data_in_len <- the #476 site, NOW GUARDED :877 atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len - .. <- nested inside :812's true arm :884 wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[..]) <- same block :1033 atapi_st->cmd = scsi_cmd <- immediately after the alloc :1034 atapi_st->cmd_len = 12 at :1023 :1039 atapi_st->cmd_len = 10 :1072 if (atapi_st->data_in != NULL) :1082 atapi_len = atapi_st->data_in_len :1087 wdc_addtoinbuf(.. atapi_st->data_in[j]) ``` **The first three are the reachable family and all three are inside the arm `#476` guards** -- `:812` runs only when `atapi_len == 0 && atapi_st != NULL`, and `:877`/`:884` are nested within its true branch. **The remaining six sit after `scsi_transfer_alloc()`, WHICH CANNOT RETURN NULL** -- verified by opening it: on malloc failure it prints and `exit(1)`s. (That exit is a separate, pre-existing, OOM-only concern and is not guest-reachable.) *Worth noting for anyone reasoning about the free: `scsi_transfer_alloc` runs a FREELIST, so a fresh alloc typically REUSES the just-freed chunk. That is why a pointer-identity oracle reads a false negative on a plain build and only separates under a sanitiser's quarantine -- a seat measured exactly that.* **So no second host kill of this family is in the tree.** Recorded as an enumeration a reader can re-derive rather than as an assurance. *** A REGRESSION I SHIPPED, FOUND BY THE MEASURING SEAT ONE COMMIT LATER, FIXED THE SAME HOUR. 2026-08-27. *** ``` d894e35 (before #475) a DATA read with no transfer survives exit 0 d64a1fc (with #475) a DATA read with no transfer survives host killed, signal 11 ``` **THE MECHANISM IS ENTIRELY #475's.** Before it, a data-port read with `atapi_len` already 0 drove the counter NEGATIVE, so `if (atapi_len == 0)` never fired again and the `d->atapi_st->data_in_len` deref on the next line was **dead code**. The clamp makes `atapi_len` STAY 0. The test fires. `atapi_st` is NULL. > **A FIX THAT STOPS A COUNTER GOING NEGATIVE CAN MAKE A PREVIOUSLY-UNREACHABLE BRANCH > REACHABLE.** The clamp was right; the branch it woke was never NULL-safe. *Repairing a > counter can enable code that was only ever protected by the broken value* -- and nothing > in `#475`'s own kill table could see it, because every mutant there attacked the clamp > rather than what the clamp let through. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1. * NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA. * IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent. * *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set. * THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling. * DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. The oracle must be EXACTLY ONE, THEN ZERO** -- announcement AND suppression, which is the pair a latch actually promises. *** PASS 2 (panel_20260825_204943) FOUND THREE ESCAPES AGAINST A DETECTOR MEASURED 14/14, AND ONE OF THEM IS A STRUCTURAL BLINDNESS OF THE ROWS RATHER THAN A GAP IN THEM. *** All three are L1 -- pre-ship construction, fixed in-round, not filed. **(1) glm -- THE RESET-ON-NORMAL-OPERATION ESCAPE, and it is the sharpest.** ONE line, reusing the existing flag, guard and branch, added inside an existing case for a VALID command: `d->warned_unimpl_cmd = 0;`. **Every site row fires its site TWICE IN SUCCESSION with no normal device operation between**, so the flag is never reset between fires and the row stays green -- while a real guest that probes an unimplemented opcode, issues IDENTIFY, probes again, issues IDENTIFY, floods forever. Here a latch write CLOBBERS mode_byte (destroying the RW format the guest set earlier) and ZEROES d->mode[counter], because the latch command's mode bits are 0. SO EVEN A GUEST THAT NEVER READS THE LATCHED VALUE HAS HAD ITS COUNTER SILENTLY REPROGRAMMED. That is a distinct consequence from pitlatch's (a latch-then-read returns 0 and floods the host log): this one damages state on the WRITE alone. Reachability inherits pitlatch's: OpenBSD's microtime() issues the latch command (_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/i386/isa/clock.c:207-209), so the clobber happens on every call. NOT MEASURED -- no probe has yet shown the downstream effect of the corrupted RW format, and the honest grade is READ until one does.
