sh4sqwritesh4sqwrite The SQ WRITE half is never judged -- so an SQ page can raise no initial-page-write and no write-side protection fault, while the PREF still raises the read-side setsh4sqwrite The SQ WRITE half is never judged -- so an SQ page can raise no initial-page-write and no write-side protection fault, while the PREF still raises the read-side set — witness: none yet -- GUEST-REACHABLE and witnessable at rung 3 (a real guest store through real decode, observable in EXPEVT), but a witness needs a build, which the machine embargo forbids. — note: *** SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-27: THE DEFECT IS THE **WRITE HALF ONLY**, and saying the window 'bypasses the MMU ENTIRELY' reintroduces wording this row's title was already corrected away from. *** **Why the unqualified form is wrong:** the round's own `sq miss evt` detector observes a **read-type TLB miss (`0x040`)** on the fixed build, so the read side is NOT unrouted. `memory_sh.c:290-301` carries the corrected scope. > **THE CORRECT STATEMENT: no initial-page-write exception and no write-side protection check on stores into the SQ window.** The read/prefetch path translates; the store path does not. That asymmetry IS the defect, and it is narrower and more defensible than 'bypasses the MMU'. **AND THE SECTION CITATIONS ARE BOTH RIGHT, FOR DIFFERENT THINGS -- reconciled here so the next reader does not have to choose:** * **section 3.6.7** *defines* the Initial Page Write exception and its code: *"occurs when the D bit is 0 even though a UTLB entry contains address translation information matching the virtual address to which a data access (write) is made... Sets exception code H'080 in EXPEVT."* (`sh7750_hardware.txt:9918-9928`) * **section 4.7.4, 'SQ Protection'** *applies* it to the store queues: *"Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or initial page write exception is generated."* (`:11742-11748`) **The code cites 4.7.4; I cited 3.6.7. Cite BOTH -- 4.7.4 is the one that makes it apply to this window, and 3.6.7 is the one that says what the exception is.** **Ranking, from today's adjudication: 7th of 8.** Latent -- no known guest depends on SQ write-protection. *It is a fidelity gap, not a live corruption, and my earlier 'most severe row in the batch' was severity within that batch, not across the queue.* *** INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, and the step that could have KILLED it -- whether SH-4 exempts the store queue from translation -- goes the OTHER WAY. The manual refutes the exemption. (Already documented in-source and filed; today's work is re-verification.) *** **THE BYPASS IS UNCONDITIONAL.** `memory_sh.c:353-357`: ```c /* Store queue region: */ if (vaddr >= 0xe0000000 && vaddr < 0xe4000000) { /* Note/TODO: Take SH4_MMUCR_SQMD into account. */ *return_paddr = vaddr; return 2; } ``` **No `MMUCR.AT` test, no UTLB walk, no PR/D check**, and it returns 2 (read/write). `cpu_sh.c:106` is the only assignment of `translate_v2p`, and the sole SH consumer of `0xe0000000` in `src/cpus/` is `pref_rn` -- **no store instruction special-cases the window**, so every `mov.l Rm,@Rn` into it takes this branch. The preceding arm (`:339-350`) matches neither, so the path is identical with AT=1 and AT=0. *** THE MANUAL SETTLES IT AGAINST THE EXEMPTION, from three directions: *** * **section 4.7.4, SQ Protection** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:11742-11748`): *"When MMU is on -- Operation is in accordance with the address translation information recorded in the UTLB, and MMUCR.SQMD. **Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs** ... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or **initial page write exception** is generated."* * **section 4.7.3** (`:11691-11696`): *"the ASID, V, SZ, SH, PR, and D bits have the same meaning as for normal address translation."* * **QACR is explicitly the MMU-OFF-only mechanism** (`:11719-11723`, `:10473`), so it is NOT an alternative translation path under AT=1. **AND PRIVILEGE DOES NOT RESCUE IT.** The Data TLB Protection Violation table (`:12632-12640`) gives `PR=00` as **"Only read access possible"** in PRIVILEGED mode, with EXPEVT `0x0A0` read / `0x0C0` write at `:12650`. *** THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CLEANEST STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: THE READ SIDE IS TRANSLATED AND THE WRITE SIDE IS NOT. *** The flush path at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3706-3765` explicitly checks `SH4_MMUCR_AT` and calls `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` -> `translate_via_mmu()`. The store path does none of it. **WHY THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CANNOT SEE THIS, and it is not a detector defect:** `regress/sh_halt_probe.py:590-599` pins `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` to **NOEXC deliberately** -- those rows exercise the read-type PREF path, where no protection or dirty case exists. **No row exercises the STORE side at all**, so the detector is silent here rather than contradicting the finding. **ADJACENT, DISTINCT, ALREADY FILED:** the `SQMD` TODO on that same branch is a SECOND gap -- section 4.7.4 requires an ADDRESS ERROR for a user-mode SQ access when `MMUCR.SQMD = 1` even when translation succeeds, and the store path checks neither. `pref_rn` does check it (`cpu_sh_instr.c:3709-3715`) but raises `EXPEVT_RES_INST` instead -- filed as `sh4sqexpevt`. *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. A store into the store-queue window BYPASSES THE MMU, so page protection is not enforced on it. The most severe row in this batch. *** **The mechanism:** the SQ write path does not go through `sh_translate_v2p()` / `translate_via_mmu()` (`memory_sh.c:353-357`, `:203-241`, with the source's own commentary at `:289-303`), so a store into the SQ window lands directly in the device's `sq` array. **Guest access sequence, fully specified by the seat:** 1. guest kernel enables paging (`MMUCR.AT = 1`); 2. guest maps the SQ virtual page `0xe0000000` in the UTLB **valid** (`V=1`) and either **clean** (`D=0`) or **read-only** (`PR=00`); 3. guest issues `mov.l r0, @r1` with `r1 = 0xe0000000`. **Expected on hardware (SH7750 sections 4.7.4 / 3.6.7):** an **Initial Page Write** exception (`EXPEVT = 0x080`) on `D=0`, or a **Data Write Protection** exception on a read-only page. **Actual here:** the store simply succeeds. > **So a guest that maps a page read-only, or clean-for-dirty-tracking, and then stores through the SQ window gets a write that hardware would have faulted.** That is protection and dirty-bit tracking silently not enforced -- not a fidelity nit. **Observable:** the guest `EXPEVT` register after the store -- `0x080` (or the write-protect code) when correct, unchanged when broken. Readable by an ordinary guest load, so no new probe capability is needed. **CHECKABLE AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE WE HAVE:** the seat cites SH7750 sections 4.7.4 and 3.6.7, and `_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt` is present and greppable. **Confirm the two sections before the round** -- and read the PROSE, not a figure, per the extraction rule. *** PROMOTED BY THE CODEX RATING PASS, 2026-09-07, ON A ROW IT WAS NOT ASKED ABOUT -- and the promotion is the answer to the brief's Q3, *what does my reading order miss?* *** *"Promote `sh4sqwrite` ahead of the latent ASIC proposals. Its title sounds like missing tests, but `memory_sh.c` (anchor `Store queue region:`) grants read/write access directly, and `dev_sh4.c` (anchor `DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4_sq)`) accepts the writes into queue storage. Hardware requires write-type exception checks on stores into those queues."* (Renesas SH7750 manual, S4.7.4.) > **THAT IS A GUEST-REACHABLE MISSING PROTECTION CHECK, not a coverage gap** -- and it was invisible > to my keyword scan because the TITLE reads like harness debt. *"No known guest depends on it" > does not establish unreachability.* **And the row's existing witness cannot carry it:** `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` in `regress/sh_halt_probe.py` exercise **PREF's READ-type judgement**, so they cannot witness a missing STORE-side check. A witness for this row has to drive a store. *Filed as the strongest single finding of that pass; it needs a `sev` and a round of its own.*open

sh4itlbprsh4itlbpr ITLB data array 1 is one bit too wide, and SIX shipped rows now REQUIRE the extra bitsh4itlbpr ITLB data array 1 is one bit too wide, and SIX shipped rows now REQUIRE the extra bit — witness: none -- ASSESSED 2026-08-27 and NOT CHANGED. A rung-3 probe is designable (privileged store/load at 0xf3000000, key on r2 & 0x20) but is deliberately not built: the oracle-correction rule requires re-pinning six SHIPPED rows and measuring the committed build RED *before* any edit, which needs a build the machine embargo forbids. — note: *** FIRST EVIDENCE 2026-08-27, from a farmed codex job. The mask arithmetic is CONFIRMED exactly; the SEVERITY is lower than the seat implied, and the reason is a phrase in the manual the seat did not weigh. *** **CONFIRMED, and recomputed here from the header's own constants rather than transcribed:** `dev_sh4.c:1020-1021` builds the ITLB data-array-1 mask with `SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK` = **0x60, a TWO-bit field**, giving 0x1ffffdfa. Narrowing PR to the ITLB's own `SH4_ITLB_DA1_PR` = 0x40 gives 0x1ffffdda. Both values match the seat digit for digit. **The extra bit is 0x20.** **THE PRIMARY SOURCE AGREES, and it was read as PROSE, not off a figure** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:10035-10036`, section 3.7.2): *"In the data field, PPN is indicated by bits [28:10], V by bit [8], SZ by bits [7] and [4], PR by bit [6], C by bit [3], and SH by bit [1]."* **Bit [6], singular** -- so for the ITLB, bit 5 is not part of PR. The sibling `sh4_utlb_da1` at `:1220-1224` keeps the two-bit mask and is CORRECT: the UTLB's PR really is [6:5]. *** BUT THE SAME FIGURE'S LEGEND (`:10062`) SAYS RESERVED BITS ARE "0 write value, UNDEFINED READ VALUE" -- SO RETURNING 0x20 IS ARCHITECTURALLY PERMITTED, NOT WRONG. *** That single clause is what moves this from 'defect' to 'fidelity nit', and no seat quoted it. **THE SEAT'S LOAD-BEARING PREMISE -- 'no translation decision uses that bit' -- IS TRUE, BUT ONLY VIA A TWO-STEP CHAIN IT DID NOT GIVE, AND I FIRST SCORED IT FALSE.** The single consumer is `memory_sh.c:163`, `pr = (lo & SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK) >> SH4_PTEL_PR_SHIFT` -- a TWO-bit read, and `lo` **can** be `itlb_lo` (`:120-122`). That looks like the bit reaching a decision. It does not, because: 1. `:114-117` -- ITLB entries are walked **only** when `FLAG_INSTR` is set; 2. `:195-200` -- the instruction arm tests **only** `if (!(pr & 2))`, i.e. `pr` bit 1, which is `lo` bit 6, the REAL PR bit. Bit 5 becomes `pr` bit 0, which that arm never reads. The data-side `switch (pr)` at `:206`/`:219` DOES separate 0/1/2/3 -- but the ITLB never reaches it. > **THE LATENT COUPLING, which is the part actually worth carrying:** the bit is inert because of ONE arm's specific test, not because of any structural guarantee. An edit making instruction protection 'more complete' -- replacing `if (!(pr & 2))` with a `switch (pr)` mirroring the data path -- would make a guest-stored reserved bit LIVE, flipping pr=2 into pr=3. Narrowing the store mask would make the inertness structural. *That is the real argument for the change, and it is a defence-in-depth argument, not a correctness one.* **NOT CHANGED, and the cost is why.** Six SHIPPED rows in `#452`'s detector pin the current mask -- R3 and A4i in `sh4_tlbda2_probe.py` (`:37`, `:251`), C1 in `sh4_tlbda2_witness.py` (`:126`) -- all keyed off `ITLB_MASK = ... | _PR | ... # 0x1ffffdfa` (`probe:71`, `witness:53`), which the probe uses as a **per-device signature** (`:68`) to tell ITLB from UTLB. The ADDITION LICENCE wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant; the manual supplies neither, since it makes the present read value legal. And the ORACLE-CORRECTION RULE requires re-pinning those rows FIRST and measuring the committed build RED under the new expectations **before** touching code -- which needs a build. **Correctly queued behind the machine embargo, not skipped.** (The signature property would survive a narrowing: 0x1ffffdda vs the UTLB's 0x1ffffdff still differ.) *Apparatus note, against my own checking rather than the seat's: my first grep for the header constants used `[ ]` in ERE, which is the set {space, backslash, t} and does NOT match a tab -- so it returned NOTHING and I nearly scored the seat unverifiable. Second instance of the same class today, after the `0x3e0` literal-vs-symbol miss on `sh4pcic15`.* open

But priority initialisation in `cpu_sh.c` runs for (i = SH4_INTEVT_IRQ0; i <= SH4_INTEVT_IRQ14; i += 0x20) **-- it stops at IRQ14.** Line 15 therefore keeps priority 0, and an assertion at priority 0 returns without scheduling delivery. **A line the device registers can never be delivered.** **IT IS LATENT, and the seat established that rather than asserting it:** PCIC MMIO never generates an interrupt; no modelled device connects to `.pcic.15`; landisk's only prospective PCI device is compile-disabled AND would use line 5 anyway. **There is no guest access sequence in the shipped tree**, so this ranks below anything guest-reachable. **THE OBSERVABLE a detector would key on:** guest interrupt-vector entry with `SH4_INTEVT == 0x3e0` -- delivery sets INTEVT and transfers to `VBR+0x600`; the broken code never reaches that handler. That is one channel, not a design. *The seat labelled its own work honestly: 'MEASURED -- Not run; no build is needed to settle these source facts.' Correct, and it is why this row could be settled under the machine embargo.* *** ONE VERIFICATION NOTE, because it cuts against my own checking rather than the seat's: my grep for the literal `0x3e0` in the device file returned NOTHING and I nearly scored the citation as wrong. The file uses the SYMBOL `SH4_INTEVT_IRQ15`. The seat cited the right site; my pattern could not see it. THE MANUAL, READ LOCALLY rather than taken from a search summary: _scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt:18607-18608 reads 'FRQCR is initialized only by a power-on reset via the RESET pin. The initial value of each bit is determined by the clock operating mode', and the bit table immediately below at :18610-18614 gives initial values CKOEN=1 (bit 11), PLL1EN=1 (bit 10), PLL2EN=1 (bit 9) with bits 15-12 = 0. So the reset value carries at least 0x0E00 and is NEVER 0x0000. The register table at :18476 marks the reset column 'Undefined*'; :18607 is the footnote that explains the asterisk, so 'undefined' means MODE-DEPENDENT, not zero -- a distinction that would have been easy to read the wrong way from the table alone. A guest reading FRQCR therefore sees both PLLs disabled and clock output disabled, the opposite of the reset state. WITNESS: one 16-bit guest load from 0xffc00000 on an unmodified SH-4 machine. HONEST LIMIT, the same shape as sh4pcic15's: the model has no clock-operating-mode concept, so a round must DECIDE what to present rather than read one value off the manual. The three bits above are mode-INDEPENDENT and settle the floor; IFC2 and the divider bits are not.·······

probeslowprobeslow gdrom_default_probe.py's cost is SESSIONS, not rows -- the 1800s overrun was real at 44 rows and is measured false at 52probeslow gdrom_default_probe.py's cost is SESSIONS, not rows -- the 1800s overrun was real at 44 rows and is measured false at 52 — witness: none needed -- a harness cost measurement, not a device defect — note: *** AND THE FEATURE'S VALUE WAS DEMONSTRATED THE SAME HOUR, BY A SEAT THAT BUILT ONE. *** While measuring Round 2's mutants the opus seat wrote its own probe WITH session selection (`tprobe2.py <bin> <img> 'S1 badfmt,S4 acceptA'`) and used it immediately: for the Site A fallthrough mutant it ran TWO sessions instead of eight, because only those two can distinguish a decline from an accept. **That is the argument for the feature and, read carefully, also the argument for why it is a separate round.** Selection is CHEAP in a purpose-built probe where it is designed in; the cost measured here is RETROFITTING it to a 1200-line probe whose 36 sessions run at module level. The two facts are not in tension -- they are the same fact seen from each end, and a future round should read them together rather than citing one. *** A FOURTH COST FACT, MEASURED 2026-08-28, AND IT IS ABOUT THE FIX RATHER THAN THE COST: A ROW FILTER IS NOT A SMALL CHANGE TO THIS PROBE. *** Round 2 was going to fold one in -- the owner approved it on a cost I stated -- and the estimate was wrong by roughly 10x. Measured before building: session() calls at MODULE level (column 0) 36 session() calls inside a block 3 -- 39 **Skipping a row therefore means skipping TOP-LEVEL STATEMENTS.** A filter in `row()` alone changes what is SCORED and saves NOTHING, because the expensive part -- the session -- has already run by the time row() is called. Real per-row selection needs either a label threaded through all 36 call sites with an early-return in session(), or the probe restructured into per-row functions. **WITHDRAWN FROM ROUND 2 BY OWNER DECISION** so the strengthening diff stays about the replacement channel, which is what its pass 2 reviews. It ships as its own round with its own panel and its own negative controls -- a filter that silently selects nothing is this project's most-recorded failure class, and it must not ride in on a diff reviewed for something else. WHEN IT IS BUILT, the guards are already specified: print a DENOMINATOR (`selected N of 58`) beside every result; HARD-FAIL on zero matches; HARD-FAIL on a selector naming a row that does not exist (so a renamed row cannot silently stop being tested); and unset MUST be byte-identical to today, which is the negative control the gate itself provides. Name derived from the tree rather than invented: `GDROM_DEF_ROWS` -- the house idiom is `os.environ.get("<TOOL>_<KNOB>")` (SELFMUTANT_RUN_TIMEOUT and friends) and this probe already owns the GDROM_DEF_ namespace via GDROM_DEF_RESULT= / GDROM_DEF_VECTOR=. *** AND THE GATE PINS THE DENOMINATOR AT 58: *** gate_sh_rounding.sh names rows in a `for v in ...` list and checks the ratio, so any filter must leave the unset-path denominator untouched. *** A THIRD COST VARIABLE, MEASURED 2026-08-27: COMMANDS PER SESSION. *** This row's headline is *"cost is SESSIONS, not rows"*, and that was derived from probes whose rows each run one short session. **A row added to `asic_badaddr_probe.py` today is ONE session -- cheap by this row's own measure -- and took roughly SIX MINUTES.** ``` the other 13 rows ~15 s each one session, a handful of debugger commands `sweep 256` ~6 min one session, 768 debugger commands ``` It walks all 256 offsets of the SYSASIC window with `r1=<addr>; pc=<code>; step 1` per offset. Each of those is a pty round-trip, and the round-trips dominate: the emulator work itself is 256 byte loads. **SO THE RULE NEEDS A SECOND TERM.** A probe's wall clock is roughly `sessions x boot_cost + total_debugger_commands x round_trip`, and the two terms are traded against each other by DESIGN CHOICES that look unrelated: folding N rows into one session removes N boots and keeps every command. **THE CHEAPER SHAPE, not built:** drive the walk from GUEST CODE -- a loop, or an unrolled block written once with `put h` -- so one `step N` replaces hundreds of round-trips. Not done today because hand-assembling SH is this project's documented encoding trap, and a wrong encoding yields a probe that measures the wrong thing while looking green. *Recorded rather than acted on: the six minutes buys a row that defends 256 offsets where nine were defended before, and the alternative risks a silently-wrong instrument.* open

Final review (flagship adjudication)✓2026-08-24 — There is NO copy of Linux's drivers/cdrom/gdrom.c or NetBSD's sys/arch/dreamcast/dev/gdrom.c anywhere in this tree, yet #462's design rested on three claims about them. *** ONE WAS REFUTED FROM ITS OWN QUOTED LINE. *** Four records cited `while ((GDROM_BUSY & 0x88) != 0x08) ;` as an unbounded NetBSD poll of +0x18. That loop exits only when bit 3 is SET and bit 7 CLEAR; +0x18's domain is {0 idle, 1 busy} and neither ANDs to 0x08 -- IT WOULD HANG ON CORRECT HARDWARE. Independently, dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:722-737 -- code this round never touched -- documents that same wait as NetBSD's COMMAND-START handshake on the CONTROL window's BUSY register and sets d->busy |= 0x08 in reply. The exhibit was lifted from that comment and re-pointed at a register it says nothing about. The conclusion survives on Linux; the reason does not, and a wrong reason gets reused -- this project already has the fatal()-is-byte-for-byte-debug() case on record. All four corrected IN PLACE. This is the #357/#362/#365 shape: citations from panel output rather than a local source. gdromcondavailgdromcondavail COND_DATA_AVAIL permanently lies after an overread -- the device advertises data while returning 0xffff (split out of gdromcondlies)gdromcondavail COND_DATA_AVAIL permanently lies after an overread -- the device advertises data while returning 0xffff (split out of gdromcondlies) — witness: none -- a state-consistency defect; its oracle is what the device ADVERTISES — note: *** THE ONE PRODUCT DEFECT OF THE NINE. TRUE, with a qualification that narrows my title. *** `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:1073`, anchors `cur_cnt >= d->cnt` and `GDROM_W_OVERREAD`: clearing availability at exhaustion depends on the MUTABLE count, and the overread branch returns all-ones without correcting availability. Guest-reachable through Dreamcast MMIO -- the count can disagree with the buffer extent. **THE QUALIFICATION MY TITLE OVERSTATES:** *"ordinary exhaustion DOES clear availability; the inconsistent state persists until another operation changes it."* So 'permanently lies' is too strong -- it lies until the next operation that touches the state. The defect is real; its permanence is not. **The stimulus already exists and the ORACLE does not:** `regress/gdrom_data_probe.py:374` (anchors `overread`, `overread x1`) drives exactly that disagreement but checks SURVIVAL and DIAGNOSTICS, never the subsequent COND state. *That is the channel-line failure -- a row whose stimulus reaches the defect and whose oracle cannot see it.* Falsifier offered and checked: *would be wrong if exhaustion independently cleared availability, or the count could not diverge during a response. Neither holds.* `#496` fixed the separate bad-value paths, not this. *Evidence: codex evidence pass 2026-09-07, regress/artifacts/queueunrated/codex_bare2_20260907.txt. Source-reading only -- no builds, gates or probes were run, so every mutant outcome below is a static conclusion, not a fresh measurement.* *** REACHABILITY ESTABLISHED FROM SOURCE, 2026-09-07 -- the row previously asserted it and now has the mechanism. *** **The guest writes `d->cnt` DIRECTLY, one byte at a time:** :1194 d->cnt = (d->cnt & 0xff00) | (idata & 0xff); :1202 d->cnt = (d->cnt & 0x00ff) | ((idata & 0xff) << 8); **And availability is cleared only when the COUNT exhausts**, at `:1077 if (d->cur_cnt >= d->cnt)` -> `:1078 if (d->cur_data_offset >= d->data_len)` -> `:1079 d->cond &= ~COND_DATA_AVAIL`. > **So the path is: raise `cnt` after data is armed; `cur_cnt >= d->cnt` never becomes true; `:1079` > never runs; the BUFFER still exhausts, and reads fall to the `:1087` else-arm, which returns > `0xffff` and DOES NOT TOUCH `d->cond`.** The guest then reads status, sees `COND_DATA_AVAIL`, > reads data, gets `0xffff`, and repeats -- with the diagnostic LATCHED after the first occurrence, > so the log says nothing after read one. **Two things this changes about the row.** Its title says availability *"permanently lies"*: it does not -- ordinary exhaustion clears it and another command recovers the state, so the lie is confined to repeated reads after entering the inconsistent state. And the `:1087` arm is **deliberate**, not an oversight: its comment records `#460` joining it to the `:1052` guard on the merits -- *"this and the COND_DATA_AVAIL site above are ONE predicate family, 'read when there is nothing to give'"* -- so a repair there edits a decision a previous round argued explicitly. **THE DESIGN QUESTION IS WHICH SITE OWNS THE BUG**, and it is out to the codex seat rather than settled here: clear availability in the `:1087` over-read arm, or fix `:1077`, whose condition couples a GUEST-WRITABLE count to a DEVICE-OWNED buffer extent -- the guard-field-versus-body-field disagreement in its purest form. *Brief: `regress/artifacts/gdromcondavail/DESIGN_brief.md`.* *** CODEX DESIGN PASS 2026-09-07 (`regress/artifacts/gdromcondavail/codex_design_20260907.txt`). VERDICT: confirmed PIO completion defect -- and the preferred repair BREAKS A SHIPPED ROW, which makes this an ORACLE-CORRECTION round rather than an ordinary one. *** **Q1/Q2 -- MY PROPOSED SITE IS RIGHT BUT ONE READ LATE.** Clearing at `:1087` is justified (that arm means the ENTIRE staged buffer is exhausted, and the `:1081` re-arm is the OPPOSITE branch, where bytes remain -- count SEGMENTATION of an already-populated buffer, not an async refill, so clearing cannot strand the documented 65536-into-32768 split). **But after the last VALID read a status-only poll still sees availability until another DATA read performs the cleanup.** The better repair clears when the final valid halfword consumes the BUFFER, independent of the guest count, and keeps re-arming when the count boundary is reached WITH BYTES REMAINING. *** A COUPLED EFFECT I HAD NOT SEEN, and it would have made a partial fix worse: *** `SYSASIC_TRIGGER_EVENT` at `:1085` sits behind **the same count condition**. Moving only the availability clear leaves the FINAL COMPLETION NOTIFICATION suppressed in the inconsistent-count case -- a guest that stops polling would then wait forever. **Exhaustion and its completion event must move together**, while intermediate phase events are preserved. **S3 NEEDED A DOMAIN, which I gave as bare "raise `cnt`":** raising it is not sufficient by itself -- with no further writes the new count must exceed `cur_cnt + (data_len - cur_data_offset)` to prevent any later count-boundary transition. *The existing TOC stimulus satisfies that*, and guest writes select only 16 bits while the device can internally hold 65536. *** THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE ROUND'S SHAPE: S5 UNDERSTATED THE ORACLE PROBLEM. *** `gdrom_data_probe.py:393`'s **`overread x1` requires exactly one OVERREAD diagnostic**. clear only at :1087 -> that one OVERREAD survives; later reads switch to NODATA clear on the final valid read -> later reads enter NODATA IMMEDIATELY; OVERREAD count is ZERO > **So the PREFERRED repair turns a shipped, green row RED by succeeding.** That is exactly the > oracle-correction rule's territory: **re-pin the row FIRST, measure the COMMITTED build RED under > the new expectations, and only THEN change the code** -- same scripts, opposite colour. Appending > a COND assertion is NOT sufficient; the existing row needs deliberate revision, and the round owes > the provenance and in-place correction that rule demands. **Q3 -- THE ORACLE, concrete.** No existing scoped row observes the transition (`gdrom_toclen_probe.py:282`'s `ok cond` observes availability immediately after ARMING, and its separate session cannot anchor the over-read session). The proposed `exhaust cond` row reads **GDROM_COND**, physical `0x005f709c`, through the existing P2 address `0xa05f709c`, 16-bit load, low byte, **all in ONE session with no intervening COND writes or new packets**: after arming 0xa8 immediately before the final halfword 0xa8 <- excludes premature clearing immediately after that halfword 0xa0 <- DISTINGUISHES THE TWO REPAIRS after the first empty DATA read 0xa0 after further empty DATA reads 0xa0 (This fork's values: command shadow `0xa0` plus the availability bit `0x08`; the COND read arm at `:1206` returns the shadow directly.) The first observation excludes "never set". **Q4 -- THE CLAUSE-(d) MUTANT, named precisely:** condition the completion clear on **`d->cur_cnt == d->cur_data_offset`**. The existing `overread` survival row stays green AND the proposed `exhaust cond` row stays green, because without a re-arm both fields finish at 408. **After a legitimate re-arm `cur_cnt` resets and `cur_data_offset` does not**, so the conditional suppresses clearing at actual exhaustion. *A positive-count TOC row cannot see it; the detector needs a re-armed (segmented) transfer.* **HONEST LIMIT, stated by the seat rather than glossed:** the C source cannot establish real hardware behaviour for count writes DURING an active transfer. Search-indexed excerpts of Sega's SPI specification say the host sets Byte Count before issuing the packet and DRQ clears after the last data byte -- which supports exhaustion-based completion for the documented protocol -- but the full PDF was not retrievable and those excerpts do not settle the intervening writes. *** ORACLE-CORRECTION DESIGN, codex, 2026-09-07. The defect and the shipped-oracle conflict are both confirmed -- and MY PROPOSED RE-PIN WAS VACUOUS. *** I proposed re-pinning `overread x1` to **zero OVERREAD**, reasoning that HEAD gives 1 and the repair gives 0, so the order requirement is satisfied. It is -- **but zero alone ALSO ACCEPTS COMPLETE SILENCE.** A device that announced nothing at all would pass. > **THE RE-PIN IS A PAIR: `(OVERREAD, NODATA) = (0, 1)`.** On HEAD the same stimulus gives `(1, 0)`. > The pair distinguishes HEAD from the repair AND keeps an affirmative announcement obligation. > **N is 1** because NODATA carries its own once-only latch, so repeated excess reads in a fresh > session do not multiply it. **AND MY Q2 WORRY WAS UNFOUNDED, for a reason I had not seen:** the announcement does not disappear, it **changes category**. After the repair, subsequent reads reach the existing diagnostic-bearing NODATA branch; the final VALID read should itself stay quiet. So the device keeps its truthfulness channel and the round is not silencing one. **PROVENANCE for the rewritten row, two verbatim grep-able anchors** (the old pin's authority is what is being overturned, so it cannot also be the warrant): `read when there is nothing to give` -- the `#460` family rationale -- and `DIAGNOSTIC is the truthfulness channel`, the returned-value collision rationale. The old row and its explanatory block are corrected IN PLACE, recording that its OVERREAD expectation depended on the stale availability being repaired. **A LIMIT STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED:** if NODATA already latched earlier in the same device instance, later exhaustion reads will not announce again. **So this re-pin does NOT establish a per-transfer announcement**, and claiming that stronger property would need a mixed-history oracle and its own design decision. **THE `exhaust cond` ROW, concrete:** immediately before the final valid halfword GDROM_COND is `0xa8`; the final halfword returns the synthesised payload **`0x41e6`** (independently anchored by the TOC's last two bytes); immediately afterwards, before any further DATA read, COND is `0xa0`. **HEAD predicts `0xa8 -> 0xa8`; the repair predicts `0xa8 -> 0xa0`.** The before/after pair rejects premature clearing and the immediate after-sample rejects clearing one read late. *It is insufficient alone for the combined repair* -- it cannot establish the completion EVENT or correct re-arming, so an `exhaust event` row is owed too. *** AND AN APPARATUS TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN: `printed()` RETURNS THE FIRST MATCHING PRINT. *** A before/after design that prints the SAME register twice and calls that helper twice retrieves **the same sample both times** -- so `0xa8 -> 0xa8` would be reported on a correct build. The two observations must be made distinguishable (different registers, or a helper that takes an occurrence index). *This is the third apparatus defect this week found by a seat reading the probe helper rather than the probe's rows.* *** THE codex RE-PIN ANSWER WAS UNREAD FOR A DAY. It refutes a premise, corrects the proposed oracle, names an apparatus trap, and finds a STALE RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE. Read and spot-checked 2026-09-07; artifact `regress/artifacts/gdromcondavail/codex_repin_20260907.txt`. *** ### 1. THE RE-PIN MUST BE A **PAIR**, because zero alone accepts silence The proposal was to re-pin `overread x1` to expect ZERO OVERREAD diagnostics. codex: *"Your zero- OVERREAD expectation would indeed make HEAD RED. **But zero alone also accepts complete silence.**"* diagnostic HEAD repair OVERREAD `read past the end of the GDROM_DATA buffer' 1 0 NODATA `read from GDROM_DATA with no data' 0 1 **The announcement CHANGES CATEGORY; it does not disappear** -- after the repair, later reads reach the existing NODATA branch, which carries its own diagnostic. A paired row keeps the affirmative announcement obligation while still separating HEAD from the repair. *`N` is 1 because NODATA has its own once-only latch, so multiple excess reads do not multiply the diagnostic.* **Its stated limitation, which is the honest half:** if NODATA already latched earlier in the same device instance, later exhaustion reads announce nothing -- so this re-pin does **not** establish a per-transfer announcement, and claiming that stronger property would need a mixed-history oracle. ### 2. *** MY Q5 MUTANT IS NOT A SURVIVING MUTANT -- THE PREMISE IS REFUTED. *** I offered `d->cur_cnt == d->cur_data_offset` as an escape. **Taken literally it holds after the FIRST unsegmented halfword -- both are 2** -- so it clears availability immediately and **fails the existing `accept d1` row.** No segmented transfer is needed to catch it; it is not an escape at all. **The two GENUINE candidates both require SEGMENTATION**, which is why an unsegmented probe misses them: substitute cur_cnt for cur_data_offset in the data_len comparison -> both counters reach 408 together; needs exhaustion AFTER a re-arm that reset only cur_cnt delete the re-arm's `cur_cnt = 0' -> that assignment never executes unsegmented; needs intermediate observations after a re-arm *"A segmented transfer checked only at its endpoint still misses that distinction"* -- use an UNEQUAL split and observe the advertised remainder, continued availability, payload and event timing between boundaries, keeping the TOC's required 408-byte count at dispatch or the length guard rejects it. ### 3. TWO NEW ROWS SPECIFIED, AND THE EVENT ONE HAS A STICKY-BIT TRAP * **`exhaust cond`** -- GDROM_COND immediately before the final valid halfword is `0xa8`; the final halfword still returns `0x41e6`; immediately after, before any further DATA read, HEAD predicts `0xa8` and the repair predicts `0xa0`. The before/after pair rejects premature clearing AND clearing one read late. * **`exhaust event`** -- SYSASIC pending word 1 bit 0 at `0xa05f6904`. *** THE QUALIFICATION IS THE WHOLE ROW: command dispatch ALREADY raises this event and the pending bit is STICKY, so reading `set` after exhaustion without acknowledging the earlier one proves nothing. *** The row needs dispatch-event -> write-one-to-clear ack -> verified clear -> clear before the final halfword -> set immediately after. *It observes PENDING STATUS, not CPU interrupt delivery, and coalesced events make it a non-exact counter.* ### 4. AN APPARATUS TRAP IN THE PROBE'S OWN HELPER **`printed()` returns the FIRST matching print** (`regress/gdrom_data_probe.py:167`). So a before/after pair that prints the SAME register twice and calls the helper twice retrieves **the same sample both times** -- a row that cannot fail, in the harness this round is extending. The two observations must be textually distinguishable. ### 5. *** A STALE RECORD IN PRODUCT CODE -- VERIFIED HERE, AND IT IS AN L4 OWED FIX. *** `src/devices/dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:1032-1040` states: DE-ESCALATION: this round removes FOUR host-fatal predicates and the detector carries accept rows for THREE. *** THIS ONE IS EXEMPT, AND THE EXEMPTION IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A GAP. *** ... The other three ... DO carry rows. **`regress/gdrom_data_probe.py:420` ships `row("accept w8", ...)` for that very width predicate**, and the probe's own header at `:326` says so: *"`accept w8` carries the width predicate."* The exemption was overtaken by the row and the paragraph was never corrected. > **It understates coverage, which is the safe direction for correctness and the DANGEROUS direction > for records** -- it reads as a carefully reasoned carve-out, so a future round trusts it, believes > the width predicate is unrowed, and either duplicates the row or re-argues a settled exemption. **NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately:** it is a product-code comment, so the edit owes propagation to three build trees plus the two-part clearance, and a nine-seat panel was running. A half-propagated tree during a panel is precisely the drift the no-VPATH rule exists to prevent. Owed as an L4 correction in the next round that touches this file. ### 6. AND OVERREAD DOES NOT BECOME UNREACHABLE The accepted ROM-control arm (`:1282`) *"can assert availability without providing a buffer"*, so clearing on the final valid read does not cover that path. **Re-pinning this stimulus therefore does not license deleting the OVERREAD fallback or claiming every false-availability state repaired** -- its separate diagnostic coverage remains an obligation.open

The evidence supports that targeted investment; it does not support introducing a hidden execution framework across this tree."* ### 1. *** THE ROW'S CENTRAL PREMISE WAS TOO SIMPLE: A ROW CAN REQUIRE MANY SESSIONS. *** This row (and `probeslow`) framed the gap as *"no probe can score ONE row"*, with the fix being a label on `session()`. **That is insufficient in both directions:** * `gdrom_default_probe.py`'s **`accept8` row combines EIGHT emulator runs** -- verified: it scores `len(SAYS.findall(t))` across an accumulated transcript; * and conversely several assertions routinely SHARE one transcript. **So the scheduler needs the ROW -> PRODUCER relationship, not a per-session tag.** *The specification recorded on `probeslow` -- four guards plus a name threaded through call sites -- is therefore incomplete rather than merely unimplemented.* ### 2. THREE SHORTCUTS REJECTED, each with its failure mode by session ORDINAL / caller location insertions change ordinal meaning; dummy results still enter ordinary computations; an eight-session aggregate can PASS after one real session lazy transcript/status PROXIES conditions, parsing and argument expressions run BEFORE row() gets control, so the session is forced anyway SOURCE inspection / transform loops, accumulated transcripts, generated labels and reused variables need dependency analysis -- "another execution model reviewers must understand" **The one conditional alternative it distinguishes:** RE-SCORE RETAINED RAW TRANSCRIPTS when the new assertion needs no new debugger commands. *"Transparent caching by binary pathname would be particularly wrong for a mutation table"* -- which is exactly the use this row was motivated by. ### 3. *** A LATENT TRAP IN THE EXISTING GATE, verified. *** `regress/gate_arm.sh:1156` runs the probe with **`|| true`**, discarding its exit status, and `:1160` then does **`grep -q "OPUS497T_DONE"` -- a SUBSTRING search.** > **So a filtered run emitting `OPUS497T_DONE_FILTERED` would satisfy the gate's completion check.** > Any future selector must use a token that does NOT contain the legacy one. *Nothing emits such a > token today, so this is a trap loaded for the feature rather than a live defect -- but it would > have been loaded by the very change this row asks for.* ### 4. THE CONTRACT ANY FUTURE SELECTOR OWES (stronger than the four guards on `probeslow`) * **validate against a DECLARED INVENTORY before execution** -- reject an empty selection and every unknown name, including an unknown mixed with valid ones; auto-included controls must not rescue a zero-match request; * **print the filtered INTENT before working** -- requested names, expanded execution set, planned row count, full inventory count, planned sessions; * **check completion against that PLAN** -- require the expected row identities exactly once, *"not merely `passed == len(rows)`, otherwise a selected run can itself lose rows and shrink to a convincing denominator"*; * **separate result and completion records**, preserving unset output byte-identically. **And controls are an independent obligation:** `GDROM_DEF_CONTROL`'s historical `all([])` defect is already repaired by its `rows and` guard, but *"nonempty still does not mean complete -- one surviving control could certify a selection that omitted two required controls."* ### 5. THE PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN THE TREE `regress/m88k_idle_probe.py:178` is a table-driven `ROWS = [(name, spin, argv, grace, expected)...]` selector -- **selection is simple exactly where the execution boundary already exists**, which is this row's own cheap-when-designed-in / expensive-to-retrofit finding, now with an in-tree exemplar. *** WHAT REMAINS FOR THE ADJUDICATOR, and it is unchanged: FOLD this row into `probeslow`, or keep both with this one carrying the capability framing? A comment adds no product code, so the addition licence is not even triggered. Tag it `/* #NNN: */` per house ethos. Must land byte-identical in `est/`. *Premises the adjudicator discharged: the two-commit thirdparty figure CONFIRMED -- and sharper than I had it, since `8dd86b5` touched four thirdparty headers but NOT this one, so **this fork has never edited it**; the `[3]` arrays CONFIRMED; and 'a device-file comment cannot govern a header #define' is TRUE of the comment and HALF-TRUE of the guard, which is exactly why the row folds halfway.* *** THE THREE ASIC ROWS REST ON ONE INVARIANT, AND TWO OF THEM MAY BE ONE FIX. Scoped 2026-08-26 by reading, no run. *** **THE SHARED INVARIANT: `r == 3` is unreachable by any implemented case.** VERIFIED by reading the switch labels -- they are three CONSECUTIVE words at group bases `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, so `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` yields 0, 1, 2 and never 3. All three rows are that one invariant, differing only in **which edit would break it**: asiceventaddr a #define in the vendored HEADER (event >= 96 -> offset 0x0c) asicindexcase an indexing `case` added at an r==3 offset in the DEVICE FILE asicoffsetkill an adversarial MUTANT at an r==3 offset no detector row touches **THE THIRD IS DIFFERENT IN KIND and should not be folded with the other two:** it is a DETECTOR-COVERAGE question, not a product invariant. `kill far` (+0xfc) was added to defeat a GROUP-NARROWING mutant and cannot defeat a SINGLE-OFFSET one; the seat that raised it said plainly it did not build it. *** THE FINDING THAT MAY FOLD THE OTHER TWO, and it contradicts `asiceventaddr`'s own stated reason for being a separate row: *** that row argues a device-file comment "cannot govern a `#define` added to a header". **True of a COMMENT. Not true of a GUARD.** An event `>= 96` does not stay in the header -- it becomes an ADDRESS the driver accesses, arriving at the device as `relative_addr == 0x0c` and decoding to `r == 3`. **So a guard on `r` in the device file would catch the header entry point too**, because the header case MANIFESTS as a device-file access. If that holds, one guard covers both rows and the vendored-header edit -- the expensive part, on a file this fork has touched once -- may be unnecessary. **Stated as a question rather than a conclusion because I have not built it**, and the adjudicator was asked the licence question on the header assumption; this finding is being sent to it as a correction rather than acted on unilaterally. STOP CONDITION: if the guard-covers-both reading holds, fold `asiceventaddr` into `asicindexcase` as one fix with two entry points and close it as a duplicate; if it does not, the rows stay separate and the header licence question stands. *** SCOPED 2026-08-26 WITHOUT A RUN -- the row is read-only by construction, and the scoping found a CONSTRAINT that changes the fix's cost. *** **THE FIX SITE IS A VENDORED THIRDPARTY HEADER.** The macro is at `src/include/thirdparty/dreamcast_sysasicvar.h`, which carries BOTH a GXemul `$Id$` and an upstream **`$NetBSD: sysasicvar.h,v 1.5`** line. **MEASURED: `git log --all -- 'src/include/thirdparty/*'` returns TWO commits -- the 0.7.0 import, and the single ~119-correction hardening commit.** So this fork has edited thirdparty exactly ONCE. *The precedent is not absent, and it cuts both ways: the header's own banner says it was "Extended with useful macros and also some more event definitions described in KOS comments", so GXemul UPSTREAM already extends this vendored file. Editing it is precedented -- it is just rare, and rarity is the cost.* **WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA:** the row's whole reason for existing separately is that *the edit which reaches this defect adds a `#define` to a header, with no device-file change at all* -- so a structural-invariant comment in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` cannot govern it. **The only place a guard can sit is the same rarely-touched header**, which means the fix's licence question is sharper than for an in-file addition. **THE CANDIDATE FIX, stated so it can be adjudicated rather than argued:** a compile-time assertion beside the macro, so that adding an event `>= 96` fails the BUILD rather than silently routing to relative `0x0c` and indexing three-element arrays at 3. It is self-verifying by construction -- a negative control is one test `#define` -- and it costs nothing at runtime. **BUT IT IS AN ADDITION TO PRODUCT CODE, so the ADDITION LICENCE governs: a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT, never 'it cannot hurt'.** The delta cannot be measured without a build, and the machine is reserved (owner directive 2026-08-26: hold off on anything needing an idle machine). **`asicbadaddr` is the natural warrant donor** -- same device, same `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` decode, same three-element arrays -- and whether that transfers to a THIRDPARTY header edit is exactly the judgement an adjudicator owes rather than me. *** WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT AND NEEDED NO RUN: the arithmetic. *** `(e)>>5 == 3` for every `e >= 96`; the highest defined event is 67; therefore latent today, and reachable by a one-line header addition by anyone adding a high event number. Two seats confirmed both numbers from source on 2026-08-24 and I re-derived the macro form here. NEXT ACTION: adjudicate the licence and the thirdparty-edit question. NOT shipped unilaterally -- a rarely-touched vendored header is precisely where 'it cannot hurt' does the most damage. RAISED BY THE opus5 SEAT on the asicbadaddr pass-1 panel (panel_20260824_231824), ADJUDICATED 2026-08-24. `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e)` is `SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)`, so ANY event number >= 96 gives `(e)>>5 == 3` and a relative offset of 0x0c -- which `dev_dreamcast_asic.c`'s `r = (relative_addr / 4) & 3` maps to index 3 of three-element arrays. **LATENT AND PROVABLY SO: the highest defined event is 67 (MATOUTOFMEM), and both the 67 and the 96 threshold were confirmed from source by two seats.** *** WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW RATHER THAN PART OF asicbadaddr: THE EDIT THAT REACHES IT ADDS A #define TO A HEADER, WITH NO CHANGE TO THE DEVICE FILE AT ALL -- so the structural-invariant comment asicbadaddr plans to leave in `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` CANNOT GOVERN IT. *** Post-fix the failure mode also changes rather than disappearing: an event >= 96 would write to 0x0c, fall to `default:`, and the pending bit would be SILENTLY LOST where pre-fix it was `exit(1)`. Neither is correct; neither is reachable today. *** DISPOSITION: NO RUNTIME GUARD *** -- a guard that cannot fire is the insurance-that-isn't this tree already rejects. The carrier is a one-line comment at the event-define block IN THE HEADER. **FILED RATHER THAN SHIPPED THIS ROUND, and the reason is the file class:** the header lives under `src/include/thirdparty/`, which this fork HAS edited (the 8dd86b5 hardening commit) but where NO file carries the `/* #NNN: */ ` correction tag the ethos otherwise requires -- so the convention for editing it is unsettled, and settling it is not this round's job. *** THE MANDATORY HALF IS THE RECORD, NOT THE COMMENT: `asicbadaddr` must SCOPE its invariant claim to `dev_dreamcast_asic.c` and name this header path as a separate latent item, rather than claiming the invariant is fully protected. *** *** CORRECTED 2026-08-25 BY THE #463 RECORDS AUDIT (`_scratchpad/panel_20260825_024101_audit`, grok seat), and the correction makes this row STRONGER. *** Every earlier statement of this row said the macro reaches `0x0c` for "any event >= 96". **That is false**: `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e) = SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5)` (`dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:74`) sends `e` in `[128,159]` to `+0x10`, which is r = 0 and perfectly legal. The true predicate is `(e>>5) & 3 == 3` -- `[96,127]` -> `+0x0c`, `[224,255]` -> `+0x1c`, `[352,383]` -> `+0x2c`, `[480,511]` -> `+0x3c`. So the violator is not a single range above a threshold but a REPEATING FAMILY that lands on the fourth word of every 16-byte group -- the same structural shape as `asicbadaddr` itself, one level up in the header. Verified by enumerating `4*(e>>5)` over `e>>5` in `[0,15]`. The LATENCY argument is unchanged and still holds: max over all 21 `SYSASIC_EVENT_*` defines is 67 (`:72`), and `67>>5 == 2` lands at `+0x08`. *** CLOSURE PROPOSED, NOT MADE. Verified by me against the source; held for the 2026-09-09 adjudication because a row closed on one seat's reading plus my own agreement is exactly the self-review the conflict-of-interest badge exists to disclose. *** **codex (rating pass, 2026-09-07): `low -- the named domain hazard is ALREADY GUARDED`.** *"the header now embeds `((e) >= 0 && (e) < 96) ? 1 : -1` in `SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK(e)`, which `SYSASIC_EVENT_TO_ADDR(e)` invokes."* **VERIFIED BY READING:** `dreamcast_sysasicvar.h:135` defines `SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK` and `:140` is `(SYSASIC_BASE + 4*((e)>>5) + SYSASIC_EVENT_RANGE_OK(e))` -- the guard is inside the macro, so an out-of-domain event cannot produce an address at all. Added by `#467`/`#468` (`29b450c`), whose title says *"the ASIC domain is now ENFORCED"*. **The row's own witness text is now STALE**: it reads *"LATENT, and provably so: the highest defined event is 67 < 96"*, which was the pre-fix warrant for it being latent. The current warrant is stronger and different -- the macro rejects the domain structurally -- and that is what the closure should record.open

Three rows test only `!= "died"` before calling `int(_, 16)`: `gdrom_default_probe.py:878` (`_p`), `:962` (`_a`), `:1184` (`_q`). A wedged session in any of those three makes `printed()` return `absent`, and the probe dies with a traceback and **NO `GDROM_DEF_RESULT` LINE AT ALL**. *** THE FIX IS NOT AN INVENTION: TWO OTHER ROWS IN THE SAME FILE ALREADY USE THE CORRECT GUARD. *** `devsig` (:324) and `data 0xffff` (:554) both write `if g.startswith("0x")`, which is a THREE-state-safe prefix test. So the repair is to apply the pattern the file already contains, three times -- not to design one. *That two rows got it right and three got it wrong in one file is the more useful observation than the crash itself: the correct form was available and not reached for.* **FILED, NOT FIXED IN-ROUND**, and the stopping rule is why: this is neither a measured false pass nor a wrong record. It fails in the SAFE direction -- a traceback yields no verdict line, so the gate's `rows run` check reads 0 against a wanted 58 and FAILS LOUDLY rather than passing something wrong. It is a robustness gap, ranked below live defects. **It is also cheap and natural to fix alongside `probetimebased`'s three-state predicate**, which is the round that makes `absent` a first-class state rather than an accident.open

asicpermuteasicpermute `(relative_addr / 4) % 3` permutes the ASIC register index bijectively and NO round-trip row can see itasicpermute `(relative_addr / 4) % 3` permutes the ASIC register index bijectively and NO round-trip row can see it — witness: none -- LATENT; needs a free-running assertion probe, which no SH probe here has — note: OUTSIDE the #463 detector's contract, and the contract says so rather than claiming completeness. `% 3` maps each group bijectively -- {4,5,6} -> {1,2,0} -- so every write and its readback round-trip through the SAME permuted cell and AGREE. Batching does not help: batching catches ALIASING (two offsets colliding on one cell) and a permutation collides nothing. Yet the tick's `pending_irq[i] & mask_13[i]` then pairs the wrong words, so the OBSERVABLE is interrupt assertion, which no row here reaches. **A single-stepping probe cannot observe interrupt DELIVERY** (`cpu_dyntrans.c:204-206`), so closing this needs the free-running shape. `% 3` is the most plausible naive 'repair' anyone writes at this site -- it is what you reach for when worried about an index out of range -- so this is the highest-probability future edit in the file.open

It is an ADDITION, not a reversal -- 'keep the deletion; add the line'. (b) THE CORRECTED FORM, and it matters because the obvious form is WRONG: a bare `if (r == 3) return;` SKIPS the function's common tail (`if (writeflag == MEM_READ) memory_writemax64(cpu, data, len, odata); return 1;`), handing a guest read an untouched buffer. **FOUR readers independently proposed that broken line -- deepseek, minimax, kimi AND THE ADJUDICATOR ITSELF** -- from packets that showed the guard and the switch but not the tail. The correct form declines while leaving `odata` at 0 and reaching the common tail. (c) IN-TREE PRECEDENT nobody had cited: `memory_rw.c:495-523`, in the file that DISPATCHES to this device, bounds a guest-drivable diagnostic to 8 emissions (`n_trunc_msgs`) because 'probing at the end of a device's mapped range is common and benign'. The fork's own answer to this phenomenon is BOUND THE COUNT, KEEP THE MESSAGE -- so a latched variant has precedent the round never weighed. (d) THE ANCHOR PROPERTY, verified arithmetically: an explicit decline pins the DECLINE COLUMN at `(addr & 0x0c) == 0x0c`, so a translation MOVES it onto a probed offset -- `+1` reddens `safe 8`, `+2` reddens `safe 4` (the residual that escapes even `mask9 rt`), `-1` reddens `asic ok`. The whole translation class would close with one line and rows already shipped. (e) PRECONDITION for shipping it: a 13-mutant x 13-row table re-measured byte-identical with the line in, and `mask9 rt` KEPT -- it is the only anchor surviving if the line is later deleted, and the two catch the class through different channels. *** AND A CORRECTION TO THE ADJUDICATION THAT ORDERED THIS ENRICHMENT. *** It counted five layers protecting this hazard, one being 'four measured kill rows asserting survive-plus-DECLINE-VALUE at r==3 offsets', concluding a future `case 0x0c:` assigning visible data would redden the detector. **MEASURED FALSE BY READING THE PROBE**: `kill word`, `kill byte`, `kill store` and `kill far` all compare `'survived' if alive else 'died'` against `'survived'` -- SURVIVE-ONLY, no value check. Such a case would keep them GREEN. That layer does not exist; the other four (verified enumeration, the in-code comment, this filed item, the contract's disclosure) stand. The adjudicator wrote 'the dissent read the diff, it did not read the detector' in the same answer -- it had descriptions rather than the source, and the opus5 seat, which DID read it, had already reported the rows as survive-only. **This is `asickillsurvive`, and it has now caused a wrong claim by an adjudicator, which is a sharper argument for fixing it than the original filing made.** *** #463b FULLY SPECIFIED 2026-08-25 BY ADJUDICATION. Ships decline+latch, not a bare decline. *** THE FORM: `if (r == 3)` declines with a ONE-SHOT LATCHED `fatal()` and an explicit `memory_writemax64` so the read path writes the defined 0 -- early-return, which makes a future `+0x0c`-class label DEAD CODE BY CONSTRUCTION and CLOSES THIS ROW. Per-instance struct field, not a `static`, because the device is multi-instance. WHY LATCHED RATHER THAN BARE: the loss is MEASURED, not aesthetic -- #463's finding 5 established the deleted `fatal()` printed unconditionally while the surviving `debug()` is silenced by `-q` and by free-running at verbose 0. **Code that does not make the trade beats prose confessing it.** And the latch rebuilds exactly the property the de-escalation clause mourned: under a future `+1`-style decode defect every legal `+0x?8` access lands in the decline column, and the first 8 announce -- field-time announcement complementing the gate-time detector, with no host kill and no flood. THE ROW BUDGET, and it is bounded ON PRINCIPLE rather than by restraint: (1) **UPGRADE the four r==3 rows' oracle** to assert the returned value is the defined 0. They are survive-only today; they already READ, so this only adds the assertion. This discharges an adjudicator condition open since the FIRST adjudication ('confirm the kill rows check the decline VALUE, not survival alone'), never discharged, and now load-bearing because the candidates differ exactly in decline-column semantics. (2) **ONE BOUND ROW**: the fix now ADDS a predicate (`n < 8`), so clause (d) / accept-failability owes a row that reddens when the bound is REMOVED -- count <= 8 occurrences across the probe's 64 r==3 accesses. **Pin the COUNT, not the message text.** (3) One contract sentence. EXPECTED EQUIVALENCE, recorded in advance so it is not mistaken for an escape: the decline-nulled mutant (`if (r == 3)` kept, fall-through restored) will likely measure EQUIVALENT at base, because `default:` declines identically -- the #449 pattern, an equivalence RESULT and not a failure. MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: base is an INVARIANCE CONTROL, never a discriminator -- all candidates are guest-identical at base and a detector should pin CONTRACT, not implementation. The evidence is entirely in the mutant deltas, and the translation mutants must go STRICTLY REDDER (`+1` -> safe 8, `+2` -> safe 4, `-1` -> asic ok; arithmetic verified). **Base must be RE-RUN on the latched build, not inherited** -- 8 new `fatal()` lines enter the pty logs, and `gate_hygiene` GRADES pty logs, which is a known trap class here: a new diagnostic entering graded logs must be shown green, not assumed. CLOSE-OUT: full 13-mutant table on the latched build, pass 2 on the real diff, targeted gate, one commit, and then #463 and #463b are OVER -- the next dissent on this device buys a new round or a filed row, never a reopening. *** FINAL FORM 2026-08-25: A SILENT FALL-THROUGH DECLINE. THE LATCH IS DEAD. *** `if (r == 3) { /* comment */ } else switch (...)` -- a guarded arm joining the EXISTING epilogue, NOT an early return. That form uses the tail's own `memory_writemax64` so nothing is duplicated, and it does not lean on the dispatcher pre-zeroing read buffers (`memory_rw.c:485`) -- codex's objection answered STRUCTURALLY rather than by trusting a non-local guarantee. *** WHY THE LATCH DIED, on two independent closures either of which is fatal. *** (1) THE PREDICATE IS EMPTY WHERE IT MATTERS: implemented registers occupy words 0-2 of all four groups (documentarily grounded -- Linux mach-dreamcast and KallistiOS both show three words per group, no fourth), so every r==3 lane in modelled space sits directly above an implemented word-2 register and IS the second lane of a legal 8-byte access. 'Latch only on offsets that are not a lane of a legal multi-word access' selects the EMPTY SET -- a dead guard, and this round has refused three of those already. (2) THE INFORMATION IS ABSENT, NOT MERELY AWKWARD: the decoder issues two independent 32-bit accesses, so at the handler **the second half of a legal fmov.d and a direct probe of a reserved word are BYTE-IDENTICAL CALLS.** No predicate written inside this function separates them at any complexity. A dispatcher-layer latch, where transaction context exists, is a different change to a different file -- out of scope. *** AND IT REWRITES THIS ROUND'S FINDING 5: the deleted `fatal()` did not merely print unconditionally, it printed ON LEGAL TRAFFIC -- the second half of every 8-byte access to an implemented register. The 'self-announcing property' the latch was meant to restore was PARTLY A FALSE-ALARM PROPERTY ALL ALONG, so the trade the deletion made was SMALLER than finding 5 claimed and smaller than the latch ruling claimed on top of it. *** THE COMMENT MUST CARRY THE INOCULATION, one line: *silent by design -- r==3 lanes occur inside legitimate split accesses (fmov.d, SQ), so any diagnostic here false-alarms.* That sentence is what stops the next reader re-deriving the latch. WARRANT, THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS: the measured anchor (`+1`->safe 8, `+2`->safe 4 closing the one mutant that escaped everything, `-1`->asic ok); enforcement by control flow instead of enumeration; and the UB upgrade -- a broken invariant buys UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR a compiler may exploit, not a defined overlap, which makes the decline the only C-meaningful statement of the bound in executable form. DETECTOR DELTA: **the bound-count row DIES WITH THE LATCH** -- it was the latch's own accept-failability obligation, and no predicate means no row. The r==3 value upgrade stays.open

A mutant that made an r==3 read return garbage WITHOUT crashing would keep them green. **A disagreement worth recording rather than silently resolving:** the seat called this a witness-ladder violation. The ladder's clause (ii) says *the witness* must carry a liveness control AND a device-signature control, and it does -- `live` and `asic ok` are separate rows doing exactly that. So this is coverage debt, not a ladder breach, and it is filed on that reading. Cheap to close: the rows already issue `print r2`, so the value is captured and unused -- the oracle can become 'survived 0x0' at the cost of re-measuring the table. *** PROMOTED 2026-08-25: this is not a bare residual, it is WHY A FULL RESEARCH PANEL COULD NOT BE REPLACED BY RE-RUNNING THE GATE. *** The opus5 research seat established the consequence: all four rows touching r==3 offsets (`kill word` +0x0c, `kill byte` +0x0d, `kill store`, `kill far` +0xfc) are SURVIVE-ONLY, and every value-checking row touches only r in {0,1,2}. **Therefore the 13-row detector cannot distinguish the shipped fix from a bare decline, from a decline-plus-latch, or from a latched diagnostic -- all four leave it 13/13.** So 'the detector is green' was NO EVIDENCE AT ALL for the disposition the research stage was asked to review. The detector pins the kill's absence and register distinctness; it pins nothing whatever about reserved-space semantics.open

asicarray4asicarray4 sizing the ASIC's four register arrays [4] instead of [3] would de-fang the whole out-of-bounds classasicarray4 sizing the ASIC's four register arrays [4] instead of [3] would de-fang the whole out-of-bounds class — witness: none -- design proposal, not a defect — note: RAISED BY THE kimi SEAT on the #463 pass-2 panel (_scratchpad/panel_20260825_020219), via `kimi-k3:cloud` because the kimi CLI is quota-walled -- a DIFFERENT TRANSPORT, recorded as a substitute. The struct declares `pending_irq[3]`, `mask_13[3]`, `mask_11[3]`, `mask_9[3]` consecutively, so `mask_13[4]` IS `mask_11[1]` and any mask widening corrupts a neighbour silently. Padding each to [4] converts that class from CORRUPTION back to mere silent wrongness at a cost of 16 bytes. **The seat was explicit that this is a TRADE, not a fix**, and that framing is the reason to keep it: it does not make a wrong index right, it only stops it reaching another array. Weigh against `asicindexcase`, which it would also partly de-fang. *** MEASURED AND PARTLY REFUTED 2026-08-25 by the opus5 research seat, which had first FAVOURED this option and then argued against it. *** Sizing the arrays [4] makes the `+1` translation mutant **ESCAPE** `mask9 rt`. The row's kill mechanism is that DEVICE_TICK ERASES `asserted_13` (`d->asserted_13 = ... = 0`, loop bound i<3) and the mask_9 write arm calls the tick immediately -- so at [3] the stored 0xb2 lands on asserted_13, is wiped, and the readback reddens the row. **At [4], index 3 is a real slot the tick never touches, the value survives, and the mutant escapes**: N=3 readback 0x0 (RED, killed) vs N=4 readback 0xb2 (GREEN, ESCAPES). So this option **costs a mutant kill and needs a replacement row before it can ship** -- the original filing ("de-fangs the whole OOB class for 16 bytes") understated its cost and is corrected here. Filing it rather than shipping it was right for a reason the filing did not know. *** DEAD BY THREE INDEPENDENT ROUTES, which is the strongest refutation this round produced for any alternative. *** (i) agy's phantom-state argument -- it invents hardware that does not exist and leaves the tick loop ignoring the fourth word; (ii) opus5's MEASUREMENT -- it makes the `+1` mutant ESCAPE `mask9 rt`, because that row's kill works by the tick erasing the cell and [4] gives index 3 a real slot the tick never touches; (iii) codex's HARDWARE ORACLE -- Linux's mach-dreamcast IRQ code documents three status words and three per mask group, and KallistiOS exposes exactly +0/+4/+8 with no fourth. **The three-word bound is a HARDWARE FACT, not an implementation choice.** Three seats, three methods, one conclusion -- and note this round holds NO Holly ASIC documentation of its own, so route (iii) is the first external oracle it ever obtained.open

gdrompiooddlengdrompiooddlen the GDROM PIO read guards ONE byte and then reads TWO -- LATENT, because no path can produce an odd length todaygdrompiooddlen the GDROM PIO read guards ONE byte and then reads TWO -- LATENT, because no path can produce an odd length today — witness: none, and none is possible today -- the OWED reachability measurement was done BY READING and came back NEGATIVE. The code asymmetry is real; the route to it is not. See the correction below. — note: *** FOUND 2026-08-25 WHILE VERIFYING A PREMISE IN THE `gdrompionull` PASS-1 BRIEF, NOT WHILE LOOKING FOR IT. *** The brief's Q4 asked, almost as an afterthought, whether `d->cur_data_offset` is reset anywhere -- because the round had reasoned about `data_len` throughout and barely looked at the guard's OTHER operand. It is reset (`:327`, beside the NULL). But reading the guard to check that showed something else. *** THE GUARD CHECKS ONE BYTE AND THE BODY READS TWO. *** Verified by reading, three lines: (1) `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:611` -- `if (d->cur_data_offset < d->data_len) {` (2) `:612-613` -- `odata = d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++];` then `odata |= (d->data[d->cur_data_offset ++] << 8);` -- **two increments, one bounds test** (3) `alloc_data` `:309` -- `malloc(d->data_len)`, **exactly `data_len` bytes, no padding, no rounding**. So at `cur_data_offset == data_len - 1` the guard PASSES, the first read is the last valid byte, and **the second read is `d->data[data_len]` -- one byte past the allocation**. *** REACHABILITY, STATED AS WHAT IS READ AND WHAT IS OWED. *** READ: `data_len = d->cnt` (`:307`), and `d->cnt` is GUEST-WRITABLE A BYTE AT A TIME -- `:704` sets the low byte from a CNTLO store and `:712` the high byte from CNTHI, so an ODD count is expressible. The two subsequent adjustments do not remove oddness: `:409-410` only replaces `cnt` when it is ZERO, and `:486-487` only rewrites the single value 65536. **OWED: a measurement that an odd `cnt` actually survives to `alloc_data` on a path a guest can drive.** The existing `gdrom_pio_null_probe.py` already stages commands through these registers and could answer it with two extra stores; I have NOT run it, and this row does not claim the defect is reachable until that runs. *** WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM `gdrompionull` AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. *** That row is `data` NULL while `data_len` lies -- a state-invariant violation whose fix is one assignment in the tail. This is an OFF-BY-ONE in a bounds test, on a path where `data` is a perfectly valid pointer and `data_len` is honest. Different fix design (`< data_len` becomes `+ 1 < data_len`, or the read becomes width-aware), different oracle (a heap over-read, not a SIGSEGV), so under the reopening rule they are separate rounds. **Note the two interact in the safe direction: `gdrompionull`'s fix sets `data_len = 0`, under which this guard is false and the over-read cannot occur on THAT path.** It does nothing for the odd-count path. *** AND UNLIKE THIS DEVICE'S OTHER OUT-OF-BOUNDS ISSUES, ASan SHOULD SEE THIS ONE. *** The file's own comment at `:272` records that ASan cannot detect its member-to-member overrun because that is intra-object inside one malloc. **This is a read PAST a malloc'd buffer's end**, which is the case ASan is built for -- so `build-asan/` is a real second oracle here, where for the aliasing family it was not. That is worth testing early because it is cheap and because a positive ASan result would settle reachability and severity in one run. SEVERITY, stated honestly and NOT inflated: a ONE-BYTE heap over-READ. It does not write, and the byte it returns goes to the guest as the high half of a 16-bit read. That is an information leak of one adjacent heap byte per odd-length transfer and a potential crash only if the allocation ends exactly on a page boundary. It is materially less severe than the SIGSEGV in `gdrompionull` and should rank below it. *** REACHABILITY SETTLED 2026-08-25, THE SAME DAY THIS ROW WAS FILED, AND IT SETTLED AGAINST THE ROW. *** The filing said the odd-count route was OWED and explicitly did NOT claim the defect was reachable. That was the right caution, and the answer is NO. *** `data_len` HAS EXACTLY ONE WRITER, AND BOTH ROUTES TO IT FORCE AN EVEN VALUE. *** Verified by grepping every assignment: `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c:307` in `alloc_data` (`d->data_len = d->cnt;`) is the only one -- the apparent second hit at `:413` is a printf FORMAT STRING, not an assignment, which is the kind of match that would have made this look open if counted rather than read. `alloc_data` has exactly two call sites and each is guarded: * `:342`, the Read-TOC path, is preceded by `:338-341` -- `if (d->cnt != 408) { fatal(...); exit(1); }`. **408 is even**, and nothing else reaches this call. * `:418`, the read-sectors path, is preceded by `:412-415` -- `if (sector_count * 2048 != d->cnt) { fatal(...); break; }`. **Any multiple of 2048 is even.** Note `:409-410` only substitutes a count when `cnt == 0`, so a guest-set odd count survives THAT line -- and is then rejected by the equality check two lines later. **So the guest CAN express an odd `cnt` at the CNTLO/CNTHI registers (:704, :712), and that half of the filing was right; what it cannot do is get that value past either guard into `alloc_data`.** *** DISPOSITION: LATENT, NOT LIVE. SEVERITY DROPS FROM A ONE-BYTE HEAP OVER-READ TO A STRUCTURAL HAZARD WITH NO ROUTE. *** The asymmetry itself is untouched and still worth recording: `:611` guards `cur_data_offset < data_len` and `:612-613` reads TWO bytes, while `alloc_data` mallocs exactly `data_len` with no padding. **Any future edit that admits an odd length -- a new command arm, a relaxed guard, a different transfer size -- makes this live immediately, and the code carries nothing that would stop it.** That is a real thing to know and a cheap thing to fix (`+ 1 < data_len`, or make the read width-aware), but it is NOT a defect a guest can reach today and this row may not be ranked as one. *** AND THE ASan NOTE IN THE FILING IS NOW MOOT AND IS WITHDRAWN. *** It said `build-asan/` would be a real second oracle here, unlike the intra-object aliasing family. True in principle and irrelevant in fact: ASan cannot observe an access no execution reaches. *Process note worth keeping: this row was filed with reachability marked OWED rather than asserted, and the owed check refuted it within the hour -- at the cost of two greps. Had it been filed as a live heap over-read it would have been a WRONG RECORD ranked above real work, and the correction would have arrived later and cost more.*open

But it is a LARGER change than the row implied, and shipping half of it is worse than shipping none. *** THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL LANDING SPOT FOR #465's HEADLINE LESSON, AND THE ROUND MISSED IT. *** #465 found that its detector was wired into NO GATE, recorded 'a detector no gate runs is not a detector', and discharged it by a HUMAN GREP. **The mechanical check for exactly that class already exists and was BLIND BY SCOPE** -- `gdrompionull` lived at `regress/artifacts/gdrompionull/`, one level down, where the checker cannot look. **So the round wrote its lesson as prose while the structure that should have carried it sat one directory away, silently not covering the case.** That is the carrier's structure-first rule failing in its own terms, and it is a CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL for a whole subtree -- the class this project named twice today (`panel.sh`'s phantom re-fire, `grok models` as a tier check). **EXPOSURE IS ZERO TODAY, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED IN-ROUND:** 1 of 57 tracked `regress/**.py` sat below top level, and it is now gated by hand. The defect is latent, not live. THE FIX, as the seat scoped it: re-key `MANIFEST`/`EXEMPT` from BASENAME to RELATIVE PATH and replace `os.listdir` with `os.walk`. **It owes negative controls in both directions** -- prove a subdirectory detector with no gate is now RED, and prove a gated one stays GREEN -- and the file already carries an 18-mutant `--selftest` harness to hang them on. A basename->path re-key can silently collide (two files with the same basename in different directories), so that needs its own row. *A checker whose docstring overclaims its scope is worse than one that admits a limit: the docstring is what a future round reads when deciding whether the class is already covered.*in work

The adjudicator hit this too: its own first census scored that dir cited for the same reason. **RESOLVED BY STRIPPING THE `panel_` PREFIX in the backlog list below**, so the names stay human-readable and greppable-by-timestamp while NOT matching the citation pattern. *The adjudicator asked for the names in full; written in full they re-create the circularity, so this takes the instruction's intent -- make them findable -- by a form that cannot false-cite.* THE BACKLOG (prefix stripped deliberately; prepend `panel_` to open them): 20260824_030624 5 substantial answers 20260824_034510 5 20260824_041606 7 20260824_124655 6 20260825_032831_diffrec codex 1.07 MB, minimax 61 KB 20260825_044509_ledger11 codex 1.29 MB, deepseek 281 KB, seven seats 20260825_100232_tailfacts MARGINAL -- two sub-2 KB answers; may close by annotation 20260825_110328_0798b90_pass2 *** pass 2 on a SHIPPED commit *** **THE CUTOFF IS RE-WARRANTED, because the reason I filed was an unchecked absence claim** -- the class this project mandates checking rather than asserting. I wrote 'older dirs belong to closed rounds whose findings WERE acted on' and checked none of them. The adjudicator checked THREE across two eras and found every finding ABSORBED: `20260822_184955`'s headline mutant is the shipped accept-row kill with its delivery rows in the gate; `20260823_140419`'s '(once per offset)' edit is in `dev_dreamcast_gdrom.c` verbatim at four sites; `20260813_183758`'s open question lives as the held `dfreq` row. **n=3, zero live misses** -- which supports refusing the 96-sweep on evidence instead of on convenience. So the cutoff is not 'three days'. It is **2026-08-24, the citation rule's own adoption date, forward-only** -- the same dated-cutoff idiom as `HOLDQ_CUTOFF` and `check_bugfile_sync`'s `CUTOFF`. Older dirs stay under the read-side rule: re-derive before leaning, file anything found decayed. **Note the uncited population is NOT confined to the pre-ledger age** (08-22 has 12 of 17 uncited, 08-23 six of 12), so the cutoff is a policy line, not a natural one. **PRE-SPECIFIED, so the sample size is honest: a sample of three is not a proof. If zero, close it and record the sample.** *** (5) AND THE ROW'S OWN FRAMING WAS OVERSTATED, REFUTED BY MY OWN COMMIT BODY. *** It said every unread-review instance that day was 'a finding sitting in a seat answer nobody had opened'. Commit `087a786` says of the largest instance, verbatim: *'not a review nobody read, but a review I read thoroughly and left unrecorded'*. **Today's instances are predominantly RECORDING gaps, not unopened findings.** The 'twice cost a full round to rediscover' clause is true of the HISTORICAL instances -- the kimi member-2 answer, `m8invpred` -- not of today's. That is the dropped-qualifier class: evidence for one case restated as a property of the day. *** AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS VERY FIX WAS DEFEATED BY ITS OWN EXPLANATION. *** I stripped the `panel_` prefix from the backlog list, then wrote the full name in the sentence EXPLAINING the circularity -- so the dir was still scored cited. That is the correction-quotes-what-it-refutes hazard, documented in the carrier this same morning as the reason a naive stale-text grep *gets steadily more wrong as the file gets more honest*. **Here it defeated a fix inside the paragraph describing the fix.** The rule that follows is narrow and mechanical: **when a record must NAME an artifact it is asserting is UNRECORDED, the name must not be written in the form the checker matches -- anywhere in the record, including the prose about it.** **SEVERITY SET MED, 2026-09-07, by the MAIN LOOP** (not a flagship adjudication -- opus5/fable5 are reserved for the 09-09 adjudication, and a rating is exactly the kind of judgment call that seat exists for; overturn it freely).
