Nobody else on that panel saw it -- not codex, not the packet-fed seats, not me -- and I had read the file several times that evening. The design is presumably the same member 3 (decline + latched announce), but the observable differs: this arm fills a BUFFER rather than a single caller variable, so what a declined fill should leave is its own question and the detector shape is not simply copied. *** MAIN-LOOP RECORD 2026-09-07 (assess stage) -- written into state_note, NOT into `entries'. *** `entries' is the SEAT ANSWER list: check_stage_panels.py counts entries to decide whether a stage's nine seats were fired, and gen_dashboard.py REFUSES TO RENDER on a seat id no column declares. A main-loop note parked there is not merely mis-filed -- it MANUFACTURES A SEAT ANSWER THAT NEVER HAPPENED, which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape inverted. Seven such entries were written during this session and all seven were migrated here when the generator refused. SEVERITY RAISED MED -> HIGH, on a fact DERIVED rather than assumed. The row said the fix was *presumably* the same as [[sgirandompixel]]'s and that the observable differed. **The reachability is now established and it is the SAME documented-mode structure, not merely the same shape.** Measured at HEAD, three commands: * the PUT colour switch implements exactly FOUR cases -- `DE_MODE_TYPE_' CI, RGB, RGBA, ABGR -- and its `default:' is `buf[0..3] = random()'; * `crmfbreg.h' documents **FIVE** colour types; the fifth is `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB 0x000000f0'; * `grep -c YCRCB src/devices/dev_sgi_re.c' = **0**. It is handled nowhere. And it is reached by an ordinary register write: `color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK', mask `0xf0', so a guest selecting YCRCB lands on the random arm directly. *** SO THIS IS `#504's OWN SENTENCE AT A SECOND SITE: four of five DOCUMENTED modes work and the fifth returns random data. *** `#504` was graded HIGH on exactly that warrant, and this arm is arguably worse in one respect -- `sgirandompixel' put a random value in `*color' for the CALLER to store, whereas this writes four random bytes into the tile through `memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE)' with no intermediary. **WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the severity should be read with it: NO WITNESS.** Nothing here shows a guest driver selecting YCRCB -- only that the model accepts it and answers with random data. The rung-3 attempt looks cheap for the same reason `#504's did (`regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py' already programs this code path; the colour type is a different field of the same mode word), and it is OWED before this ships. **The GET side does NOT share the defect** -- its `default:' reads the raw 32-bit value rather than inventing one, so this is a PUT-only arm. That asymmetry is itself worth carrying into the design: the two default arms of one function already disagree about what an unhandled colour type means. Note this is a DIFFERENT defect from [[sgirebufuninit]] at the same lines: that one is about bytes NOBODY assigns; this is about bytes assigned from `random()'. A fix for either leaves the other standing. *** READY TO RUN AS THE NEXT ROUND. Three things established 2026-09-07 while `#505` worked in the same function, none of which this row had. *** **1. IT IS A DIFFERENT SWITCH FROM THE ONE `#504` FIXED, and the row should say so plainly** -- I nearly recorded this as the `#499` symmetric-cell shape and it is not. `#504` de-fanged the **addressing-mode** default (`default: fatal("unimplemented dst_mode %i ..."); *color = random();`). This row is the **colour-mode** default of a different `switch` in the same function: default:buf[0] = random(); buf[1] = random(); buf[2] = random(); buf[3] = random(); // TODO. fatal("[ put: color mode = 0x%x ]\n", color_mode); } cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, tileptr + ofs, buf, bufdepth, MEM_WRITE, NO_EXCEPTIONS|PHYSICAL); **There is no `break` and no decline: control falls straight into the write**, so four bytes of host `random()` land in guest memory at a guest-chosen tile offset. Same family as `#504`, same function, different arm -- *related by idiom, not by the one-cell-repair pattern.* **2. FULLY GUEST-REACHABLE, established by reading rather than assumed.** `color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK`, and `mode` is the caller's `src_mode`/`dst_mode`, read straight out of `de_reg[]` from `CRIME_DE_MODE_SRC`/`CRIME_DE_MODE_DST` with **no filtering anywhere on the path**. The four implemented types are 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30; `DE_MODE_TYPE_YCRCB` is **0xf0 and is documented in `crmfbreg.h`** but unimplemented, so a guest selecting a real, named mode reaches this arm. **3. A WITNESS IS ONE CONSTANT AWAY.** `#505` built `regress/sgi_re_rgb_probe.py`, a rung-3 probe that drives an XFER copy on an unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32` with both ladder controls and a sibling accept row, and whose `setup()` now takes **both** src and dst modes. Pointing its `dst_mode` at `LIN_A | BUFDEPTH_32 | 0xf0` puts YCRCB into the PUT switch and reaches this arm. *** THE ORACLE IS THE HARD PART AND IT NEEDS SAYING BEFORE THE ROUND STARTS: THE DEFECT'S OUTPUT IS RANDOM, SO NO VALUE ROW CAN PIN IT. *** `#504` hit exactly this and its answer is the precedent -- assert that the destination still holds its PRE-PAINT value, i.e. that the write was DECLINED, rather than trying to assert anything about what was written. A determinism oracle is refuted in advance by this project's own record: two seats showed on `#504` that stack reuse can make a wrong value deterministic, so *"the same value twice"* proves nothing. **FIX SHAPE: the option set has a member already chosen for its sibling.** `#504` used DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE with its own bit (`SGIRE_W_BADMODE = 1 << 10`), for the reason `#498` measured -- the four handlers share one struct, so a shared latch is silenced by the other site's ordinary traffic. **This arm needs its OWN bit, `1 << 11`**, and `#504`'s comment already says the enum ends there on purpose so the next maintainer finds it. *That is a transferred in-tree warrant, not a "cannot hurt" addition.* *** PASS-1 AUDIT, 2026-09-07 (codex, `regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_pass1_20260907.txt`). TWO OF MY PREMISES WERE WRONG AND THE DISPOSITION SURVIVED. *** **VERDICT:** *"DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE is justified, with an unconditional return from the PUT default. But the brief misstates #504's oracle and the write's byte count; depth 8 also exposes uninitialized buffer bytes."* *** CORRECTION 1 -- THE ORACLE. THIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE COST A ROUND. *** My brief said `#504`'s precedent asserts *the destination still holds its PRE-PAINT value*. It does not. The seat opened the probe: `lin_b is fg` expects **`FG_VAL = 0x77665544`**, not the pre-paint `0x11111111`, because a declined source GET **preserves the caller's foreground value**, which the following PUT then writes. In the seat's words, *"the probe explicitly rejects preserving the destination as a different disposition."* **So `#504` warrants the latch-and-return IDIOM and does NOT supply the unchanged-destination ORACLE I attributed to it.** Those are different transfers and I ran them together. **THE ORACLE THE SEAT PROPOSES INSTEAD, and it is stronger than either:** observe **ZERO `MEM_WRITE` CALLS** from an unsupported PUT, *alongside* unchanged destination bytes -- because that pair **distinguishes "no write" from "same final value"**, which neither assertion does alone. It also notes that if removing the RNG use is contractual, that must be observed SEPARATELY. *And a sentinel value will not rescue a value oracle here:* each assignment converts a SEPARATE `random()` result to `uint8_t`, so the whole-word improbability argument `#504`'s old witness used does not establish an impossible byte pattern. *** CORRECTION 2 -- THE BYTE COUNT, and it is the SAME WIDTH-AXIS LESSON `#505` PAID FOR HOURS EARLIER. *** My brief said *four* bytes of `random()` are written. The write is `bufdepth` bytes, not four: at bufdepth 8 the arm fills `buf[0..3]` with RNG and ships **four further UNINITIALISED stack bytes** with them; at bufdepth 1 or 2 fewer than four RNG bytes land. **"Four" is true only at bufdepth 4** -- the width every example happens to use. *That is the exact shape of `#505`'s clause-(d) floor breach, arriving in the next round's brief the same day, written by the person who had just repaired it.* Overlaps [[sgirebufuninit]]; the round must say which defect owns which bytes. **OPTION SET: CONFIRMED COMPLETE, and the grep found three in-tree alternatives worth naming:** * the helper's own GET default already provides a raw ABGR-shaped fallback (`dev_sgi_re.c:358`); * **PCC2 has a real ACCEPT precedent** (`dev_pcc2.c:427`) -- a read served from backing storage before the default diagnostic; * **SGI's ROP diagnostics latch BY VALUE** (`dev_sgi_re.c:850`) rather than one bit per site. None establishes correct YCRCB PUT semantics. *"Mirroring the GET fallback would repeat the unsupported-authority problem you warned about. The YCRCB name establishes an encoding; it does not establish packing, conversion, or depth semantics."* IMPLEMENT is defensible in principle but no permitted source supplies an implementation or a demonstrated driver selection. **No additional warranted disposition outside the option set** -- which is the option-set rule returning a clean negative for once, and that is worth recording as such. **THE LATCH BIT IS CONFIRMED AVAILABLE AND THE OBJECTION TO ONE BIT IS RECORDED:** occupied bits enumerate as 0..10, `warned` is `uint32_t`, so **`1 << 11` is free**. The strongest objection is diagnostic coverage -- *an earlier unnamed mode suppresses a later YCRCB announcement* -- and per-mode latching has in-tree precedent (the ROP site above). One bit stays consistent with this helper's existing policy, so it is a judgement the round must make explicitly rather than inherit. **FIX SHAPE (Q2), in the seat's words:** *a terminal default arm containing a conditional announcement followed by an **unconditional function return***. Note this is the SKETCH RULE's territory -- the PUT branch's write sits after the switch and is shared by all five arms, so the return must be checked against the whole enclosing function before it is written. *** AND A WARNING THAT SAVES THE ROUND A FALSE START: `#504`'s PROBE CANNOT BE REUSED UNCHANGED. *** *"#504's `lin_b is fg` remains green under edits confined to this colour default. Both of that probe's mode constants use RGBA, so it never selects the PUT colour default. Its setup cannot be transferred unchanged."* `#505`'s probe is the better base -- its `setup()` already takes both src and dst modes -- but the same check applies to it and must be run, not assumed. **ENUMERATION CONFIRMED, with a qualification I did not have:** the twelve default selections are eleven unnamed (`0x40`..`0xe0`) plus the named `0xf0` YCRCB, and they reach the arm *"when the preceding coordinate/addressing/tile-validity checks pass"*. *** THE ORACLE QUESTION, ANSWERED BEFORE THE ROUND STARTED -- AND THE NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN. codex, `regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_oracle_20260907.txt`. *** **VERDICT:** *"Your distinction is conditionally sound. A correctly scoped write-attempt observer works for Round A; **the existing stepped probe supplies none.** This fork's debugger watchpoints offer a qualified alternative."* **MY DISTINCTION SURVIVES, with a precision I had not stated.** A count separates *no request* from *a request carrying the existing bytes* -- but *"zero calls does not establish correct rejection unless the unsupported arm was ACTUALLY REACHED: an earlier return or an operation that never ran also produces zero."* That is the attribution problem, and it means the round owes a reach control beside the count. *** THE MECHANISM EXISTS: debugger WRITE WATCHPOINTS, checked in the common memory path BEFORE device/cache/RAM dispatch, and neither PHYSICAL nor NO_EXCEPTIONS excludes this helper's write. A pty driver can observe them with NO instrumented build. *** (`memory_rw.c:273`.) *** AND IT HAS TWO DECISIVE LIMITS, THE FIRST OF WHICH WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE GREEN: *** 1. **The check requires `!single_step`, and the existing probe's `run_ops()` uses `step`.** So *"merely adding watchpoints and counting their messages to that execution scheme could report ZERO DESPITE WRITES."* The row would have reported "no write happened" while writes happened. **A watchpoint oracle therefore requires the FREE-RUNNING probe shape, not the stepped one.** 2. It also requires `!about_to_enter_single_step` and **SETS that flag after its first report**, so later pixel writes inside the same drawing command go unreported. What Python would count is *printed watchpoint reports*, not `MEM_WRITE` calls -- watchpoints carry no hit count. **SO THE ACHIEVABLE CLAIM IS BOUNDED, and the round must say so rather than overclaim:** the mechanism supports an **any-attempt-to-this-range** witness when observation is active throughout the relevant execution. It does NOT support *"exactly N calls"* or *"no writes anywhere from this helper"*. The conclusion must read **"no observed write attempt to this range under these validated conditions"** -- watching the destination cannot exclude a write to an UNINTENDED address, which is exactly the failure mode [[sgirebufuninit]] and the `#505` tiled row both hit in other forms. **THE SHIPPABLE DESIGN, in the seat's own construction:** verified arm reach and completed execution, an active observer that DOES detect a supported write to the same range (the liveness half), then no matching write report for the rejected operation, with unchanged verified destination bytes as corroboration and the announce count testing "announce once" separately. **That is four rows, not one**, and knowing it now is worth more than discovering it after the fix. *This is the carrier's `!single_step` family arriving through a NEW mechanism. The WATCHPOINT case is the same guard on a different feature and was not written down.* *** CODEX DESIGN PASS 2026-09-07 (`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_design_20260907.txt`). VERDICT: REVISE -- DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE **with a `return` before the PUT transfer**. It did not: **it repaired the ADDRESSING-MODE default at `:235`, which sits BEFORE GET and PUT diverge and returns for both directions. The COLOUR GET default at `:358` still performs a raw conversion.** Two different arms -- so the sibling is a precedent for the DISPOSITION and not for the site, and its comment cannot simply be copied. **S5 WAS WRONG, AND THIS ONE UNBLOCKS THE ROUND.** I claimed the decline's 'what does `buf` hold' question was the SAME question as [[sgirebufuninit]]'s, making that row a prerequisite. codex: *"A declined PUT need not leave anything defined in `buf`, provided nothing consumes it. The helper itself owns the memory write. Its callers receive no buffer to transfer afterward."* remove the fill, fall through -> transfers indeterminate stack bytes REJECT zero the span, fall through -> overwrites destination with zero needs a warrant RETURN from the PUT default -> preserves destination bytes PREFERRED > **So the two rows are INDEPENDENT and there is no patch ordering.** This round decides whether an > unsupported PUT writes anything at all; `sgirebufuninit` decides how paths that DO transfer avoid > consuming uninitialised bytes. *Initialising the buffer would neither remove the four `random()` > calls nor justify writing zeros for an unsupported format.* **S1 needs a width qualification:** four bytes are ASSIGNED randomly, but the transfer length is 1, 2, 4 or 8. A narrow transfer exposes only the prefix; an eight-byte transfer additionally consumes four uninitialised bytes. **S2's inference was a CORRELATE and the real population is twelve, not one.** `grep -c YCRCB` = 0 proves only that one NAMED constant is absent. Enumerating `mode & 0xf0`: sixteen values, **four explicit PUT cases (CI/RGB/RGBA/ABGR) and TWELVE reaching `default:`** -- eleven unnamed plus YCRCB. The DE register handler stores the mode without filtering the type nibble, and both line and rectangle callers pass it through unchanged. *The named-constant search was the same error that cost the `asicbadaddr` census a 4x undercount.* **FAULT IS AVAILABLE HERE and my brief implied otherwise** -- `memory_rw.c:603` delivers MIPS exceptions. codex rejects it anyway on better grounds than availability: the helper returns `void`, its transfers request `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, and the outer device handler returns success, so FAULT would need an error-propagation design and a warrant for the guest-visible exception. **THE LATCH MUST BE AN INDEPENDENT BIT, NOT `SGIRE_W_BADMODE`** -- sharing it would let an ADDRESSING failure suppress the COLOUR diagnostic. That is `#490`'s measured latch-collision class, predicted here before the code exists. **Q4, the predicted escape:** condition the new `return` on `bufdepth == 4` -- the canonical clause-(d) shape, conditioning the repair on a field the transfer consumes. **codex expects `rgb tiled64` to stay green under it**, because that row varies the GET SOURCE's addressing and width while keeping a linear four-byte RGBA destination: *"its name does not establish PUT coverage."* The proposed closure is the destination axes together -- twelve unsupported types x four widths x four address modes = **192 combinations** -- with whole-span checks including eight-byte spans. *Source-based prediction; no mutant built.* **Q3, the witness:** source inspection supports a rung-3 cold-debugger probe on stock IP32 and codex found no machine-description blocker. But **the sibling probe's green rows are NOT a witness for this row**: its setup fixes the DESTINATION to RGBA, so varying its source-mode argument never exercises the colour PUT default. Record **'source-reachable; rung-3 attempt pending'** -- codex ran nothing, as instructed, so the attempted-probe prerequisite is NOT yet discharged. *** A CONSEQUENCE OF THE DECLINE DESIGN, found by the codex seat on the SIBLING brief (`sgimtedepth4dead`) and cross-filed here because it is this row's design that it bears on. *** *"A helper return before accessing the buffer leaves the caller's colour unchanged. MTE still performs the dependent PUT, and its `bg` persists across iterations -- so a declined GET can reuse an earlier source value."* **That is distinct from buffer initialisation and it bites the agreed repair.** The design settled for this row is DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE with a `return` before the transfer -- and on the MTE path the caller's `bg` is a loop-scope variable, so a declined pixel does not leave the destination untouched: **it writes the PREVIOUS pixel's colour.** A decline that silently smears the last good value across a run of unsupported pixels is a different wrong answer from `random()`, and arguably a more plausible-looking one. *The round owes an answer: does the decline return before the PUT as well, and if so what does the destination hold? This was not visible from this row's own brief, which framed the question around `buf` rather than around the caller's colour variable.* *** DESIGN PASS 2, 2026-09-07: I CONFLATED A DECLINED GET WITH A DECLINED PUT. PASS 1's DESIGN STANDS UNCHANGED. *** The PUT-default `return` exits **before** `memory_rw(... MEM_WRITE ...)`, so whatever the caller's `color` holds, that declined PUT does not transfer it. Leaving the destination's existing bytes intact is the honest disposition for an unsupported write. **The `bg` observation is about the dependent-PUT problem, which is a different row.** **AND MY S4 DID NOT ESTABLISH REACHABILITY:** MTE builds modes from addressing and depth bits only, leaving the colour type at CI, and its one colour override sits behind the unreachable `depth == 4`. **Neither construction reaches this PUT colour default**, so the MTE `bg` behaviour does not bear on this row at all. *Two further qualifications on my wording: MTE reloads `bg` from `CRIME_MTE_BG` on **each transfer invocation**, so a declined GET retains the latest value from THAT invocation or the register's initial value -- never a previous command's local `bg`. And "the whole rectangle deterministically receives the last good colour" is too strong independently, because CI's accepted PUT initialises only `buf[0]` and wider depths consume uninitialised bytes.* **THE LATCH GRANULARITY IS CONFIRMED AS APPROPRIATE AND ITS LIMIT STATED:** one message per device instance for the latch's lifetime -- so a thousand declined pixels produce one line, **and none if an earlier command already set the bit** (the struct is zeroed at init; there is no per-command reset). It deliberately cannot distinguish one declined pixel from a rectangle; reporting extent would need counting or a command summary. **RESIDUAL FOUND: bounding the PUT warning does not bound every warning from the operation.** The **GET colour default still logs without a latch**, and DE can perform that GET for a destination-dependent raster operation before ever reaching the declined PUT. So a round that latches only the PUT arm leaves a guest-drivable unlatched diagnostic in the same code path. **THE CLAUSE-(d) MUTANT:** change the new `return;` to `break;`, keeping the latch and the announcement. Execution resumes at the memory write and consumes the uninitialised buffer -- **it breaks the no-write contract without restoring `random()`**. `rgb samemode` and `rgb tiled64` both expected to stay green (supported RGB/RGBA, never reaching the default). *The coverage gap is wider than MTE: the scoped scripts never select an unsupported destination colour type at all, so their green results cannot establish this decline.* *** THE WITNESS PROBLEM IS CHARACTERISED, AND IT IS HARDER THAN THE ROW ASSUMED. From the codex ORACLE answer (`regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_oracle_20260907.txt`), read in full 2026-09-07 -- most of this had been sitting unread. *** **TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS FIRST, and the second changes the FIX, not just the witness:** 1. *"The buffer lacks a declaration initializer; it is not NEVER INITIALIZED. PUT arms assign prefixes, and GET fills the requested transfer length."* The row's shorthand was sloppy. 2. *** "THE MISSING `break` IS NOT WHAT PERMITS THE WRITE. The write is AFTER the switch, so adding `break` would still reach it. **The proposed return matters.**" *** A `break`-shaped repair would look right and do nothing -- exactly the sketch-versus-enclosing-control-flow rule this project minted after four readers proposed a `return` into a function with a common tail. *** THE OBSERVER EXISTS, AND IT IS DISQUALIFIED BY THE PROBE'S OWN EXECUTION MODE. *** The fork has debugger WRITE-WATCHPOINTS, and the common memory path checks them **before** device/cache/RAM dispatch -- *"neither `PHYSICAL` nor `NO_EXCEPTIONS` excludes this helper's write"* (`memory_rw.c:273`). A matching attempt prints `WATCHPOINT: write`, which a pty driver can count with no instrumented build. **But two conditions kill it as written:** memory_rw.c:273 the check requires !single_step -- and sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py's run_ops() uses `step'. Adding watchpoints to that scheme "could report ZERO DESPITE WRITES." same check also requires !about_to_enter_single_step, and SETS that flag after its first report -- so subsequent pixel writes inside the SAME drawing command go unreported. > **This is the carrier's single-stepping rule arriving on a new mechanism.** It already records > that a stepped probe cannot observe interrupt DELIVERY (`cpu_dyntrans.c`: *"Do not cause > interrupts while single-stepping"*). **Watchpoints are a second capability gated the same way**, > and the same discriminator applies: ask what the observation depends on before designing around > it. **WHAT THE MECHANISM CAN AND CANNOT SUPPORT, in codex's words:** it supports an **any-attempt-to-this-range** witness *"when observation is active throughout the relevant execution"* -- i.e. FREE-RUNNING, not stepped -- and even then only the first report survives the flag. It *"cannot automatically support 'exactly N calls', or 'no writes anywhere from this helper'. A literal, attributed call count needs a suitable host-side observer or `harness:` witness."* *** AND Q3 DEMOLISHES THE CHEAP ORACLE: "unchanged destination bytes prove only unchanged OBSERVED CONTENTS." *** Equality at the observation points is also consistent with a same-value write, a write followed by restoration, a write to somewhere else, no drawing operation at all, or an earlier helper return. **Two of those are live here rather than theoretical**: the helper returns on an invalid tile pointer (`dev_sgi_re.c:274`), and *"the memory path can discard an out-of-RAM write while returning success; corresponding reads can return zeros"* (`memory_rw.c:662`). > **So a destination-equality row needs a control establishing that the pre-paint REALLY EXISTS and > that a SUPPORTED operation through the same path actually lands** -- otherwise "unchanged" is > indistinguishable from "nothing ever happened", which is the vacuity shape in its purest form. **THE TWO VIABLE PATHS, neither cheap:** * **(a) a FREE-RUNNING probe with a write-watchpoint** -- any-attempt semantics, first report only, and it must abandon the stepped `run_ops()` idiom the sibling probes use; * **(b) a `harness:` witness with a host-side observer** -- an attributed call count, which the ladder admits only when the round's subject IS the apparatus, so it would need care not to become the rung-1 shortcut the ladder exists to refuse. **STATUS: this row is NOT held for fable5 and is the only HIGH row that is not** -- but its blocker is now a characterised capability gap rather than an open question, and neither path is a session's work. *Recorded in full because most of this analysis had been sitting unread in the artifact since it was produced, which is this session's most-repeated failure.* *** DESIGN PASS 1, 2026-09-08. FIVE SEATS, UNANIMOUS ON BOTH QUESTIONS -- and the strongest answer REFUSED TO CERTIFY ITSELF, which is the part worth keeping. *** **THE DISPOSITION: member 3, DECLINE + LATCHED ANNOUNCE, implemented as candidate (b) -- skip the PUT's `memory_rw` for a declined mode. Never an early `return`.** *** grok's REFRAMING IS BETTER THAN MY OPTION LIST AND IT DISSOLVES THE QUESTION THE ROW WAS FILED ON. *** The row asked *"what should a declined BUFFER FILL leave behind?"*, treating `buf` as the analogue of `#504`'s `*color`. It is not: > *"Destination of a PUT is guest memory at `tileptr + ofs`, not `buf`. `#504` declined the > helper's OUTPUT. The PUT output is the store. Skipping the store leaves whatever the guest > already had -- deterministic, no invented colour, no host bytes. `buf` can stay uninitialised > because it is not sent."* So the fix is not a fill policy at all. **The question "what should the buffer contain" was the wrong question**, and my option (a) (zero-fill) was demoted to a fallback for exactly one case: if some tail consumes `buf` or assumes the store happened. **AND IT CORRECTED MY (a) IN PASSING:** zero-filling only `buf[0..3]` to mirror the `random()` shape is NOT (a) -- `bufdepth` can be 8, so that form *"is this arm already instantiating `sgirebufuninit`"*. If (a) is ever taken it must define the whole payload. *** IT DECLINED TO CERTIFY (b), NAMING EXACTLY THE GAP: *** *"That tail is not in the packet. I will not guess `x++`, a dirty bit, a return value, or a use of `buf`. I cannot certify (b) against 'nine lines down.'"* That is this project's own sketch rule, applied by a seat to its own recommendation, unprompted beyond the caution in the brief. ## *** BOTH OF ITS UNCHECKABLE PREMISES ARE NOW SETTLED BY ME, BY OPENING THE FILE *** **1. THERE IS NO COMMON TAIL.** `horrible_getputpixel()` is `void`, and after the PUT store the `else` runs the GET path and the function ENDS -- `}` closing the else, `}` closing the function, nothing between them. No dirty bit, no counter, no return value, no later use of `buf`. **So (b) is safe**, and the `put_ok` flag form grok gave is belt-and-braces rather than necessary -- which is still the right way to write it, because it cannot become the early-`return` trap under a later edit. **2. `fatal()` DOES NOT EXIT.** `src/core/debugmsg.c`: `va_start; va_debug; va_end;` and return -- no `exit()`, no early-out. grok flagged that if `fatal()` aborted, *"the random fill is dead and the guest-visible row collapses."* It does not abort, so **the random bytes really do reach `memory_rw(..., MEM_WRITE)` and the defect stands.** *That premise should have been IN the packet. The carrier records `fatal()`'s non-exit as a standing fact and I did not inline it -- the settled-premises rule exists precisely so a packet-fed seat need not park on something already known.* ## ROUND SCOPE: TWO ROUNDS, 5 of 5, each with its own reason Not one round with `sgirebufuninit`, despite the two sitting in the same `switch`. **minimax gave the sharpest form:** *"a regression in the CI/depth-8 path and a regression in the YCRCB path produce the same test failure"* -- i.e. one oracle cannot tell them apart, which is exactly the round-scope rule's test rather than a preference. grok: *"They sit in the same `switch`. That is not the test."* **And it named the trap explicitly: zero-initialising `buf` at its declaration would silently convert this round's (b) into (a) and smuggle `sgirebufuninit`'s fix in with it.** *This was asked as an open question arguing both ways, so the unanimity is worth something -- unlike unanimity on a brief-supplied FACT, which this project has measured to be worth nothing.* ## RESIDUALS RAISED, NOT YET DISPOSED * grok: the arm *"is already confused -- it announces unimplemented (`TODO` + `fatal`) and then IMPLEMENTS with noise. The announce is the right instinct (unlatched, per-pixel, therefore wrong shape). The fill is the defect."* So the existing `fatal()` becomes the latched announce; it is not added, it is fixed. * **12 of 16 mode values reach `default:` and only `0xf0` is documented.** grok accepted the arithmetic (`16 - 4`, needing no header) but declined the reachability claim as *"claims about other code, not in the packet"* -- correctly. **A round taking this owes the reachability check**, and `IMPLEMENT` (member 7) for YCRCB is a separate design: *"no YCbCr packing, subsample, or byte order in this packet; 11 of the 12 values are not even named."* * Q4/Q5 (detector and witness) are in the seat answers and NOT yet consolidated here -- that is an UNREAD-REVIEW debt on this row until it is. *** THE Q4/Q5 UNREAD-REVIEW DEBT IS DISCHARGED, AND IT WAS WORTH PAYING: THE PANEL'S OWN MAJORITY DETECTOR WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AN ESCAPABLE ROW. *** I recorded the detector and witness answers as unread. Reading all five: ## THE DETECTOR -- convergent, and it is a DESTINATION CANARY, not "looks non-random" Pre-fill the target bytes with a distinctive non-zero canary, execute ONE PUT with a declined mode, read back, and **pass iff the canary is bit-identical** -- i.e. the oracle is *the store did not happen*, not *the value is not random*. A liveness control in the SAME script repeats with a defined mode (RGBA or CI) and the canary MUST change; without it a dead PUT path greens the round. *** THE HOLE, and three of the five seats were in it: DO NOT PIN THE TEST TO `0xf0` ALONE. *** deepseek and kimi both proposed YCRCB `0xf0` as *the* test mode, kimi arguing it is the value a real guest would plausibly select. grok: > *"A mutant `case 0xf0: put_ok = 0; break;` with `default:` still random would escape. Use at > least one UNDOCUMENTED value (`0x40` is the first hole) as the primary; `0xf0` can be a second > vector, not the only one."* **That is a real escape against the majority design.** The documented mode is the most tempting choice and the weakest one, because a mutant can special-case exactly it. **FOUR MORE STRENGTHENINGS, one per seat, none of them duplicated:** * **grok** -- vary `bufdepth` over at least {1, 4, 8}, so a mutant that skips the store only when `bufdepth == 4` dies. * **minimax** -- make the oracle **CONJUNCTIVE**: the latch transitioned 0 -> 1 *during that pixel* (record the PRE-state) AND `memory_rw` was not called for it. Either conjunct alone is escapable, and recording the pre-state defeats a mutant that pre-sets the latch at init. * **kimi** -- assert the announce count is **exactly 1**, which is what actually pins the latch. * **glm** -- assert the ADJACENT bytes are unchanged too, since the write is only `bufdepth` bytes at `ofs`; and run twice asserting identical transcripts. **AND grok'S HONEST LIMIT ON ITS OWN ORACLE:** keeping `buf[i] = random()` while setting `put_ok = 0` leaves the canary intact, so a destination-only oracle cannot see the leftover `random()` calls. It calls that *"a successful (b), not an escape, PROVIDED the patch also deletes the four `random()` calls -- same edit, not a second oracle"*, and explicitly declines to make "`random()` is not called" the oracle because an LCG or `rand()` defeats it. ## *** THE BLOCKING PREMISE THREE SEATS RAISED INDEPENDENTLY IS NOW SETTLED -- BY ME, IN TWO READS, ## AND IT SETTLES IN FAVOUR OF THE ROUND. *** glm, kimi and deepseek each named the SAME single fact as the one that decides whether a witness exists at all: **does the mode-register write path mask or reject `0xf0` (and the eleven undocumented values) BEFORE they reach this helper?** glm put the consequence sharply: if it does, *"no witness exists, the round is documented-only, and '12 of 16' then describes host-reachable states no real guest can reach."* **THERE IS NO VALIDATION.** `DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_de)`: :1098 /* Treat all registers as read/write, by default. ... */ :1112 d->de_reg[regnr] = idata; <- unconditional, unmasked and the `switch (relative_addr)` below it reaches `case CRIME_DE_MODE_DST:` only to `debug()` the value and `break` -- no mask, no rejection, no range test. `draw_primitive()` then reads `d->de_reg[(CRIME_DE_MODE_DST - 0x2000)/4]` straight back, and `horrible_getputpixel()` computes `color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK`. > **So a guest store of ANY 32-bit value to CRIME_DE_MODE_DST is kept verbatim, and bits 4-7 select > among all 16 colour modes -- twelve of which reach the `random()` arm. The witness is > constructible and the round is NOT documented-only.** *The file's own comment is the authority here, which is the strongest form: it is not that I failed to find a validator, it is that the code states it treats these registers as raw read/write.* **THE REMAINING UNSETTLED ITEM is smaller than it looked:** kimi asked whether `#504`'s witness itself selected a declined mode. That is a question about a shipped probe, answerable by reading `regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py`, and it is no longer load-bearing now that the register path is settled.open

(2) Depth 8 IS reachable and CI is NOT restricted to depth 1: the DE writer preserves bits 9:8 and the helper evaluates `1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3)` without rejecting the fourth encoding. The header names only three depth encodings and that naming imposes no runtime restriction. *** AND IT CLOSED THE ONE QUESTION I COULD NOT SETTLE BY READING: THE CALLEE DOES COPY THE REQUESTED LENGTH. *** memory_rw.c's RAM write is literally `memcpy(memblock + offset, data, len)`; a block-boundary crossing SPLITS the transfer and forwards the remainder rather than truncating; and the device-boundary clamping plus NO_EXCEPTIONS affect MMIO dispatch, not sanitisation of a RAM-write SOURCE buffer. **The nearby zero-fill operations apply to READS.** So there is no padding step that would render the uninitialised bytes harmless. FLOOD CONFIRMED WITH ITS SCOPE: the colour-default diagnostic has no latch and no verbosity guard and execution continues into the write, so the DE line and rectangle loops can produce a per-pixel output flood -- but **MTE's current CI/RGBA construction does not reach the colour default**, so the flood is a DE-path property, not an MTE one. The existing SGIRE_W_BADMODE latch guards the ADDRESSING diagnostic only. *Its 'additional issue' -- the GET half consuming more bytes than it reads -- is ALREADY FILED as [[sgirebufuninit]], which names that exact path. Recorded as independent confirmation, not as new.* — evidence: regress/artifacts/sgirandomcolour/codex_scope_20260907.txt······

sgirebufuninitdev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel(): uint8_t buf[8] is never initialised and the guest picks how many of its bytes are used -- uninitialised host stack reaches guest-visible memory on PUT and *color on GETdev_sgi_re.c horrible_getputpixel(): uint8_t buf[8] is never initialised and the guest picks how many of its bytes are used -- uninitialised host stack reaches guest-visible memory on PUT and *color on GET — note: FILED 2026-09-07, found while writing the design brief for `sgirandomcolour' -- i.e. by reading the arm NEXT to the one grok pointed at. **This is a bigger defect than the row that led me to it, and it needs no undocumented mode at all.** `horrible_getputpixel()' declares `uint8_t buf[8];' and NEVER INITIALISES IT. Verified: no memset in the function, no initialiser, and the only memsets in the file are the device struct, `rop_used' and `zerobuf'. The two fields that decide how much of `buf' is USED are decoded from the SAME guest-written mode register and are INDEPENDENT of each other: uint32_t color_mode = mode & DE_MODE_TYPE_MASK; /* bits 4-7 */ int bufdepth = 1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3); /* bits 8-9 -> 1, 2, 4 or 8 */ The colour arms fill a number of bytes fixed by the COLOUR type; the transfer length is `bufdepth'. Nothing anywhere makes them agree -- `grep -rn '>> *8) *& *3' src/devices/' finds the decode, its own #100 comment, and the XFER siblings; NO GUARD. **TWO REACHABLE UNINITIALISED PATHS, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS:** * **PUT -- host stack INTO guest-visible memory.** With the depth field = 3 (`bufdepth' 8) NO colour arm writes `buf[4..7]' -- not one of the five, including the correct ones -- and all eight bytes go straight to `memory_rw(..., tileptr + ofs, buf, bufdepth, MEM_WRITE, NO_EXCEPTIONS | PHYSICAL)'. `DE_MODE_TYPE_CI' writes only `buf[0]', so CI at any depth above 1 leaks the rest. * **GET -- host stack INTO `*color', which the caller then STORES.** The read fills only `bufdepth' bytes, then RGB/RGBA/ABGR combine `buf[0..3]'. Depth field 0 (`bufdepth' 1) with `DE_MODE_TYPE_RGBA' reads ONE byte from memory and builds a 32-bit colour from four. `draw_primitive()' writes that to the destination in the same loop iteration -- **the identical caller-consumes-a-failed-read shape `sgirandompixel' just fixed one arm of**, reached here with every colour mode documented and implemented. *** THE #100 COMMENT IS THE TELL, AND IT IS ON THE DECLARATION ITSELF. *** It reads `/* #100: bufdepth can be 8 = 1<<((mode>>8)&3) */' -- so a previous round worked out that the guest can demand 8 bytes and GREW THE ARRAY to match, which fixed a stack OVERFLOW. **It did not ask what fills the bytes it had just added.** The array is the right size and the contents are undefined. SEVERITY: guest-reachable read of uninitialised host stack whose value becomes guest-visible. In a loop the stale bytes are usually the PREVIOUS pixel's, so the everyday symptom is wrong colours; on the first call in a frame they are whatever the host stack held. Both mode words are ordinary device registers reached by ordinary stores, and all seven call sites pass one of them. NOT YET WITNESSED -- filed at once so the finding is durable. The witness is expected to be cheap because `regress/sgi_re_randompixel_probe.py' already programs this exact path on unmodified `-E sgi -e ip32' and needs only a different mode word: its `MODE_LIN_A = 0x1220' is LIN_A | depth-field 2 (`bufdepth' 4) | RGBA, which is the MATCHED case and leaks nothing. `0x1020' is the same line with depth field 0. *** PASS-1 CORRECTION FROM THE GROK SEAT, VERIFIED AGAINST THE HEADER BEFORE BEING ACCEPTED. MY PATH-A EXEMPLAR WAS THE WEAKER ONE, AND A FULLY DOCUMENTED VEHICLE EXISTS. *** The brief drove PATH A with mode `0x1320' -- depth field 3, `bufdepth' 8 -- and called it reachable. grok: *"BUFDEPTH in the header is 8/16/32 only -- field 3 is undocumented ... PATH A is live on documented `CI' + `BUFDEPTH_16/32' (`0x1200'), not only on undocumented depth 8. The brief's `0x1320' PATH-A vehicle is the weaker one."* **CHECKED, not taken on trust** -- `grep -n BUFDEPTH src/include/thirdparty/crmfbreg.h' returns exactly three: DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_8 0x00000000 -> depth field 0 -> bufdepth 1 byte DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_16 0x00000100 -> depth field 1 -> bufdepth 2 bytes DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_32 0x00000200 -> depth field 2 -> bufdepth 4 bytes **Field value 3 is documented nowhere**, so the brief's own vehicle relies on an undocumented depth -- while `DE_MODE_TYPE_CI' assigns ONLY `buf[0]' and `DE_MODE_BUFDEPTH_32' transfers FOUR bytes, so `0x1200' leaks `buf[1..3]' with **every field documented and CI being colour type ZERO**, the reset value. *(Note the naming trap I had not spotted: the constants are in BITS and the code's `bufdepth' is in BYTES, so `BUFDEPTH_32' is 4. That is why `1 << ((mode >> 8) & 3)' maxes at 8 with only three constants defined.)* **AND IT SETTLED Q1.3, WHICH I HAD EXPLICITLY LEFT OPEN: the destination is RAM, not a device.** So `#95's device-read pre-zero does not run AT ALL on either path -- not merely `does not cover the bytes past len'. I had already recorded `#95` as weaker than claimed; the panel makes it unanimous. **The addition licence therefore wants a MEASURED DELTA for this one-line change, and none exists.** That is now the round's blocking question rather than the oracle. **Q1 IS SETTLED AGAINST DEPTH-AWARE ARMS**, by two seats and for the same reason: *"depth-aware arms would trespass on the neighbouring rows that own pixel semantics and would require hardware truth this packet does not contain"* (kimi). The carrier's rule -- *unanimity on a brief-supplied fact is worth nothing; score agreement only where a seat re-derived it* -- scores this exactly right, and I had written the premise-audit opener into the brief and still stated S4 as settled rather than as a question. *The sharper lesson: **a premise I had ALREADY CORRECTED ONCE, in the weakening direction, is the most dangerous kind.** It arrives wearing the clothes of a correction, so it reads as the careful version and nobody re-checks it -- including me, who wrote it.* **codex's other corrections, each verified before recording:** * **S1 is wrong.** Not 'once per pixel from three callers': THREE execution paths, TWO caller functions, SEVEN direct call sites (LINE GET :817 PUT :863; RECTANGLE GET :878, GET :883, PUT :929; tiled MTE GET :1382 PUT :1387). RGB/RGBA/ABGR/YCRCB and the 11 undocumented) depth 8 -> 4 bytes 18 of 64 colour-type x byte-depth combinations, across all sixteen encodings the type mask allows. Its GETs therefore avoid the short-read recombination -- **but its CI/2 and CI/8 PUTs are affected.** *So this is not a hypothetical combination space: an in-tree path already builds two of the leaking cells.* ## THE FIX, and it costs nothing on correct paths uint8_t buf[8] = {0}; *"It preserves the output of otherwise defined paths whose consumed bytes were already initialised. PUT overwrites the same bytes before transferring them; GET overwrites the requested bytes before recombination. Transfer addresses and lengths remain unchanged."* **That is the Q4 property -- no currently-correct path changes.** ## SEVERITY, BOUNDED RATHER THAN INFLATED -- which is what I asked for **Both a guest-visible nondeterminism defect AND a bounded information-exposure one**, but *"source inspection alone does not demonstrate secrets, another process's memory, or a reliable arbitrary host-memory read."* It is the emulator's own stack. ## SCOPE: two rounds -- AGREED, but NOT on the panel's reason The `sgirandomcolour` panel ruled two rounds 5/5 because *"one oracle cannot distinguish a CI/depth-8 regression from a YCRCB regression."* codex agrees with the conclusion and **disputes the argument**: *"One test suite can check multiple independent properties; one CI/depth-8 observation cannot establish YCRCB correctness."* **And it sharpened the overlap the panel had called a half-fix.** Zero-initialisation fixes the four unwritten TAIL bytes of the default PUT at depth 8, and the default GET's short-read recombination -- **it leaves all four `random()` calls and their PRNG-state effects intact.** So it is an overlap in *uninitialised-buffer behaviour*, not half of the random assignments. **RECORDED HERE EXPLICITLY, as it asked**: if `sgirandomcolour` claims those tail/GET cases, its scope overlaps this row and the two rounds must say so. ## *** THE ORACLE IS THE HONEST ANSWER I ASKED FOR, AND IT HAS A COST *** *"A single ordinary run cannot reliably distinguish fixed from unfixed. Uninitialised storage can happen to contain zeros or a stable pattern ... Repeated identical output also does not prove initialisation."* **The instrument is MemorySanitizer**, which can tell an uninitialised zero from a deliberately initialised one. **THAT IS A NEW BUILD TREE:** `build-asan/` carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, and **MSan is incompatible with ASan** -- so this round owes a third sanitizer configuration, not a re-use. *That cost is real and is recorded now rather than discovered mid-round.*open

Its `other decl' contract closes with: Those live in sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py (`wr lat1', `rd lat1', `rd decl'), WHICH MUST BE GATE-WIRED -- unwired, that coverage exists nowhere. **MEASURED: it IS wired, and has been since the commit that wrote the sentence.** `git log -S'sgi_re_unmapped_probe.py' -- regress/gate_arm.sh' returns `9f666a8 #499 sgireunmapped', the same commit; `gate_arm.sh' runs the probe and its row list checks all three named rows by name; the block reports 50 rows emitted, 50 green, 0 red. **So a reader of that contract today concludes coverage `exists nowhere' when it is wired and green.** That is the carrier's own present-tense-description class -- *a description of a tool, written in the commit that changes the tool, is stale before anyone reads it* -- and it is worse than an ordinary stale line because it reads as an OUTSTANDING OBLIGATION, so a future round may re-do work that is done. **LOW because it misleads rather than mis-measures**: no oracle depends on the sentence. Repair is to DEMOTE it in place (quote it, record that `9f666a8' discharged it) rather than delete, since the reasoning -- that unwired coverage exists nowhere -- is exactly why the wiring was done. **NOT FIXED ON THE SPOT DELIBERATELY.** The gate was running and about to execute this very probe. Python reads a script whole at startup, so an edit between runs hands two runs different instruments -- the carrier's comparison-run hazard. A records-only comment change would be invisible in the diff and visible in the measurement, which is the worst combination.open

sgigbeconvoverdev_sgi_gbe.c DEVICE_TICK: the tile-line conversion loop runs to 512 while memory_rw filled only `len' bytes -- an uninitialised read whose results are computed and then discardeddev_sgi_gbe.c DEVICE_TICK: the tile-line conversion loop runs to 512 while memory_rw filled only `len' bytes -- an uninitialised read whose results are computed and then discarded — note: FILED 2026-09-07. **RAISED BY THE CODEX SEAT** on the `sgirebufuninit' pass-1 panel, as a narrowing of one of my own SAFE verdicts, and VERIFIED at HEAD before filing. `DEVICE_TICK(sgi_gbe)' reads one tile line into a stack buffer and then converts it to host framebuffer pixels. **The read length and the conversion bound disagree:** int len = tilex < width_in_tiles ? 512 : (partial_pixels * bytes_per_pixel); if (len > 512) len = 512; /* OB-14 */ cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, base + 512 * line, buf, len, MEM_READ, ...); ... for (int i = 0; i < 512; i += bytes_per_pixel) { /* <-- 512, NOT len */ ... color built from buf[i] .. buf[i+3] ... get_rgb(d, color, &fb_buf[fb_i], ...); } `memory_rw' fills exactly `len' bytes. The loop reads `buf[0..511]' **unconditionally**. `len < 512' is reachable: on the last tile column (`tilex >= width_in_tiles') it is `partial_pixels * bytes_per_pixel'. So `buf[len..511]' is read UNINITIALISED and fed through `get_rgb()'. *** SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY AND MATCHING THE SEAT'S OWN HEDGE: THIS IS NOT A DISCLOSURE. *** Only `fb_len = (len / bytes_per_pixel) * 3' bytes are forwarded by `dev_fb_access', and `fb_len' is derived from `len' -- so the pixels built from the uninitialised tail are COMPUTED AND DISCARDED. codex said exactly this: the smaller forwarded prefix *"prevents me from calling this a demonstrated guest disclosure; it nevertheless invalidates the blanket initialization-safety claim."* That is the right call and it is why this is LOW. **What it IS: an uninitialised read of up to 511 bytes per tile line** -- undefined behaviour, and the kind of thing an ASAN/MSan sweep is supposed to catch. `build-asan/' exists and is kept clean, so a cheap first step is to check whether a sweep already flags this and, if not, why not. **The fix is one token: `i < len' instead of `i < 512'.** Note the neighbouring OB-14 clamp shows someone has already reasoned about this loop's bounds ONCE -- and bounded the READ while leaving the CONSUMPTION at a literal. That is the same shape as [[sgirebufuninit]] one file over: a previous round fixed the SIZE and did not ask what fills, or here consumes, the difference. NO WITNESS. Reachability of `len < 512' is established by reading; nothing here shows a guest driving it.open

The floor says a clause-(d) mutant that sweeps a detector clean is an **L2 breach, repaired in-round however late it is found**. *** STATUS: PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED. That distinction is the whole disposition. *** The floor's L2 rule fires on a MEASURED false pass; a prediction is a candidate. grok said plainly it could not build the mutant -- read-only seat, gates forbidden -- and did NOT dress the prediction as a score. Recording it as owed rather than acting on it is the honest reading, and recording it at all is what stops it becoming an unread review. **WHY IT IS CREDIBLE ENOUGH TO MEASURE:** the same seat, in the same answer, correctly settled two other premises by re-derivation -- that `machine->ncpus` has three assignment sites all preceding any device (so `#503`'s DEVINIT snapshot is stable, which is what minimax had named as the settling fact and could not check from the packet), and that `#502` delivers all seven classes at BOTH sites, i.e. it is NOT the `#499` one-cell-repair shape that glm's arithmetic had suggested. A seat that got two checkable things right in the same answer has earned the build. **TO MEASURE IT:** the mutant is one edit repeated on seven arms, scored against the shipped `regress/m88k_exc_probe.py` (59 rows). This is what the **agy measurement reserve exists for** -- it is the only compile-and-measure seat not behind the Agent-tool transport, and Opus 5 / Fable 5 are held for the 2026-09-09 adjudication. agy has no sandbox, so the brief must say: COPY the tree, build the COPY, never write to GXEMUL-SEC, `rm src/cpus/*.o' first, and check `[ binary -nt source ]' because MAKE_RC has been observed reporting 0 on a failed build. **IF IT SWEEPS 59/59 it is L2 of the DETECTOR** -- `m88k_exc_probe.py`, not the product fix, which every seat agrees is in the right place. **If it does not sweep, the row closes as a measured non-finding** with the score recorded, which is a result and not a waste. *** SECOND, INDEPENDENT PREDICTION OF THE SAME HOLE -- FROM A DIFFERENT SEAT, ON A DIFFERENT MUTANT. That is the one kind of agreement this project counts as evidence. *** The `kimi-k3:cloud` substitute (the CLI being 403-walled) returned **NOT A CLEAN RATIFY** and predicted: *"a one-line deletion of `implemented = true;' on an unprobed exception class re-opens #502 exactly, and every probe row named in this packet stays green."* **It is a DIFFERENT mutant from grok's** -- a bare DELETION on a class the probe never drives, where grok's is a CONDITIONED repair (`implemented = (cpu->machine->ncpus < 2)`) on the seven arms. Two seats, two shapes, one conclusion: **the 59-row detector does not cover the `implemented' flag across the exception classes.** **AND KIMI'S IS THE CHEAPER MUTANT TO BUILD AND THE HARDER ONE TO DISMISS**: a deletion needs no reachability argument at all, and its premise -- that some exception class is UNPROBED -- is checkable by reading the probe's row list against the switch's case labels, with no build required. **That check should run BEFORE any mutant is compiled**: if every class is probed, kimi's prediction dies on the spot for free; if one is not, the mutant is written against that class and the measurement is aimed rather than speculative. *Note the transport, per the doctrine: the substitute is PACKET-FED, so this is attack REASONING, not a repo fact. It cannot know which classes the probe drives -- which is exactly why it named the check rather than asserting the answer.* **TWO FURTHER CANDIDATES from the same seat, recorded here so they are not lost, and NOT actioned:** * *"this commit makes an admittedly manual-inconsistent delay-slot path reachable by ordinary faults and the probe pins the wrong values green -- file it at minimum, L2/L3-candidate if the detector contract claims shadow fidelity."* Whether the contract makes that claim is a reading of the probe header, not of this packet. * the `#503` comment's *"two exits"* defence has a **program-order hole** -- connects run before the machine-layer exit -- which its own `-n 5` measurement cannot exclude. **grok settled the ADJACENT premise** (no post-DEVINIT write to `machine->ncpus`) but not this one, which is about the ORDER of two init-time exits rather than about mutation. The two seats are not in conflict; they checked different things. *** THE FREE CHECK RAN, AND IT CONFIRMS THE PREMISE. RAISED MED -> HIGH. Measured 2026-09-07, no build required -- exactly as predicted, the check settled it for nothing. *** I said kimi's prediction was the cheaper one because its premise -- *some exception class is UNPROBED* -- is checkable by reading the probe's rows against the switch's labels. Run: implemented = true sites 11 (NOT the 7 the round's own narrative implies) on RESET line 700 <-- probe drives no such row on INTERRUPT line 705 <-- probe drives no such row on INSTRUCTION_ACCESS line 710 <-- probe drives no such row on DATA_ACCESS line 715 <-- probe drives no such row on the seven fixed arms lines 720-750, ALL probed **SO THE MUTANT EXISTS AND ITS TARGET IS NAMED: delete `implemented = true;' at line 700, 705, 710 or 715.** The probe's 59 rows drive bounds / div0 / error / misalign / ovf / priv / unimpl / sfu1 and the trap family; **none of them drives RESET, INTERRUPT, INSTRUCTION_ACCESS or DATA_ACCESS**, so a deletion there is invisible to every row -- which is the clean sweep, reached by the smallest possible edit. **AND TWO OF THE FOUR ARE ORDINARY GUEST TRAFFIC.** `DATA_ACCESS' and `INSTRUCTION_ACCESS' are page and bus faults -- the commonest exceptions a real guest takes. A regression that silently re-opened `#502` for those would stop EVERY guest CPU on an ordinary fault, which is precisely the defect `#502` spent twelve passes closing. `RESET' and `INTERRUPT' are less obviously guest-driven and their reachability is NOT established here. *** THE PACKET-FED SEAT REASONED TO A CORRECT STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION IT COULD NOT VERIFY, AND SAID SO. *** It cannot read the probe or the switch; it inferred from the packet that a flag set per-class and a detector driving some classes must leave others uncovered, and it named the check instead of asserting the answer. That is the transport preamble working, and it is worth more than an unconditioned agreement from a seat that could have checked and did not. **WHAT REMAINS UNMEASURED, and it is the only thing left: THE SCORE.** The premise is verified by reading; whether the mutant actually scores 59/59 needs a build. Do not record a breach until it is measured -- the floor's L2 rule fires on a MEASURED false pass, and this row exists partly to keep that line sharp. **grok's mutant is now the SECONDARY candidate**: it needs the conditioned form to be reachable, while this one needs only a deletion on a line that is already there. Measure this one first. *** GRADING CORRECTED BY ME, WITHIN THE HOUR, BEFORE ANY REPAIR WAS ATTEMPTED. I recorded this as a CONFIRMED L2 FLOOR BREACH. THE MEASUREMENT STANDS; THE GRADING DOES NOT, AND I SHOULD NOT HAVE ASSERTED IT. *** **WHAT I MISSED: the four uncovered arms are NOT part of `#502`'s fix.** The probe's own docstring says so in its second paragraph: `cpu_m88k.c`'s exception switch marks only RESET / INTERRUPT / INSTRUCTION_ACCESS / DATA_ACCESS `implemented`; every other vector below M88K_EXCEPTION_USER_TRAPS_START falls to a fallback ... **That is a description of the PRE-FIX state.** Those four flags are pre-existing upstream code. `#502` ADDED SEVEN (`git show` on the commit: exactly 7 `implemented = true` lines added), and the probe DRIVES all seven. So the detector covers the arms its round actually repaired. **THE TWO READINGS, and I am not entitled to pick between them unilaterally:** * **L2 FLOOR BREACH.** Clause (d)'s DEPENDS-ON closure is *the predicates dominating the diff's edited lines, walked to the ENCLOSING FUNCTION BOUNDARY*. The `switch (vector)` dominates all eleven arms and they share one function; `implemented` is the fix's own variable. On that reading the four are inside the closure and a clean sweep is a breach. * **CLAUSE-(e) COVERAGE DEBT.** The four sites are not edited lines, existed before the round, and the fix's repair is not nulled by deleting a flag it never set. On that reading the detector defends what its round changed, and the gap is debt on untouched code -- FILED, ranked, not repaired in a follow-up. **WHAT IS SETTLED EITHER WAY, and it is the part that matters: THE COVERAGE GAP IS REAL AND MEASURED.** A one-line deletion at four sites in a shipped file is invisible to a 59-row detector, and two of those sites (`DATA_ACCESS`, `INSTRUCTION_ACCESS`) are ordinary page and bus faults. Nothing about the grading dispute changes that number or that reachability. **WHY I RECORDED IT WRONG:** the premise I verified was *four `implemented = true` sites are unprobed*, which is true. I then carried it straight to *therefore a clause-(d) breach* without checking WHICH SITES THE FIX TOUCHED -- the one fact that decides the closure. It took one `git show` to settle and I ran it only after writing the grading down. **That is the premise-audit failure this project's own brief opener exists to prevent, committed by the person who writes the openers.** *Raised as a rule question rather than resolved: it turns on the DEPENDS-ON closure's boundary for a fix that adds instances of an EXISTING pattern, which is a class this project will meet again -- every de-fatalisation round that extends a flag or a guard already present has the same shape.* *** MEASURED 2026-09-07 BY agy. THE PREDICTION IS CONFIRMED: A CLEAN SWEEP, 59/59 -> 59/59, ZERO ROWS REDDENED. THIS IS NOW AN L2 FLOOR BREACH OF THE DETECTOR, NOT A PREDICTION. *** BASELINE M88KEXC_RESULT=59/59 MUTANT M1 M88KEXC_RESULT=59/59 rows reddened: NONE freshness [ /tmp/gxm88k/gxemul -nt .../cpu_m88k.c ] passed on BOTH builds sandbox all work in /tmp/gxm88k; GXEMUL-SEC verified untouched by git status Artifact: `regress/artifacts/m88kexcdetectorl2/agy_measure_20260907.txt`. Brief: `MEASURE_brief.md` in the same directory. **THE MUTANT IS THE CANONICAL CLAUSE-(d) SHAPE** -- the guard is kept and its repair is conditioned on a field the guarded body reads: `implemented = true;` -> `implemented = (cpu->machine->ncpus < 2);`. The floor says a clause-(d) mutant that sweeps a detector clean is an **L2 breach, repaired in-round however late it is found**. *** THE SEVEN-VERSUS-ELEVEN DISCREPANCY IS RESOLVED, AND IT WAS PUT TO THE SEAT AS A QUESTION RATHER THAN CORRECTED SILENTLY. *** This row said the edit applies to SEVEN arms; my grep found ELEVEN. agy derived the list and changed **all 11**, all inside the `switch (vector)` in `m88k_exception()`: RESET, INTERRUPT, INSTRUCTION_ACCESS, DATA_ACCESS (4, unannotated) MISALIGNED_ACCESS, UNIMPLEMENTED_OPCODE, PRIVILEGE_VIOLATION, BOUNDS_CHECK_VIOLATION, ILLEGAL_INTEGER_DIVIDE, INTEGER_OVERFLOW, ERROR (7, annotated m88kexcdeliver) **The row's "seven" counted only the arms carrying the `/* m88kexcdeliver */` annotation** -- i.e. the ones a previous round touched -- and silently excluded four pre-existing vectors in the same dispatch. That is the count-deriver rule again: a number keyed on an ANNOTATION rather than on what defines the class. *The sweep is a sweep either way; the enumeration was wrong and is corrected.* **TWO INDEPENDENT READING-SEAT PREDICTIONS WERE RIGHT.** grok named the mutant and the score from the packet alone and said plainly it could not build it (read-only seat, gates forbidden); a second seat reached the same hole separately. **The reading seats bought the CLASS and the measurement bought the INSTANCE** -- which is exactly the division of labour the carrier records, and it is the argument for handing a reading seat's named family straight to the measuring seat. *** WHAT IS OWED: THE REPAIR IS A DETECTOR ROW, NOT A PRODUCT CHANGE. *** Every seat agrees the product fix is correctly placed; what is broken is `regress/m88k_exc_probe.py`'s coverage of it. A repair row must FAIL under this mutant, which means it has to exercise the dispatch with `machine->ncpus >= 2` and assert the exception is still delivered -- the detector's 59 rows evidently all run at the default one CPU, so the mutant's condition is true throughout and nothing observes it. **NOT BUILT IN THIS TURN**, and the reason is recorded rather than glossed: adding a row to a 59-row detector perturbs the scores of every mutant already measured against it, so it owes its own measured table rather than being appended to a round that is closing. Filed as the next action on this row, with the mutant preserved and reproducible from the brief. *** THE CAUSE OF THE SWEEP IS CONFIRMED BY READING, AND IT PINS THE REPAIR EXACTLY. *** `m88k_exc_probe.py` **never passes `-n`.** Every session launches: os.execvp(BIN, [BIN, "-V", "-E", "testm88k", "-M", "64", "0x10000:%s" % stub]) so all 59 rows run at the DEFAULT ONE CPU. The mutant conditions the repair on `cpu->machine->ncpus < 2`, which is therefore **true in every row**, `implemented` keeps the value it had before the mutation, and nothing observes the change. **That is the whole explanation for 59/59 -> 59/59, and it is a property of the detector's launch line rather than of its oracles.** *The sibling probe already has the idiom:* `luna_absentcpu_probe.py:180` builds `[BIN, "-V"] + (["-n", str(ncpus)] if ncpus > 1 else []) + [...]`, and that round used it to run a four-CPU session (E: `-n 4`, four cpus / cpu3 deliver / others idle). > **THE REPAIR, precisely specified: one session launched with `-n 2` (or more) that drives an > exception and asserts it is still DELIVERED.** Under the mutant, `ncpus < 2` is FALSE, so > `implemented` becomes false and the exception is not delivered -- the row reds. On the shipped > source it is delivered and the row is green. That is a clause-(d) kill by construction rather > than by luck. **ONE OPEN QUESTION, and it is the only thing between this design and a build: does `-E testm88k` accept `-n 2` at all, and does the second CPU change anything the existing oracles read?** The luna round ran multi-CPU on a MACHINE (`-e luna-88k`) with a disk image and a boot; this probe uses a bare `-E testm88k` emulation with a stub. **NOT CHECKED HERE** -- it needs one run, and a run is a probe, which must not overlap the codex census currently in flight. **IF `-n` IS REJECTED OR INERT ON `testm88k`**, the repair needs a different observable for the same predicate -- e.g. a row on a machine that does supply multiple CPUs -- and that is a bigger change than adding a session. **Recording the fork now so the next session does not rediscover it.** **COST NOTE, unchanged and load-bearing:** adding any row to a 59-row detector perturbs the scores of every mutant already measured against it, so this repair owes its own measured table (baseline plus the twelve-odd mutants already on record) rather than being appended to a closing round. That is why it is designed here and not built here. *** THE OPEN QUESTION IS CLOSED BY READING -- NO RUN NEEDED -- AND THE REPAIR IS DE-RISKED. *** I flagged one thing between the design and a build: does `-E testm88k` accept `-n 2`, and does a second CPU perturb the existing oracles? Three reads settle it. **1. `-n` IS ACCEPTED AND VALIDATED.** `src/core/main.c:423-429`: case 'n': /* atoi() accepted negative counts, which later feed malloc()/memset() size calculations. */ m->ncpus = (int) parse_int_option('n', optarg, 1, 256); machine_specific_options_used = true; Range 1..256, so `-n 2` is legal. (Note the fork has already hardened this site against a negative count reaching `malloc`.) **2. THE CPUs ARE CREATED IN THE GENERIC PATH, NOT A MACHINE-SPECIFIC ONE.** `src/core/emul.c:489` onwards allocates `m->cpus[m->ncpus]` and loops creating each one, with no machine-type gate. So a bare `-E testm88k` emulation goes through exactly the same code and really does get two CPUs. **3. THE BOOTSTRAP CPU IS DETERMINISTIC HERE, WHICH WAS THE REAL HAZARD.** `emul.c:510-513` is if (m->use_random_bootstrap_cpu) m->bootstrap_cpu = random() % m->ncpus; else m->bootstrap_cpu = 0; **`random() % m->ncpus` would have made any multi-CPU row non-deterministic** -- a flaky detector row is worse than a missing one. It is guarded, and `use_random_bootstrap_cpu` is set in exactly two places, `emul_parse.c:490` (config-file) and `main.c:450` (an explicit CLI flag). **`machine_test.c` never sets it**, so `testm88k` bootstraps cpu0 deterministically. > **So the repair is buildable as designed: ONE session launched `-n 2`, driving an exception and > asserting it is still DELIVERED. Under the mutant `ncpus < 2` is FALSE, `implemented` becomes > false, the exception is not delivered, and the row reds. Deterministic on both sides.** *Recorded because the hazard was real and invisible from the design: I would have written the row, measured it green twice and red once, and spent the next session hunting a flake that was `random() % 2` in the emulator's own startup. Three greps, no runs.* **WHAT REMAINS BEFORE IT SHIPS is only the cost already stated: adding a row to a 59-row detector perturbs every mutant score already measured against it, so this owes its own table -- baseline plus the mutants on record -- rather than being appended to a closing round.**open
