alphaswpctxptbrcpu_alpha_palcode.c swpctx: apcb_ptbr is assigned TWICE -- the second write puts new_flags into the PAGE TABLE BASE REGISTER, and apcb_flags is never assigned at allcpu_alpha_palcode.c swpctx: apcb_ptbr is assigned TWICE -- the second write puts new_flags into the PAGE TABLE BASE REGISTER, and apcb_flags is never assigned at all — commits: 7a41b3f — witness: probe:regress/alpha_harness_probe.py -- RUNG 3, MEASURED 2026-09-07 on the COMMITTED build (a264a34) on an unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1'. HEAD 7/9: `swpctx ptbr' reads 0xbbbb2222 (A.flags) where A.ptbr 0xaaaa1111 is required, and `swpctx notflags' reds on the defect's exact signature. Artifacts: regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/probe_head_20260907.out — note: FILED 2026-09-07. **RAISED BY THE CODEX SEAT** under the found-something-else licence, on a brief that asked only whether Alpha machines can run anything (regress/artifacts/alphapfnoffset/codex_boot_20260907.txt) -- and VERIFIED by reading before filing. `PAL_OSF1_swpctx' loads a new context and assigns it into the pcb. **`apcb_ptbr' is assigned TWICE and `apcb_flags' is never assigned at all:** // Update all variables in the pcb simultaneously: cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ksp = new_ksp; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_usp = new_usp; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ptbr = new_ptbr; <- correct cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_cpc = new_cpc; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_asn = new_asn; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_unique = new_unique; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ptbr = new_flags; <- *** should be apcb_flags *** cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_decrsv0 = new_decrsv0; cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_decrsv1 = new_decrsv1; *** WHY THIS OUTRANKS THE OTHER ALPHA ROWS: `apcb_ptbr' IS THE PAGE TABLE BASE REGISTER. *** `alpha_translate_v2p()' opens with `uint64_t base = cpu->cd.alpha.pcb.apcb_ptbr << ALPHA_PAGESHIFT;' -- so after ANY `swpctx' the page-table walk reads its tables from an address derived from the FLAGS word. Every translation after a context switch walks garbage. **And `apcb_flags' keeps the OUTGOING context's value**, because nothing ever writes it -- a second, quieter defect from the same line. **THE COMMENT DIRECTLY ABOVE ASSERTS WHAT THE CODE DOES NOT DO:** *"Update all variables in the pcb simultaneously"*. Two of the nine are wrong -- one clobbered, one never set. That is the second time in this one function that a comment states an intent the code contradicts; the other is [[alphaswpctxreg]]. **FIX: one token** -- the second `apcb_ptbr' becomes `apcb_flags'. As with its sibling, the intent is not in doubt: `new_flags' is loaded from the context block and would otherwise be dead, and `apcb_flags' exists in the struct and would otherwise never be written. **REACHABILITY: cold-debugger reachable, per the same pass** -- `swpctx' is an active handler reached by ordinary guest instruction dispatch with no OS dependency. A witness plants a `call_pal 0x30' and observes `apcb_ptbr' afterwards. *** THE INTERACTION WITH [[alphapfnoffset]] IS WORTH STATING, because it changes how that round should be designed: this defect CORRUPTS THE WALK'S BASE, and that one CORRUPTS THE WALK'S RESULT. *** A witness for either must control for the other -- a probe that does a `swpctx' and then observes a bad translation cannot attribute it without pinning which of the two produced it. **Fix this one first**: it is certain, one token, and it removes a confound from the harder row. *** DESIGN PASS, codex 2026-09-07 (regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/codex_design_20260907.txt). THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED AND TWO OF MY SUPPORTING PREMISES WERE WRONG. Corrected here. *** Verdict: *"A and B are defects, and both proposed corrections are right. They are TWO changes under your reopening rule. `apcb_flags is never written' is false; no third destination typo was found."* **CORRECTION 1 -- `apcb_flags' IS WRITTEN, and I filed the opposite as fact.** This row said it *"is never assigned at all"*. `grep -rn apcb_flags src/' returns `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:221' -- **`wrfen' assigns it** from `r[ALPHA_A0]' and then writes it back to PCB memory, and `swpctx' itself READS the field when saving the outgoing context. **The honest statement is narrower and still a defect:** `swpctx' never assigns `apcb_flags' WHEN LOADING A NEW CONTEXT, so the incoming context's flags are silently dropped and the outgoing context's value persists across the switch. That is a real defect; *never written anywhere* was not. **CORRECTION 2 -- `new_flags' is NOT dead, and the distinction matters.** I wrote that it *"would otherwise be dead"*. codex: it *"has exactly one use after its declaration: the erroneous PTBR assignment. It is otherwise unused, but **not dead in the current program**: it changes PTBR."* My phrasing implied the compiler would flag it; it would not, because the erroneous line consumes it. **A QUALIFICATION ON THE SIBLING [[alphaswpctxreg]] THAT BOUNDS ITS IMPACT:** the handler captures its input into a LOCAL `a0' before dispatch, so overwriting `r[ALPHA_A0]' does **not** change which context is loaded. That defect is therefore purely a wrong RETURN VALUE -- it does not corrupt the switch itself. I had not established that, and it is the difference between a reporting bug and a state-corruption bug. **SCOPE: TWO CHANGES, NOT ONE.** I intended to fix both in one diff -- same function, same class. codex rules they are two under the reopening rule. **Accepted**: the observables differ (a guest register versus internal PCB state reachable only through a translation), so one test cannot cover both without a new observation, which is exactly what that rule forbids. **MY Q3 HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED, and recording that matters as much as a finding.** I said a third wrong-destination assignment was *"more likely than not"* given two in one function, and asked for the whole handler to be read. It was, and there is no third. **A predicted class that does not materialise is a result** -- and it stops the next round hunting for one. *** READ-ONLY AUDIT, 2026-09-07 (codex, `regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/codex_read_20260907.txt`). THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED FIELD BY FIELD, THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN, AND A PREMISE OF MINE ABOUT REACHABILITY WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE WITNESS. *** **VERDICT:** *"`swpctx` assigns `apcb_ptbr` twice, leaves `apcb_flags` unchanged, and uses all nine locals. Its return line writes `a0`. Opcode-0 dispatch has no privilege check, but `alpha_palcode()` itself checks user mode before the switch."* **CONFIRMED, from the seat's own nine-row assignment table rather than from my description:** `apcb_ptbr` is assigned twice, `apcb_flags` never, and **all nine locals are used** -- so the defect is precisely a mis-typed destination, not a dropped load. **The fix is ONE IDENTIFIER TOKEN on ONE LINE** (`cpu_alpha_palcode.c:282`), which the seat states explicitly. The `a0`-for-`v0` return is confirmed as a second, separate defect in the same handler. *** THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS A HARNESS-BREAKER RATHER THAN A RECORDS NICETY. *** I wrote -- in the brief AND in the first draft of the Alpha harness -- that `call_pal` dispatch is unconditional. **Dispatch INTO `alpha_palcode()` is; the function then GATES ITS OWN SWITCH** at `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:183`: uint64_t userMode = cpu->cd.alpha.ps & ALPHA_PSL_USERMODE; /* 0x0008 */ if (userMode && !(palcode == 0x80 || 0x81 || 0x83 || 0xae || 0xaa || 0x86 || 0x9e || 0x92 || 0x9f)) { fatal("[ Privileged Alpha PALcode called from user mode: TODO ]"); cpu->running = 0; return; } **`0x30` is not on that whitelist**, so in user mode `call_pal 0x30` does not reach swpctx -- it HALTS THE CPU. **That failure presents as a probe whose step never completes**, i.e. as a broken harness rather than as a mode problem, which is the worst kind of failure to debug. Verified by reading the lines rather than taken on the seat's word. `cpu->cd.alpha.ps` has NO explicit initialiser anywhere in `src/`, so it is zero from the zeroed cpu struct and USERMODE is clear -- kernel mode, and the gate does not fire. **That is a derivation, and the harness turns it into a measurement**: `regress/alpha_harness_probe.py` now carries a `palgate` row asserting the diagnostic is absent, and a `palalive` row asserting the machine survives a swpctx call at all. *Note the shape: the premise that was wrong is the one I did NOT think to question -- I checked the instruction decoder carefully and never looked inside the function it dispatches to. That is the third instance this week and it is the subject of the queued rule question [[sgilinearnegidxpostmortem]], which asks whether the premise-audit instruction needs a self-directed twin. **This is its third data point and the first where a seat caught it before it cost anything.*** **AND THE BRIEF THAT ASKED THIS WAS THE SECOND ATTEMPT.** The first -- carrying a four-step witness DESIGN -- was REFUSED by the same seat as chain-shaped content (see [[codexbriefscoping]]). The chain-free re-ask, which requests a field-by-field audit and names no procedure, was answered in full. **The design question went to grok instead**, so neither question was dropped. *** THE WITNESS DESIGN WAS REFUTED, BY THE SEAT THE REFUSED BRIEF WAS ROUTED TO. grok, `regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/grok_witness_20260907.txt`, 13.5 kB. *** **VERDICT:** *"YES, a rung-3 witness is buildable on the three constructing Alpha machines -- but the proposed 'no MMU at all, two `swpctx`, read `A+16`' design is unsound as written if `A.flags` is nonzero. After the first switch, `apcb_ptbr` IS the flags word, the identity map dies, and the second `call_pal` (and the save that is supposed to publish the bug) can fail to land or can `exit(1)` the host. Use K0SEG for code and both PCBs, or keep `flags==0` and accept a weaker oracle. The one-token fix is not a PAL convention; it is a copy-paste of the previous LHS."* *** THE DESIGN WAS SELF-DEFEATING AND I HAD NOT SEEN IT: THE DEFECT DESTROYS THE PATH THE WITNESS NEEDS TO OBSERVE IT. *** Verified in `memory_alpha.c` rather than taken on the seat's word, and the source is sharper than the verdict: * **K0SEG is checked BEFORE `base` is used at all** (`:62`): `if (!userMode && vaddr >= ALPHA_K0SEG_BASE && vaddr <= ALPHA_K0SEG_END) { *return_paddr = vaddr & 0x3ffffffffff; return 2; }`. A K0SEG access never consults `apcb_ptbr`, so grok's remedy is sound. `ALPHA_K0SEG_BASE = 0xfffffc0000000000`; `ALPHA_PHYS_TO_K0SEG(x) = x | BASE`. * **The identity map is an explicit 'UGLY hack' conditioned on `base == 0`** (`:73`). That is the ONLY reason a naive harness works at all -- `ptbr` is zero at reset. **The moment the buggy assignment makes `apcb_ptbr` nonzero, `base != 0` and every later access falls into a real page-table walk over garbage**, with an `exit(1)` sitting on one vaddr at `:75-78`. * **AND THE POLARITY TRAP grok did not state, which kills the 'keep flags==0' fallback too:** if the marker is put in `A.ptbr` instead, then under the *FIXED* build `apcb_ptbr` becomes that nonzero marker and the identity map dies on the FIX rather than on the defect. **Neither polarity survives with a nonzero value anywhere in that field.** So K0SEG is not the better option, it is the only one. **THE CORRECTED DESIGN, and it needs no 64-bit immediates:** `lda`/`ldah` build 32-bit constants only, and a K0SEG address needs bit 63..42 set. The way through is to **load the pointers BEFORE the first `swpctx`, while the identity map is still alive**: place the 64-bit K0SEG pointers in identity-mapped scratch with the debugger's `put q`, have the guest `ldq` them into registers, and only then issue the calls. Every access after that carries a K0SEG address in a register and is immune to whatever `apcb_ptbr` becomes. **A SEPARATE TRAP FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS, which the harness avoids only by luck:** `memory_alpha.c:87` silently remaps `(vaddr & ~0x1fff) == 0x20000000` to `PROM_ARGSPACE_PADDR` (0x12000). The harness's code at `0x20010000` and scratch at `0x20020000` fall OUTSIDE that 8 kB window -- but nothing said so, and a probe placed 64 kB lower would have had its stores quietly land in PROM argument space. **Q4 ANSWERED:** *"The one-token fix is not a PAL convention; it is a copy-paste of the previous LHS."* Both seats agree the correction is `apcb_flags` at `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:282`. *** THE ROUTING WORKED AND IS THE REUSABLE LESSON. *** codex REFUSED this brief as chain-shaped; grok answered it in full, read the handler, the dispatch path and the existing harness, and refuted the design on a mechanism I had missed. **The chain-free re-ask to codex and the chain-shaped original to grok together cost one extra invocation and lost nothing** -- which is the argument the 2026-09-09 adjudication is asked to rule on under [[codexbriefscoping]]. *** CODE REVIEW OF THE HARNESS, BEFORE ITS FIRST RUN. grok, `regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/grok_harness_20260907.txt` -- codex REFUSED this brief too (sixth refusal, chain/witness shape), so it is grok's third answer to a brief codex would not take. *** **VERDICT:** *"DO NOT TRUST THE FIRST RUN. The lda/ldah/ldq bootstrap and the swpctx SAVE/RESTORE walk are right. The encodings that this file actually emits match the decoder. `put d` is the right debugger command. What is wrong is the ADDRESS PLAN, and it makes three rows able to go green while measuring 'unmapped reads return 0', not the handler."* *** FINDING 1 -- FATAL, AND IT WOULD HAVE BEEN SILENT AND GREEN. *** The machine is built `-M 64` = 64 MB and every address in the file sat at `0x200xxxxx` (512 MB+). K0SEG translation is `vaddr & 0x3ffffffffff`, so **the K0SEG idea survives contact with `alpha_translate_v2p` and the PHYSICAL BACKING does not.** And the failure mode is silent: `memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr` only halts when `halt_on_nonexistant_memaccess` is set, i.e. under `-T`. **Without it, writes succeed and are DISCARDED and reads RETURN ZEROS** -- and an instruction fetch of zeros is a real instruction, `call_pal 0`. **MY ORACLE MADE THAT UNDETECTABLE.** It asserted `PCB_A+16 == 0` for the correct case, and 0 is also what an unmapped read returns. **The witness would have gone green having written nothing, read nothing, and executed `call_pal 0` off a zero-filled code page.** **REPAIRED, and the repair is better than moving the addresses:** K0SEG means translation never consults `apcb_ptbr`, so `apcb_ptbr` may now hold a distinctive NONZERO value -- which the FIRST design could not allow, because a nonzero ptbr killed the identity map. So: correct handler -> PCB_A+16 == PTBR_VAL (0xaaaa1111) the defect -> PCB_A+16 == FLAGS_VAL (0xbbbb2222) anything broken -> 0, which is NEITHER, so BOTH rows red plus a third row `swpctx mapped` asserting the value is not 0 -- **because without it a probe whose addresses drifted back outside RAM would fail one row and pass the other, which reads exactly like a real defect.** Addresses moved inside 64 MB with an `assert` that says so. *** FINDING 2 -- `palalive` IS A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL, AND I WROTE IT WHILE APPLYING THE RULE AGAINST THAT. *** *"`alive` is 'the pty is still readable'. `alpha_palcode`'s default arm does `cpu->running = 0` and stays in the debugger because `-V` is single-step. The emulator does not exit. `palalive` stays green."* **Kept as a LABELLED NON-ORACLE rather than deleted**, so the next reader sees why it is there and does not re-add it as a real row; the mode question is answered by `palgate`, which greps the diagnostic text. **FINDING 3 -- the encoder self-test does not test the decoder.** It re-runs `load_const`'s own 32-bit wrap masked with `& 0xffffffff`, while LDAH sign-extends through an `(int32_t)` cast -- `0xdeadbeef` would be `0xffffffffdeadbeef` in a register and the self-test would still print ok. **It is sound only because every value this file uses has bit 31 clear.** Correct by luck; recorded in the file as such rather than quietly fixed. **FINDING 4 -- `put q` is not merely 128-bit, it is UNIMPLEMENTED** (`"quad-words: TODO"`). The premise was true and understated. **CONFIRMED, so the design work was not wasted:** encodings match the decoder; the bootstrap method is valid and nothing between the `put d` writes and the first `call_pal` touches `apcb_ptbr`; K0SEG is checked before `base`; PCB offsets match `struct alpha_pcb`; `ps` is zero from `zeroed_alloc`; `0x30` is not on the unprivileged whitelist. It also supplied two facts I did not have: `cpu->cd.alpha.ctx` starts at `0x10100`, and PROM setup (on by default) sets `a0 = 2048`. *** THE REVIEW COST ONE INVOCATION AND SAVED A GREEN WITNESS THAT PROVED NOTHING. *** The lifecycle says ask a seat to try a rung-3 probe; this says ask a seat to READ the probe before running it, and on this evidence the second is worth as much as the first. *** RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT AND RUN, 2026-09-07. The confound is now measured rather than suspected. *** A SECOND CONSEQUENCE THIS ROW DOES NOT RECORD, found by COUNTING the assignments rather than reading them. 2026-09-07. *** Over `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:274-292`, the load block's field assignments are: apcb_ksp 1 apcb_usp 1 apcb_cpc 1 apcb_asn 1 apcb_unique 1 apcb_decrsv0 1 apcb_decrsv1 1 apcb_ptbr **2** <- :278 = new_ptbr, :282 = new_flags apcb_flags **0** <- never assigned at all **So `:282` is a field-name transposition: it should be `apcb_flags = new_flags`.** The value IS loaded -- the SAVE block stores `apcb_flags` to `ctx + 40` and the loader reads `new_flags` from `ctx + 40` -- and then lands in the wrong field. > **CONSEQUENCE 1 is the clobber the witness measures: `apcb_ptbr` ends up holding the flags word.** > **CONSEQUENCE 2 is new: `apcb_flags` is NEVER LOADED, so a context switch silently drops the > incoming context's flags.** The row's title names only the first. *And the block's own comment at `:275` reads **"Update all variables in the pcb simultaneously"** -- which is exactly the property it fails to have. Enumerating the comparison gives `-2 -> VADDR', `-1 -> VADDR', `0 -> ALL', `1 -> VADDR', `2 -> VADDR', `3 -> VADDR'. The header's independent definitions require all-entry and all-per-process invalidation for the negative selectors."* So `tbi(-1)' and `tbi(-2)' -- the OS's way of saying *invalidate everything* / *invalidate all per-process entries* -- are treated as *invalidate one virtual address*. **A TLB flush that silently flushes almost nothing is the dangerous direction**: the guest believes stale translations are gone. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY ME. The citation is given and the check is one comparison plus the header's selector definitions. Filed rather than confirmed because the Alpha queue is now six rows deep and this one needs the header read alongside the code. *** VERIFIED IN PART, 2026-09-08, BY codex -- AND IT REFUSED TO VERIFY THE HALF MY BRIEF HAD MADE UNANSWERABLE. *** **THE DISPATCH IS CONFIRMED.** `cpu_alpha_palcode.c`, `case 0x33 /* PAL_OSF1_tbi */`: if (a0 >= 1) cpu->invalidate_translation_caches(cpu, a1, INVALIDATE_VADDR); else cpu->invalidate_translation_caches(cpu, 0, INVALIDATE_ALL); `a0` is a `uint64_t` local copied from `cpu->cd.alpha.r[ALPHA_A0]`, itself `uint64_t` (`src/include/cpu_alpha.h`). **There is no active signed cast** -- the only cast is inside a commented-out `debug()`, which has no effect. So `-2` is `0xff..fe`, `a0 >= 1` is TRUE, and both negative selectors take the VADDR branch. All six enumerated: `-2, -1, 1, 2, 3 -> VADDR`, `0 -> ALL`. **THE HEADER DEFINITIONS ARE REAL AND THEY ARE THE POINT** -- `src/include/thirdparty/alpha_cpu.h`: #define ALPHA_TBIA() alpha_pal_tbi(-2, 0) /* all TB entries */ #define ALPHA_TBIAP() alpha_pal_tbi(-1, 0) /* all per-process */ #define ALPHA_TBISI(va) alpha_pal_tbi(1, (va)) #define ALPHA_TBISD(va) alpha_pal_tbi(2, (va)) #define ALPHA_TBIS(va) alpha_pal_tbi(3, (va)) So the two selectors meaning *invalidate broadly* are exactly the two the comparison misroutes. Selector `0` is NOT defined by the header, so its fallback to INVALIDATE_ALL is not a requirement. *** WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE SEAT WAS RIGHT TO SAY SO: WHETHER THE TWO BRANCHES DIFFER IN EFFECT. *** *"The handler proves that different callback arguments are selected. It does not prove what the callback does with them ... I would not promote this to a verified functional invalidation defect yet."* **THAT GAP IS MY BRIEF'S FAULT.** I scoped its reading to the PALcode file and the header -- a habit adopted to keep the codex content filter from refusing -- and that scope EXCLUDES `invalidate_translation_caches`, which is the only thing that can answer the question. > *** THE TENSION IS WORTH NAMING BECAUSE IT WILL RECUR: NARROWING codex's READING SCOPE TO AVOID > THE CONTENT FILTER CAN STARVE THE QUESTION. *** The scoping remedy in [[codexsubjectrefusal]] is > about which CORPUS trips the filter; it is not free, and here it cost the answer. A dispatch oracle (assert the callback's `(address, flags)` for the six selectors) is decisive about DISPATCH and says nothing about guest effect. *** Q3 IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS (a): THE TWO BRANCHES DIFFER, AND `ALPHA_TBIA()` -- THE OS's "INVALIDATE EVERY TLB ENTRY" PRIMITIVE -- CURRENTLY INVALIDATES **VIRTUAL PAGE ZERO** AND NOTHING ELSE. codex, 2026-09-08, with the widened reading scope it asked for. *** **THE TRACE, end to end, each hop quoted in the answer:** `cpu_alpha.c` binds the callback to `alpha_invalidate_translation_caches`; `tmp_alpha_tail.c` generates it via `#define DYNTRANS_INVALIDATE_TC ... #include "cpu_dyntrans.c"`; and the two branches in `cpu_dyntrans.c` are genuinely different code: VADDR for (r=0; r<...; r++) if (entry[r].valid && (entry[r].vaddr_page & cpu->vaddr_mask) == (addr_page & cpu->vaddr_mask)) INVALIDATE_TLB_ENTRY(...) <- ADDRESS PREDICATE ALL if (flags & INVALIDATE_ALL) { for (r=0; r<...; r++) if (entry[r].valid) INVALIDATE_TLB_ENTRY(..., 0); <- NO ADDRESS PREDICATE return; } *** THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES IT BITE. *** `ALPHA_TBIA()` is `alpha_pal_tbi(-2, 0)` -- selector `-2`, **vaddr `0`**. The unsigned comparison sends it to the VADDR branch, which then matches on `a1 == 0`. Alpha uses 8 KiB pages and ordinary CPU construction leaves `vaddr_mask` ALL-ONES, so the predicate matches **cached virtual page zero only -- and nothing at all if that page is not cached. Every other mapping survives a flush the guest OS believes cleared the whole TLB.** **THE GUEST-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE IS ESTABLISHED, not inferred:** a previously cached, subsequently remapped nonzero virtual page can still reach its OLD physical backing, because the Alpha load/store fast path consumes the surviving `host_load`/`host_store` pointers that `DYNTRANS_INVALIDATE_TLB_ENTRY` would have NULLed. *** AND IT REFUTED THE ESCAPE HATCH I OFFERED. *** My brief invited *"if Alpha has no bootable in-tree rig that exercises paging, say so -- documented-only is a real answer."* The seat declined it and gave three reasons: `memory_alpha.c` carries an ACTIVE three-level page-table walker (the "Not yet implemented" diagnostic is inside a specific zero-PTBR bootstrap case, not the walker); AlphaBook 1 IS registered in `machine_alpha.c`; and `regress/alpha_harness_probe.py` and `alpha_pfnoffset_probe.py` already drive the ordinary Alpha machine with liveness and PAL-dispatch controls. **"Neither inherent unobservability nor absent paging support justifies closing it as documented-only."** **HONEST STATUS, in its words: "source-confirmed functional defect; witness unvalidated."** It ran no before/after comparison and found no dedicated test. So the round still owes the rung-3 differential -- but the basis for building one exists and is named. *** SEVERITY RAISED med -> high. *** A documented OS primitive for *invalidate everything* clears one page or none, silently, while the guest proceeds on the assumption that it worked -- and the consequence is a guest reaching stale physical backing through the fast path. That is the same class as the other HIGH rows here (silent wrong data reaching the guest), not a cosmetic one. **This is a judgment and it is flagged for the adjudication rather than treated as settled**: the underlying facts are codex's, verified by citation; the ranking is mine. > *** THE CLUSTER ORDERING NEEDS REVISITING, AND codex'S OWN CAVEAT SAYS WHY. *** It ranked > `alphaswpctxreg` FIRST and labelled that *"a confidence judgment, not a claim that it has the > greatest potential severity"* -- explicitly because `alphatbinegsel` had "confirmed dispatch > behavior but unverified functional consequences." **Those consequences are now verified.** The > ordering input has changed since the ranking was given, so the ranking should not be quoted as > though it still holds. **REPAIR, unchanged and now on a settled basis:** `if (a0 >= 1 && a0 <= 3)`, sending both defined negative selectors to INVALIDATE_ALL. codex supplied the accurate CHANGELOG claim and its limit: > *"Correct Alpha PAL `tbi` handling of negative selectors so broad invalidation clears all cached > address mappings."* It **retains coarse full flushing for `-1`** and does NOT implement `ALPHA_TBIAP()`'s selective preservation of global (ASM=0) entries -- so the round must claim the coarse repair and disclose that, rather than claiming the architectural semantics. *One stale in-tree comment fell out of the same trace and is worth a separate look: a comment claiming the VADDR path "clears only the quick array" is stale for this implementation -- the 64-bit entry helper NULLs `host_load`, `host_store`, `phys_addr` and `phys_page` and clears the TLB entry's `valid` flag.* *** WITNESS DESIGN: codex REFUSED IT AT THE PROMPT (2026-09-08), and the refusal is informative rather than merely inconvenient. *** `codex_witness_20260908.txt` is 0 bytes; its `.err` is 6,291 bytes with **zero file-read lines** -- so it refused before opening anything, which makes this the CHAIN-SHAPE trigger recorded in [[codexsubjectrefusal]] rather than the archive-reading one. The same seat answered three other briefs on this very defect tonight, including the callback trace that settled Q3. **The distinction is between ANALYSING existing code and CONSTRUCTING a guest sequence that reaches the defect. Witness design is inherently the second**, so codex is the wrong seat for it -- not a degraded one. Re-fired the identical brief, byte-for-byte, at grok. *** THE WITNESS IS CONSTRUCTIBLE, AND grok SUPPLIED IT. 2026-09-08, on the brief codex refused at the prompt -- reused BYTE-FOR-BYTE, so this is a seat-capability result and not a rewrite. *** **RUNG 3, unmodified `-E alpha -e alphabook1`.** `machine_alpha.c` already `device_add`s LCA for `ST_ALPHABOOK1`, so nothing is added to reach PAL 0x33 -- which is the ladder's clause (iii). **THE OBSERVABLE IS A STALE DYNTRANS HIT AFTER A PTE REMAP, not a dispatch spy.** That is the guest-visible channel codex could not name from its narrower scope: fill a mapping, remap the PTE behind it, `ALPHA_TBIA()`, then load and see the OLD value. *** THE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE ROW IS REAL OR VACUOUS, and it is a probe-design trap I would have walked into: THE DEBUGGER PROMPT ALL-FLUSHES BETWEEN INTERACTIONS. *** `debugger.c`, when `debugger_n_steps_left_before_interaction` reaches 0, calls `cpu_create_or_reset_tc` and `invalidate_translation_caches(..., INVALIDATE_ALL)`. > **So the FILL, the REMAP, the `tbi` and the OBSERVING LOAD must all be inside ONE `step N`. Split > them across two `step`s and BOTH builds re-walk after the remap -- the row goes GREEN ON HEAD and > the witness proves nothing.** Every existing probe in this tree is written as a sequence of > debugger interactions, so the obvious construction is the broken one. **AND THE OBVIOUS SUBSTRATE CANNOT WITNESS IT EITHER:** an identity map (`ptbr == 0`) has no PTE to change, and **K0SEG is checked BEFORE `ptbr`** in `memory_alpha.c` -- so a K0SEG address never consults the page table at all. The witness needs a real three-level walk, which is why it reuses `alpha_pfnoffset_probe.py`'s page-table substrate rather than starting from scratch. **THE SEQUENCE** (one session, one `step N`), with the walk planted through K0SEG while `ptbr` is still 0: ldq a0, k0(PCB) call_pal 0x30 # swpctx: arm the walk, and it ALL-flushes lda t0, 0x2000 # a NON-ZERO VPN -- see the page-0 constraint ldq t1, 0(t0) # FILL: cold walk, host_load -> P_OLD ldq t4, planted PTE(P_NEW) stq t4, 0(k0(L3+8)) # remap via K0SEG, NOT via the walked VPN lda a0, -2(zero) # a0 = 0xfffffffffffffffe lda a1, 0(zero) # TBIA's a1 -- must NOT be the test VPN call_pal 0x33 # PAL_OSF1_tbi ldq t2, 0(t0) # OBSERVE: VAL_OLD on HEAD, VAL_NEW after the fix **Q3 (page-0) answered and extended:** the buggy arm invalidates virtual page 0, so a test VPN of 0 would pass on BOTH builds -- vacuous by address choice. grok adds a second constraint I had not asked for: **`a1` must not be the test VPN either**, or the VADDR arm matches it and the row goes green for the wrong reason. **AN INSTRUMENT CONTROL IT VOLUNTEERED:** `lda a0, -2(zero)` really does sign-extend (`lda_0` does `(int64_t)(int32_t)arg[2]`, and LDA sign-extends its int16), **but print `a0` and `a1` after the program anyway** -- a truncated `0xfffe` would ALSO take the VADDR arm on HEAD and the ALL arm under the fix, so the row would still move while no longer testing `TBIA`. *That is a control against the instrument rather than against the emulator, and it is exactly the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has recorded four times.* **IT ALSO CONFIRMED ALL SIX PREMISES AND CORRECTED A STALE IN-TREE COMMENT** -- the comment claiming the VADDR path "only clears the quick array, not `vph_tlb_entry[]`" is stale: the 64-bit helper does NULL `host_load`/`host_store`/`phys_addr`/`phys_page` and clear `valid`. **The bug is WHICH entries are selected, not that the helper is inert.** It adds that the ALL arm does not implement ASM=0 either, *"extra, not a contradiction"* -- consistent with codex's caveat that the proposed repair is coarse and does not give `ALPHA_TBIAP()` its selective semantics. **REMAINING: build it.** The design is complete enough to implement; nothing here has been run, so the row's status stays *source-confirmed functional defect; witness DESIGNED, not yet measured*. *** THE DEBUGGER ALL-FLUSH IS VERIFIED BY ME, not taken from the seat. The anchor is `grep -n debugger_n_steps_left_before_interaction src/debugger/debugger.c` -- note the path is `src/debugger/`, NOT `src/core/`, which is where my first grep looked and found nothing. *** :781 if (debugger_n_steps_left_before_interaction > 0) { :782 debugger_n_steps_left_before_interaction --; } else { :793 cpu_create_or_reset_tc(debugger_machine->cpus[i]); :795 invalidate_translation_caches( So the flush fires on the branch taken when the counter is NOT positive -- i.e. whenever the debugger is about to interact. **The one-`step N` constraint is real.** *A file-not-found from a wrong path is the safe direction: it is loud. Had I grepped a path that EXISTS but is the wrong copy, I would have gotten a confident empty result instead -- which is the pristine-`src/` trap this project has recorded, and the reason the citation-form rule prefers a verified grep anchor over a bare line number.* *** THE ASSESS STAGE HERE IS NOT A PANEL, AND THE GATE IS RIGHT TO SAY SO. 2/9. *** `check_stage_panels` reports this stage as having moved on without the full panel -- missing fable5, opus5, agy, kimi, glm, deepseek and minimax. **That is accurate.** What ran was TWO TARGETED BRIEFS, not a panel: codex on the dispatch and the callback trace, then grok on the witness design after codex refused it. **I am recording this rather than backfilling.** The owner's rule is FULL PANEL ON EVERY STAGE and STOP AND ASK if a seat cannot be run -- *not degrade quietly* -- and quietly is exactly how a two-seat investigation becomes a "panel" in the record. *** THE THREE SEATS THAT COULD NOT HAVE RUN, by name and reason: opus5 and fable5 are PRESERVED for the 2026-09-09 adjudication by standing owner directive, and agy is the MEASUREMENT RESERVE by the 2026-08-30 ruling. The four packet-fed transports COULD have run and were not fired -- that is a choice I made, not a constraint. *** **So this row's assess stage owes a real panel before it is treated as adjudicated**, and the findings it produced -- the dispatch defect, the callback trace, the witness design -- stand on their own as two seats' work, correctly attributed. *** THE ASSESS PANEL FIRED (four packet-fed seats) AND THREE OF FOUR FOUND THE SAME DEFECT -- IN MY BRIEF, NOT IN THE CODE. *** **THE SEVERITY RAISE AND THE COARSE REPAIR ARE CONFIRMED 4/4.** glm, kimi, minimax and deepseek all sustain med -> high and all accept shipping `if (a0 >= 1 && a0 <= 3)` with the ASM=0 limit disclosed. *** DEFECT 1, FOUND INDEPENDENTLY BY glm, kimi AND minimax: MY POLARITY WAS INVERTED. *** The brief said *"VADDR keeps an entry only when `(vaddr_page & vaddr_mask) == (addr_page & vaddr_mask)`"*. **The VADDR branch INVALIDATES the matching entry; it does not keep it.** Verified by opening `cpu_dyntrans.c`: `if (flags & INVALIDATE_VADDR)` runs a loop whose own comment reads *"they must be invalidated based on the bits that matter"*. **The CONCLUSION is unaffected** -- with `a1 = 0` the arm invalidates page zero and leaves every other mapping, which is the defect as filed -- **but the sentence stating the mechanism contradicted its own THEREFORE**, and glm said so in exactly those terms. *A packet-fed seat can only reason from the packet, so an inverted premise there is the one error they cannot route around; that three of four caught it anyway is the premise-audit instruction working.* *** DEFECT 2, FOUND BY glm AND minimax: "THE CONSEQUENCES ARE NOW VERIFIED" OVERCLAIMS. *** codex's own status line was *"source-confirmed functional defect; witness UNVALIDATED"*, and I compressed that to "verified" when asking whether the ordering should change. **What is verified is the DISPATCH. The witness is DESIGNED, NOT BUILT.** glm: *"'witness constructible, shape known' is not verification -- do not promote this row to first on the packet as written."* **SO THE ORDERING QUESTION IS NOT SETTLED AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS IF IT WERE.** kimi says this row goes first; glm says not on the evidence as stated. **Both are answering honestly and they disagree because my premise was wrong.** It goes to the adjudication as a live question with the overclaim corrected. **RESIDUALS WORTH KEEPING:** * **kimi's adversarial re-break: `a0 + 2 <= 5`** -- an unsigned shifted-window test that re-admits the negative selectors while looking like a range check. deepseek's is `if (a0 != 0 && a0 != (uint64_t)-1)`. **Both belong in the round's mutant list.** * **the designed witness is BLIND to stale STORES** (a same-VA store then load reads back green on a broken build) **and to permission-only remaps** -- kimi. A round building it owes those channels or a disclosure. * deepseek, Q4: the witness is vacuous when the old and new data happen to match -- so the remap must change the observed bytes, not merely the mapping. *** THE agy SEAT ANSWERED AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ANSWER ON THIS ROW: A FILE-READING SEAT THAT RE-DERIVED EVERY PREMISE FROM SOURCE RATHER THAN RATIFYING THE PACKET. *** **It confirms Q1 high and Q2 the coarse repair, and it re-verified the six inlined premises with file and line** -- the uint64_t declaration, the two OS wrappers, the two dyntrans branches, vaddr_mask, the 8 KiB page size, the debugger ALL-FLUSH, the K0SEG early return, and the MEM_MIPS/MEM_M88K-only device-failure arms with ALPHA_KENTRY_MM having zero consumers. *** IT IS THE FOURTH INDEPENDENT STATEMENT OF THE CORRECT POLARITY, and it did not have to be told. *** Unprompted, it writes that INVALIDATE_VADDR *"invalidates only entries matching (vaddr_page & cpu->vaddr_mask) == (addr_page & cpu->vaddr_mask)"* -- which is the opposite of my brief's *"keeps an entry only when"*. glm, kimi and minimax caught the inversion from the packet alone; agy simply states the truth from the file. **Q2 gained a REASON the packet-fed seats could not supply**, and it is the reason that makes the coarse repair right rather than merely acceptable: *"GXemul's translation cache does not track ASM bits or ASN tags per entry in vph_tlb_entry / l1_64 at all"*, so ASM=0 selectivity is not a finer semantics this round declined to implement -- **it has no representation to be implemented in.** Flushing everything on ALPHA_TBIAP() is conservative and correct against that structure. *** FOUR ADVERSARIAL RE-BREAKS FOR Q3, AND THE FOURTH IS A CLAUSE-(d) NULL-REPAIR. *** (uint32_t)a0 >= 1 looks like the 32-bit PALcode argument convention; 0xfffffffe >= 1 a0 > 0 looks like a clean equivalent of a0 >= 1; -2 as uint64_t is > 0 a0 >= 1 || a0 <= 3 a one-character typo that is true for every 64-bit value else -> INVALIDATE_VADDR the GUARD is correctly fixed and the ELSE ARM still says VADDR **The fourth is the one a mutant table would most likely miss**, because every row aimed at the GUARD sees a correct guard. It is clause (d) exactly: keep the repair, null its effect -- and it belongs in the round's mutant list beside kimi's `a0 + 2 <= 5` and deepseek's `a0 != 0 && a0 != (uint64_t)-1`. *** FIVE WITNESS BLIND CHANNELS, AND TWO ARE NEW AND SHARPER THAN THE THREE ALREADY FILED. *** * **TEST VPN = PAGE 0 IS SELF-DEFEATING.** HEAD's defective arm flushes page zero, so a witness that happens to pick VPN 0 goes GREEN ON THE DEFECTIVE BUILD. *The defect is that only page 0 is flushed, so page 0 is the one page that cannot witness it.* * **A POLLUTED a1 MASKS IT.** If a1 is not explicitly zeroed before `call_pal 0x33`, HEAD flushes whatever a1 holds -- so if a1 happens to carry the test VPN the broken build looks correct. * the other three restate what kimi and deepseek already gave: value collision, split debugger steps, and K0SEG or ptbr == 0 bypassing the page table. **Q5 ORDERING: agy says THIS ROW FIRST, and it is careful about why.** It does NOT repeat my withdrawn overclaim -- it writes *"witness FEASIBILITY"*, which is what is actually established, and it grounds the ranking on a severity comparison it made itself: `alphaswpctxreg` is *"medium severity (writing the return value to a0 rather than v0)"*, and swpctx's own context arming via apcb_ptbr works regardless of which register receives the old context address. *** I WROTE "THE ORDERING NOW READS 3-1" AND IT READS 2-3 THE OTHER WAY. Corrected the same hour, from the answers, before this record shipped. *** I tallied from my own summary instead of from the five files, and got both numbers wrong -- including deepseek, whose closing sentence is *"if this row is high and verified, it may go first, but that is not established from the packet."* **That is a tally of seats written from memory, which is the exact class this project keeps paying for.** Read from the artifacts: kimi THIS ROW FIRST "the ranking variable was uncertainty; it is now zero" agy THIS ROW FIRST on a severity comparison it made itself from source glm NOT YET "constructibility is not verification; no executed differential" deepseek NOT ESTABLISHED cannot rank without alphaswpctxreg's severity minimax NOT YET "mark ready to elevate once the witness actually runs" > **BUT THE COUNT IS THE LEAST INFORMATIVE THING HERE, AND THE ARGUMENTS CONVERGE COMPLETELY.** > All three NOT-YET seats give ONE reason and it is the same reason: **the witness has not been > RUN.** None of them disputes the severity or the mechanism. So this is not a 2-3 split to be > resolved by weight -- it is a unanimous statement of the CONDITION under which the ordering > flips, and that condition is exactly what opus5's hold is for. *Count the arguments, not the > seats.* **minimax put the trap in the sharpest form:** *"The previous ranking was honest. Flipping it on the strength of 'constructible in principle' is the same shape of error in reverse."* *** FOUR FINDINGS THAT WERE SITTING BELOW THE VERDICT LINES, AND I HAD READ ONLY THE TAILS. *** * **glm: THE THEREFORE NAMES ONLY `ALPHA_TBIA()`, AND `ALPHA_TBIAP()` IS EQUALLY BROKEN.** `-1` misdispatches identically, so **the CONTEXT-SWITCH primitive is broken too** -- which glm says *"strengthens Q1 and matters for Q5"*. agy's verdict line independently names both wrappers. My brief's conclusion sentence understated the defect's own reach. * **glm: MY SEVERITY ARGUMENT HAS AN UNESTABLISHED PREMISE -- "during ordinary operation".** Nothing shown demonstrates a supported guest executing `tbi` with a negative operand during normal running; the wrappers existing in the OS header is not the same claim. **Settling fact named: a trace of PAL 0x33 invocations with their `a0` values during an ordinary boot.** glm confirms high on per-invocation consequence regardless, but flags that if the rubric wants demonstrated in-guest incidence, that trace is the missing artifact. *That is a premise audit landing on the one judgment in this row that is mine.* * **glm: A CROSS-ROW ATTRIBUTION HAZARD.** This repair changes context-switch flush behaviour and `swpctx` IS the context-switch PAL -- so **whichever of the two lands SECOND must re-baseline its witness with the other's fix present**, or a TBIAP on the switch path confuses attribution between the two rows. Neither row records this today. * **kimi's Q2 open question was CLOSED BY agy, and neither seat knew.** kimi: *"the one fact that would change this answer: do tc entries carry an ASN/ASM field? Not stated; if they do not, the fine semantics are not even implementable here."* agy read the source: **they do not** -- `vph_tlb_entry` and `l1_64` carry no ASM/ASN. So Q2's answer is not *coarse repair accepted with a disclosed limit* but the stronger **the finer semantics have no representation to be implemented in**, and the disclosure should say that instead. **AND kimi's Q3 CARRIES A REVIEWER INVARIANT WORTH MORE THAN THE MUTANT:** its `a0 + 2 <= 3 + 2` admits exactly {-2,-1,0,1,2,3} by mod-2^64 wrap, so **every one of the five documented wrappers takes the identical branch it took on the broken build** and any test authored against the defective behaviour stays green. The honest look-alike `(a0 - 1) <= 2` is CORRECT -- which is precisely why the `+2` form survives review. kimi's invariant: *"the true-branch preimage over all 2^64 inputs must be exactly {1,2,3}; any test expressed as addition or subtraction on the unsigned a0 is a red flag."* **A SECOND ROW GAINS AN UNSOLICITED SEVERITY READ:** `alphaswpctxreg` medium, argued from the register semantics. It is carried to that row rather than acted on here.open

alphactxfailcpu_alpha_palcode.c swpctx: the context save and load ignore every memory-access failure, and this fork zeroes read buffers on a failed translation -- so an ignored failure becomes committed zero-valued PCB statecpu_alpha_palcode.c swpctx: the context save and load ignore every memory-access failure, and this fork zeroes read buffers on a failed translation -- so an ignored failure becomes committed zero-valued PCB state — note: FILED 2026-09-07 from the `swpctx' design pass (regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/codex_design_20260907.txt). codex: *"SAVE discards store return values; the load helpers discard read status. `ctx' changes before loading finishes, with no failure check before committing the PCB. In this fork, failed translations zero read buffers, so ignored failure can become committed zero-valued state. 'Simultaneously' does not establish failure atomicity."* *** THE INTERACTION WITH `#95' IS THE SHARP PART, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT THAT FIX HAS TURNED UP WITH AN UNCONSIDERED EDGE. *** `#95' zeroes the caller's buffer on a device READ so a partial fill cannot leak host memory -- unambiguously right. Here that same zeroing means **a failed load returns a well-formed zero instead of an error**, and the caller, which checks nothing, commits it to the PCB. A safety fix converting a detectable failure into a plausible value is worth knowing about generally. The comment above the assignments says *"Update all variables in the pcb simultaneously"* -- and as codex notes, simultaneity of ASSIGNMENT is not atomicity under FAILURE. That comment now has three separate things wrong with it across this row, [[alphaswpctxptbr]] and this one. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY ME -- two further concerns from the same trace are recorded with it and are also unverified: the helpers request translated accesses without `PHYSICAL', and `store_64bit_word' sign-extends the address where the matching loads and 32-bit stores do not. *** CLUSTER SCOPING, codex, 2026-09-08 (ev: regress/artifacts/alphatbinegsel/codex_verify_20260908.txt). SIX SEPARATE ROUNDS -- no merger has sufficient evidence. *** one fix design : propagate context-memory failures through a defined failed-switch outcome one oracle : an injected memory failure produces that outcome without reporting a successful switch **The ordering ruling matters more than the grouping:** codex put **`alphaswpctxreg` FIRST**, on the ground that it is the only one with verified behaviour AND a decisive witness (a returned register value), and it labelled that *"a confidence judgment, not a claim that it has the greatest potential severity"* -- which is the rung-versus-severity distinction the ladder already insists on, arrived at independently. *** AND IT REFUTED A GROUPING HYPOTHESIS I HAD FLOATED: "the claim that `alphapteprot` prevents all guest paging is not established by this review." *** I had suggested the page-walk row might be a prerequisite for testing the others; that is not supported, and scheduling on it would have been scheduling on an assumption. `alphafaultclaim` and `alphavmkill` may be reconsidered together only after proving they share a file, one fault-handling repair and one fault-delivery oracle -- *"correcting a comment and preventing termination do not establish that grouping."* *** codex ASSESS, 2026-09-08. THE CLAIM SPLITS ACROSS TWO LAYERS, AND ONLY ONE HALF IS THIS HANDLER'S FAULT. *** **THE STORE HALF IS TRUE.** `store_64bit_word` returns `int` -- it is `return cpu->memory_rw(...)` -- and `swpctx` discards that status at every save site. *** THE LOAD HALF IS NOT THIS HANDLER'S TO IGNORE. *** `load_64bit_word` returns `uint64_t` DATA and has **no failure indication at all**: it calls `memory_rw`, discards the result, byte-swaps, and returns the assembled word. **A caller cannot check what the helper does not report.** So "the load ignores every memory-access failure" mis-assigns responsibility -- the defect there is the helper's ABI, and `load_64bit_word` **erases** the failure information rather than the caller dropping it. **Neither helper passes `NO_EXCEPTIONS`** -- both use `CACHE_DATA`, so my Q2 premise was wrong. **The consequence codex states: failed translations can become committed zero-valued PCB state.** ## *** MY OPTION SET WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THE MISSING MEMBER IS THE RIGHT ONE *** I offered three dispositions: real defect with an observable consequence; fidelity gap with no channel; or not a defect at all. > *"Your three possibilities omit the present combination: **observable behavior is proved, but > architectural incorrectness is not yet proved.**"* *"This is not 'nothing to ignore': stores expose failure, and loads erase underlying failure information. It is also not 'no observable channel': PCB saveback and PTBR supply one. But changing behavior for invalid input requires establishing what that input permits or requires. **I would not invent a fault or transactional switch rule and use that invention as the oracle.**"* **Provisional severity: LOW, affecting guest state integrity; no host compromise, no unprivileged route.** If promoted, the claim must narrow to *reported failures being discarded or hidden*. *This is the option-set-completeness rule landing on me, on a brief where I thought I had enumerated exhaustively -- the same failure the three-membered de-fatalisation set records.* ## THE IN-TREE IDIOM -- and a SIBLING SITE WITH THE SAME DEFECT * **`wrfen` (`cpu_alpha_palcode.c`) ALSO discards `store_64bit_word`'s status.** So this is a small CLASS inside the PAL layer, not a single site. *Filed as part of this row rather than separately: same file, same helper, same fix design.* * **`debugger_cmds.c` DOES check it** -- assigns to `res` and tests `!res`, for both widths. **That establishes the status is meaningful**, which is what makes discarding it a defect rather than a convention. * **`cpu_alpha_instr_loadstore.c` checks direct `memory_rw` calls** and returns on failure before consuming read data or reporting store-conditional success -- *"the strongest nearby implementation idiom, though it is not a PAL context switch."* * **NO checking PAL context-switch sibling exists**, which is why the fix has no exact precedent. ## *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF [[alphafaultclaim]], UNASKED *** *"The latter's comment saying the translator already signalled a fault is also unsupported by the inspected Alpha failure path."* **Three separate briefs tonight -- alphatbinegsel Q3, alphapteprot, and this one -- have now reached that same conclusion from three different directions**, none of them asked about it. ## SCOPE: NO MERGER with [[alphaswpctxreg]], despite being lines apart row fix concern oracle concern --------------- ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------- alphaswpctxreg correct result-register assignment the switch's return value appears in the required register alphactxfail preserve access status and apply a a failed access produces the required VERIFIED failure policy state and control flow *"Either correction can exist while the other problem remains."* **Proximity is not the test** -- which is the round-scope rule stated exactly. **BLOCKED, like `alphapteprot`, on an Alpha architecture manual**: none of the sixteen PDFs in `_scratchpad/` is an Alpha reference, and the seat declined to certify fault, restartability or rollback semantics without one. **That is now THREE rows blocked on absent primary sources** (`armbfcdecode` on DDI 0406; `alphapteprot` and this one on an Alpha ARM).open

sgirespanchkdev_sgi_re.c: the TLB_A/B/C and LINEAR_A/B write loops bound only the FIRST element of a multi-element span -- a handler ROBUSTNESS gap, with the alignment that makes it unreachable VERIFIED in the CPU load/store path rather than assumeddev_sgi_re.c: the TLB_A/B/C and LINEAR_A/B write loops bound only the FIRST element of a multi-element span -- a handler ROBUSTNESS gap, with the alignment that makes it unreachable VERIFIED in the CPU load/store path rather than assumed — witness: none — note: FILED 2026-09-07, SPLIT OUT OF THE WITHDRAWN [[sgilinearnegidx]] ROW. **Kept separate on purpose: a withdrawn entry is the worst possible place to hide a live finding.** The same codex audit that REFUTED the negative-index claim (`tile_nr` is unsigned, so the `>= 32` guard rejects every negative x) continued in its verdict line: "There are missing checks on complete write SPANS in TLB_A/B/C and LINEAR_A/B, whose safety depends on caller alignment." **A SPAN CHECK IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM AN INDEX BOUND.** A bound of the form `if (i >= n) return;` answers *where does the access START*; it says nothing about where a multi-element access FINISHES. An index can be in range while the span running from it leaves the array. So the refutation of the negative-index chain does not touch this at all -- they are independent claims about the same arrays. *** STATUS: AN AUDIT VERDICT, NOT A VERIFIED FINDING, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF FILING IT THIS WAY. *** The verdict CONDITIONS the safety on caller alignment rather than asserting a defect -- the seat's own words are *"whose safety depends on"*, which is a statement about an unchecked assumption, not about a reachable bug. **An unchecked assumption that happens to hold is a different thing from a checked one**, and this row must not be promoted until somebody says which of the two it is. **OWED, and the third is the load-bearing one:** 1. the arrays with their declared element counts, and every multi-element access site; 2. where each span's WIDTH comes from -- a constant, or a register-derived value; 3. **whether any CALLER can present an unaligned or oversized span.** If every caller is bounded by construction this is a robustness note; if one is not, it is a defect. A read-only audit is out (`regress/artifacts/sgirespanchk/SPAN_brief.md`, fired at the codex seat 2026-09-07 under the C5 scoping rules -- reading scoped to `src/`, no chain, no reachability question). **The brief opens by telling the seat that my last brief stated a false premise about an index variable's TYPE and asks it to read the declarations**, which is the premise-audit instruction aimed at the exact error that produced this row's parent. *Provenance worth keeping: this finding was in the SAME verdict line as the refutation, and I nearly lost it -- the refutation was the arresting half and the span sentence sat after it. That is the under-harvest shape this session has already hit five times: take the finding, skip the rest of the sentence.* *** UPDATED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND IT IS A DOWNGRADE: THE SAME ANSWER ALREADY CONTAINED THE CALLER-ALIGNMENT CHECK I HAD JUST FIRED A SECOND BRIEF TO OBTAIN. MED -> LOW. *** **I filed this row from the verdict LINE and had not yet read the body.** The body enumerates the spans and then answers the question the verdict left open: | Each TLB write loop | 253 | 253, 254, 255, **256** | | Each TLB write loop | 254 | 254, 255, **256, 257** | | Each TLB write loop | 255 | 255, **256, 257, 258** | | Each LINEAR write pair | 31 | 31, **32** | "These are HANDLER ROBUSTNESS GAPS, not established guest out-of-bounds writes. For the normal SGI CPU access paths checked, eight-byte accesses have eight-byte alignment. Enumerating aligned addresses gives TLB starting indexes 0,4,...,252, and LINEAR starting indexes 0,2,...,30; their complete spans fit. I VERIFIED THE ALIGNMENT HANDLING IN THE ORDINARY ACCESS CODE AND UNALIGNED-ACCESS HELPER, RATHER THAN ACCEPTING THE DEVICE COMMENTS." -- `src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr_loadstore.c` and `src/cpus/cpu_mips_instr_unaligned.c`, both named. **THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE THIS ROW WAS FILED TO DEMAND, AND IT WAS ALREADY DISCHARGED.** The row asked whether the safety is a CHECKED property or an unchecked assumption that happens to hold. The seat checked it, in the right files, and said so in the words that distinguish the two. So: a robustness gap in the device handler, unreachable through the CPU paths that exist. **WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and it is narrow: the word "checked".** The seat verified the MIPS load/store and unaligned paths. It did NOT enumerate every route into `dev_sgi_re`'s access function -- a DMA engine, a device-to-device access, or the debugger's `put` reach a handler without going through a CPU load. A second read-only audit is already running (`SPAN_brief.md`) whose Q4 asks exactly this, and it was written and fired BEFORE this body was read, so its answer is independent rather than a re-confirmation. *** THIS IS THE FIFTH UNDER-HARVEST OF THE SESSION AND THE FIRST WHERE IT COST A WHOLE INVOCATION. *** The previous four dropped a seat's REFUTATION while keeping its finding. This one dropped the seat's own DISCHARGE of the obligation I then wrote into a row and spent a codex run re-asking. **The verdict line is a summary written against the brief's framing and is the LEAST likely part of an answer to carry the qualification** -- this file already says so about corrections, and it is equally true of discharges. *Also harvested from the same body, each a check I had not asked for: `de_reg[1024]` accessed at `[regnr]` and `[regnr+1]` reaches at most 512 (safe); the two static `rop_used[256]` arrays are masked `& 255`, which supplies BOTH bounds; `zerobuf[4096]` is length-capped then page-shortened, never enlarged; and `buf[8]` takes enumerated lengths 1/2/4/8 which fit -- with the seat noting unprompted that its INITIALISATION is a separate defect, which is [[sgirebufuninit]], already filed.* **AND ONE FINDING THAT IS NEW AND IS NOT A SPAN QUESTION:** *"the coordinate rectangle check does not by itself establish the TLB capacity bound."* At depth field 3 (`bufdepth` 8, tile width 64) the pre-guard `tile_nr` reaches **271**, not 255 -- the `x,y < 2048` rectangle admits indexes past the end of a `[256]` array, and it is the LATER `tile_nr >= 256` guard that rejects them. Both bounds are present so nothing is broken; what is worth recording is that **the two guards are not redundant, and an edit removing the second one as "already covered by the rectangle check" would open a 16-element overrun.** That is a clause-(d) shaped hazard sitting in code nobody is currently editing -- noted here, not filed.open

sgilinearnegidxpostmortemRULE QUESTION: a chain resting on an index or a bound should quote the DECLARATION of every variable in it -- raised by the withdrawal of a HIGH finding that was false because I never read a type three lines above the code I quotedRULE QUESTION: a chain resting on an index or a bound should quote the DECLARATION of every variable in it -- raised by the withdrawal of a HIGH finding that was false because I never read a type three lines above the code I quoted — witness: none — note: *** A RULE QUESTION FOR THE 2026-09-09 ADJUDICATION, RAISED BY THE FAILURE ITSELF. See [[sgilinearnegidx]], withdrawn at `a264a34`. *** **THE FAILURE, stated plainly:** I filed a HIGH finding, escalated it to *a guest-chosen physical write address*, wrote it into a commit message as a headline claim, and reported it as the session's most severe result. It was FALSE. `tile_nr` is declared `unsigned int` at `dev_sgi_re.c:207`, three lines above the code I quoted, so a negative `x >> 12` converts to ~4294967295 and the `>= 32` guard REJECTS it. *** WHAT MAKES IT A RULE QUESTION RATHER THAN A LAPSE: I APPLIED THE DISCIPLINE AND IT DID NOT REACH. *** I identified the link I doubted (whether `src_x` is masked in the linear path), verified it by grep, and ran an `offsetof` rather than trust hand arithmetic about the struct layout. **All three were aimed at links I had already decided to question.** The defeating fact sat in a declaration I never thought to read -- in a range I had printed to my own screen earlier in the same session, while looking for something else. **THREE QUESTIONS, in the order I think they matter:** 1. **Does the premise-audit instruction need a SELF-DIRECTED TWIN?** It tells SEATS not to ratify my premises, and it works -- the carrier records it finding four wrong premises in one brief. Nothing tells ME to enumerate the premises I never questioned, and that set is exactly where this lived. **A premise you did not notice you were making is not audited by an instruction aimed at your reader.** I think this is the more valuable of the two candidate remedies. 2. **Is the narrow mechanical rule worth a template line?** *"A chain resting on an index or a bound quotes the DECLARATION of every variable in it."* It is cheap, it is mechanical, it would have caught this in one line -- and it is minted from ONE instance, which this project's own freshly-minted-exemplar rule says makes its shape a hypothesis rather than a class. **Restricting it to chains whose conclusion is a BOUND or an INDEX keeps the population small and recognisable**, which is the form I would propose. 3. **What does this say about C5?** The chain-shaped brief asking for this exact chain to be attacked was REFUSED. The same seat, asked the same subject WITHOUT the chain, put the refutation in its verdict line. **So the refusal did not stop a bad question -- it delayed a correct answer by hours, and in that interval I escalated a false finding and committed it.** That is new evidence [[codexbriefscoping]] did not have when it was filed: does it change that row's disposition, and does it warrant splitting every chain into LINK QUESTIONS by default rather than as a fallback? **WHAT I AM NOT ASKING, because it would be the wrong lesson:** whether packet-fed seats are unreliable. glm raised the asymmetry and was right that two guards disagree; what it could not do -- exactly as the doctrine says -- is check a DECLARATION, because a type is a repo fact. **The doctrine's warning is about crediting such a seat with repo fact, and that is precisely the error I made on its behalf.** The doctrine came out of this correct; I did not. *Queued in `fable_queue.md` section 6 with the other four rule questions, written out in full so the adjudication can begin without reconstructing any of them.*open

sgirgbscanoutrow#505's arm-attribution warrant is a claim about dev_sgi_gbe.c's scanout that NO row observes -- the detector runs the drawing engine only and has no framebuffer oracle#505's arm-attribution warrant is a claim about dev_sgi_gbe.c's scanout that NO row observes -- the detector runs the drawing engine only and has no framebuffer oracle — witness: none — note: FILED 2026-09-07 by `#505`'s own PRE-TABLE CLAIM->ROW check, which is what that check exists to produce. `#505` chose the GET arm as the defective one on a warrant from a DIFFERENT DEVICE: `dev_sgi_gbe.c`'s scanout composes a 32-bit tile pixel as `(buf[0]<<24)+(buf[1]<<16)+(buf[2]<<8)+buf[3]` and then `CRMFB_MODE_TYP_RGB8` takes R,G,B from bits 31..24 / 23..16 / 15..8 -- so byte 0 is R and byte 3 is unused. **That is the strongest evidence in the round and NO ROW OBSERVES IT.** The detector drives the drawing engine and reads the destination word back through the guest. It never reaches scanout, so it cannot tell a tree where DE and GBE AGREE on the container from one where they have both been changed consistently and wrongly. **WHAT A ROW WOULD NEED:** drive a DE draw in RGB mode, then make GBE scan the same tile out and compare framebuffer bytes -- i.e. an oracle on `dev_fb_access` output rather than on a guest load. That is a different probe SHAPE, not another row in this one, which is why it is filed rather than added: the round's own detector is above the floor without it. *Recorded as an explicit no-row sentence rather than omitted, because the CLAIM->ROW check's rule is that an added comment asserting an observable consequence owes a row OR an explicit statement that it has none -- and an unrun check and an inapplicable one must not render the same.*open

sgirebufshiftubdev_sgi_re.c: FOUR of the five GET arms compute `buf[i] << 24` on a uint8_t, which promotes to signed int -- for any byte >= 128 that is a signed left-shift overflow, i.e. UB, on all four armsdev_sgi_re.c: FOUR of the five GET arms compute `buf[i] << 24` on a uint8_t, which promotes to signed int -- for any byte >= 128 that is a signed left-shift overflow, i.e. UB, on all four arms — witness: harness:regress/artifacts/sgirebufshiftub/ubsan_emulator_20260907.txt -- MEASURED 2026-09-07 under build-asan's -fsanitize=undefined, driving the shipped 10-row #505 probe through a stderr-capturing wrapper; positive AND negative controls in-band (ubsan_control_20260907.sh). 8 diagnostics, all left-shift. — note: FILED 2026-09-07 by the **grok seat** under the found-something-else licence, on `#505`'s pass-1 panel (`_scratchpad/panel_20260907_051055`). Verified by reading before filing. uint8_t buf[8]; ... *color = (buf[0] << 24) + (buf[1] << 16) + (buf[2] << 8); `buf[i]` is `uint8_t`, which the usual arithmetic conversions promote to **signed `int`** -- not to `unsigned int`, because `int` can represent every `uint8_t` value. So `buf[0] << 24` for any byte >= 128 shifts a 1 into or past the sign bit of a 32-bit `int`: 0xaa = 170; 170 << 24 = 2,852,126,720 > INT_MAX (2,147,483,647) which is **undefined behaviour** in C99 6.5.7p4 (E1 << E2 where E1 is signed and the result is not representable). In practice gcc/clang produce the wrapped value everyone expects, which is exactly why it has survived -- but `-fsanitize=undefined` reports it, and this tree HAS a UBSan sweep (`gate_asan_sweep.sh`). **IT IS PRE-EXISTING AND IT IS ON ALL FOUR ARMS**, not on the one `#505` edited: the RGB, RGBA, ABGR and default GET arms all use the same `buf[i] << 24` idiom, and the shipped pre-`#505` RGB arm used `buf[1] << 24` identically. `#505` replaced one instance of the idiom with another instance of the same idiom, which is the correct minimal-surgical choice: fixing the cast on ONE line would leave the file internally inconsistent for no measured gain. **DISPOSITION: FILED, not fixed in-round, and the seat that raised it agrees** -- *"Pre-existing on every GET arm, not unique to RGB, not a reason to block."* The stopping rule licenses an in-round fix only for a MEASURED FALSE PASS or a WRONG RECORD, and this is neither. **THE FIX WHEN IT COMES IS ONE CAST PER TERM** -- `((uint32_t)buf[0] << 24)` -- across all four arms in one diff, which is the class-closure form rather than a cell at a time. **OWED FIRST: whether the UBSan sweep already reaches this function**, since if it does, the absence of a report is itself a finding about the sweep rather than about the code. *Note the shape: a seat asked about byte ORDER volunteered a defect about integer PROMOTION in the same expression. The found-something-else licence is where three of this session's filed rows came from.* *** THE SAME DEFECT WAS RAISED AGAIN BY THE CODEX SEAT ON THE `sgirebufuninit` PANEL, 2026-09-07, AND I FILED IT AS A SECOND ROW (`sgishift24ub`) WITHOUT CHECKING THIS ONE. *** The duplicate is merged here and deleted. **grok had it first, on `#505` pass 1, under the found-something-else licence** -- so this is the unread-review class one more time: the finding was already in the ledger, and the round that re-derived it paid for it twice. **WHAT THE SECOND RAISING ADDS, and it changes the disposition:** a CENSUS of the idiom, which neither raising had. Keyed on whether the shifted element carries a cast, over `src/devices`, `src/cpus`, `src/core`: <ident>[..] << 24 111 total CAST 25 e.g. cpu_alpha_instr_loadstore.c, `((uint64_t)data[3] << 24)` BARE 86 in 22 files dev_px.c 20 tmp_arm_rc.c 15 dev_sgi_re.c 4 (a 5th grep hit is a comment, not code) > **THE BARE FORM IS THE HOUSE IDIOM BY 86 TO 25, AND IT IS UPSTREAM'S** -- it sits in the CPU > instruction decoders, and `cpu_mips_instr.c` carries both forms forty lines apart. So > `dev_sgi_re.c` is NOT an outlier, and repairing four sites in one device would be arbitrary. > **The sibling-disposition check answers AGAINST a local fix**, exactly as it did for > `sgireunmapped`. **AND THE ROUND THIS DESERVES IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN EDIT.** `build-asan/src/devices/Makefile:9` already carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, and UBSan's shift check is in that set by default. So *does it fire, on a path a gate already walks?* is answerable with a tool in the tree and no source change at all. If it fires, the finding is 86 sites and a tree-wide policy question for the owner (`-fwrapv`? cast the idiom? accept and document?). If it does not fire, find out why before believing either answer. *Verified before recording: `src/devices/Makefile:9` is `-fstrict-aliasing -fomit-frame-pointer -fpeephole -fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG` -- **no `-fwrapv`, no `-fno-strict-overflow`** -- so the build gives the idiom no cover, and `#505`'s probe drives `0xaa` through it on every run.* *Deriver, because my first TWO censuses were wrong -- one keyed on variable NAMES (a correlate, which silently counted already-cast sites) and one whose bare-form count returned **0 while its own sample output showed bare forms three lines below**:* T=$(grep -rhoE '[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\[[^]]*\] *<< *24' src/devices/*.c src/cpus/*.c src/core/*.c | wc -l) C=$(grep -rhoE '\)[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*\[[^]]*\] *<< *24' src/devices/*.c src/cpus/*.c src/core/*.c | wc -l) echo "total $T cast $C bare $((T-C))" *** OWNER DECISION 2026-09-07, asked with the four options on the table: MEASURE WITH UBSan FIRST, THEN DECIDE. The alternatives -- add `-fwrapv`, cast all 86 sites, or accept-and-document -- were all declined PENDING the measurement. *** **STEP 1, THE POSITIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS THE PART THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT MEAN ANYTHING.** A silent run is ambiguous between *the code does not do this* and *this toolchain does not check this* -- the pattern-that-matches-nothing shape, which this project has met five times. So the idiom was compiled STANDALONE with `build-asan`'s own flags, read out of its generated Makefile rather than retyped: -fstrict-aliasing -fomit-frame-pointer -fpeephole -fgnu89-inline -O3 -DNDEBUG -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g The control takes its byte from `argv` so `-O3` cannot constant-fold the shift away. Measured, both directions: byte 0xaa ctl.c:13:18: runtime error: left shift of 170 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int' <- REPORTS byte 0x02 stderr 0 lines <- SILENT > **SO THE CHECK IS PRESENT AND DISCRIMINATING IN THIS TOOLCHAIN, and a silent real run now MEANS > the path did not execute the UB.** Without this control it would have meant nothing, and the > honest disposition would have been *uninterpretable* rather than *not reached*. *Note what the control also settles: the UB is REAL rather than theoretical -- gcc's own sanitizer calls it out by name at `-O3` with the fork's exact flags. What remains open is REACHABILITY, which is exactly the axis the row said bounds the severity.* **STEP 2 is the shipped 10-row `#505` probe run against `build-asan/gxemul`** -- it drives `0xaabbccdd`, so `buf[0] = 0xaa`, the very value the control reports on. Both build-tree clearance parts are checked before the run and it REFUSES to measure a stale or divergent ASAN tree. Output preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgirebufshiftub/ubsan_real_20260907.txt` -- a durable path, because a number this row will cite must not live in `/tmp`. *** TAKE 1 OF THE REAL RUN RETURNED **ZERO** AND THE ZERO WAS AN APPARATUS ARTEFACT. I had the control that makes a zero interpretable and then measured the WRONG STREAM. *** probe result SGIRGB_RESULT=10/10 under the ASAN binary 'runtime error' lines 0 preserved file 1310 bytes -- ten probe rows and nothing else **The probe spawns `gxemul` inside a PTY.** UBSan writes to the EMULATOR's stderr, which never enters the probe's own stdout or stderr -- so what I captured could not have contained a diagnostic whether or not one was emitted. The 1310-byte file is the tell: an emulator run that had produced any console output at all would be larger. > **THE ZERO MEANT 'NO UBSAN OUTPUT ARRIVED HERE', NOT 'NO UB EXECUTED'.** And it is worse than an > ordinary miss, because the CONTROL had just certified that a zero would be meaningful -- the > control certified the CHECK and said nothing about the PLUMBING, and I read its certificate as > covering both. *This is the carrier's own 'check that the apparatus selected something before reading what it says' rule, met from a new direction: the apparatus selected the right FILES and the wrong STREAM. It also very nearly produced the most expensive kind of wrong record here -- a MEASURED-LOOKING NEGATIVE, which would have closed the row as 'not reached' with a preserved artifact and a control behind it.* **TAKE 2 uses `UBSAN_OPTIONS=log_path=...`**, which writes diagnostics to `<path>.<pid>` files regardless of how the child's console is plumbed -- and it carries an **IN-BAND POSITIVE CONTROL**: the known-UB binary is run through the SAME `log_path` mechanism first, and the script REFUSES to interpret the emulator run if that control produces no log file. *A measurement whose negative result cannot be distinguished from a broken apparatus is not a measurement*, and take 1 is the proof. *** MEASURED: IT FIRES. Owner decision was measure-then-decide; this is the measurement. *** Take 3 drove the shipped ten-row `#505` probe against `build-asan/gxemul` through a wrapper that appends the emulator's stderr to a file. The probe itself scored **10/10** -- the emulator behaves correctly -- and the run emitted **EIGHT** UBSan diagnostics, every one a left shift: 5 dev_sgi_re.c:350:21 left shift of 170 by 24 places cannot be represented in type 'int' 1 dev_sgi_re.c:353:21 left shift of 170 by 24 places 2 dev_sgi_re.c:221:41 left shift of 32770 by 16 places `:350` is **the line `#505` ships**. `170` is `0xaa`, the probe's own first byte. *** THE `:221` SITE WAS NOT IN MY CENSUS AT ALL, AND IT IS THE WORSE ONE. *** `32770` is `0x8002`. `:221-225` are `tileptr = d->re_tlb_{a,b,c}[tile_nr] << 16;` over `uint16_t[256]` arrays -- and **bit 15 of a tile pointer is the VALID bit**. So it is not that a large value occasionally appears: **every VALID tile pointer has bit 15 set, so every tiled access through this path is UB by construction.** The RGB sites need a red channel >= 0x80; this one needs only a tile that is marked present. *** AND MY CENSUS WAS WIDTH-BLIND, WHICH IS WHY I MISSED IT. *** I keyed on `<< 24` because that is where a `uint8_t` overflows. **The threshold moves with the shift**: a shift of N bits overflows `int` once the value reaches `2^(31-N)`, so uint8_t << 24 UB at >= 0x80 <- what I censused uint16_t << 16 UB at >= 0x8000 <- the same defect, invisible to that census uint8_t << 16 max 0xff0000 <- SAFE, cannot overflow uint8_t << 8 max 0xff00 <- SAFE **So the class is defined by (operand's reachable maximum) x (shift width), not by the shift width alone** -- the deriver rule again, and the third time today a census of mine keyed on a correlate. Re-derived counts, bare (uncast) occurrences across `src/devices`, `src/cpus`, `src/core`: << 8 total 207 cast 8 bare 199 (mostly SAFE -- a byte cannot reach 0x800000) << 16 total 154 cast 8 bare 146 (UB wherever the operand is 16-bit and can set b15) << 24 total 126 cast 25 bare 101 *The `<< 8` population is large and mostly harmless, which is exactly why a raw shift-count census is the wrong instrument: it over-counts the safe family and under-counts the dangerous one.* > **SEVERITY SET TO `med`, and the axis is CONSEQUENCE rather than reachability.** Reachability is > total -- it fires on an ordinary probe run and, at `:221`, on every tiled access. What holds it > below `high` is that gcc emits the obvious shift at `-O3` today and no miscompilation has been > observed; the harm is a standards violation the optimiser is entitled to exploit, not a measured > wrong answer. **That is a judgement about a compiler's future, which is exactly the kind of thing > this project says to hand to the adjudication rather than settle in a round.** **THE DISPOSITION IS NOW THE OWNER'S, WITH DATA.** The three options the measurement was gating: `-fwrapv` (one flag, defines all of them, changes codegen tree-wide and therefore every gate oracle measured afterwards); cast the idiom (correct, matches the 25+8 sites that already do it, but a large diff across upstream CPU decoders); or accept-and-document (cheapest, and now harder to justify at `:221` than it was an hour ago). *Apparatus note, because the number is only worth what the plumbing is worth: takes 1 and 2 both returned a false or refused zero -- take 1 measured the probe's streams rather than the emulator's, take 2 tried `log_path`, which GCC's libubsan silently ignores (measured: zero files, diagnostic still on stderr). The in-band control refused take 2 rather than letting it report. Take 3's control fires on `0xaa` and is silent on `0x02`, so the eight is discriminating in both directions.* *** THE TITLE SAID "every GET arm" AND THAT IS FALSE. Corrected 2026-09-07 after the `#509` pass-2 codex seat caught it while checking a DIFFERENT claim. *** Read across all five arms: CI :323 *color = buf[0]; NO SHIFT AT ALL RGB :350 *color = (buf[0] << 24) + ... shifts buf[0] RGBA :353 *color = (buf[0] << 24) + ... shifts buf[0] ABGR :356 *color = (buf[3] << 24) + ... shifts buf[3], not buf[0] dflt :359 *color = (buf[3] << 24) + ... shifts buf[3], not buf[0] So the UB population is **four arms, two of them shifting a different byte**, and the CI arm is not a member. *The defect is unchanged in substance and the enumeration was wrong in two directions at once -- it over-counted CI and mis-named the byte for ABGR and the default arm.*open
