Ranking is what the carrier says orders the queue -- *rung is a floor on admissibility, never a priority; SEVERITY and gate blind-spots order the queue* -- so an unranked witnessed row is invisible to the only ordering rule this project has. *** THE FIX IS NOT A REGEX, AND I NEARLY SHIPPED ONE. *** A keyword scan over titles buckets 7 rows under host-kill language, 5 under memory-safety and 17 under wrong-data. **Those buckets are CORRELATES.** What makes a row HIGH here is *a guest can reach it and something bad happens*, and no keyword tests reachability -- which is the deriver rule (*key on what DEFINES the class, not on a correlate of it*) applied to my own triage script. The scan is kept only as a READING ORDER. **Candidates the scan surfaced, recorded as UNVERIFIED reading order and explicitly NOT as gradings:** `gdromcondavail` (COND_DATA_AVAIL permanently lies after an overread), `asicindexcase` (a deleted guard that was also a bounds check), `gdrompiooddlen` (guards one byte, reads two), `asickillsurvive` (four kill rows survive-only, so an OOB read is unobserved), `gdromdmawidth` (a tail store ignoring `len`), `sh4pcic15` (an interrupt line that can never be delivered), `asicpermute` (an index permutation). **Each needs its reachability read before any `sev` is written.** > **DISPOSITION: a RATING pass, evidence-first, one row at a time, with the reachability sentence > quoted from the source.** It is read-only, so it parallelises freely and belongs to the file-reading > seats -- the exact work the standing directive says to give codex. It is NOT a round: nothing is > edited, and the deliverable is `sev` plus a one-line warrant per row. *Related but distinct from [[baretitle]], which counts rows with an EMPTY NOTE. A row can be richly documented and still unranked -- most of these 73 are.* *** MY '73 WITNESSED' FIGURE IS WRONG, AND IT IS THE CORRELATE TRAP FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY. *** codex: *"**37 of those 73 have witness strings beginning `none`** -- sometimes followed by historical measurements, sometimes explicitly denying reachability. **The snippet counts strings, not demonstrated witnesses.**"* My test was `r.get('witness') and r.get('witness') != 'none'` -- which passes any string that merely STARTS with `none`, and this ledger's convention is to write `none -- <why>` with the reasoning attached. **So the honest figure is about 36 witnessed-and-unrated rows, not 73.** *The paragraph above this one warns against keying on a correlate, and the snippet printed immediately below it does exactly that. Re-derive with a prefix test, and note that `none -- ...` rows are often the BEST documented ones, since a denial of reachability takes more evidence than an assertion of it.* *** A PATTERN IN MY OWN METHOD, WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS NOW FOUR FOR FOUR TODAY: EVERY CENSUS I RAN KEYED ON ONE SPELLING AND MISSED A VARIANT. *** severity the ledger's field is `sev` -> 0 of 260 rows matched witness != 'none' the convention is `none -- <why>` -> 37 of 73 miscounted as witnessed << 24 uint16_t << 16 is the same defect -> the structural site missed entirely (int)idata the tree also writes `(int) idata` -> 226 where the answer is 309 **Each was found by someone else running a different derivation, never by me re-reading mine.** The carrier's rule says *when two derivers disagree, neither is trustworthy until you look at what each MATCHED* -- but all four of these had only ONE deriver, so there was nothing to disagree with, and a single method produces a confident number with no signal attached. > **THE PRACTICE THAT FOLLOWS: a census that will be written into a durable record runs TWO > derivations with different keys, and prints BOTH.** Agreement is weak evidence (they can share a > blindness -- `sgirekills` measured that) but DISAGREEMENT is a free, immediate signal, and it is > the only one available before a seat reads the work. *** AND THE CLOSURE PASS CAUGHT A FIFTH COUNT ERROR OF MINE, IN THE BRIEF THAT ANNOUNCED THE OTHER FOUR. *** I stated "note/witness cites a `#NNN` round: **40**". codex: *"I cannot reproduce 40 from the stated fields. `#\s*\d+` over top-level `note` and `witness` selects **51**; including `state_note` produces **98 at HEAD / 104 in the working ledger**. **The field selection needs to accompany that count.**"* My KEY2 ran over `witness` plus `state_note[:400]` -- a truncation I never wrote down. **It also caught that my census MIXED SNAPSHOTS:** HEAD has 184 open/in-work rows, the working (uncommitted) ledger has 190. Both contain the same fourteen commit-bearing candidates, so the KEY1 result stands -- but a count taken from a dirty tree and compared against HEAD is two populations wearing one number. *The two-deriver practice adopted this morning would not have caught either: both are failures to state the DOMAIN, not to vary the key. **A count owes its field selection and its snapshot, not just its command.*** *** ADDENDUM 2026-09-07: THE GAP IS NOT A CLOSED LEGACY BLOCK, SO THE ORDER OF THE FIX MATTERS. *** Re-derived from the other direction while filing a DUPLICATE of this row ([[ledgersevmissing]], now withdrawn -- see it for the process lesson). Counting rows that lack the `sev` KEY outright, rather than rows that are unrated: total ledger rows 411 lacking a `sev` key entirely 261 of those, open or in work 78 by state: open 65, in work 13, held 72, closed 93, dropped 18 **The set spans the whole history, not just the early rounds.** It contains `d1`, `a4`, `n1`..`n6` from the first rounds -- and also `wdcdataoutdrain`, `gdromlatchcross`, `divratchetband` and others opened within the last fortnight. So rows are STILL being created without the field. > **CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S DISPOSITION: the writer-side check lands BEFORE the rating pass, not > after it.** A backfill alone fixes the past and not the cause, and the queue refills behind it. > The check is the `check_cited_artifacts` idiom -- forward-only from a cutoff, so a NEW row without > a rating fails and the existing ones warn. That ordering is the only thing the duplicate > contributed, and it is why it was folded here instead of being left as a second row. *Also observed while sorting: a row with no `sev` is not sorted LAST -- depending on the tool it is omitted entirely or it raises KeyError and kills the sort. Both happened. That is worse than a low ranking, because nothing reports that the row was skipped.* *** THREE SUBSTANTIVE codex ANSWERS SAT ON DISK FOR THIS ROW WITH **ZERO** LEDGER ENTRIES, AND ONE OF THEM CONTAINED A LIVE DEFECT NOBODY HAD SEEN. Recorded 2026-09-07. *** The three (`codex_shiftub`, `codex_bitsbytes`, `codex_helpers`, all dated 2026-09-07) were verified by CONTENT and TAIL -- real answers, no wall text, no echo -- and cited nowhere. **`codex_bitsbytes` named the `(1 << width) - 1` idiom in the ARM bit-field handlers. Its UBFX/SBFX citations were STALE (repaired by `#510` before it ran), but following the finding into the file found the THIRD site, `X(bfi)`, still live with a WIDER undefined domain than either the round had fixed** -- now filed as `armbfiwidth`. > **A STALE FINDING THAT LEADS TO A LIVE ONE IS NOT A WRONG ANSWER.** It is the sibling grep the > round should have run itself, arriving a day late from a seat. The carrier's mechanical rule 2 > -- *when correcting a claim, grep for its siblings before calling it fixed* -- is the rule `#510` > missed, and it is recorded there with a prior instance of exactly this shape. *And the same batch corrected my own arithmetic in a way I then confirmed by brute force: 496 nonpositive widths of 1024 pairs, not the figure I had supplied.* *** RE-DERIVED 2026-09-07, AND THE ROW'S OWN NUMBERS WERE WRONG -- WHICH IS THE DEFECT THIS ROW IS ABOUT, COMMITTED BY THIS ROW. *** claimed in the title measured 2026-09-07 47% unrated 34% (65 of 189 open rows) 73 unrated + witnessed 16 **AND MY FIRST RE-MEASUREMENT WAS ALSO WRONG, IN THE WAY I HAD DOCUMENTED AN HOUR EARLIER.** I filtered `witness not in ('none', '')` and got **59** -- because the field holds prose like `none yet -- GUEST-REACHABLE and witnessable` and `n/a -- a harness gap`, which are not equal to `none` and are not witnesses either. **That is the deriver rule's own failure: I keyed on a correlate (the string differs from a sentinel) instead of on what DEFINES the class (the field matches the enforced schema).** Keyed on `check_witness.py`'s own regex -- `^(boot:|probe:| construction:|harness:|detector:)` -- the answer is **16**. *Three counting methods, three answers (73, 59, 16), and only the one keyed to the enforced schema is defensible. The tell was the same one this project keeps recording: when derivers disagree, look at what each MATCHED rather than choosing a number.* ### *** THE CHARACTERISATION IS THE USEFUL PART, AND IT ANSWERS THE PRIORITISATION WORRY. *** Of the 16 unrated-and-witnessed rows, **14 carry `harness:` witnesses**, one `boot:` and one `detector:`. **The unrated backlog is overwhelmingly TOOLING DEBT.** So the rating gap is not concealing critical emulator defects -- which is what the row's alarming headline implied and what a reader would reasonably fear. **All 16 were rated on 2026-09-07 by the MAIN LOOP** (2 of them raised on the day's own evidence; see `panelcite0824`). The remaining 49 unrated open rows carry NO witness of any kind, so they are correctly ranked below every witnessed row regardless of what severity they would eventually get -- *a witness makes an item ELIGIBLE; severity orders what is already eligible.*open

cxseatchecktools/cxlaunch.sh: a codex seat check that could report a REFUSED seat as a clean run, and a wall-grep over stderr that matched the project's own ledger texttools/cxlaunch.sh: a codex seat check that could report a REFUSED seat as a clean run, and a wall-grep over stderr that matched the project's own ledger text — witness: harness:controlled in four states on the day it landed -- refusal, echoed-source false positive, real wall, healthy answer; all four give the wanted disposition. — note: Built 2026-09-07 after the `lcaconfwidth` census was REFUSED by codex's content filter and my launcher reported it as a completed run. **Three defects, all mine, all found within an hour of each other, and all of one family: a check that answers the same whether or not the thing it tests is true.** 1. **The refusal check read the wrong stream.** A content-filter refusal writes NOTHING to stdout and puts `ERROR: This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk.` on STDERR. The check grepped stdout and printed `refusal hits: 0` on a refusal that had already destroyed 108,432 tokens of completed work. 2. **The script exited 0 while holding `rc=1`.** It captured codex's status, printed it, and ended on a successful command, so the harness reported the task COMPLETED. Failure laundered into a clean completion -- the fourth instance of that class recorded here. 3. **The FIX introduced a third defect, measured on its first real run.** Grepping stderr freely for wall text reported `wall: 3` on a HEALTHY seat, because **codex streams the source it reads into stderr** -- and all three hits were this project's own ledger prose about seat walls, one of them the line *"whose quotation of the pattern MATCHES"*. That is the carrier's quoting-a-machine-read-marker rule, landing on a tool written by someone who had just read it. > **THE DISCRIMINATOR: codex's OWN diagnostics are `ERROR:` at line start; everything else on stderr > is echoed content.** Anchor stderr tests on `^ERROR:`; grep stdout freely. Exit 7 refusal, 8 > wall, 6 empty-with-neither, else `rc`. **Controlled in four states**, and (b) is the one that matters: a stderr line containing *usage limit* inside echoed source must NOT trip the wall check. a ERROR: flagged... -> REFUSED (want REFUSED) b echoed source w/ 'usage limit', good stdout -> answered (want answered) c ERROR: usage limit -> WALLED (want WALLED) d ordinary reasoning, good stdout -> answered (want answered) *** THE CLAIM I ORIGINALLY CLOSED THIS ROW WITH WAS FALSE, AND I MADE IT IN A ROW ABOUT CHECKS THAT DO NOT CHECK. Corrected within the hour, by reading `panel.sh` instead of assuming. *** I wrote that *"`panel.sh` fires the same seat with its own check and has NOT been given this discriminator."* **It has had one longer than mine, and a better one.** Its `check()` anchors error sentinels to the **first 400 bytes** and its wall test to the **last 400 bytes**, with the reason in its own comment: *"a review that merely quotes 'was retired' or 'usage:' gets mis-flagged (it did, on the first live run)."* **So the tree already held the lesson and I re-learned it by breaking it.** The two discriminators differ and both are sound: panel.sh POSITION -- head/tail 400 bytes. Transport-agnostic; works for any seat whose own status lands at the edges of the file, which is all of them. cxlaunch.sh FORMAT -- codex's `^ERROR:` lines. Sharper for codex, useless for the others. *The honest ordering: `panel.sh`'s is the general one and mine is a codex-specific refinement. A future consolidation should take POSITION as the base test and add FORMAT where a seat's own error prefix is known -- not the other way round.* *Kept open for that consolidation, not for the phantom gap I invented.* *** A SECOND SHAPE OF THE SAME CLASS, MEASURED ON MYSELF 2026-09-08: THE HARNESS REPORTED "completed (exit code 0)" FOR A codex RUN THAT NEVER STARTED. *** A background launch used a RELATIVE artifacts path. The background shell's cwd was not `GXEMUL-SEC`, so both halves failed: cat: regress/artifacts/alphatbinegsel/Q3_brief.md: No such file or directory bash: regress/artifacts/alphatbinegsel/codex_q3_20260908.txt: No such file or directory EXIT=1 and the task notification said **completed (exit code 0)** -- the WRAPPER's status, not the command's. `codex` was never invoked; no `.txt` and no `.err` were created at all. **The tell is the carrier's own three-state rule, and it is the state people forget:** log MISSING = never started; log 0 bytes = started, mid-run or dead; log growing = alive. A REFUSED codex run leaves a 0-byte `.txt` AND a large `.err`. **This left neither** -- which is how it is distinguished from a refusal, and why a check that only looks for the refusal text would have called it a clean run. Two things follow, and the second is the cheap one: * **an explicit `echo "EXIT=$?"` after a backgrounded seat launch is what caught it.** Without it the missing answer would have looked like a refusal or a wall. * **use ABSOLUTE paths for every seat launch.** The carrier already says the session cwd DRIFTS and mandates absolute paths for `panel.sh`; the same applies to any hand-rolled seat invocation, and a BACKGROUND shell does not reliably inherit the foreground `cd` at all.open

alphaclrfenPAL_clrfen (0xae) is named and user-mode-whitelisted but has NO case, so a guest call reaches the default arm and stops the CPUPAL_clrfen (0xae) is named and user-mode-whitelisted but has NO case, so a guest call reaches the default arm and stops the CPU — witness: none — note: Volunteered by the grok seat under the found-something-else licence while enumerating every `apcb_flags` reader for [[alphaswpctxptbr]]'s fix review, 2026-09-07. `PAL_clrfen` is *named* in the palcode file and appears in the user-mode whitelist, but the dispatch switch has **no `case` for it** -- so a guest that calls it falls to the default arm, which sets `cpu->running = 0` and stops the machine. **NOT verified by me** -- recorded as the seat reported it, and a round on this owes the reading first. It is the same shape as [[alphaswpctxptbr]] (a PAL entry that does not do what its name says) and plausibly the same family as the option-set work: an unimplemented PAL call is member 7 territory (IMPLEMENT) rather than a decline, because declining a context-flag operation leaves the machine in a state the guest cannot reason about.open

mtesrcdupdo_mte_transfer computes the same source-TLB expression twice under two names (`src` and `src_tlb`)do_mte_transfer computes the same source-TLB expression twice under two names (`src` and `src_tlb`) — witness: none — note: Noticed 2026-09-07 while verifying that `sgi_mte_fill_probe.py`'s mode clears the pre-switch guards. :1312 int src = (mode & MTE_MODE_SRC_BUF_MASK) >> MTE_SRC_TLB_SHIFT; :1333 int src_tlb = (mode & MTE_MODE_SRC_BUF_MASK) >> MTE_SRC_TLB_SHIFT; **Byte-identical expressions.** `src` guards `:1336 if (src > MTE_TLB_C)`; `src_tlb` builds `src_mode` at `:1365`. They cannot disagree today, so this is **not a defect** -- recorded because the two-names-for-one-value shape is exactly what `#508` found in `memory_alpha.c` (`ALPHA_PAGESHIFT` and a local `pageSizeShift` both meaning 13), where the hazard is that a later edit changes one and not the other. *The read that found it was checking something else: `:1336` tests `src`, not the `src_tlb` computed one line above, which LOOKS like a variable mix-up until you find the earlier declaration. That momentary alarm is the actual cost of the duplication.* Documented-only unless a round is already editing that function.open

gateworktreeprecommit_check.sh validates the WORKING TREE, not the staged content, so it cannot see a staging omissionprecommit_check.sh validates the WORKING TREE, not the staged content, so it cannot see a staging omission — witness: none — note: MEASURED on my own commit, 2026-09-07. `2956c7e` committed regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py and NOT the check_probe_wiring.py MANIFEST entry that classifies it, so a fresh clone at that SHA reds with `UNCLASSIFIED'. **precommit_check.sh reported PRECOMMIT_PASS 0 hard immediately before that commit**, because the working tree already carried the manifest edit -- it was simply never staged. git show HEAD:tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py | grep -c sgi_mte_fill_probe.py -> 0 grep -c sgi_mte_fill_probe.py tools/pipeline/check_probe_wiring.py -> 1 > **A CHECK THAT VALIDATES A STATE OTHER THAN THE ONE THAT SHIPS CANNOT SEE A STAGING OMISSION.** This is NOT the check-that-cannot-fail shape -- the gate failed eleven times tonight and every failure was real. Its SUBJECT is one step to the left of the thing it guards. *** IT INTERACTS WITH A POLICY THIS PROJECT ALREADY HOLDS, which is why it is a row and not a note. *** The carrier forbids `git add -A' and directory adds, so every commit here stages by EXPLICIT PATH. That is strictly safer against INCLUDING the wrong file -- the failure the rule was written for -- and strictly MORE EXPOSED to OMITTING the right one. **Two rules pulling opposite ways, and only one of them has a checker.** The same commit also missed its own pass-2 receipt (caught by section F) and the ledger row naming it (section L), both on the NEXT commit. So the gate's coverage is real; what it cannot do is bind that coverage to the staged set. **THE OBVIOUS FIX IS REJECTED ON ITS OWN RISK:** running the gate under `git stash --keep-index' would let a mid-run crash lose uncommitted work, and the gate takes ~2 minutes. That is worse than the defect. **The narrower candidate** is an existence check over the STAGED set for known file PAIRS -- a new `regress/*.py' and its MANIFEST entry; a `src/' change and a CHANGELOG round block -- in the check_cited_artifacts.py idiom (existence-only, forward-only from a cutoff). NOT BUILT: it changes what every commit must satisfy, which is an owner decision, and owes two negative controls -- red on a probe staged without its manifest entry, green when both are staged. *** CONFIRMED BY codex AND WIDER THAN I FILED IT. THE GATE SELECTS FILES FROM THE INDEX AND THEN READS THEIR CONTENTS FROM THE WORKING TREE. *** CHANGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only) <- NAMES, from the index cmp -s "$SEC/$f" "$EST/$f" <- BYTES, from the filesystem **There is NO indexed-blob reader -- no `git show :<path>` -- anywhere in the invoked checking paths.** `git ls-files` appears, but that tests index MEMBERSHIP, not content; L's `git show` retrieves filenames from an existing COMMIT. codex audited all 21 sections and marks 18 of them false-green/false-reject on content: a working-tree correction can conceal an invalid indexed version, and working-tree damage can reject a valid one. *** SECTION D IS THE WORST AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE SHAPE: IT READS **UNSTAGED** ADDITIONS, SO THE MORE CORRECTLY YOU STAGE, THE LESS IT CHECKS. *** ADDED=$(git diff -U0 | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++') **MEASURED ON THIS SESSION'S OWN COMMIT, and it is exact.** At `#513`'s gate run the only tracked-modified-but-unstaged file was `regress/sgi_de_primop_probe.py`, which is deliberately kept OUT of every commit -- `git show --stat e302c98 | grep -c sgi_de_primop_probe` is **0**. So D's two green rows, *"no new file:line citations"* and *"no added occurrence counts"*, were computed **entirely from a file that is not in the commit**, while 129 staged files were invisible to it. A fully-staged commit gives D the empty set and D reports green on it. > **That is the check-that-cannot-fail family in its purest form: not a badly written assertion, > but a check whose input goes to zero exactly when the thing it guards is done properly.** *** A SHIPPED INSTANCE, found by codex in history rather than argued: commit `2956c7e` added `regress/sgi_mte_fill_probe.py` while its own `check_probe_wiring.py` carried ZERO manifest entries for that file. *** An actual shipped invariant violation of this class. (codex was explicit that it did not verify historical gate OUTPUT -- the violation is established from the commit contents, not from a green row.) *** TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF, BOTH LOAD-BEARING FOR SECTION J. *** * I described J as comparing two tracked files. **The project-root originals are OUTSIDE the git repository**; only the `GXEMUL-SEC/tools/` copies are in the index. So J's `cmp -s "$ROOT/$_c" "$SEC/tools/$_c"` compares an UNTRACKED external file against a tracked copy -- and updating the external original and its working copy while omitting the copy from staging lets J pass while the commit retains the OLD carrier. * **J's tracked-copy existence test is a bare `-f`.** It does not verify index membership at all. *** THE FIX IS NOT A FLAG, AND codex NAMED THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS ONE. *** Blindly replacing reads with `git show ":$path"` would inspect the WRONG version during the common before-staging run, because *"nothing staged" normally means the index equals HEAD, not that the index is empty*. The shape it prescribes: * **announce a SNAPSHOT MODE before the first pipeline invocation**, not at the late `CHANGED` assignment -- INDEX mode (membership, contents and checker selftests all from the candidate index; D switches to `git diff --cached -U0`) or WORKING-TREE PREVIEW (keep the useful before-staging audit; D keeps `git diff -U0`); * keep the deliberately EXTERNAL inputs -- carrier originals, build trees, panel dirs -- and the historical git queries explicitly separate, since those are correct as filesystem reads; * the helpers derive their paths from `__file__`, **so redirecting the shell's `ROOT` is not sufficient** -- a complete isolated index snapshot (a worktree) is the practical route, and it must carry unchanged dependencies too; * byte comparisons need a deliberate decision about git filters and newline conversion (locally the carrier copies are LF and `core.autocrlf` is false). **SEVERITY: this does not change what any product code does. What it changes is what a GREEN GATE MEANS**, on every round this project has recorded -- which is why it is filed high among harness items rather than as a tidy-up. It is a tooling change owing negative controls in both directions (prove a staged-only defect REDS in index mode; prove a working-tree-only defect does NOT), so it ships as its own harness round, never as a rider.open

The row is genuinely ambiguous between *executed and returned the defect* and *never executed at all*, which is the ambiguity a pc control exists to resolve. **[THIS SENTENCE IS WRONG. It was filed into OUTSTANDING_BUGS and given no ledger row, which is precisely the failure check_bugfile_sync.py was written to stop, in the direction it does not check. *** *** TWO CONCRETE MEMBERS OF THIS CLASS, FOUND BY THE grok PASS-2 SEAT ON `#511` AND VERIFIED, 2026-09-07. *** dev_uninorth.c:70-72 for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++) if (idata & (1 << dev)) break; dev_v3.c:164-166 for (dev=24; dev<32; dev++) if (relative_addr & (1 << dev)) break; Both reach `dev == 31`, so both evaluate `1 << 31` = 0x80000000 -- **a signed overflow in a 32-bit int, C99 6.5.7p4**, the same defect `#511` repaired in `dev_lca.c`. Both are PCI IDSEL scanners: the same idiom, in three chipsets, and only one had been noticed. **THE ONE-TOKEN REPAIR IS THE SAME (`1U << dev`)**, and each site needs the same check `#511` needed: what is the type of the left-hand operand of the `&`, and does the truth value move? In `#511` that operand was a plain `int`, so the `&` happened at 32 bits and nothing observable changed; **neither of these two has been checked, and the answer may differ** -- `dev_uninorth.c` ands against `idata`, which in that handler is likely 64-bit, and that is EXACTLY the case where the old sign-extension and the new zero-extension give different masks. *Do not assume `#511`'s conclusion transfers; it turned on a type.* **WHY THIS ROW GAINED THEM RATHER THAN A NEW ROW:** it is already the filed home for the class and already marked HONESTLY PARTIAL. These make the partiality concrete. *Provenance worth keeping: my own sibling census for `#511` MISSED both, because it excluded literal `1` as "the ordinary bitmask idiom". `1` has the most headroom and is therefore the only literal that overflows at the maximum shift a `< 32` loop produces -- the exclusion removed exactly the population it should have kept.* *** THE TYPE CHECK EACH SITE OWED IS DONE, AND THE TWO SITES DIVERGE -- ONE REPAIR IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING AND THE OTHER IS NOT. A THIRD SITE WAS FOUND IN THE PROCESS, ON THE LINE ABOVE, THAT NEITHER SEAT NAMED. *** **`#511`'s conclusion turned on `tag` being a 32-bit `int`, so the `&` happened at 32 bits and the bit pattern was unchanged. That reasoning must be redone per site, and it does not give the same answer twice.** **(A) `dev_uninorth.c:70-71` -- THE REPAIR CHANGES BEHAVIOUR, AND FIXES A REAL DEFECT.** :56 uint64_t idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len | MEM_PCI_LITTLE_ENDIAN); :70 for (dev=11; dev<32; dev++) :71 if (idata & (1 << dev)) `idata` is **`uint64_t`**, and it is the same variable at both lines (one block, declared at `:56`, used at `:71`). So the `&` is `uint64_t & int`: OLD at dev==31: `1 << 31' is int, 0x80000000, NEGATIVE -> sign-extends to 0xffffffff80000000 NEW at dev==31: `1U << 31' is unsigned, 0x80000000 -> zero-extends to 0x0000000080000000 **Those masks differ, and `idata` really can carry bits 32..63** -- it comes from `memory_readmax64` with the access width, and is stored whole into `d->cur_addr` (a `uint64_t`). **So under the CURRENT code a guest write with any bit in 32..63 set matches spuriously at dev==31 and the scan breaks on the wrong device.** The `1U` repair does not merely remove UB there; it corrects a guest-visible mis-decode. *This is exactly the case the `#511` pass-2 seats warned about in the abstract -- glm, minimax, deepseek and the kimi substitute all raised the wider-operand sign-extension scenario -- and it is REAL here even though it was not real in `#511`.* **(B) `dev_v3.c:164-165` -- THE REPAIR IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING.** :161 relative_addr &= 0xfffff; :162 relative_addr |= ((d->lb_map0 & 0xfff0) << 16); :164 for (dev=24; dev<32; dev++) :165 if (relative_addr & (1 << dev)) `relative_addr` is `uint64_t` (the `DEVICE_ACCESS` macro), so the same sign-extension happens -- but by `:164` its **bits 32..63 are all ZERO**: `:161` masks to 20 bits and `:162` ORs in a value that cannot exceed bit 31. The extra ones in `0xffffffff80000000` therefore meet only zeros, and the result is identical either way. **Still worth repairing -- the shift itself is UB regardless of what the `&` does with it -- but nothing observable moves.** *** (C) A THIRD SITE, ON `dev_v3.c:162` ITSELF, WHICH NEITHER SEAT NAMED AND MY OWN CENSUS ALSO MISSED. *** :63 uint16_t lb_map0; :162 relative_addr |= ((d->lb_map0 & 0xfff0) << 16); `lb_map0` is `uint16_t`, which INTEGER-PROMOTES to `int`; `0xfff0` is an `int`; so the `&` yields an `int` and the `<< 16` is a signed shift. 0xfff0 << 16 = 0xfff00000 = 4293918720 INT_MAX = 2147483647 OVERFLOWS **It overflows whenever bit 15 of `lb_map0` is set** -- i.e. for half the values the register can hold -- and `lb_map0` is GUEST-WRITABLE at `:212` (`d->lb_map0 = idata`). Repair: `0xfff0U`, or cast the operand. *My census could not see this one either, for a different reason than the `1 << 31` misses: the shift count here is a CONSTANT (16), so a filter keyed on "shifted by a VARIABLE" -- which mine was -- excludes it by construction. **Two filters, two blind spots, both of my own choosing.** The honest form of this row remains what it already said: HONESTLY PARTIAL.* **STATUS: three verified members, none repaired.** Each is a one-token change but (A) has a guest-visible consequence and therefore owes a witness of its own, while (B) and (C) are language-level repairs. They are NOT bundled: (A) is a defect round, (B)/(C) are hygiene.open

So the class IS pinnable, as a DIFFERENTIAL: fixed source produces no shift diagnostic, the `1U'->`1' mutant produces one. **Not bolted onto #510**: a second binary and a STDERR oracle is a new measurement lane, and #510's pass 2 had already run. Covers the same species at [[lcashiftub]], [[sgirebufshiftub]], m88k_rot:513, cpu_mips_instr.c:1757 and the two is_userpage sites -- EIGHT sites across three CPUs, none directly visible to a value oracle. *** THE FILED QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER COMES WITH A FREE VEHICLE: THE PROBE SHIPPED FOR [[lcaconfbus1kill]] ALREADY EVALUATES THIS EXPRESSION ON EVERY RUN. *** This row asks *"whether a UBSan sweep already flags it, and if not, why not."* Both halves settled by reading, 2026-09-07. **UBSAN IS PRESENT.** `build-asan/Makefile:9` carries `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g`. **BUT THE SWEEP CANNOT REACH THIS SITE, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.** `gate_asan_sweep.sh` runs, per machine type and subtype: timeout 25 stdbuf -o0 -e0 "$bin" -V -E "$t" -e "$s" "$DUMMY" </dev/null That is a **CONSTRUCTION** sweep -- it builds each machine and lets it start. The shift lives in `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)`'s device-scan loop, which runs only when a guest performs a PCI CONFIG-SPACE ACCESS. **Constructing `alphabook1` never executes that loop**, so no amount of sweeping flags it. *This is the witness-ladder distinction one level down: rung 2 (construction) cannot reach an access-path defect, which is exactly what the ladder says about registration proving presence and not reachability.* *** AND THE VEHICLE ALREADY EXISTS, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH ACTING ON. *** `regress/lca_confbus_probe.py` (shipped 2026-09-07 as the witness for [[lcaconfbus1kill]]) drives a guest `ldq` into the PCI config window with `ioc_conf == 0`. That takes the `bus == 0` branch: for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++) if (tag & (0x800 << dev)) break; Its control read uses `relative_addr == 0`, so `tag = (relative_addr >> 5) & ~0xff` is **0**, the `if` is never true, and **the loop runs all 21 iterations** -- evaluating `0x800 << 20` at the last one. `0x800` is `2^11` and a plain `int`, so `0x800 << 20` is `2^31`: **signed overflow, C99 6.5.7p4, undefined behaviour, on every single run of that probe.** > **SO THE MEASUREMENT IS: run the existing `lca_confbus_probe.py` against `build-asan/gxemul` and > read stderr for a UBSAN shift diagnostic. No new probe, no new row, no new apparatus.** The > expected diagnostic names `dev_lca.c` and a left-shift of a signed value. **NOT RUN YET** -- a probe run must not overlap the codex census currently in flight. Queued. **IF IT FIRES**, this row gains a measured witness and its one-token repair (`0x800U << dev`) can be graded properly. **IF IT DOES NOT**, that is itself a finding about [[ubsanshiftlane]] -- it would mean the ASAN build is not reporting a shift UB that is provably evaluated, and the whole proposed UBSAN differential lane rests on an assumption that does not hold. **Either outcome is worth the one run**, which is the argument for doing it before designing the lane. *Found while answering this row's own filed question rather than by looking for it -- and note the irony the row already recorded: this loop is the file's OWN graceful-degradation precedent, cited by [[lcabadval]] as a transferable warrant. The safe path contains the UB.* *** MEASURED 2026-09-07. THE UBSAN DIAGNOSTIC FIRES, NAMING THE FILE, LINE, COLUMN, VALUE AND SHIFT COUNT. Artifact: `regress/artifacts/lcashiftub/ubsan_HEAD_20260907.raw`. *** GXemul> step 5 fffffc0001040000: 243f0102 ldah t0,0x102 fffffc0001040004: a4410010 ldq t1,16(t0) fffffc0001040008: a4810000 ldq t3,0(t0) fffffc000104000c: a4210008 ldq t0,8(t0) fffffc0001040010: a4620000 ldq t2,0(t1) dev_lca.c:125:21: runtime error: left shift of 2048 by 20 places cannot be represented in type 'int' GXemul> print t2 0xffffffffffffffff **`2048` is `0x800`; `by 20 places` is the final loop iteration; `dev_lca.c:125` is exactly `if (tag & (0x800 << dev))`.** The diagnostic lands on the guest `ldq t2,0(t1)` -- a real guest instruction through real address decode on an unmodified `alphabook1`, with the empty-slot signature `0xffffffffffffffff` printed immediately after. **NO NEW APPARATUS WAS BUILT.** This is `regress/lca_confbus_probe.py`, shipped earlier the same day as the witness for [[lcaconfbus1kill]], run against `build-asan/gxemul` instead of `build/gxemul`. The control read takes the `bus == 0` branch with `tag == 0`, so the scan loop runs all 21 iterations and reaches the overflow every time. *** AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE OF MY OWN MAKING, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE RESULT. *** Run 1 reported NO diagnostic and I nearly recorded that as a finding against [[ubsanshiftlane]]. The cause: **I grepped the PROBE's stdout, and a UBSAN message goes to the EMULATOR's stderr**, which lands in the probe's internal pty buffer and is never echoed. That is *exactly* the defect I had fixed hours earlier for the `bus attrib` row -- a green row whose evidence never reaches the artifact -- recurring one level out, on the harness rather than the row. > **A PROBE ONLY SHOWS YOU WHAT IT CHOOSES TO PRINT. When you are looking for output the probe was > not written to surface, dump the buffer -- do not grep the summary.** Re-run from a frozen COPY > in `/tmp` (the shipped probe is not edited for a measurement) with the full buffer echoed, and the > diagnostic was in the first ten lines. *The wrong answer REASSURED, which is this project's recurring signature: "no diagnostic" is exactly what a clean build looks like.* *** THE LANE'S PREMISE IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: THE ASAN BUILD DOES REPORT SHIFT UB AT RUNTIME, WITH FILE, LINE AND COLUMN. *** This row proposed a UBSAN DIFFERENTIAL to pin the shift-UB class that no guest-value row can see, and rested on the untested assumption that `build-asan` would actually emit such a diagnostic. **It does**, and the message is precise enough to key an oracle on (`dev_lca.c:125:21`, the value, the shift count, and the type). **So the differential shape is viable as filed:** fixed source emits no diagnostic for that site, the `1U`->`1` mutant emits one. What this measurement does NOT establish is the other half -- that the diagnostic DISAPPEARS once the site is repaired -- which needs the repaired build and is the two-direction control the lane owes. *One incidental observation, recorded and NOT filed: the same run ends with `LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks -- 3211582 byte(s) leaked in 21 allocation(s)`. The session ends via `exit(1)` from the kill under test, so leaks at abrupt termination are expected and this is not evidence of a defect.* *** codex, `#511` PASS 2: "INVOKING THE EXISTING PROBE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT" -- AND IT IS RIGHT, WHICH CHANGES THIS ROW'S DESIGN. *** *"The shipped `lca_confbus_probe.py` `session()` and the top-level evidence-printing code captures emulator output but does not score or generally print shift diagnostics. Future wiring must explicitly expose and check that evidence."* **That is exactly the defect I hit by hand earlier the same day** and recorded as an apparatus lesson: the probe captures the whole pty buffer but PRINTS only the rows it chooses, so a UBSAN message is present in memory and absent from the artifact. My working measurement used a frozen COPY in `/tmp` with the buffer dumped -- **not the shipped probe.** > **SO THIS LANE'S RECIPE IS NOT "point the existing probe at build-asan".** It owes an explicit > SCORING step: a row whose oracle is the presence or absence of a shift diagnostic in the captured > buffer, printed into the artifact so a later reader can check it. Without that the lane would > pass by construction -- a green run that never looked. *That is this project's check-that-cannot-fail shape, and it would have been built into the lane's first version if codex had not named it.*open

Instance 3 is the clean demonstration: I derived the `(once)` gap from the probe, wrote it up as new, and the row `randompixdiagonce` had been filed EARLIER THE SAME DAY under a name I would never have guessed from the code. **PROPOSED STRUCTURAL FIX, and it is deliberately two things because they catch different halves:** * **(a) WRITER-SIDE, mechanical -- a duplicate check on ADDED ledger rows.** When a commit adds a row, compare its title's content words against every open/in-work row's title and REPORT the nearest matches for a human to dismiss. It cannot auto-reject (titles are prose and near-misses are real rows), so it warns; the value is that it fires at the moment of filing. Forward-only from a cutoff, the `check_cited_artifacts` idiom. **Owes two negative controls -- a genuine near-miss pair must NOT be reported as a duplicate, and an actual duplicate MUST be -- so it ships as its own harness round, not as a rider.** * **(b) READER-SIDE, a habit with a command -- before investigating a device or a probe, list what is already open against that FILE.** This is the half that would have caught instances 1, 2 and 5, which were never going to be caught at filing time because I never filed them. The command is one line and the artifacts directory is the other half of it: grep -l "<file>" regress/artifacts/*/*.txt python -c "...print rows whose title or note names <file>..." **HONEST LIMIT: (b) IS PROSE, AND THIS FILE'S OWN FINDING IS THAT PROSE DOES NOT FIRE.** I am not claiming it will. It is recorded because (a) genuinely cannot catch instances 1, 2 and 5 -- there is no filing event to hook -- and saying "no structure reaches this half" is more useful than pretending a habit is a control. If a later session finds a mechanical trigger for the reader side, that supersedes this. *Severity med, not high: nothing shipped wrong. Every instance was caught, four of them within the hour, and the one that reached the ledger was withdrawn the same day. The cost is wasted effort and an inflated backlog, not a defect in the emulator.* *** A NEIGHBOURING RECORDS CLASS, MEASURED 2026-09-08: A MULTI-ROUND COMMIT LEFT ALL FOUR OF ITS ROWS WITHOUT COMMIT ATTRIBUTION, AND ONE OF THEM ALSO KEPT A STALE STATE. *** `7a41b3f` shipped `#505 #506 #507 #508`. Afterwards: sgirergbroundtrip #505 state STILL `open', commits None, witness None <- worst lcaconfwidth #506 commits None alphaswpctxptbr #507 commits None alphapfnoffset #508 commits None **The `commits` gap is a records defect with no measured decision cost yet.** The `state` gap DID cost one: I read `sgirergbroundtrip` as an open med defect while scoping the `sgirandomcolour` round in the same file, and began designing around a defect `#505` had already fixed. *Those are different fields and should not be conflated into one severity.* **HOW BOTH WERE FOUND, and the order matters:** the state gap by ACCIDENT (opening the source while scoping something else); the three commit gaps by then asking the general question -- *"which non-closed rows are named by a CHANGELOG round-block heading?"* -- which is a precise query because the heading format is fixed (`# \`#NNN\` <rowid>: <title>`). It returned **7 candidates, of which 4 were legitimate `in work` rows and 3 were real gaps**, so the query needs row-by-row verification and is not a population claim. **NO CHECKER IS PROPOSED.** The carrier's escalation discipline applies: the commit-attribution gap has consumed zero decisions, and a check that fires on legitimate `in work` rows would be switched off. *If a stale STATE ever consumes a second decision, that is the trigger to revisit -- and this note exists so the count is findable.*open

lcaconfbus1killdev_lca.c: writing 0x1 to LCA_IOC_CONF is ACCEPTED by its guard and arms a host kill in lca_pci_conf -- `bus != 0` is a bare fatal()+exit(1) five lines below the file's own graceful-degradation precedentdev_lca.c: writing 0x1 to LCA_IOC_CONF is ACCEPTED by its guard and arms a host kill in lca_pci_conf -- `bus != 0` is a bare fatal()+exit(1) five lines below the file's own graceful-degradation precedent — commits: 41923ac — witness: probe:regress/lca_confbus_probe.py -- rung 3, MEASURED 3/4 on the committed build (witness_HEAD_20260907.raw); the RED row is the defect. Post-fix half PENDING (no fix chosen yet). — note: FILED 2026-09-07. Surfaced while verifying a claim in the grok seat's `lcabadval` pass-1 BODY (its verdict line did not carry it) -- and **verified to be sharper than the seat stated it**, by opening both functions. **THE DEFECT: an ACCEPTED write to one register arms a host kill in a DIFFERENT function.** `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_ioc)`, `case LCA_IOC_CONF`: d->ioc_conf = idata; /* Only bit 0 is implemented so far, the PCI bus 0 vs bus non-0 selection bit. */ if (idata & ~1) { fatal("TODO: Write to unimplemented bit of IOC_CONF: 0x%" PRIx64 "\n", ...); exit(1); } **`0x1` PASSES that guard.** `idata & ~1` is 0, so the write is accepted, stored, and the arm's own comment describes bit 0 as the implemented selector. `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)` then consumes it: bus = d->ioc_conf & 1; if (bus == 0) { for (dev=0; dev<21; dev++) if (tag & (0x800 << dev)) break; if (dev >= 21) { /* fatal("[ LCA: No bus 0 device? TODO ]\n"); exit(1); */ dev = 0; } } else { fatal("TODO. Non-zero bus.\n"); exit(1); } So: **guest writes 1 to IOC_CONF (accepted), then performs any PCI configuration-space access, and the host process exits.** Two guest accesses, both to registers the model implements, neither of them rejected. *** WHY IT IS ITS OWN ROW AND NOT PART OF [[lcabadval]]. *** Every kill `lcabadval` covers is a guard REFUSING a value it does not recognise. **This one fires on a value the guard ACCEPTS**, in a different function, on a later access. The acceptance and the kill are separated in both code and time, which is why a per-arm audit of `lca_ioc` walks straight past it -- as mine did, twice. *** AND THE SEAT'S FRAMING NEEDED CORRECTING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING. *** grok wrote that this exit becomes *"newly reachable from a CONF extra-bit write that also sets bit 0; today that write dies in the CONF guard first."* That is true of an EXTRA-BIT write (e.g. `0x3`), and it made the kill sound like a CONSEQUENCE of adopting option A. **It is not: `0x1` alone reaches it today, with no fix applied.** A widens which CONF values arrive here; it does not open the door. The door is open now. *Checked by reading both arms rather than by accepting the seat's sentence -- which is this project's own rule, and the seat was right about the site while being wrong about the timing.* **THE IRONY, and it is a design signal rather than a joke:** the `bus == 0` branch is the file's own graceful-degradation PRECEDENT -- a commented-out `fatal()`/`exit(1)` with `dev = 0;` substituted -- and [[lcabadval]] cites that very loop as a transferable in-tree warrant. **The `else` five lines below it is a bare kill.** Same function, opposite dispositions, no comment explaining why. **REACHABILITY, stated honestly rather than assumed.** Bit 0 is a bus SELECTOR, so a guest reaches this by selecting a bus the model does not implement and then doing config access -- plausible for firmware or an OS that probes beyond bus 0, and trivially reachable by a probe. **Whether any shipped guest on `alphabook1` actually does it is NOT established here**, and the row does not claim it. What is established is that no guard stands between an accepted write and the kill. **WITNESS: a rung-3 probe is available and most of it already exists.** `device_add(machine, "lca")` is `ST_ALPHABOOK1` ONLY (`machine_alpha.c`), and `regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py` ALREADY drives a guest `stq`/`ldq` at `LCA_IOC_CONF` (`0xfffffc0180000020`, K0SEG | physical) on unmodified `alphabook1`. This row needs one more session: `stq 0x1` to CONF, then a PCI config-space access. **Three traps that probe already paid for:** debugger `dump` skips `DM_DEFAULT` handlers; a debugger `put d` of a killing value IS a host kill but is NOT a guest instruction, so it does not witness; and HAE at window offset 0 silently succeeds, so a miss control must not use `LCA_IOC_BASE+0`. **DISPOSITION, not yet adjudicated:** it is the same de-fatalisation family, but the option set differs because the kill is not a value refusal -- the honest members here are DECLINE THE CONFIG ACCESS (return without dispatching, with a latched announce) or IMPLEMENT bus != 0. **Note the architecturally correct error path is blocked for the same reason grok gave on the sibling row: `LCA_IOC_STAT0`/`STAT1` have no case at all and hit the `default:` arm's `exit(1)`, so LCA cannot report a device error through the register the header designates for it.** sev HIGH: a guest-drivable host kill, reached by two ordinary accesses with no rejected value anywhere on the path. *** SIBLING CHECK DISCHARGED WITH A DENOMINATOR, 2026-09-07 -- the class has EXACTLY ONE member in this file. *** The rule is grep for the siblings before calling a finding whole; here the question is which lca_ioc fields have a consumer at all, since a field nothing reads cannot arm a delayed kill. Counting references that are neither the readback (`odata = d->X`) nor the store (`d->X = `): ioc_conf 1 consumer <- `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1` in lca_pci_conf. THIS ROW. tlb_enable 0 window_base_0 0 window_base_1 0 window_mask_0 0 window_mask_1 0 window_t_base_0 0 window_t_base_1 0 **So the accepted-write-arms-a-later-kill shape cannot recur elsewhere in dev_lca.c**: the other seven fields are write-and-read-back with nothing downstream. That is also why [[lcabadval]]s five pure-storage arms are a different problem from this one, and why a fix here does not generalise to them. *Not claimed beyond this file. The general class -- an ACCEPTED store that a later access consumes into a terminating path -- is a plausible cross-device census and is NOT run here.* *** THE WITNESS-DESIGN CHECK WAS REFUSED BY codex ON A CONTENT FILTER, 2026-09-07 -- recorded as a SEAT FAILURE, never as agreement. *** Zero-byte `.txt`, exit 0, the error only in the `.err`: *"This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk."* Full analysis and the two same-day negative controls are on [[codexsubjectrefusal]]. **Re-fired on grok**, which reads the tree, takes its brief from a file and has no such filter -- so the question is covered, not lost. The brief itself is preserved at `regress/artifacts/lcaconfbus1kill/WITNESS_brief.md` so the trigger can be studied rather than guessed at. *** THE WITNESS DESIGN IS SOUND -- grok, 2026-09-07, ON THE BRIEF codex REFUSED. The alternate-transport rule paid off completely: the recovery is BETTER than the refused seat would have given, not a degraded substitute. *** **DENOMINATOR, and it is the largest this row has seen:** all of `dev_lca.c` (390 lines -- both handlers, `DEVINIT`, ISA, interrupt stubs); `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_pci_conf)` and `DEVICE_ACCESS(lca_ioc)` end to end; `bus_pci_data_access`/`bus_pci_setaddr` in `bus_pci.c`; `alpha_translate_v2p` K0SEG in `memory_alpha.c`; the device and unmapped paths in `memory_rw.c`; `LS_GENERIC_N`/`LS_N` in `cpu_alpha_instr_loadstore.c`; `fatal()` in `debugmsg.c`; `ST_ALPHABOOK1` in `machine_alpha.c`; and all of `regress/lca_confwidth_probe.py`. **CONFIRMED:** S2 reaches `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1` for ANY access in the window -- no `switch` on `relative_addr`, no `len` test, no `writeflag` test that can skip it, no early `return`; the only `writeflag` use before it is filling `idata`, which is not a guard. `len` is first used AFTER the kill. And `ioc_conf` has **exactly two readers**, so nothing else can be armed by S1. *** FOUR CORRECTIONS THAT CHANGE THE CONSTRUCTION: *** 1. **MY LIVENESS CONTROL IS MISLABELLED.** `ioc rt` proves the WRITER (`lca_ioc`'s CONF arm) round-trips `0x1`. **It says nothing about S2's window.** PCI_CONF liveness is the armed session's unique message (the handler ran) PLUS the control surviving (the same access is not an unconditional kill). A positive signature is available if wanted: an empty-slot read returns `0xffffffffffffffff`, where unmapped returns 0. 2. **S2 MUST BE A READ, NOT A WRITE.** Both reach the kill, but an empty-slot WRITE makes `bus_pci_data_access` print `[ ... write to non-existant device ... ]` -- so the CONTROL would carry a second `fatal()` on stderr. An empty-slot READ of reg 0 is the architectural ID probe and is silent. 3. **A TIGHTER VARIANT: ONE PROCESS, not two sessions.** control `ldq` (survives), then S1, then the armed `ldq` (dies) -- **only `ioc_conf` changes between the two loads.** Separate sessions are still adequate, but this removes the residual that two processes could differ in something that ran before the debugger prompt. 4. **KEEP IT ON `step`.** `continue` would make the `lca_interrupt_assert`/`_deassert` stubs a confounder -- and `cpu_dyntrans.c` skips interrupt delivery while single-stepping anyway. *** THE CONTRACT LIMIT, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE FOR THE FIX ROUND: THIS IS A WITNESS OF THE `exit(1)`, NOT A DETECTOR OF THE REPAIR. *** grok: *"'Host survives, session completes' greens for a silent `return 1` that skips `bus_pci_*` and `memory_writemax64`, for a latched announce, AND for falling through into existing `bus_pci` with `cur_bus=1` (empty type-1 also survives)."* So the post-fix oracle cannot discriminate between fix members, and a round that ships one must build a row that can. **Post-fix caution in the same breath: if someone later implements type-1 by falling through to `bus_pci_setaddr(bus=1, ...)`, empty bus 1 is a non-killing miss today, so the witness goes green -- do NOT read that green as "type-1 is modelled."** **WHY OFFSET 0 IS THE RIGHT CONTROL ADDRESS, which I had asserted without warrant:** it is not HAE-like (HAE is an exact-address `break` in `lca_ioc`; `lca_pci_conf` has no per-offset special case). On the ARMED session the offset is irrelevant -- `bus == 1` exits before `tag`/`dev` are used. On the SURVIVING control, `tag == 0` matches no IDSEL bit, so the `dev >= 21` body runs -- **and that body is already the commented-out kill with `dev = 0;`** -- then an empty-slot read returns `(uint64_t)-1` without exiting. `0x18` (the NetBSD `| 0x3 << 3` encoding) yields the same `tag`/`reg` and is equivalent. **Do NOT use `relative_addr = 0x800000`**, which talks to the registered `i82378zb` at device 7. *** AND grok FOUND THE DESIGN ARGUMENT SITTING FIVE LINES ABOVE THE DEFECT: the `dev >= 21` arm is ALREADY DE-FATALISED, in the same function, and the surviving control USES that path. *** *"If that `exit(1)` were still live, the control would die and you would misread PCI_CONF as unconditionally fatal. The file already contains the decline precedent the `else` lacks."* That is the strongest available warrant for declining here, and it is one function away from the kill. Also confirmed: FAULT (member 5) is unavailable -- `memory_rw.c` delivers a failed device access as an exception only under `MEM_MIPS`/`MEM_M88K`, and this path always `return 1` on the live path, so the kill is `exit(1)` and not `return 0`. And `lca_isa`'s `ofs > len` kill is a DIFFERENT window (`LCA_PCI_SIO`), not reachable from `0x1e0000000`. *** CROSS-REFERENCE, AND A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN NOVELTY CLAIM. [[lcabadval]] ALREADY ENUMERATED THIS KILL ON 2026-09-06. *** Its eleven-kill census for dev_lca.c lists **line 134, class BUS, condition `bus != 0`, i.e. `d->ioc_conf & 1`** -- so the site AND its dependence on ioc_conf were both already recorded, and I filed this row saying only lcabadval mentioned lca_pci_conf without reading how. **Sixth rediscovery this session; see [[refilingclass]], which predicts exactly this.** **WHAT THIS ROW GENUINELY ADDS, stated narrowly:** the census records the MECHANISM; it does not record that **`0x1` PASSES the CONF guard**. That is what makes the kill reachable with no rejected value anywhere on the path -- an accepted write in one handler arming a terminating branch in another -- and it is why the disposition differs from lcabadval's six value guards, whose kills all fire on refusal. Plus the witness design, now reviewed SOUND by grok. **KEPT AS A SEPARATE ROW** because it has its own disposition (decline the config access, or implement bus != 0) and its own witness, and because folding it into a row named for VALUE GUARDS would hide it -- which is the census's own closing lesson: *a row named after one class hides the members of the others.* *** AND THE CENSUS NAMES SOMETHING PLAUSIBLY WORSE THAN THIS ROW, WHICH I SHOULD SAY OUT LOUD RATHER THAN LEAVE IN A TABLE: the two INTERRUPT STUBS at :73 and :85. *** `lca_interrupt_assert` and `lca_interrupt_deassert` are bare `fatal("...TODO"); exit(1)` with **NO GUARD AT ALL**, so *any* device asserting an interrupt through the LCA ends the process regardless of what it writes. In the census's words: the value-guard registers *"need a firmware revision that writes something else; these two need only that an interrupt is asserted."* That is member 7 (IMPLEMENT) of the option set -- a whole path stubbed out, with no value being refused -- and it is a stronger candidate for the next critical round than this one. *** THE RUNG-3 WITNESS EXISTS AND THE DEFECT IS MEASURED, 2026-09-07. regress/lca_confbus_probe.py, artifact regress/artifacts/lcaconfbus1kill/witness_HEAD_20260907.raw, sentinel LCACONFBUS_DONE. *** bus ctl yes yes CONTROL: identical read at ioc_conf==0 survived ok bus ctlsig 0xffffffffffffffff 0xffffffffffffffff DEVICE SIGNATURE: empty-slot ID probe ok bus kill dead alive <- THE DEFECT FAIL bus attrib yes yes death carried THIS arm@s diagnostic ok EVIDENCE: TODO. Non-zero bus. LCACONFBUS_RESULT=3/4 **One emulator process, unmodified `alphabook1`, real guest instructions through real address decode.** The sequence is: guest `ldq` from `LCA_PCI_CONF+0` with `ioc_conf == 0` (SURVIVES), then guest `stq 0x1` to `LCA_IOC_CONF` (ACCEPTED -- `idata & ~1` is 0), then the IDENTICAL `ldq` again (HOST DIES). Only `ioc_conf` differs between the two loads, which is what attributes the death to the VALUE rather than to the address, the width, or touching the window at all. *** grok@s PREDICTED DEVICE SIGNATURE CAME BACK EXACTLY. *** It reasoned from `bus_pci.c` that an empty-slot read returns `0xffffffffffffffff` via `memory_writemax64` while UNMAPPED returns 0. The control row reads **0xffffffffffffffff**. That is a prediction from source, confirmed by measurement -- so the signature control is established, not assumed. **ORACLE POLARITY is the ladder@s: the rows assert the CORRECT (post-fix) behaviour, so `bus kill` is RED on the committed build and goes GREEN when the defect is fixed, with the SAME script.** Clause (i) is therefore HALF discharged -- the pre-fix symptom is shown; the post-fix green awaits a fix, which is correct for test-first. *** TWO APPARATUS DEFECTS CAUGHT IN THE FIRST RUN AND FIXED, both worth keeping. *** 1. **The first artifact carried NO EVIDENCE for `bus attrib`.** The row tested the PTY buffer and printed nothing, so the preserved log showed a green row whose diagnostic a later reader could not check. The probe now ECHOES the matched line into its own output. *A green row whose evidence is not in the artifact is not verifiable, however sound the logic.* 2. **I nearly filed a false correction to grok.** It said the `TODO. Non-zero bus.` literal is unique in `src/`; my grep returned TWO. The second hit is `dev_lca.o`, the compiled object. One source site, `dev_lca.c:133`. grok was right; my apparatus swept binaries. *** THE FIX DESIGN IS CLEARER THAN THIS ROW ASSUMED, AND IT DIVERGES FROM ITS SIBLING FOR A REASON WORTH STATING. Derived 2026-09-07 from the codex fix design on [[lcairqstubkill]] plus this row's own witness. *** **THE TWO LCA ROWS LOOK LIKE ONE PROBLEM AND ARE NOT.** Both are bare `fatal()+exit(1)` reached by ordinary guest access, so it is tempting to give them one disposition. The difference is what the guest is ASKING FOR: * [[lcairqstubkill]] -- an interrupt DELIVERY. There is no correct answer that is not delivery: a decline LOSES AN EVENT, silently or otherwise, and the guest can never learn of it. codex's disposition there is "diagnose and stop the guest CPU", because continuing is a lie. * **THIS ROW -- a PCI configuration cycle on bus 1. There IS a correct answer, and hardware gives it: a config read of an absent device returns ALL ONES.** An unimplemented BUS is legitimately EMPTY. Declining is not a lost event; it is the architecturally right reply. > **So the dispositions properly differ, and the reason is not "one is worse". For a DELIVERY path > an unimplemented target has no honest continuation; for an ADDRESSING path it has one, and the > tree already implements it.** *** AND THE TREE ALREADY DOES THE RIGHT THING ONE STEP DOWN, which the witness measured by accident. *** The `bus == 0` branch already reaches `bus_pci_setaddr` / `bus_pci_data_access`, and this row's own witness recorded the result: **a read of an empty slot returns `0xffffffffffffffff`** (the `bus ctlsig` row, MEASURED). grok noted the same about the armed side in its design review -- *"falling through into existing bus_pci with cur_bus=1 (empty type-1 also survives)"*. **SO THE LIKELY FIX IS NOT A DECLINE AT ALL BUT A FALL-THROUGH:** stop special-casing `bus != 0`, let the existing `bus_pci` path handle it, and an empty bus 1 answers all-ones by itself. That is option-set member 7 (IMPLEMENT) reached cheaply, because the machinery exists -- unlike the sibling row, where member 7 is blocked at the dyntrans core. *** THE DISCRIMINATING ROW IS THEREFORE THE RETURNED VALUE, NOT THE RUNNING STATE. *** codex's oracle for the sibling row ("stopped guest state, plus the reason") is right THERE and wrong HERE, because a correct fix must leave the guest RUNNING. The observable that separates the candidates here is what the armed read returns: fall through to bus_pci (empty bus 1) 0xffffffffffffffff <- architecturally correct silent return without servicing 0x0 or unchanged <- looks like UNMAPPED latched announce then return unserviced 0x0 or unchanged <- same, plus a message the existing exit(1) host gone **And this probe ALREADY HAS THAT ROW SHAPE**: `bus ctlsig` asserts exactly `0xffffffffffffffff` on the bus-0 control, and distinguishes it from the `0x0` an unmapped read gives. The fix round adds the mirror of it on the ARMED side. *No new capability is needed, which is not true of the sibling.* **NOT YET VERIFIED, and it is the one thing to check before building:** that `bus_pci` genuinely tolerates `cur_bus == 1` rather than asserting or indexing something sized for one bus. grok's review says empty type-1 survives; **that is a seat's reading and this row has not measured it.** The cheap check is to build the fall-through and run the existing probe -- the armed row should turn from `dead` to `0xffffffffffffffff`. *** THE UNVERIFIED LINK IS CLOSED BY READING: `bus_pci' IS BUS-AGNOSTIC BY CONSTRUCTION, SO THE FALL-THROUGH FIX IS SOUND WITHOUT A NEW CAPABILITY. *** The paragraph above flagged one thing to check before building -- whether `bus_pci' tolerates `cur_bus == 1' rather than asserting or indexing something sized for a single bus. It does: bus_pci.h:84 int cur_bus, cur_device, cur_func, cur_reg; <- a plain int, not bus-0-only bus_pci.h:87 struct pci_device *first_device; <- a LINKED LIST, not an array indexed by bus number bus_pci.c:102 if (dev->bus == pci_data->cur_bus && ...) <- devices carry their OWN bus field and are MATCHED against it bus_pci.c:200 pci_data->cur_bus = bus; <- set from the caller, unchecked **So a lookup with `cur_bus = 1` walks the list, matches nothing (no device carries `bus == 1`), and falls into the no-device path -- which this row's own witness has already MEASURED returning `0xffffffffffffffff` on bus 0.** Nothing is sized for one bus and nothing asserts. *** THAT CONFIRMS grok's READING AND UPGRADES IT FROM A SEAT CLAIM TO A CHECKED ONE. *** Its design review said *"falling through into existing bus_pci with cur_bus=1 (empty type-1 also survives)"*, which this row correctly recorded as unmeasured. It is now verified by source rather than accepted. **CONSEQUENCE: the fix is a DELETION, not an addition.** Remove the `bus != 0` special case and let the existing path serve the cycle; an absent device on an absent bus answers all-ones by itself. That is the cheapest member-7 in the option set -- and the addition licence is satisfied trivially, because nothing is added. **WHAT STILL OWES A MEASUREMENT, and it is one run:** build the fall-through and re-run `regress/lca_confbus_probe.py`. **PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION: the `bus kill' row turns from `dead' to `alive', and a mirror of `bus ctlsig' on the armed side should read `0xffffffffffffffff`** -- the same value the bus-0 control already returns, which is what distinguishes a serviced empty-bus cycle from a silent unserviced return (`0x0`, indistinguishable from unmapped). *** PASS-1 FIX PANEL, 2026-09-07 -- PROVISIONAL: recorded on THREE landed seats (deepseek, minimax, the kimi-k3:cloud substitute) while codex, grok and glm were still answering. Any ruling short of the roster is provisional on its face. *** **Q1 IS SETTLED AND MY WORRY WAS UNFOUNDED -- AND THE PROOF IS INSIDE THE EXISTING CODE, WHICH I HAD NOT THOUGHT TO USE.** I asked whether the file's tag comment describes the same `tag` this code computes (`(relative_addr >> 5) & ~0xff`) or a pre-shift value. minimax: > *"The existing IDSEL check proves the code's `tag` IS the comment's `tag`. The `bus == 0` branch > checks `tag & (0x800U << dev)` for dev 0..20. The mask `1 << (dev+11)` only matches real hardware > if `tag` holds IDSEL bits at positions 11..31 -- exactly the comment's type-0 layout. That branch > is EXERCISED TODAY on real bus-0 traffic and works, so the interpretation is FORCED."* `0x800` is exactly `1 << 11`, and the kimi substitute reaches it independently (*"func at bits 10..8 in both rows"*). **So `dev = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f` is the faithful type-1 decode.** *A working branch of the same function is a stronger oracle for a layout question than the comment is -- the comment could be stale, the working code cannot be.* *** Q2 IS THE REAL DEFECT IN MY SKETCH, AND ALL THREE SEATS FLAG IT: THE FIX AS WRITTEN WOULD BE INCOHERENT. *** deepseek: *"the sketch is incomplete/incoherent because it keeps `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1` while the type-1 tag comment says bus is in tag bits 23..16."* The kimi substitute sharpens it: **the model computes THREE bus/type sources from the address -- the AD[1:0] type bits, the tag's bus field, and `ioc_conf & 1` -- and DISCARDS TWO.** *"The packet cannot say which one real hardware honours."* > **So decoding `dev` from the type-1 layout while taking `bus` from a register bit mixes two > addressing models.** Either the tag is authoritative (and `bus` must come from bits 23..16) or the > register is (and the type-1 tag layout does not apply). **The fix cannot be written until that is > chosen, and no seat could choose it from the packet.** **Q4: THE DISCRIMINATING ROW IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT -- unanimous among the three.** My proposed armed-side all-ones row separates *serviced an empty bus* from *returned without servicing* (`0x0`, indistinguishable from unmapped). **It cannot separate IMPLEMENT from an explicit all-ones return**, because an EMPTY bus 1 answers all-ones under both. kimi: *"only a populated bus-1 device can"* tell them apart -- and nothing in this tree places one. *That is a real limit on what this round can claim, and it is better to know it before building the row than after.* **NOT ADOPTED PENDING THE ROSTER.** The Q2 question is a hardware-behaviour question the packet cannot settle, and `_scratchpad/` holds no LCA/21066 datasheet (the `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` list has DC21285 but no 21066), so it may not be settleable from this machine at all -- which would make it a candidate for the 2026-09-09 adjudication rather than for a fix round. *** grok LANDED AND SETTLED Q2 -- THE ANSWER THE PACKET-FED SEATS COULD NOT REACH, AND IT DISSOLVES THE INCOHERENCE RATHER THAN CHOOSING A SIDE. *** > **VERDICT: IMPLEMENT, but the sketch is one assignment short.** `dev = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f` is the > right extract of *this* `tag` (Q1 is not a double-shift). **Also assign > `bus = (tag >> 16) & 0xff` -- `ioc_conf & 1` is the PCI cycle TYPE, not the bus number.** > Member 7; fall through into `bus_pci`. The proposed all-ones row is necessary and not sufficient: > the witness address is not a type-1 tag, and empty-slot data cannot pin the extract. **WHY THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT INSTEAD OF PICKING A WINNER.** deepseek and the kimi substitute were right that taking `dev` from the tag while taking `bus` from a register bit mixes two addressing models. grok's reading shows the register bit is not a bus selector at all: it chooses the CYCLE TYPE -- type 0 addresses the local bus, type 1 addresses a bus behind a bridge -- and in type 1 the bus number comes from the tag. **The file's own comment, "the PCI bus 0 vs bus non-0 selection bit", is a loose description of exactly that**, so the code comment and grok agree once the names are straightened. *The variable is simply misnamed: `bus = d->ioc_conf & 1;` stores a cycle type in something called `bus`.* **THE FIX IS THEREFORE TWO ASSIGNMENTS, NOT ONE:** } else { bus = (tag >> 16) & 0xff; /* type-1: bus is bits 23..16 */ dev = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f; /* type-1: device is bits 15..11 */ } *** AND grok BREAKS MY PROPOSED DISCRIMINATING ROW FOR A REASON I HAD NOT SEEN: "the witness address is not a type-1 tag". *** The existing probe reads at `LCA_PCI_CONF + 0`, so `tag == 0` -- which under the type-1 decode means bus 0, device 0. **The row would therefore exercise the new code with a degenerate tag and prove nothing about the extract**, and "empty-slot data cannot pin the extract" because an absent device answers all-ones whatever bus/dev were decoded. > **So the round needs a row that drives a NON-ZERO type-1 tag and observes something that depends > on the decoded bus/dev -- and with no device on bus 1, there is nothing to observe.** That is the > same limit the three packet-fed seats reached from the other side (*"only a populated bus-1 device > can"* separate IMPLEMENT from a faked all-ones return). Two independent routes to one conclusion. **HARDWARE CLAIM, FLAGGED AS UNVERIFIABLE FROM THIS MACHINE:** that `ioc_conf & 1` is the cycle type is a statement about the 21066/LCA, and **`_scratchpad/` holds no LCA datasheet** -- the PDF list has DC21285 but nothing for this chipset. It is consistent with the file's comment and with standard PCI type-0/type-1 addressing, but it is not CHECKED here, and this project's rule is to cite only what has been read. **That is a good candidate for the 2026-09-09 adjudication rather than for me.** *** THE PANEL IS COMPLETE (6 seats) AND UNANIMOUS ON THE DESIGN -- AND codex CITED A PRIMARY SOURCE SITTING ON THIS MACHINE THAT I HAD JUST DECLARED UNAVAILABLE. *** I wrote, one paragraph above, that the cycle-type claim is *"a statement about the 21066 ... not CHECKED here"* because `_scratchpad/` holds no LCA datasheet. **codex pointed at `_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/alpha/pci/lca_pci.c` -- the REAL OpenBSD LCA driver, 4,925 bytes, dated 1997, on disk in this project.** Verified and read: :103 if (bp != NULL) *bp = (tag >> 16) & 0xff; /* BUS */ :106 if (dp != NULL) *dp = (tag >> 11) & 0x1f; /* DEVICE */ :108 if (fp != NULL) *fp = (tag >> 8) & 0x7; /* FUNCTION */ **That is grok's proposal, verbatim, from the driver the hardware was written for.** `bus` is bits 23..16 of the tag and `dev` is bits 15..11 -- not inference, not a datasheet paraphrase, the actual decomposition routine. *** AND `lca_conf_read` SETTLES Q2 OUTRIGHT: *** :125 /* secondary if bus # != 0 */ :126 pci_decompose_tag(&lcp->lc_pc, tag, &secondary, &device, 0); :127 if (secondary) { :130 REGVAL(LCA_IOC_CONF) = 0x01; :132 } else { :134 /* on the LCA, must frob the tag used for devices on the primary bus, :136 in the same ways as is used by type 1 configuration cycles on PCs. */ :139 tag = (1 << (device + 11)) | (tag & 0x7ff);
