exit 1; } N=$(grep -cE '^@@' "$B" 2>/dev/null) [ "${N:-0}" -ge 3 ] || { echo "REFUSING: only ${N:-0} hunk markers"; exit 1; } grep -q "<a token from the diff body>" "$B" || { echo "REFUSING: diff body absent"; exit 1; } Three properties, and each is load-bearing: `-s` catches missing AND empty; `${N:-0}` makes the comparison well-formed whatever grep did; and the CONTENT grep catches a brief that has hunk markers but lost the body. **NOT MECHANISED, deliberately.** This guard is written ad hoc at each launch rather than living in `panel.sh`, and moving it there is a change to the script every panel runs -- which owes two negative controls (prove it refuses a missing brief, prove it does NOT refuse a good one). **That is its own harness round.** Note `panel.sh` ALREADY refuses correctly (`no such brief`); what is missing is that the CALLER believes it launched. *Provenance: my own guard, written earlier in the same session, in the same shell block, on the belief that it made the launch safe. It had worked on three previous briefs -- because they existed.* *** THE FIXED GUARD CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST USE, AND IT WAS THE **CONTENT** CHECK THAT FIRED -- not the existence test and not the count. 2026-09-08. *** Building the `sgirekills` round-design brief, I inlined the arm cascade as lines 420-545 and the guard refused: REFUSING: cascade truncated before LINEAR_B **The range was wrong.** `LINEAR_A`'s arm alone runs to line 585 and `LINEAR_B` starts at 588, so the true cascade is 420-660 -- **241 lines, not 126.** The brief would have said *"the FULL arm cascade, VERBATIM"* while omitting the sixth of the six windows it was about, and the seat would have answered a question about five arms believing it had seen six. > **THE COUNT CHECK WOULD HAVE PASSED IT.** 126 inlined lines is a perfectly healthy-looking > number; the file existed and was 11 KB. **Only asking "is the thing I claim to have inlined > actually in here?" could fail.** > > That is the denominator rule's own limit, restated: a denominator proves the apparatus SELECTED > something, never that it selected the RIGHT something. A content assertion is the only check that > distinguishes them. **So the three-part guard has now earned each of its parts by a different failure:** `-s` was minted by the missing-file cascade that filed this row; `${N:-0}` by the empty-variable comparison; and the CONTENT grep by this truncation, which the other two pass cleanly. *Recorded because the guard was written defensively an hour earlier with no expectation of firing, and the thing it caught was mine.*open

armbfcdecodecpu_arm_instr.c: the bfi decoder accepts source field 15 and passes r[15] to X(bfi), but the architecture assigns that encoding to BFC (Bit Field Clear) -- so BFC is decoded as `BFI with Rn = PC'cpu_arm_instr.c: the bfi decoder accepts source field 15 and passes r[15] to X(bfi), but the architecture assigns that encoding to BFC (Bit Field Clear) -- so BFC is decoded as `BFI with Rn = PC' — witness: none -- NOT YET ATTEMPTED. Raised by the codex seat from source inspection while answering armbfiwidth; the decoder arm and handler were read, no instruction was planted. This field says `not yet done`, never `did not think to ask`. — note: FILED 2026-09-08 from the codex `armbfiwidth` design answer. **BFC is BFI with Rn = 15**, and the architecture defines it as clearing the field rather than inserting from a register. This fork's decoder does not distinguish them, so a BFC would insert bits taken from `r[15]` -- the PC -- instead of clearing. **NOT VERIFIED HERE.** It comes from one seat's source reading, and neither the decoder arm's exact guard nor the architectural claim has been re-derived by me. *The round-scope rule keeps it separate from `armbfiwidth`: same file and adjacent lines, but a different defect with a different fix and a different oracle, so it is a candidate ROUND rather than a rider.* *** THE codex ASSESS ANSWER, 2026-09-08. THE IMPLEMENTATION HALF IS VERIFIED; THE ARCHITECTURAL HALF IS NOT, AND THE SEAT SAID SO RATHER THAN FILLING THE GAP FROM MEMORY. *** ### 1. VERIFIED: source field 15 does reach the handler The generic decoder computes `rm = iword & 15`, and the bfi arm binds `ic->arg[1] = (size_t)(&cpu->cd.arm.r[rm])` with **no guard excluding 15**. `X(bfi)` then opens with `uint32_t x = reg(ic->arg[1]);` and has **no source-15 clear path**. All three of my settled premises about the extraction and packing were confirmed against the file. ### 2. *** MY OWN CHARACTERISATION WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS SHARPER THAN THE CLAIM. *** I wrote that BFC becomes *"BFI with Rn = PC"*. **`r[15]` is not the PC in this interpreter.** Translation reconstructs the instruction address into `cpu->pc` WITHOUT refreshing `r[15]`, and the PC+8 that PC-relative loads need is computed into a separate `tmp_pc`. So `r[15]` holds whatever was last written there -- **a previous load-to-PC target, or an exception-vector address** -- which is a *stale* value, not a predictable one. *That matters for the fix and for any oracle: a row that assumes r[15] holds the current PC would be pinning something the emulator does not maintain.* ### 3. *** AND MY MANUAL PREMISE WAS WRONG TOO -- THE PREMISE-AUDIT LINE EARNED ITS PLACE AGAIN. *** I told the seat DDI 0100I was ARMv5. **Its preface explicitly includes ARMv6.** It still does not contain BFI or BFC -- the seat searched and found neither mnemonic -- because those are ARMv6T2 additions. > **SO THE ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM AT THE HEART OF THIS ROW REMAINS UNVERIFIED AGAINST ANY LOCAL > DOCUMENT, and the seat refused to paper over it:** *"source 15 -> architectural BFC is not > document-verified within this reading scope; I cannot attach a local manual page citation to it."* > **That is the honest form this project asks for, and it is a BLOCKER: #357/#362/#365 shipped page > citations that came from model output rather than a local manual.** This round does not ship a > behavioural change on a recalled architectural rule. **It needs an ARMv7-A ARM (DDI 0406) in > `_scratchpad/`, and until then the row stays open with the implementation half verified.** ### 4. THE WITNESS IS CONSTRUCTIBLE, and the design turns on the r[15] correction above Because `r[15]` is stale rather than the PC, the witness must PUT a known value there: r0 = 0xffffffff a word load into PC whose target is 0x00001008 -- this is what leaves 0x1008 in r[15] at that target: BFC r0, #8, #4 -- lsb=8, msb=11, width=4 clear the field -> r0 = 0xfffff0ff insert the stored r[15] -> r0 = 0xfffff8ff **Merely placing the instruction at 0x1008 does NOT establish that register value** -- the load-to-PC setup is what does it, which is precisely the consequence of finding 2. Width 4 is chosen to avoid the sibling mask-boundary cases. *Source-derived and arithmetic-checked; not run.* ### 5. TWO ROUNDS CONFIRMED, on the round-scope rule *"Correcting source-15 semantics leaves mask construction unchanged; correcting mask construction leaves source-15 semantics unchanged."* Different fix, different oracle -- so `armbfiwidth` stays separate, as filed.open

IT IS THAT IT WAS RECORDED SOMEWHERE THE DECIDER DOES NOT LOOK. *** where the ruling was CHANGELOG.md, and an artifact under ANOTHER row's directory (regress/artifacts/pcc2widthkills/fable_adjudication_20260902.md) where I looked the LEDGER ROW, which said `state: open, sev: low` and carried no note result a full round of design, a nine-seat brief, and a panel fired against a question that had been adjudicated six days earlier **The ruling even contained the finding I re-derived**: *"the proposed `>> 1` fix would IMPORT the siblings' overrun."* I enumerated that from scratch and wrote it up as new. > **A STANDING DISPOSITION THAT LIVES ANYWHERE EXCEPT THE ROW IT GOVERNS WILL BE RE-OPENED BY THE > NEXT PERSON WHO READS THE ROW -- which is exactly the population that might re-open it.** *** THE POPULATION IS NOT MECHANICALLY ENUMERABLE, AND I TRIED. *** Two greps disagreed: narrow (a close-word within ~120 chars AFTER the row id) 0 rows broad (any ruling word within 400 chars either side) 9 rows Spot-reading three of the nine: `wdcbeoddtail`'s hit is a SEVERITY assignment in an audit table (noise); `sgirandomskipput`'s is a FILING decision (*"filed as X rather than dropped"*), not a do-not-code; `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd` and `m88kexctaildefault` are *"filed now as documented-only LOW rows"*, which IS a disposition worth carrying. **So the broad check is a CORRELATE -- "a ruling word near the row id" -- and not the class**, which is *a disposition decided elsewhere that the row does not carry*. That distinction needs READING, not grepping. *This is the deriver rule landing on my own audit within the hour of my citing it: before writing a deriver, ask what makes a member a member. Here the answer is a property no regex tests.* **NAMED CANDIDATES for a proper read, not a claim about them:** `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd`, `m88kexctaildefault` -- all three cited in one sentence as filed documented-only, none carrying that in the row. **The other six flagged rows are probably noise and are NOT claimed.** **NO CHECKER PROPOSED.** A proximity grep would fire on ~9 rows with a majority false-positive rate, which is how a check gets switched off -- this project's own recorded reason for declining the stale-count checker. What is cheap and reliable is a HABIT at the point of decision: **before opening a round on any row, grep the CHANGELOG and `regress/artifacts/*/` for the row id and read what comes back.** It cost one command here and would have saved the round. *Related in shape, one row over: `sgilinearoob` carried a bare title and an EMPTY note while the 2026-09-02 adjudication referred to "the siblings' overrun" as known -- the class was known to the adjudication and not findable from the row that carries it.* *** THE THREE "NAMED CANDIDATES" DISSOLVE ON A FULL READ. THE POPULATION OF THIS CLASS IS ONE. Corrected within the hour, 2026-09-08, before anyone acted on the list. *** I named `m88kmxmkill`, `m88ktbnd` and `m88kexctaildefault` as probable members because the CHANGELOG says they were *"filed now as **documented-only** LOW rows"*. **Reading the whole sentence changes it:** *"three rows this round CITED were never FILED ... filed now as documented-only LOW rows **RATHER THAN CITED AS IF THEY EXISTED**."* **The disposition being recorded there is FILING -- creating rows that had been cited without existing -- not a prohibition on coding them.** "Documented-only" describes their EVIDENCE state, which is the ordinary condition of an open row, and not a DO-NOT-CODE. `sgitexindex`'s ruling was explicit and adversative: *"DO NOT CODE and DO NOT DROP."* **And checking the rows settles it a second way: all three have EMPTY state_notes.** That makes them members of `baretitle` -- *"20 of 55 OPEN rows are a bare title with an EMPTY note"* -- which is a DIFFERENT row, already filed. A bare row cannot be carrying a ruling it does not carry. > **SO THIS CLASS HAS A POPULATION OF ONE, AND THAT ONE IS FIXED.** The near-miss was real and the > lesson stands; the *scale* I implied was not. *Twice in one hour I named a population from a proximity grep and had to withdraw it -- nine rows, then three. The class is defined by "a DISPOSITION decided elsewhere that the row does not carry", and neither a grep nor a partial read can test that. **The honest form of this row is: one measured instance, a habit that prevents it, and NO claim about how often it recurs.**open

n2n2 timer.c: no upper limit on a requested timer frequency (panel discovery)An2 timer.c: no upper limit on a requested timer frequency (panel discovery) — commits: 863d238 b9daca1 cdc4849 — REVIEWED AND FOLLOWED UP: 863d238 (round) + b9daca1 (records) + cdc4849 (follow-up). Eight of nine seats answered; none found anything wrong with the three shipped fixes -- the domain clamp, the catch-up bound, the RTC narrowing and the above-the-early-out placement were each confirmed by every seat that could trace them. EVERY DEFECT FOUND WAS IN THE INSTRUMENT OR THE RECORDS. Detector 14 -> 24 rows; gate 2 148 -> 157 checks; census 13 mutants, 13 killed, 0 survived, 0 faults. The generalisable finding: reading a constant from the header defeats transcription drift AND creates blindness to the constant itself, so a row must also assert an absolute consequence. Regression review batched to Sunday night per P12. [A: the diff under review was mine, disclosed.] — witness: harness:offline differential of the SAME driver against `git show 39748e3:src/core/timer.c` -- 12 rows on t->interval == 1.0/t->freq, 0 fails on shipped, 5 fails on upstream. NOT a rung-2-4 witness and must not be read as one: it is a rung-1 direct-call detector, which the ladder says is NEVER a reproduction. It proves the row was real (not vacuous) and that the defect is gone; it does not prove the path was guest-reachable -- and separately grep shows t->freq is read NOWHERE outside timer.c, so the guest could never have observed it.closed

Research (fix proposals)✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — REFRAMED THE ROUND: the panel's 300:1 spread on the ceiling is itself evidence that A FIXED CEILING IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT - the measured harm is iterations per signal, and even the largest proposed ceiling leaves ~153,846 of them. The catch-up CAP is the protection; the ceiling is domain normalisation. Also: the report belongs at the CLAMP SITE (device context, where fatal() is already idiom), not in the handler - and the SIGALRM hazard codex worried about does not exist there. NaN is caught by NEGATING the comparisons that must exist anyway, at zero marginal cost: A FREE GUARD AT A TRUST BOUNDARY NEEDS NO REACHABILITY PROOF. Committed against shipping the loop bound alone, because interval=0 would then burn the cap every signal for ever. — evidence: pipeline/evidence/n2/research/fable5_2026-08-16.md✓2026-08-16 — CONFIRMED — MEASURED EVERYTHING, AND OVERTURNED TWO PROPOSALS. Built the offline driver and proved timer.c CAN be driven in the diff_*.c idiom (one stub: gettimeofday). CENSUS: emulated_hz is an int, so INT_MAX bounds every legitimate request - the ceiling is DERIVED, not picked. POLICY TABLE: 'drop missed ticks' is NOT A POLICY BUT A DEFECT (it caps every timer at 65 Hz - a 100 Hz timer runs at rate 0.65 with no burst at all); the flagship's cap of 65536 BREAKS a legitimate 4e7 Hz timer (1.0000 -> 0.1065); 2^20 is the smallest power of two that leaves every legitimate case BIT-IDENTICAL to shipped. And clamping at :137 alone is not just insufficient but A REGRESSION - it loses idempotence on five of six classes because the early-out then compares a clamped record against a raw request. Caught its own first probe (it held time fixed and would have cleared the defect). — evidence: pipeline/evidence/n2/research/opus_measured_2026-08-16.md✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — NORMALISE AND REPORT excessive rates rather than silently clamping; guard intervals; bound the catch-up; clamp RTC values BEFORE narrowing to int. b118Lb118L A disk that fails to be added stays on the listb118L A disk that fails to be added stays on the list — HOLD: FILE - no measurable effect until a caller survives — Split from b118. The disk is linked before several failure returns, so a half-built entry can remain. Both callers exit on failure today and a null file pointer is guarded, so a fix has no measurable effect yet. Worth doing when a non-exiting caller appears. — witness: none -- TRUE but NOT OBSERVABLE. Established by reading 2026-08-27: both call sites terminate the process on failure and nothing walks the disk list in between, so no witness at any rung can exist without first adding a caller that survives the error. — note: *** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27, established by READING under the machine embargo -- no build needed, and none would help. *** **THE CLAIM IS TRUE, and the asymmetry is unmistakable rather than arguable.** `diskimage_add()` (`src/disk/diskimage.c:1631-2104`) links the new disk into the chain at `:1822-1830`. **Six `return -1` exits sit AFTER that link** -- `:1964`, `:1980`, `:1991`, `:2074`, `:2088`, `:2099` -- and not one of them unlinks `d`. The most reachable is the plain `fopen` failure at `:1984-1991`: a disk whose file cannot be opened is left on `machine->first_diskimage` with `d->f == NULL`. **What makes it clearly unintended rather than a design choice: the PRE-link failures clean up correctly.** `:1803` does `free(d)` before the link exists. So the function frees on early failure and leaks-onto-the-list on late failure -- the split falling exactly at the link point, which is the signature of checks added after the link rather than of a decision. *** BUT IT IS NOT OBSERVABLE, AND THE CENSUS IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN SAMPLED. *** `grep -rnw diskimage_add` over `src/` returns **8 references, of which exactly TWO are calls**: * `main.c:707` -- on `< 0` prints `Aborting.` and `return 1` (`:708-709`), with NO disk cleanup between; * `emul_parse.c:558` -- on `< 0` calls **`exit(1)`** (`:561`). **Both terminate the process immediately.** There is no debugger or runtime path that adds a disk to a live machine (0 hits in `src/core/debugger*.c`), so the stale entry cannot outlive the call. **The one second-order route was checked and is also closed:** a shutdown walker would dereference the half-built entry (`d->f == NULL`). `atexit` appears **once** in the whole tree -- `emul.c:913`, `atexit(fix_console)` -- which restores terminal state and never touches the disk chain. *That check is the reason this is recorded as latent rather than as a possible NULL dereference at exit.* **DISPOSITION: TRUE, LATENT, NOT FIXED.** Unlinking on the late failures is a few lines and would be tidier, but the addition licence wants a measured delta or a transferred warrant and there is neither: the entry is unreachable by construction, so no row could redden on it and no detector could be built that is not vacuous. **It becomes live the moment any caller survives a failed add** -- that is the trigger to re-open this, and it is the thing to check in any round that adds a runtime disk-attach path. closed

Silent corruption or a silent hang surfacing in a driver far from the DMAC, strictly HARDER to diagnose than today's exit(1), which names the mode in one line. * AND THE LATCH MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER: for a hot STATUS register latching is right, but for a STATEFUL OPERATION the first dropped transfer reports and every later one is invisible -- the latch actively SUPPRESSES the evidence of accumulating divergence. So a mechanical pass over 170 sites would ship it at least three more times. * THE ARM, stated so it applies per site: complain-and-continue is safe ONLY when the dropped write's only observable consequence is the register's own value. If the write's PURPOSE is to change how the emulator decodes, translates, transfers or invalidates -- address windows, TLB/cache flushes, DMA descriptors, coherency ops -- dropping it makes the model LIE rather than LAG, and the guest cannot tell. For that class: implement it, or stop honestly with cpu->running = 0 (which unlike exit(1) preserves the debugger and the emulator's own diagnostics) -- NEVER a latched drop. Three meanings, not two. * AND THE ARM VINDICATES THE ROUND'S OWN SITE RATHER THAN BLOCKING IT: INT_ST_MASK IS state-changing (it is an SPL write), BUT the guarded portion -- bits 25..0 -- is MEASURED DEAD, so store-as-is drops nothing and the latched shape is correct at :816. Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — TWO SIDE QUESTIONS SETTLED, and both corrections went in the direction that keeps the substance. (1) THE ASan CLAIM: refuted on its premise, upheld on its conclusion, and a THIRD reason found that neither I nor the reporting seat had. build_asan.sh:38-39 does set -fsanitize=address,undefined, and the artifact carries eleven __ubsan_handle_* imports INCLUDING __ubsan_handle_add_overflow -- the exact handler an int++ overflow calls. So 'no -fsanitize flag' is false; the seat had grepped the CONSUMER (gate_asan_sweep.sh) rather than the PRODUCER. *** But gate 9 still cannot catch this, and the reason I gave (timeout 25 vs a 42.95 s floor) was only half of it: DEVINIT(footbridge) NEVER CREATES A struct timer AT ALL. *** Only a guest write to TIMER_x_LOAD or TIMER_x_CONTROL|ENABLE does, and a construction sweep runs no guest -- so timer_tick0 is never called and the counter never increments, timeout or no timeout. Either reason alone is fatal. (2) THE '~7.9 s FOR FOUR TIMERS' FIGURE: confirmed impossible, and the seat found WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM, which is better than refuting it. 2^31 / (4 x 1048576 x 65) = 7.876 s -- the single-element floor divided by four. The counters are per-timer (:73), each callback increments its own element (:86-92), and the catch-up budget is per-timer too (timer.c:281, inside the per-timer loop), so four timers overflow four DIFFERENT elements at their own rates. True floors: 42.950 s cats (2^31/50,000,000, machine_cats.c:56-57) now measured three times at 43.03/43.10/44.58, and 33.686 s netwinder (2^31/63,750,000, machine_netwinder.c:56). ONE REFINEMENT worth recording: a hard floor of 31.51 s exists from the catch-up ceiling (2^31/68,157,440), but it needs a timer at or above 68.16 MHz, which neither machine's emulated_hz permits. cats's is guarded by `if (== 0)` so a config-file emulated_hz word could reach it; netwinder's is unconditional. Neither is guest-reachable, so severity is unchanged. — evidence: build_asan.sh:38-39; nm of /tmp/gx-asan-head/gxemul; timer.c:281; machine_cats.c:56-57·······

Denominators self-reported by the harnesses: diff_m8820x 46 rows + diff_m8invread 33 rows = 79, with two deliberate @@SELFCHECK@@ FAIL lines in each file as negative controls, so a raw grep of 2 IS the green baseline. *** THE CONTROLS ARE WHAT MAKE THIS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, and they show the blindness is STRUCTURAL: *** M3 (`sar = 0`) reddens D1/D3, proving the harness CAN see a consumer-side SAR defect; M4 (drop the SAR store) reddens E7/E8/G6/G7, proving it CAN see a producer-side one. **Both ends are covered; only the SEAM is blind** -- because every SCR-flush row runs after `fresh()` (which memsets the device, so cpu_nr = cmmu_nr = 0) and issues from cpu0, and at (0,0) every candidate base for `regs` coincides. **M1 IS A LIVE-DEFECT CLASS ON THE SHIPPED RIG, NOT A SHAPE PIN**, and the seat verified the load-bearing fact from source rather than trusting a harness comment: `dev_luna88k.c:926-957` registers BOTH CMMUs on every boot, and `dev_m8820x.c:542-543` maps `addr2 & 1` -> cmmu_nr, so cmmu_nr = 1 is guest-addressable on every luna88k boot -- with the data CMMU taking 318,457 of 613,342 SAR writes (51.9%%). Under M1 **half the machine's PATC flushes never dispatch at all**, which is the silently-under-invalidating TLB the file's own comment calls 'not a cosmetic gap'. (M2, the `(cpu, d)` swap, is by contrast a shape pin: the booting rig is single-CPU.) *** THE COMPOSED ROW IS BUILT AND MEASURED -- THREE ROWS, EACH WITH ITS OWN KILL, NONE DECORATION: *** K1 (matching entry dropped) reddens under M1/M1b; K2 (non-matching entry retained) under M5; K3 (flush from a NON-OWNER cpu) under M2. **The two axes are independent: K1 does not catch M2 and K3 does not catch M1.** The original filing asked for 'cmmu_nr 1 AND from a non-owner CPU'; the measurement shows both halves are load-bearing and neither subsumes the other -- sharper than the filing knew. Goes in diff_m8invread.c, which has the two-cpu/two-cmmu fixture; ~20 lines; prototype committed to the artifact dir. The missing IRQ is READ from the source; that it hangs a real driver forever is an inference. Do not carry the hang as measured. closed

Research (fix proposals)OK2026-08-27 — CONFIRMED — *** THE HARM CLAIM IN THIS ENTRY IS OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED BELOW IT (L4, 2026-08-27). *** The ledger's own `wdcstandby` measurements are a counter-instance: OpenBSD 7.6 reaches BOTH defective arms routinely and COMPLETES boot and shutdown against today's no-interrupt behaviour, 4 of 4. There is no measured hang. Whether a timeout interval is burned is NOT SETTLED. Read 'waits forever' / 'functional hang' below as the hypothesis it was, not as a measurement. VERDICT: PROCEED, one round, two hunks -- on a warrant STRONGER than the brief claimed and a severity WEAKER than the brief claimed. Both corrections are against my own text. *** THE CENSUS IS NOT 3-OF-5 ABORT ARMS. IT IS 11 OF 13 TERMINAL ARMS. *** Every arm that terminates a command -- success or abort -- sets int_assert. The only arms that do not are WRITE and ATAPI_PKT_CMD, where the command is NOT OVER (the interrupt comes later in the data path, and PKT_CMD records its 'no' as a COMMENTED-OUT line) -- plus the two defect arms, which ARE terminal. Five arms carry a `/* TODO: interrupt here? */` hedge and every one resolves to assert. So the two defect arms are the ONLY TERMINAL ARMS IN THE FUNCTION WITH NO INTERRUPT DECISION RECORDED AT ALL -- no assert, no comment. That reads as a question never reached, not a decision to stay silent. *** AND THE STEELMAN'S FACTUAL PREMISE IS FALSE BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN MEASUREMENTS. *** 0xF5 SEC_FREEZE_LOCK -- the SEC arm -- is issued on a plain OpenBSD 7.6/landisk boot with a disk attached (rung 4). 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE -- the default arm -- on every `halt -p`, 4 of 4. A stock guest lifecycle reaches BOTH defective arms routinely. It is not 242 opcodes nobody sends; it is two boot/shutdown opcodes plus a long tail the tree's own header names (WDCC_SMART, WDCC_FLUSHCACHE). nIEN: VERIFIED STRONGER THAN HOPED. `WDCTL_IDS` (0x02) exists in wdcreg.h and is referenced NOWHERE in dev_wdc.c. The model has no nIEN state to be inconsistent with. *** SEVERITY DEMOTED, AND THIS IS AN L4 AGAINST THIS SEAT'S OWN PRIOR ENTRIES. *** My ledger text said 'an interrupt-driven guest waits forever' and 'boot-reachable functional hang'. The ledger holds a MEASURED COUNTER-INSTANCE: the same OpenBSD guest reaches both arms routinely and COMPLETES BOOT AND SHUTDOWN against today's no-interrupt behaviour -- `wdcstandby`, 'the guest swallows it silently', 4 of 4. Whether it burns a timeout interval is NOT SETTLED; nobody timed it. HONEST SEVERITY: routine rung-4 reachability of a protocol violation, measured harm today NONE OBSERVED, hypothesised harm unmeasured. The round is licensed by protocol correctness at trivial cost, not by dramatised harm. *** THE REPRO IS AT THE WRONG REVISION. *** PREFIX_committed_ed3f9cc.out was produced at ed3f9cc; HEAD is cf300c0, four commits and 135 dev_wdc.c lines later. #484 touched the ring producer, not the command switch -- but 'almost certainly unaffected' is exactly what test-first exists to refuse, and the score-names-its-artifact rule forbids citing an ed3f9cc log as this round's pre-fix red. RE-RUN BEFORE ANY EDIT. CLAUSE (d) FOR A FIX THAT ADDS NO PREDICATE -- the mutant is M_latch: put `int_assert = 1` INSIDE the `warned_unimpl_cmd` guard. The first unknown command per device interrupts and every later one hangs again -- exactly what a tidying maintainer writes. *** THE CURRENT SWEEP IS BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION: one fresh device per opcode means the latch is 0 on every leg. *** (The glm seat reached the same finding independently from the packet.) Owed row: two different unimplemented opcodes on ONE device, demanding a wire assert on the SECOND and exactly one fatal line total. M_blanket: hoist a single assert to after the switch -- 'fixes' all 242 and silently breaks the phase protocol for ATAPI_PKT_CMD and WRITE. Owed: negative rows pinning irq == 0 at dispatch for both. That is the de-escalation clause's accept side. THIRD OBSERVABLE: THE DEASSERT EDGE. int_assert is a LEVEL -- the tick re-asserts every tick until a status read clears it. A two-observable sweep cannot tell a completion event from a stuck line. One register read per leg converts the detector from 'an edge happened' to 'the completion protocol works'. ORDER CHANGED: wdcfloodstale FIRST, BY DEADLINE NOT SEVERITY. #485's own targeted gate scores the flood probe, so this round's gate would be BORN RED for a known unrelated cause and mis-attributed to it. Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-19 — CONFIRMED — *** RULED THIS SHOULD BE ITS OWN ROUND, and the ruling is accepted. *** On the reopening rule's objective prong: a detector for this defect must assert 'SETUP within T seconds', which is a WALL-CLOCK ORACLE -- the class this project's records treat as most dangerous -- and the rule admits a second site only with NO NEW ORACLE. It also rejected the ledger's own grouping argument ('both fixes are a dozen lines together') as a SIZE argument, which is not one of the prongs. Separately it found that `timeout=` as I specified it is not enough for the BUILD phase, and that `start_new_session` is what makes killpg safe -- without it the children share the GATE's process group and killpg is gate suicide. Its stated MECHANISM (a blocking post-kill drain) was measured FALSE on POSIX; the conclusion held for a different reason. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260819_232621/✓2026-08-19 — CONFIRMED — DERIVED THE TIMEOUTS FROM MEASUREMENT rather than choosing them: slowest build across all 12 lanes 1.37 s, slowest run 0.31 s, on an idle machine. Recommends build=120 s (~88x) and run=60 s (~190x), SEPARATE, env-overridable -- separate because the diagnoses differ (a two-minute compile means the host is sick; a spinning run is the EXPECTED mutant outcome) and because the SETUP message must name the phase. On margin it cited this project's own gate_ab, which uses 3x and measurably false-FAILed a 45-minute battery under load, so 3x is KNOWN-INSUFFICIENT here. It measured the process-group kill both ways: run(timeout=) returned at 3.00 s and left the spinner alive; Popen(start_new_session)+killpg reaped the whole tree, child pgid 32 against the gate's 11, so killpg provably cannot reach the gate. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** DO NOT DROP -- RETITLE. THE ROW'S OWN TITLE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, AND ITS PROPOSED FIX LOCATION IS THE ONE PLACE THE FIX CANNOT GO. *** dev_vr41xx.c:606 is `int hz = RTCL1_L_HZ / idata` -- an INTEGER divide with RTCL1_L_HZ = 0x8000. The entire domain idata >= 32769 collapses to hz = 0, which timer_clamp_freq then floors SILENTLY to 1e-8 Hz: one tick per 3.17 years. *** A GUEST ASKING FOR 0.5 Hz GETS A TIMER THAT NEVER FIRES. *** Not 'lands below the floor' -- destroyed BEFORE timer.c ever sees it. Flooring 0 -> 1e-8 in timer.c is CORRECT; a floor complaint there would make this noisier while still wrong. RUNG-3 WITNESS BUILT TODAY, two subtypes, unmodified in-tree machine, no device_add, every planted word disassembled and text-compared before stepping: hpcmips/z50 (VR4121) cold debugger, no boot LIVENESS idata=0x00008000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 1 Hz ] control green SUBJECT idata=0x00010000 -> [ vr41xx: rtc interrupts at 0 Hz ] guest asked 0.5 Hz Identical on mobilepro770. Both required controls present: liveness AND device signature ((vr41xx@0xb000000)+0xd0 plus the device's own message -- RAM produces no line at all). The encoding guard earned its keep: the first run REFUSED a verdict because the expected mnemonic strings were wrong, and reported SETUP rather than passing. TWO OTHER LEGS MEASURED, one FALSE: *** footbridge is REFUTED *** -- bounded below by emulated_hz / 2^32, so emulated_hz would have to be < 42.95 Hz; on a 33 MHz machine the worst case is 0.0077 Hz, six orders of magnitude above the floor. The jazz leg is much weaker than filed: 64-bit store only (any 32-bit store bottoms out at 2.33e-7 Hz, 23x above floor). THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT, WHICH DOES MERGE: dev_vr41xx.c:614 `case 0xd2: /* RTCL1_H_REG_W */ break;` is a NO-OP. vr_rtcreg.h:87-88 names RTCL1_L/H_REG_W as the halves of a 32-bit reload, so the high half is silently discarded -- and since L is 16 bits, THE SUB-1-Hz DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE DOMAIN THAT NEEDS H. Same device, same class, same oracle, one fix design. Does NOT merge with n4/#429 despite both being 'a guest rate narrowed': different device, OPPOSITE END of the domain, different mechanism (wide-domain ceiling vs integer-division floor collapse), new oracle. — evidence: rung-3 probe on hpcmips/z50 + mobilepro770; dev_vr41xx.c:606,614·······

Two full LSB/MSB pairs after one mode write produced THREE recomputes -- 97 Hz, **0 Hz**, 97 Hz -- where hardware does two. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the first is what makes it matter: it transiently drives the counter to ZERO, i.e. straight into the i8253zero defect, FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER PROGRAMS COUNT 0. That inverts the reachability finding on i8253zero, where no available guest asks for count 0 directly. Second: if the second pair's LSB is nonzero it is SILENTLY LOST -- intending 0x3055 the device holds 0x3000. MUT-B is a REAL break, not an unobservable one: on the datasheet's own convention-1 sequence (Control Word, write LSB, Control Word, write LSB, write MSB) the counter reads back 0x1140 instead of 0x4011 and the guest is given 265 Hz where it asked for 73. *** AND IT NAMED THE ASYMMETRY AS LUCK RATHER THAN DESIGN: *** MUT-A is caught only because PROLOGUE's A1 signature read leaves rd_msb[0] at 1, giving the body's MODE<-0x34 something to rewind. It also measured Q4 false in the direction that mattered (odd parity gives 0x9c00, not 0x0000), grepped the local datasheet to show it never uses the phrase 'read/write flip-flop' at all, and produced the [[pitclobber]] witness. The file's own header carries the author's TODO at line 35: '(Split counter[] into reset value and current value.)' So d->counter[] is the PROGRAMMED RELOAD VALUE, FROZEN. gxemul models the timer's RATE (timer_add / timer_update_frequency) and its INTERRUPTS, but never a counting register. WHY THAT REFRAMES THE FIX: OpenBSD's microtime() latches and reads the counter to INTERPOLATE SUB-TICK TIME. If a 'correct' latch returns a constant, the guest's interpolated time does not advance within a tick -- a different wrong answer from 0, and arguably a WORSE one because it is plausible rather than obviously broken. So the candidate that looks most correct (return the programmed value) may be the one that misleads a guest furthest, and the honest round may be smaller than the row implies: make the latch not-an-error and not-a-flood, and DOCUMENT that sub-tick interpolation is unmodelled. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-21 — CONFIRMED — *** THE ORACLE DESIGN IS THE POINT: it asks the REAL m88k_translate_v2p() what an address resolves to, rather than re-implementing the BATC formula in the detector. *** Computing the right answer in the harness and comparing it against the device's array asserts something STRICTLY WEAKER than 'the device's array is what translation reads' -- which is exactly the fixed-point-oracle shape the flagship pass named as escape family #1 this morning. Three controls rather than one, so 'the expected paddr came back' cannot be a constant. *** FINDING 1: A MUTANT ESCAPED EVERYTHING, AND THE ROUND'S OWN HARDENING CREATED IT. *** Widening the translator's virtual match from 0xfff80000 to 0xfff00000 survived all 45 rows and both differentials. The first port table used CONSECUTIVE LBAs (0x100..0x107), which caught that mutant BY ACCIDENT -- port n's address hit port n-1's entry. Scattering the LBAs to close a DIFFERENT hole (a masked top bit no row could see) SILENTLY REMOVED THAT ACCIDENTAL COVERAGE, and only re-running the whole census after the fixture change surfaced it. That is a general lesson worth more than the row: A FIXTURE CHANGE CAN DELETE COVERAGE NOBODY KNEW THEY HAD, and no row goes red to say so. Closed by F17, which asserts the block boundary EXPLICITLY -- first byte in, last byte in, byte below, byte above, per port -- instead of relying on an occupied neighbour. F17 is currently the ONLY row defending that property. FINDING 2: the seat's own chosen mutant escaped -- c-> vs cpu-> on the purge callback POINTER -- and it graded it honestly as an EQUIVALENT MUTANT and a SHAPE PIN rather than a live defect, because cpu_m88k.c:121-122 gives every m88k cpu the same function with no branch. But it checked whether that is ARCHITECTURAL and found it is not: cpu_mips.c:120-133 and cpu_ppc.c:122-135 install DIFFERENT callbacks per cpu width. Closed with a second spy and row J6. It also SIMULATED selfmutant.py's tree shape exactly -- symlink mirror plus one real file -- to prove the new #include resolves and both row-ids still name exactly one row, WITHOUT running a gate. Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-22 — CLOSE (assess and review), both questions answered. *** Q1 (joint vs guard-only): NEITHER a fixed recipe nor an exception. *** Restate the rule by its DISCRIMINATOR: the accept row must redden under the LEAST-OBSERVABLE growth form that is measured NON-EQUIVALENT at that site, found by the reading the rule already mandates. Where the latch operand can mask the guard (#449), guard-only is equivalent and JOINT is the least-observable non-equivalent form. Where the latch operand is a compile-time constant the guard cannot feed (#451), guard-only is non-equivalent AND quieter than joint -- the harder form, so the one to build. 'Build the form the latch operand does not mask' is the correct generalisation, and it is NOT a rule change: it is the rule's own reason made explicit, of which JOINT was the first measured instance. Cost stays one mutant per predicate; where the reading is uncertain, build both -- a spare build is cheaper than a wrong reading. *** Q2 (ask again once the table is clean): ADOPT, capped at ONE ask-again per detector per round. *** It is not the #392 chain: #392 was unbounded fix-of-fix passes with no stop condition; this is a single extra adversarial query against a CLEAN table with a measured stop. The yield is measured -- 2 of the 5 rows #451 added came only from the fifteenth-mutant ask -- and the mechanism is real: a clean table redirects seats away from the shapes the author already covered. panelseatlabelpanelseatlabel panel.sh reports a 403 quota wall as 'RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)' and its tally omits the substitute transportApanelseatlabel panel.sh reports a 403 quota wall as 'RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)' and its tally omits the substitute transport — commits: faffad7 — both defects verified discharged against LIVE panel output, not by reading the code — witness: none needed -- both are visible in _scratchpad/panel_20260824_231824/SEATS.txt — note: *** BOTH DEFECTS WERE ALREADY FIXED BY `faffad7` AND THIS ROW SAT OPEN. MEASURED on `_scratchpad/panel_20260824_231824`. Two separate reporting defects in the seat check, neither of which changes a disposition but both of which mislead a later reader. (1) The kimi CLI failed with `provider.auth_error: 403 ... usage limit for this billing cycle` and SEATS.txt printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)`. The carrier draws a sharp line between failure classes -- a WALL you wait out versus a REFUSED CONNECTION one command fixes -- and a status code named wrongly is how that line gets blurred. (2) It printed `SEATS: 6/7 scriptable` while `ollama_kimi.txt` (17,382 bytes) sat answered in the same directory: the check counts the CLI seat only, so a seat that is walled on one transport and LIVE on another is tallied purely as a loss. That undercounts the panel exactly when the substitution is working. Note the related counting trap the carrier already records: the two Agent seats leave NO FILE, so any file-based count under-reports by two more. *** THE THREE CLI SEATS HAVE DIFFERENT WRITE BEHAVIOURS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MAKES A SIZE CHECK MEANINGFUL MID-RUN. Measured 2026-08-25 on the #463 records audit. *** `codex` STREAMS its reasoning, so its file grows continuously and was 311 KB while still working. `grok` streams slowly -- 229 then 357 bytes, each sample a partial sentence. **`agy` writes NOTHING until it finishes**: its file sat at EXACTLY 0 bytes for minutes with a live `agy.exe` (pid 23548), then lands in one shot -- 8,044 bytes on the pass-2 panel. So for agy, and ONLY for agy, a zero-byte file is the normal mid-run state, and it is indistinguishable BY SIZE from the plain-`&` failure the carrier records (where a killed child leaves a zero-byte log). **The discriminator is the PROCESS, not the file**: `tasklist | grep agy` settles it in one command. Note the related trap already recorded -- check `tasklist` WITHOUT `/v`, because `/v` changes the column layout and a follow-up check using it once reported no processes when three were alive, nearly destroying a true positive. *** AND THE THIRD DEFECT IS IN THE FIX: A WALL-KEYWORD CHECK PRODUCES A FALSE POSITIVE ON ANY SEAT THAT READS THIS LEDGER. Measured 2026-08-25. *** After widening the seat check to catch the quota/403/429/stalled family, it scored a LIVE codex seat as WALLED. The seat was mid-answer at 225 KB and still running; what the check matched was **this project's own prose about walls** -- the rows describing a 403 mislabelled as 429, and the empty-response class -- echoed back by a seat that had been asked to read the ledger. **A keyword detector applied to a document ABOUT that keyword cannot work**, and the tasks most likely to trip it are exactly the records and matrix audits this project now runs routinely. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS POSITION AND TERMINATION, not presence -- which is what the carrier already says (`verify the CONTENT, never the size`) applied one level down: a walled seat's notice is the LAST thing in the file with nothing substantive after it, and the answer either ends mid-sentence or is the echoed brief. A live seat mentions a wall in the middle of a large body of its own reasoning and keeps going. `seat_verdicts.py` already uses a POSITION discriminator for exactly this reason; the seat check should borrow it rather than grep the whole tail. Cheapest interim guard, and it costs one line: **if the process is still alive, it is not walled** -- `tasklist` settles it, and this project has now used that test twice in one session (once to prove a 0-byte agy file was buffering rather than dead). *** SECOND MEASURED INSTANCE 2026-08-25 (`panel_20260825_112845`), AND THE SECOND DEFECT IS WORSE THAN THIS ROW SAYS -- IT IS NOT A TALLY PROBLEM, IT IS A LOST SEAT. *** Defect (1) reproduced exactly: the kimi CLI returned `provider.auth_error: 403 You've reached your usage limit for this billing cycle` and SEATS.txt printed `*** RATE-LIMITED (HTTP 429)`. Same wrong status code, same blurring of the wall-versus-transport line the carrier draws. *** BUT DEFECT (2) IS NOT MERELY AN UNDERCOUNT. *** This row records that the tally omits a substitute transport that ANSWERED. Measured today: `panel.sh` **never fires the substitute at all**. It launches exactly one kimi seat -- the CLI, at `:222` -- and its three Ollama seats are hardcoded to `$OLLAMA1/2/3` (glm, deepseek, minimax) at `:270/:274/:278`. Meanwhile `curl -s localhost:11434/api/tags` lists **`kimi-k3:cloud` as LIVE**, and three earlier panels (`panel_20260824_191634`, `panel_20260824_231824`, `panel_20260825_000248`) each hold an `ollama_kimi.txt`, so the seat was being fired BY HAND and then stopped being. *** SO THE HONEST STATUS OF THIS SEAT IS NOT "DOWN". *** kimi's CLI transport is walled; kimi itself is reachable and idle. Every panel since the CLI wall has silently run one seat short while a working transport sat unused -- which is the seat-failure-counted-as-agreement shape with an extra step, because here the roster does not even record a failure to investigate. RECOVERED IMMEDIATELY: the seat was fired by hand onto the live `wdcflood` pass-1 panel dir as `ollama_kimi.txt`. FIX OWED IN panel.sh, deliberately NOT APPLIED YET because panel.sh was RUNNING when this was found and bash reads a script incrementally -- editing a running script is its own defect class. The fix: fire `kimi-k3:cloud` as a fourth Ollama seat, and have the seat check report the CLI wall and the substitute SEPARATELY so a walled transport with a live substitute reads as one seat answered, not as a loss. Also correct `429` to the actual status text rather than a hardcoded code. *** AND THE GENERAL RULE THIS EARNS: WHEN A SEAT WALLS, ASK WHETHER THE MODEL IS REACHABLE BY ANOTHER TRANSPORT BEFORE RECORDING IT DOWN. *** The carrier already separates a wall from a refused connection; this is the third class -- **one transport walled, another live** -- and it is the only one where the seat is available the whole time and nobody asks.closed

scoreclaimhexscoreclaimhex check_score_claims reads a slash-separated HEX LIST as a score claim, and reports a stale score that was never writtenAscoreclaimhex check_score_claims reads a slash-separated HEX LIST as a score claim, and reports a stale score that was never written — commits: df0dfcc — author self-review disclosed; negative-controlled both directions and coverage verified not to shrink — witness: measured -- _scratchpad/precommit_463.log, section U, three FAIL lines — note: *** THE FIX IS IN THIS COMMIT; THE ROW CLOSES IN THE NEXT ONE WITH THE REAL HASH. *** Section L correctly refused a `PENDING` placeholder -- a closed row must name a hash, and the hash does not exist until the commit lands. That is the documented two-step, not a defect. *** FIXED 2026-08-26: one character, `x` added to the negative lookbehind. *** `check_score_claims.py` now reads `(?<![\dx/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])`. The `00` in `0x00/0x10` is preceded by `x`, which the old `(?<![\d/])` allowed, so a slash-separated HEX LIST parsed as a score claim. **NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE LANDING, which is the whole discipline for a regex change:** five real score claims (13/13, 26/26, 8/32, "52 / 52", 16/16) all still match; two hex lists no longer do; zero regressions. **AND MEASURED ON THE FILE THAT PRODUCED THE ORIGINAL FALSE FAIL** rather than on synthetic strings: over the whole of `asic_badaddr_probe.py` the old regex found 11 matches and the new one finds 7. **The four killed are `04/4`, `08/4`, `10/4`, `18/4` -- every one a fragment of a hex offset. The kept are `12/12` and `12/13` -- every real claim, intact.** *** COVERAGE VERIFIED NOT TO HAVE SHRUNK, because 'the false positive is gone' and 'the checker stopped looking' produce the same output: *** the gate still carries 12 rows naming the probe, the checker still reports SCORE_CLAIMS_PASS over 19 pinned probes, and the docstring still yields its 5 genuine `12/13` claims under BOTH regexes. A fix that silently drops a probe from coverage would have read as success. *The row's own diagnosis was correct and complete; nothing in it needed revising. Worth noting because most rows worked today needed their evidence corrected -- this one was filed right the first time.* MEASURED 2026-08-25 during #463's pre-commit. Section U reported THREE stale score claims in `asic_badaddr_probe.py`'s docstring -- `claims 00/0`, `10/0`, `20/0`, pin is 12. **None of them was ever written.** All three come from ONE line of ordinary prose: `bases 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30`, a slash-separated list of hex group bases. The pattern `(?<![\d/])(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)(?![\d/%])` sees `0x00/0x10` and takes `00` / `0`. *** IT IS A FALSE FAIL, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE FAILURE FROM THE ONE SECTION U EXISTS TO CATCH, AND IS STILL EXPENSIVE. *** A gate that reddens on prose trains its reader to explain away red rows, which is exactly how a REAL stale score would then get waved through. And this project writes `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` constantly -- the fourth-word invariant is naturally expressed that way -- so it will recur in any file section U checks. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, and deliberately: #463 reworded its own docstring to use commas, because the round's material is unshipped (L1) while `check_score_claims.py` is a shared gate and editing it is a different scope. **The workaround is also the weaker fix** -- it relies on every future author avoiding a natural notation. THE REAL FIX is one lookbehind: reject a match whose left digit run is preceded by `0x` or `0X`, i.e. require the numerator not be part of a hex literal. Note the existing escape hatch (`write '<N>-row' on the same line`) does NOT help here, because the denominator the checker invented is 0 and nobody would write `0-row`.closed

So it pinned a property still true afterwards. **It was red on the committed build, which is exactly why it looked like a reproduction.** > **A detector aimed at a primitive cannot verify a fix made in its caller.** Replaced by a row that drives the ARM through `dev_wdc_access`, with the SCSI stub made CONTROLLABLE (a file-static byte count, zero by default) so it stays inert for every other row. That primitive has no internal bound and **the fix did not give it one** -- the repair is in the CALLER. So the row pins a property that is still true after the fix, and it can never go green from it. > **A DETECTOR AIMED AT A PRIMITIVE CANNOT VERIFY A FIX MADE IN ITS CALLER.** The row is not wrong about the primitive; it is measuring the wrong level. **It looked like a reproduction because it went red on the committed build -- and it did, for a reason the fix does not address.** That is the same shape as a red-for-the-wrong-reason, one level up: right defect, wrong instrument. **WHAT THE ROW MUST BECOME:** an assertion at the INITIAL ARM -- after the arm runs, the ring holds at most 32768 bytes. That needs the arm driven, and the arm sits behind `res == 1` from `diskimage_scsicommand`, whose stub currently returns 0. **A packet-command fixture is owed**, and it must be selectable per row: Opus's review warns that a stub returning a fabricated transfer would corrupt the RE-ARM row's carefully placed state. *** CONSEQUENCE FOR SHIPPING, stated plainly: the re-arm half is fixed AND covered; the ring half is fixed and UNCOVERED. *** Vacuity floor clause (a) requires a row that fails pre-fix and passes post-fix, and this half has none. **#473 is not shippable as a whole until the arm-level row exists** -- and shipping the re-arm half alone is exactly the split the adjudication rejected, because a bounded push without a working re-arm was the dangerous ordering. *** ADJUDICATED 2026-08-27: ONE ROUND, TWO ROW IDS -- and my coupling analysis was WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The corrections matter more than the ruling. *** **THE RULING:** ship design (d) whole, in one round, closing two row ids. The re-arm rewrite is **not a second site joining the round** -- it is a CORRECTNESS PRECONDITION of the settled fix, so the join clause is never engaged. Bound and refill are inseparable: a bounded push with the zeroing left in place breaks a band that works today, and a refill without the bound double-pushes bytes already in the ring. One function, one state machine, and the rule's own purpose-parenthetical *(so one fix design covers both)* is literally this case. **Two ROW IDS regardless**, per the carrier's own warning about a queue id covering two defects. The re-arm defect is filed as [[wdcrearmzero]], closed by the same diff, cross-referenced, with its own pre-edit witness. *** CORRECTION 1 -- MY PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND IT WAS THE ONE THE WHOLE SCOPE QUESTION RESTED ON. *** I wrote *today those transfers 'work' by overrunning the ring*. **They do not work today.** The re-arm zeroing is LIVE: a >64 KB transfer delivers its first 32768 bytes, the re-arm zeroes, the byte count reports 0, and **no path ever completes the command.** The stall band exists NOW, unaided by any fix -- and the (64K, 256.5K] band never overruns the ring and is still broken. **So no fix ordering 'converts corruption into a hang'; the hang is already there.** *** CORRECTION 2 -- AND THE DANGER RAN THE OTHER WAY. *** Bounding the push alone would not trade corruption for a hang; it would **INJECT NEW SILENT CORRUPTION into the (32K, 64K] band that works today.** `wdc_get_inbuf` returns `(uint64_t)-1` on an empty ring, so a 50 KB transfer would complete with SUCCESS and an 18 KB tail of `0xff` -- **precisely the MAXPHYS-sized band real drivers use.** My proposed 'safe' first round was the most dangerous option on the table. *** CORRECTION 3 -- MY (a)-RULES-OUT WARRANT CITED THE WRONG LINES. *** I cited the multi-byte assembly of a single read. **The load-bearing mechanism is the empty-ring `-1` delivery** -- that is what makes bounding-alone deliver garbage. Conclusion unchanged, warrant replaced. *A wrong reason gets reused.* *** CORRECTION 4 -- WITNESS KIND. *** My reproduction pushes 514 blocks by DIRECT CALLS to `wdc_addtoinbuf`. That is rung 1: a **DETECTOR, not a witness.** The round still owes a guest-driven reproduction, and the ledger field must say so rather than implying a rung it does not have -- the same error I made on `b115` and had corrected there. *** WHERE THE ADJUDICATION IS ITSELF WRONG, checked because two readings disagreed: *** it says `logical_block_size` is *512 or 2048 by machine* and that 2048-block machines reach ~128 MB / ~511x. **The 2048 branch is `#if 0`'d** (`diskimage.c:1884-1889`) and `:1890` sets 512 unconditionally. The cited range `:1886-1890` sits INSIDE the disabled block plus the line after it -- **read without its guard**, the class the carrier warns about. My 32 MB / 127.7x figure is correct FOR THIS TREE. **But the point underneath it is accepted: the figure named no deriver.** DERIVER: `READ(10)` count is 16-bit (`(cmd[7] << 8) + cmd[8]`, `diskimage_scsicmd.c`), times `logical_block_size` = 512 unconditionally today, = 33,553,920 bytes; ring = `512*(WDC_MAX_SECTORS+1)` = 262,656. **Re-derive rather than quote, and re-check the `#if 0` if the CD block size is ever enabled -- then the ratio really does quadruple.** *** A SCOPE COUPLING FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING, PUT TO THE ADJUDICATOR RATHER THAN DECIDED. Fixing the push ALONE would STALL transfers that previously 'worked' by corrupting. *** **The convergent design, in one sentence (minimax put it best): the device ALREADY moves data in <=32768-byte DRQ chunks -- the re-arm proves it -- and THE INITIAL ARM IS THE ONLY PLACE THAT PUSHES THE WHOLE TRANSFER.** So the fix is to make the initial arm behave like the re-arm. *** BUT THE RE-ARM IS ITSELF BROKEN, AND THE TWO ARE COUPLED. *** `dev_wdc.c:758-759`: ```c if (d->atapi_len > 32768) d->atapi_len = 0; /* the INITIAL arm clamps to 32768 here */ ``` So when the remainder exceeds 32768 the re-arm reports **zero bytes remaining while `atapi_received < data_in_len`** -- phase DATAIN with length 0. Verified independently by agy; deepseek's answer says outright *fix the re-arm zeroing*. > **THE COUPLING: bound the push without fixing the re-arm and any transfer above ~64 KB STALLS** -- the first chunk drains, the re-arm zeroes, nothing more arrives. Today those transfers 'work' by overrunning the ring and silently corrupting. **Fixing one alone converts silent corruption into a visible hang.** **THE SCOPE QUESTION, and I am not deciding it alone:** the reopening rule takes ONE site per round, admitting a second only in the SAME semantic class covered by the SAME detector. These look like DIFFERENT classes -- *ring overrun destroys data* versus *the reported length is wrong* (the truthfulness class the file's own comments trace to `#283` and `#338`). But they are coupled such that fixing the first alone is a behaviour regression. **Three readings, for the adjudicator:** 1. ONE round -- the coupling makes them one repair, and shipping half is worse than shipping neither; 2. TWO rounds, re-arm FIRST -- fix the truthfulness defect, then bound the push on a re-arm that works; 3. ONE round bounding the push AND accepting the stall, filing the re-arm -- **rejected on its face**: it knowingly ships a hang. *Recorded before any edit. One legal 514-block transfer overwrites the guest's unread data and the guest reads wrong-offset bytes. *** THE TWO-ROW SPLIT PROVED ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: the latch row PASSES while the corruption row FAILS. *** The warning DID fire -- one store too early, as the ring became full. **A single row conflating them would have looked half-right and hidden which half.** **TWO APPARATUS FAULTS CAUGHT BEFORE THEY BECAME FALSE RESULTS:** 1. **A SEGFAULT that looked exactly like the defect.** `inbuf` is a POINTER allocated in DEVINIT with `zeroed_alloc()`, not an array -- a zeroed struct leaves it NULL. Only rule 4 (*did it fail for the reason under test?*) separated a crash from a reproduction. 2. **The `\\n` backslash trap again** -- a Python-written escape became a LITERAL newline inside a C string literal, breaking the build. Fixed with `chr(92)`, the carrier's prescribed remedy. *Hit repeatedly today despite being written down.* *** THE TRANSFER CEILING, MEASURED -- it bears directly on the fix options: *** ``` READ(10) count 16-bit: (cmd[7] << 8) + cmd[8] max blocks 65535 block size 512 even for CD-ROMs (the 2048 branch is #if 0'd) max transfer 33,553,920 bytes = 32 MB SCSI_MAX_XFER_BYTES 64 MB -- does NOT bound this ring capacity 262,656 bytes = 256.5 KB RATIO 127.7x the ring ``` **So 'grow the ring to the largest reachable transfer' means a 256 KB -> 32 MB allocation PER DEVICE.** That is not a clamp question, it is a 128-fold growth, and it effectively rules the option out -- recorded so the panel argues about the remaining ones. **NO BOUNDED-PUSH IDIOM EXISTS in the file** -- there is no capacity check anywhere in the push path -- so unlike `#472` there is NO in-tree warrant to transfer. The reproduction is DESIGNED, COSTED and CHEAP -- and it needs no device dispatch at all. *** **Every fact re-verified from source today:** ``` :47 WDC_MAX_SECTORS 512 :48 WDC_INBUF_SIZE (512*(512+1)) = 262,656 = EXACTLY 513 blocks :922 atapi_len = data_in_len :923 for (int j=0; j<atapi_len; j++) wdc_addtoinbuf(...) <- UNBOUNDED :926 if (atapi_len > 32768) atapi_len = 32768; <- AFTER the loop ``` *** THE ROOT CAUSE IS IN THE CODE'S OWN WORDS at `:187`: *** *"head == tail means BOTH empty and full here -- there is no [way to distinguish]"*. **That ambiguity is why the latched warning at `:194` fires as the ring FILLS rather than when data is LOST** -- the destroying store is the next one, and it is silent. `:217` names this row explicitly. *** THE REPRODUCTION NEEDS NO DEVICE DISPATCH, WHICH IS WHY IT IS CHEAP: *** * `wdc_addtoinbuf(struct wdc_data *d, int c)` (`:180`) and `wdc_get_inbuf(struct wdc_data *d)` (`:207`) take ONLY the device struct; * `inbuf[]`, `inbuf_head`, `inbuf_tail`, `warned_inbuf_overrun` are all fields of that struct (`:67`, `:68`, `:113`), so a **ZEROED struct is a valid empty ring**; * `regress/diff_wdc_identify.c` already `#include`s `dev_wdc.c` and builds `struct wdc_data` accessors plus a `stub_machine`/`stub_cpu` pair -- so the fixture exists. **THE SHAPE:** zero a `struct wdc_data`; push 514 blocks' worth of position-encoded bytes; pop and assert. **Correct: block 1's bytes come back first. Broken: block 514's content appears where block 1 should be, then `(uint64_t)-1` for the rest.** **AND THE ORACLE MUST BE POSITIONAL, NOT A COUNT** -- unlike `#472`'s. Here the ring returns *wrong-offset data*, so encode position into the bytes and assert WHICH block comes back, not how many of something there are. *** TWO ROWS OWED AT MINIMUM, because the warning and the corruption are different events: *** one that the latched warning fires exactly once as the ring fills, and one that the data at the tail is block 1's. **A single row conflating them would go green on a fix that silences the warning without fixing the overwrite.** *Blocked only on `#472` landing first -- same file family, and two uncommitted rounds at once is how a bisect stops working.* *** INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27 by an adversarial pass that tried to break all four steps and failed. ONE WORD OF THE CLAIM IS WRONG, the reachability is STRONGER than filed, and the corruption SHAPE is sharper. (This row was already filed and escalated -- treat today's work as re-verification, not discovery.) *** **ARITHMETIC HOLDS.** `dev_wdc.c:47-48`: `WDC_MAX_SECTORS 512` and `WDC_INBUF_SIZE (512*(WDC_MAX_SECTORS+1))` = **262,656 = exactly 513 blocks.** *** THE CORRECTION: 'SILENTLY' IS WRONG FOR THE FIRST FILL. *** There IS a check -- `dev_wdc.c:194-198`, a **latched one-shot** `fatal("... wdc inbuf overrun! ...")`. But its predicate is `head == tail` **after** the increment, so from empty it fires on store *N*, the moment the ring becomes FULL -- and **the store that actually destroys data is N+1**, which leaves `head == tail+1` and is silent. The latch then silences every later overrun too. > **Correct wording: announced ONCE as the ring fills; the overwriting store, and all subsequent ones, are silent.** The in-tree comment at `:185-193` already says this and names this row. *** REACHABILITY IS STRONGER THAN THE ROW CLAIMED. *** `:922-924` is `atapi_len = data_in_len` then `for (j=0; j<atapi_len; j++) wdc_addtoinbuf(...)` -- unbounded -- and **the `> 32768` clamp at `:926` runs AFTER the loop**, trimming only the REPORTED length. `READ(10)`'s block count is 16-bit (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:763`), and `logical_block_size` is **512 even for CD-ROMs** (`diskimage.c:1874`; the 2048 branch is `#if 0`'d at `:1868-1873`). Count 514 gives 263,168 bytes. The only cap, `SCSI_MAX_XFER_BYTES` = **64 MiB, 256x the ring**, does not save it. **TWO AMPLIFIERS NOBODY HAD NOTED, and together they remove the last natural bound:** `dev_wdc.c:919` tests only `res == 1` and `data_in != NULL` and **never consults `xferp->status[0]`**; and `diskimage_scsicmd.c:811-826` zero-fills and returns CHECK CONDITION on an out-of-range read **but still falls through to `return 1` with the full `size` buffer.** *** SO THE DISK IMAGE'S SIZE DOES NOT BOUND THE TRANSFER AT ALL -- a one-block `.iso` still yields whatever the guest asked for. *** *** AND THE CORRUPTION SHAPE IS WRONG-OFFSET DATA, NOT MISSING DATA -- which is worse and changes the detector. *** Pushing L > N bytes into an empty N-ring leaves `tail` unmoved and `head = tail + (L-N)`. The guest is told 32,768 bytes are ready and then reads transfer bytes **N..L-1 where block 1 should be**, with `wdc_get_inbuf` returning `(uint64_t)-1` for the rest. **At count=514 the guest receives block 514's contents AS BLOCK 1, followed by ~32 KB of 0xff.** **DOES the guest have unread data at risk? YES.** The ring is provably EMPTY at push time (dispatch requires `inbuf_len == 12` at `:864`, all drained at `:876-879`), so no PRIOR command's data is lost -- but the DATAIN design **requires the whole transfer to sit in the ring** (`:751-763` re-arms from `data_in_len - atapi_received` and drains in <=32,768-byte chunks across many DRQ cycles). **The bytes destroyed are the early part of THIS transfer, still unread.** **TWO HONEST QUALIFIERS, both from the seat:** the 513-block threshold **depends on that `#if 0`** -- restore the 2048 branch and it falls to block **129**; and a stock BSD ATAPI driver caps at MAXPHYS ~64 KB = 128 blocks, **well under 514**, so stock-OS incidence is UNMEASURED. Guest-reachable by construction (`ATAPI_PKT_CMD` at `:619-625` is accepted unconditionally), but not shown to happen under a stock guest. *** ESCALATED 2026-08-26 BY A FARMED codex JOB, RE-VERIFIED HERE BY READING: THIS IS GUEST-REACHABLE, NOT LATENT, AND IT TAKES ONE LEGAL COMMAND. *** `dev_wdc.c` sets `d->atapi_len = d->atapi_st->data_in_len;` and then loops `for (j=0; j<atapi_len; j++) wdc_addtoinbuf(...)` -- **the ENTIRE transfer is pushed into the ring with no bound against ring capacity**, and `atapi_len` is only capped afterwards. `SCSICMD_READ_10` takes a GUEST-CONTROLLED transfer length. ARITHMETIC, verified: `WDC_INBUF_SIZE = 512*(WDC_MAX_SECTORS+1) = 512*513 = 262,656` bytes = exactly 513 blocks of 512. **So block 514 of a SINGLE READ(10) begins overwriting unread data.** **COMBINED WITH THE BOOKKEEPING DEFECT ALREADY ON THIS ROW, the consequence is silent:** the ring cannot distinguish EMPTY from FULL (`head == tail` is the only state indicator -- no count, no full flag, no spare slot); the overrun check is POST-HOC, so the diagnostic fires when the ring BECOMES full while **the store that actually CORRUPTS is the NEXT one and is SILENT**; and the reader dereferences `inbuf[tail]` before testing anything, then reports "reading too much" and returns -1 while real data sits in the buffer. **THREE REACHABILITY PATHS, ranked:** (1) ONE ATAPI READ(10) with a large length -- the serious one, since it needs no unusual guest behaviour; (2) ATA READs totalling 256+256+1 undrained sectors through the diagnostic-free direct producer; (3) 513 undrained IDENTIFY commands. *** THE DETECTOR DESIGN, AND THE SEAT NAMED WHY THE OBVIOUS ORACLE IS INSUFFICIENT: *** fill the ring EXACTLY (513 undrained IDENTIFYs = 513*512 == WDC_INBUF_SIZE), require DRQ still set, write marker byte `0x5a` to DATA, then read ONE byte and require `0x40` -- the oldest byte of ordinary-disk IDENTIFY data. Broken code gives DRQ clear and `0x5a`; a count fix or a spare-slot fix gives DRQ set and `0x40`. **"The marker is the crucial oracle: it proves the next producer did not overwrite the oldest queued byte. Merely counting the overrun and over-read diagnostics does not."** *The committed probe ALREADY reaches the exact-full helper path -- 1,026 guest-executed MMIO stores, with the overrun line recorded in its artifact -- and does NOT measure the overwritten value. So the round's cost is one row on an existing probe, not a new witness.* **RANKING, honestly bounded by the seat itself:** guest-reachable, so above dormant defensive debt -- but normal stock-OS incidence is UNMEASURED, so below a demonstrated boot-path corruption. **NEEDS A BUILD**, so it is queued behind the owner's machine embargo with its analysis, reachability and detector design complete. *** RAISED ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-1 PANEL (panel_20260825_195526) BY THE kimi SEAT -- THE SEAT `panel.sh` HAD STOPPED FIRING. *** It was recovered by hand that same minute after its CLI transport walled (see `panelseatlabel`), and it produced the deepest finding of the panel. The brief asked, as its least-certain premise, whether latching `:160` would HIDE a real defect. agy (file-reading) answered no -- `:160` is a guest error, safe to latch. kimi answered *"your worry is real but located ONE SITE OFF"*. **Settled by reading, not by vote: kimi is right, and the defect is larger than either seat stated.** *** FOUR FACTS, ALL VERIFIED BY OPENING THE FILE. *** (1) `head == tail` IS THE ONLY STATE INDICATOR -- there is no count, no full flag, no spare slot. Verified by grepping every write to `inbuf_head`/`inbuf_tail`: :143, :165, :347, :349, :878 and nothing else. So the ring cannot distinguish EMPTY from FULL. (2) `wdc_addtoinbuf` (:141-146) checks POST-HOC: it stores, advances head, THEN tests `head == tail`. The warning therefore fires when the ring BECOMES full -- and the store that actually CORRUPTS is the NEXT one, which advances head to head+1 != tail and is SILENT. (3) `wdc_get_inbuf` (:157-163) reads `inbuf[tail]` at :157 BEFORE testing anything, then treats `head == tail` as EMPTY. **So after an overrun it reports "someone is reading too much" and returns -1 while 262,656 bytes of valid data sit unreachable in the buffer.** That is `:160`'s predicate becoming unsound -- exactly the shape the brief worried about, one site removed. (4) *** AND THE TWO BULK PATHS BYPASS THE CHECK ENTIRELY. *** `:343-349` advances head by up to `512 * to_read` after comparing ONLY against `WDC_INBUF_SIZE`, the physical end of the array -- it never compares against `tail`, so head can jump straight PAST tail leaving `head != tail` on a grossly overfull ring, with NO warning, because :144's test exists only in the byte-at-a-time path. `:876-879` does the mirror image to `tail`. *** THE CONSEQUENCE FOR `wdcflood`, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY RATHER THAN FOLDED IN: *** latching `:145` and `:160` silences the ONLY two diagnostics this ring has, while the bookkeeping defect goes untouched. The flood fix must therefore not be read as having addressed the ring. Under the reopening rule these are different rounds -- different fix design (a latch versus a state-representation change) and a different oracle (log-line count versus data integrity through the ring). SEVERITY, stated honestly: the byte-path half is a WRONG-DATA path (a guest is told the buffer is empty when it is full), not a host kill. The bulk half is a silent buffer overwrite WITHIN the allocated 262,656 bytes -- `zeroed_alloc(WDC_INBUF_SIZE)` at :1049 -- so it is data corruption, NOT an out-of-bounds host write. That distinction is deliberate and should not be inflated. *** MEASUREMENT OWED BEFORE ANY FIX: *** whether a real guest driver can reach the overrun at all. WDC_MAX_SECTORS is 512, so the ring holds `512*(512+1)` = 262,656 bytes; filling it by guest stores costs ~65,664 32-bit stores, while the bulk disk path fills 512 bytes per sector and would reach it far sooner. That measurement needs `landiskdisk`. *** CORROBORATED BY THREE FURTHER SEATS ON THE SAME PANEL, EACH REACHING IT INDEPENDENTLY AND NONE OF THEM ASKED ABOUT IT DIRECTLY. *** The brief asked only whether latching `:160` would hide a defect. glm: *":145 is an emulator error -- do NOT latch without fixing the ring overrun."* minimax: *":145 IS a real defect that the latch does not fix -- it corrupts the ring and continues, so a TODO is owed there."* grok: *":145 is the unfixed pckbc/asc wrap, not a twin of the measured :160 flood"* -- which additionally suggests the SAME ring-wrap class exists in `dev_pckbc.c` and `dev_asc.c` and is worth a census before this row is worked. **Four of eight seats located a defect the brief did not ask about, at a site the brief named only in passing.** *** A CONSTRAINT THIS ROW WILL NEED, ESTABLISHED 2026-08-25 BY THE kimi SUBSTITUTE SEAT ON THE `wdcflood` PASS-2 PANEL. *** The obvious repair for a ring that cannot distinguish empty from full is the classic WASTE-ONE-SLOT disambiguator. The obvious objection is that this ring is exactly sized -- `WDC_INBUF_SIZE` is `512 * (WDC_MAX_SECTORS + 1)` = 262,656 -- so wasting a slot might break a max-length transfer. **It does not: a max-length transfer is 512 * 512 = 262,144, and 262,144 <= 262,655.** Only the 513-undrained-IDENTIFY fill exceeds the reduced capacity, and that load is the DEFECT'S OWN WITNESS rather than legitimate traffic. Recorded here so the round does not have to re-derive it, and so the objection is answered before it is raised.closed

Assessment (initial problem)·OK2026-08-27 — CONFIRMED — THE ROW'S CLAIM IS TRUE AND IS SETTLED BY ARITHMETIC. `DEVINIT(wdc)` defaults `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206`, then a switch applies per-machine hacks. The MACHINE_HPCMIPS arm fires only when `devinit->addr == 0x14000180` and sets `alt_status_addr = 0x14000386`. 0x14000180 + 0x206 == 0x14000386 Identical. For the ONLY address it can see it recomputes the default, and for any other address the `if` does not fire. The arm is dead. AND THE ADDRESS IT CAN SEE IS FIXED, so 'the only address' is a closed claim rather than a guess: the sole producer is `dev_pcic.c`, which builds the devinit string with a HARDCODED literal -- `snprintf(..., "wdc addr=0x14000180 irq=%s.giu.9", ...)`. `machine_hpcmips.c` registers no wdc of its own. Repo-wide, `0x14000180` and `0x14000386` occur only in those two files (plus an unrelated SGI IP32 alias comment). *** BUT THE DISPOSITION THE ROW IMPLIES -- DELETE THE DEAD ARM -- IS PREMATURE, AND THE REASON IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT ALREADY WRITES DOWN ABOUT REMOVING TRIPWIRES. *** The arm carries `/* TODO: Fix */`, and that TODO is NOT discharged by proving the arithmetic is a no-op. It asserts something the arithmetic cannot: that somebody once thought hpcmips needed a DIFFERENT alt-status address. Whether `+0x206` is architecturally right for hpcmips at all is a hardware question, and it is UNSETTLED here -- `ls _scratchpad/*.pdf` lists fifteen manuals and NONE covers VR41xx or hpcmips. If `+0x206` is right, the arm is redundant and deleting it is tidy-up with zero delta. If `+0x206` is WRONG for hpcmips, the arm is a MARKER pointing at a live defect, and deleting it removes the only thing in the tree that says so. I cannot tell which, and a removal needs a measured delta or a transferred warrant -- 'it cannot hurt' is not a licence in either direction. PROVENANCE, checked rather than assumed: `git log -L` on those lines returns ONE commit, `39748e3` (the unmodified upstream import). **This is upstream's arm and upstream's TODO, not the fork's.** That matters for the disposition: the fork tracks its divergence from upstream deliberately, and deleting harmless upstream code for zero behavioural gain buys tidiness at the cost of a divergence entry. DISPOSITION: ASSESSED, NOT CHANGED. No product edit. What the row asked -- is the arm a no-op? -- is answered YES with its arithmetic shown. What it did not ask, and what would have to be answered before touching the code, is now stated as the successor question. *Filed under the ethos line this project already keeps: an honest 'assessed, not changed' record. The alternative was a three-line deletion I could not warrant, on upstream code, for no measurable effect.* — evidence: direct reading of dev_wdc.c, dev_pcic.c and git log -L·······

Assessment (initial problem)OK2026-08-27 — CONFIRMED — VERDICT: FIX B -- zero-fill the hole in place, count the requested length, continue. It filled the ninth seat it had been deferred from, and it corrected me twice on facts I had already checked once. *** (1) 'A IS NOT FAIL-STOP -- IT IS FAIL-MORE.' THE SINGLE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES THE ROUND. *** The read path's system-level postcondition is FIXED by the caller whichever fix ships: the tail memset runs, the function returns 1, and the only read-side `return 0` (the bounds arm) is unreachable from a short read. So the ONLY degree of freedom either fix controls is WHICH BYTES ARE FABRICATED ZEROS. B fabricates exactly the lost bytes -- the minimum possible. A fabricates the lost bytes PLUS every healthy byte after them, up to 63.5 sectors of a 64-sector wdc__read chunk. 'Stop and report the prefix' is a principled shape only where the report can change the outcome; here the caller converts the report into more zeros and success either way. And a non-reason, stated so nobody credits it later: A's larger zeroed region is NOT 'louder' to the guest. Zeros carry no signal -- the fork's own #416 comment in diskimage_scsicmd.c records exactly this, that a zero-filled short read 'reports a successful read of zeros, which is why a short or refused transfer was invisible'. *** (2) I HAD READ HALF THE PRECEDENT. diskimage_access__cue CONTAINS BOTH SHAPES, KEYED BY CAUSE -- AND ITS FIRST ARM IS FIX B. *** The `t == NULL` arm zero-fills in place, COUNTS THE CHUNK, and CONTINUES. My sibling-parity write-up cited only the short-fread arm and concluded 'precedent points at A'. Option D (clamp the read LENGTH before the pop) keeps tail and counters in lockstep and is the only option that does, if the dirty-ring premise holds. *My brief asked whether a dirty ring breaks option A. It does, but not by the mechanism I proposed -- not an under-count of undelivered bytes, but a tail/counter divergence.* *** SEVERITY RAISED 2026-08-27 BY READING THE SCSI LAYER: THE ODD LENGTH IS GUEST-CHOSEN, NOT AN EDGE CASE. *** `diskimage_scsicmd.c` sets the transfer length from a SINGLE GUEST BYTE: ``` :370 INQUIRY retlen = xferp->cmd[4]; <- allocation length, 0..255 :371 ...clamped to a MINIMUM of 36, never to an even value :572 MODE SENSE retlen = cmd[4], or cmd[7]*256 + cmd[8] :589 retlen += 100; <- still freely odd :746 REQUEST SENSE retlen = cmd[4]; ``` and `scsi_transfer_allocbuf(&xferp->data_in_len, &xferp->data_in, retlen, 1)` makes that value `data_in_len` directly. **WORKED PATH, no re-arm and no oversized transfer involved:** a guest issues INQUIRY with allocation length **37**. `atapi_len` starts at 37; nine four-byte reads consume 36 and leave 1; the tenth four-byte read makes `consumed` 4 and drives `atapi_len` to **-3**. `== 0` never fires again, the command never completes, and `atapi_received` reaches 40 against a `data_in_len` of 37. *This was filed as a residual of `#473` and is considerably more than that. `#473` added a second road via an odd FINAL chunk; the FIRST road is a one-byte field in one of the most ordinary SCSI commands there is.* *** MEASURED 2026-08-27, on the committed tree, in a scratch fixture. *** ``` atapi_len = 3 (ODD), guest does a FOUR-byte read of wd_data -> atapi_len = -1 (wanted 0) -> atapi_received = 4 (data_in_len is 3) ``` **TWO defects in one subtraction.** The counter steps PAST zero, so `if (atapi_len == 0)` never fires again and the command never completes -- and `atapi_received` ends up LARGER than `data_in_len`, so the device claims it delivered more bytes than the transfer holds. **THIS IS THE `#341` CLASS SURVIVING AT THE SAME SITE.** `#341` fixed `consumed` so it counts what the reads actually POP (`len == 4 ? 4 : (len >= 2 ? 2 : 1)`) rather than what the guest asked for. It did NOT make the subtraction saturate, and its own comment describes exactly this symptom -- *"let atapi_len step PAST zero, which its `== 0` test then never catches"* -- as the thing being fixed. The mismatch it removed was len-vs-consumed; the mismatch that remains is consumed-vs-REMAINING. **PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY `#473`.** A small odd transfer (MODE SENSE, REQUEST SENSE) reaches it with no re-arm at all. But `#473` gives it a SECOND road: before that round every transfer over 32768 bytes died at the first re-arm, so a multi-chunk transfer with an ODD FINAL CHUNK could never be walked to its end. Now it can. *Strictly fewer transfers break than before -- this is a residual of a real improvement, not a regression, and it is filed rather than reverted.* **FOUND BY ATTACKING A PREMISE, WHICH IS WHY THE BRIEF ASKED FOR IT.** `#473`'s pass-2 brief named the refill's "the ring is empty at the re-arm" claim as its load-bearing premise and asked seats to break it. A grok working note -- *"the re-arm's emptiness claim is only a drain-path invariant"* -- prompted the trace. **The emptiness claim itself HELD**: `head`/`tail` are never reset anywhere, but the packet path requires `inbuf_len == 12` EXACTLY, so a dirty ring can never issue a packet command and the arm is only reachable from an empty ring. The counter defect was found on the way past. **THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND IS NOT YET MADE:** saturate the subtraction, or test `<= 0`. Which one is a real question -- saturating hides the over-count in `atapi_received`, while `<= 0` completes the command but still reports having delivered 4 of 3 bytes. **The truthfulness half needs its own answer**, and this fork's own precedents (`#283` ASC, `#338` mb89352, `#341` here) all say the count reported has to be the count that happened. closed
