Final review (flagship adjudication)OK2026-08-29 — CONFIRMED — CLOSED 2026-08-29 AS A RECORDS ACTION. **The fix shipped 2026-08-27 and this row never learned.** `#479` (`2343036`) added `wdc_new_command_reset()`, clearing exactly the three tenants at the top of `wdc_command()` -- the F-narrow variant the 2026-08-27 five-variant matrix recommended. `#480` is its pass-2 receipt, `#481` extended it to the ALT-CTRL caller, `#482` hardened the rows per tenant. *** THE GHOST-ROUND MECHANISM, recorded because it cost a whole panel: *** the row carried a full 9/9 RESEARCH stage; the work then shipped under FOUR commit numbers; **zero entries landed back on the row**; the ledger froze at 'in work'; and two days later the main loop -- correctly treating the ledger as the queue -- drafted a fresh PASS-1 brief to do it all again and fired nine seats at it. **The CHANGELOG knew (its Round 479 block names all three row ids); the ledger did not.** This is the unread-review class one step worse: an unrecorded ROUND. The existing gates are structurally blind to it -- section H skips stages that never STARTED, and the implement/review stages never started on these rows. **DETECTION WOULD HAVE COST TWO COMMANDS**: `git log -- src/devices/dev_wdc.c` and `grep <rowid> CHANGELOG.md`. Neither was run, because the ledger said 'in work' and was believed. *** WITNESS TERM CORRECTED, and the old one was LAUNDERING. *** It read `probe:offline differential, 73 rows` -- but `probe:` on an offline differential is exactly the mis-scoring `check_witness.py`'s own header calls laundering, and the `detector:` term was adopted on 2026-08-27 for precisely this shape. The count was also stale and is now UNCITED: the string said 73, `TABLE.txt` says 80, and a fresh derivation gives 95 -- three numbers for one quantity, so the artifact PATH is cited instead of any of them, per the names-its-log rule. BADGE `A`: the recommender (fable5's matrix), the implementer's reviewer and the closer overlap. Disclosed rather than implied. FILED, not closed here: `Mq_pktretry` escaped `#480`'s table honestly and is recorded as such. *** AND ONE ELEMENT OF THE ORIGINAL RECOMMENDATION IS SUPERSEDED, NOT PRESERVED. *** It said to record the ALT-CTRL gap as a deliberately RED row. `#481` CLOSED the gap instead, which is better, and the adjudicator ruled against its own disposition on the reasoning that a permanently red row is the dual of a check-that-cannot-fail -- **a check that cannot PASS** -- and violates the blanks rule, since a deliberate red and a regression red render identically. Measured twice this week: a battery red went unread for five days over five further defects, and a stuck HELD count read as 'stable' across two regenerations. — evidence: [panel_20260829_213915] ghost-round adjudication; commits 2343036 (#479) + #480/#481/#482········
Regression testingOK2026-08-29 — CONFIRMED — REGRESS REVIEW of a closure that is RECORDS-ONLY: no code changed here, so what is reviewed is whether the SHIPPED detector still holds at HEAD. It does, and it was measured today rather than assumed. **Both kill tables are preserved and were re-verified**: `regress/artifacts/wdccmdreset/killtable_20260827/TABLE.txt` (13 of 13, including `MdEndRing` KILLED 5 red, and `MdNoPhase`/`MdNoWip` as SOLE carriers) and `regress/artifacts/wdcaltctrl/killtable_20260827/TABLE.txt` (10 of 10). **The detector was RUN at HEAD in a scratch tree: 128 rows, 0 failures, sentinel `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS`.** Nine fresh mutants aimed at the partial-reset shape were then built against it: SEVEN KILLED -- including the per-SITE subsets (`MdAltRingOnly`, `MdAltWipOnly`, `MdAltNoRing`) and `MdNoFlag`, which drops a FOURTH tenant neither shipped table enumerates and still dies 6 red -- and TWO ESCAPED and were PROVED EQUIVALENT by a positional differential rather than assumed: the inbuf is a correct circular buffer, so head/tail position is unobservable through occupancy, capacity or readback. *ATTRIBUTION, because the regress hat is fable-only and the measurement was not fable's:* the chronology reconstruction and both table verifications are fable5's; the 128-row run and the nine-mutant table are the opus5 seat's, run read-only in `/tmp/gxopus_wdc`. Recorded as two hands rather than one, so a reader is not misled about who measured what. *** ONE RESIDUAL, NOT CLOSED BY THIS REVIEW: the kill DRIVERS score a crash as a result. *** `kill479.sh`'s `build_run` checks the COMPILE status, then runs the mutant and greps FAIL lines WITHOUT reading the run's exit status or the `WDC_IDENTIFY_PASS` sentinel the detector already emits. A mutant that dies partway is scored KILLED-or-ESCAPED by how far it got. Nothing was mis-scored today (every mutant exited clean), but the driver cannot tell. Filed rather than fixed here, because this closure changes no code. — evidence: killtable_20260827 (13/13) + wdcaltctrl (10/10) + a 128-row run at HEAD········

The existing gates are structurally blind to it -- section H skips stages that never STARTED, and the implement/review stages never started on these rows. **DETECTION WOULD HAVE COST TWO COMMANDS**: `git log -- src/devices/dev_wdc.c` and `grep <rowid> CHANGELOG.md`. FILED, not closed here: `Mq_pktretry` escaped `#480`'s table honestly and is recorded as such. *** AND ONE ELEMENT OF THE ORIGINAL RECOMMENDATION IS SUPERSEDED, NOT PRESERVED. *** It said to record the ALT-CTRL gap as a deliberately RED row. `#481` CLOSED the gap instead, which is better, and the adjudicator ruled against its own disposition on the reasoning that a permanently red row is the dual of a check-that-cannot-fail -- **a check that cannot PASS** -- and violates the blanks rule, since a deliberate red and a regression red render identically. Its first use immediately paid: #489's headline claim went from derived to MEASURED -- 7 heap-buffer-overflow WRITEs through the real guest instruction path. — witness: harness:build-asan/ now builds and runs -- `GXemul asan`, 107 MB, ldd shows libasan.so.8 linked, two-part clearance passes. The round's subject IS the test apparatus, which is what harness: admits. — note: *** AND ITS FIRST RUN PAID FOR IT THE SAME HOUR. *** #489's bare-deletion mutant under the shipped 19-row detector: **7 x heap-buffer-overflow, every one a WRITE**, five `0 bytes after 407-byte region` and two `0 bytes after 1-byte region`. The stack runs from `main` through `sh_run_instr` and a guest `mov.w` store into `handle_command`, onto a buffer from `alloc_data`'s `malloc(guest cnt)`. `regress/artifacts/gdromexitsix/asan_m0_20260828/`. *The FIRST attempt reported `6/19, zero reports` -- noise, not a negative. LeakSanitizer fires at exit on every session and ASan's default exit code is 1, so every survival row read as a death while the genuine reports went to a pty the probe does not retain. The tell was `ok surv` reading exit1 on the LEGAL length, which the mutant cannot affect.* *** FIXED 2026-08-28. THE TREE BUILDS, RUNS, AND HAS ASAN LINKED. *** Four build attempts, each peeling one layer, every layer INVISIBLE to the propagation gate: 1. stale HEADERS -- diskimage.c vs a diskimage.h missing nr_of_tracks, DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT, struct diskimage_track. Fixed by back-filling 474 .c/.h from SEC. 2. stale GENERATORS -- new sources against an OLD makeautodev.sh emitted `int devinit_Makefile.skel(...)`, a glob expansion the script's own comment warns about. Fixed by syncing 16 scripts/.index/Makefile.skel. 3. stale GENERATED MAKEFILE -- OBJS predating dev_ne2000.c (a SEC-only file), giving `undefined reference to devinit_ne2000`. Fixed by re-running ./configure with CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g'; COPTIM verified to still carry the sanitizer afterwards, and the 15 prior Makefiles were backed up first. 4. none -- it built. *** MAKE_RC REPORTED 0 ON EVERY FAILED BUILD. *** Caught only because the check was `[ -x gxemul ]`. The carrier already says the exit status lies here; this is three more instances in one session. **THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL AND OUTLIVES THIS TREE: AN INCREMENTAL PROPAGATION CHECK CANNOT SEE A STALE BASELINE.** precommit_check.sh enforces propagation for `$CHANGED` -- the files THIS commit touches -- which is deliberate and right (*a gate that hard-fails on a tree someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*). But the tree was ALREADY stale when the 2026-08-27 ruling landed, and nothing back-fills. diskimage.h and makeautodev.sh are touched by no recent round, so no gate ever required them. **The tree passed every commit's check while compiling nothing at all** -- worse than the gate comment's own fear of *a detector that has silently stopped detecting, worse than no detector because it reassures*. *** OWNER DECISION 2026-08-28: a SOFT-WARNING full `diff -rq` of the .c/.h set, SKIPPED ENTIRELY when the tree is absent. *** Warning rather than hard-fail, and absent-is-skipped, so the absence-is-not-a-failure rule that keeps the gate switched on is preserved. Filed as `asanbaselinedrift` to ship as its own harness round with its two negative controls. NOW UNBLOCKED: #489's headline claim. Its bare-deletion mutant scored 12/19 with the host SURVIVING a 408-byte write past a malloc(0) -- which shows the write does not FAULT, not that it is ABSENT. An ASAN run settles that, and the tree to run it on now exists. *A check of mine scored the finished binary as having no ASan: `nm | grep -c __asan` = 0. Wrong test -- the sanitizer symbols are in the SHARED LIBRARY. `ldd | grep libasan` is the test, and the build I nearly discarded was already correct.* *** DIAGNOSED AND FIXED 2026-08-28, AND THE CAUSE IS A GAP IN THE HARNESS RATHER THAN A STALE FILE. *** MEASURED FIRST: `make -j8` in build-asan/ reported **MAKE_RC=0 AND PRODUCED NO BINARY** -- the documented trap, caught only because the check was `[ -x gxemul ]` rather than the exit status. The real errors were in diskimage.c: `struct diskimage has no member named nr_of_tracks`, `DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT undeclared`, `invalid use of undefined type struct diskimage_track` -- a current .c against a STALE .h. *** THE CAUSE: THE PROPAGATION RULE IS INCREMENTAL AND THE TREE NEEDED A BASELINE. *** The owner ruled on 2026-08-27 that build-asan/ joins the propagation set, and precommit_check.sh implements that for `$CHANGED` -- the files THIS commit touches. That is deliberate and well-reasoned (its own comment: *a gate that hard-fails on a tree someone chose not to build is a gate that gets switched off*). **But the tree was already stale when the ruling landed, and nothing back-fills.** `diskimage.h` is touched by no recent round, so no gate ever required it -- and it is what broke the build. **So the tree could pass every commit's check and still not compile.** That is worse than the gate comment's own fear -- it says a stale ASAN tree is *a detector that has silently stopped detecting, worse than no detector because it reassures*. This one did not build at all, so it detected nothing, while every commit touching it reported green. MEASURED DIVERGENCE at diagnosis: **111 differing .c/.h files, 1 present only in SEC** (360 paths total, the rest .o and generated Makefiles). No divergence is permitted for shared files -- unlike est/, build-asan has no allowlist -- so all 111 were staleness. FIXED by back-filling every .c/.h from GXEMUL-SEC/src (474 files copied, source divergence measured 0 afterwards), under a `.MUTANT` sentinel so an interrupted sync could not be mistaken for a clean tree. Rebuilt with `rm src/cpus/*.o` first. *** WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS THE HARNESS GAP, NOT THIS TREE: an incremental propagation check cannot detect a stale BASELINE, and there is no periodic full comparison. The next baseline drift will be just as invisible. *** A full `diff -rq` of the .c/.h set is cheap and would have caught this in one command; whether it belongs in the gate (and at what cadence, given the absence-is-not-a-failure rule) is an owner decision, not a round's. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: `#489`'s strongest single result is the bare-deletion mutant scoring 12/19 with the host SURVIVING a 408-byte write past a `malloc(0)`. The measuring seat stated its own limit -- that shows the write does not FAULT, not that it is ABSENT. An ASAN run is exactly what closes that gap. *** `build-asan/` DOES NOT BUILD AND HAS NO BINARY. Found 2026-08-27 while propagating #484, and it PREDATES that round -- `dev_wdc` appears ZERO times in the failure log. *** make 103 errors, and it reported EXIT 0 -- the documented false-zero, again build-asan/gxemul DOES NOT EXIST stale objects 222 .o files with no binary to link them into ROOT CAUSE, verified rather than guessed: `build-asan/src/disk/diskimage.c` is IN SYNC with SEC while `build-asan/src/include/diskimage.h` is NOT. The new .c uses members the old .h does not declare -- `nr_of_tracks`, `total_disc_sectors`, `first_data_track_lba`, `DISKIMAGE_MAX_SPT`, `struct diskimage_track` -- each present in SEC's header and absent from this one. **A .c was propagated without its header**, which is the no-VPATH rule obeyed halfway. AND IT IS NOT ONE FILE: **363 files under `build-asan/src` differ from SEC.** This tree is broadly abandoned, not narrowly stale. *** THE CONSEQUENCE IS SILENT COVERAGE LOSS, THE SAME CLASS AS A GATE THAT SKIPS. *** `gate_asan_sweep.sh` exists to run the machine-construction sweep under ASAN. With no binary it cannot do that -- and this project has already been bitten once by a gate skipping on a missing binary and scoring the skip as a pass. NOT FIXED IN #484, and deliberately: the stopping rule fixes a finding in-round only if it is a MEASURED FALSE PASS of this round or a WRONG RECORD. This is neither -- it is a pre-existing tree defect in a tree #484 does not measure against. Folding a 363-file resync into a ring-buffer round is exactly how rounds stop converging. REMEDY when it is worked: re-derive the tree from SEC rather than patching the header. A tree 363 files out of date has no property worth preserving, and a header-only fix would leave the other 362 to be discovered one build at a time.closed

With `#481` shipped, the six `0x08` writes are INERT, and `landiskaux` is safe to ship on its own. *The queue entry says these two 'MUST SHIP TOGETHER'. They no longer must. It is the third stale-severity finding of the day, and the same shape each time: a severity that was an answer to a question rather than a property of a row, left standing after the question changed.*closed

The correct edit is an `else if` SPLICE: the decline arm ends and control falls to the common tail. One structural token changes per site (`if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)` becomes `} else if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE) {`). *Unanimity on a defect in the brief is the premise-audit instruction working: the seats were told not to ratify, and none did.* **2. `return 1`, NOT `return 0` -- and two seats CHECKED it rather than reasoning.** `memory_rw.c` coerces a 0 return to -1 and the `res <= 0 && !no_exceptions` arm raises `mips_cpu_exception(..., EXCEPTION_DBE, ...)`. After the fix a declined READ falls through and executes it for the first time, handing the guest a defined 0 instead of an untouched buffer. NAME `sgidewidth` IN THE PRETABLE AND ROUND RECORD.** It is a SEVENTH live width kill in the same file, deliberately excluded (different handler, different accept set, readable registers). The existing rules do not cover it: no sentinel was owed, no tree was mutated, and every status was 0. **THE FIX IS THE ONE THE CARRIER ALREADY MANDATES FOR SCRIPTS, EXTENDED TO SOURCES: put the file on a `/mnt/c' path both sides can see.** The re-run also `rm's the binary first and refuses if none is produced, so a stale artifact cannot answer for a failed build. *** THE LINK I FLAGGED AS DOUBTFUL IS CONFIRMED, AND THE ANSWER IS SHARPER THAN THE CHAIN I WROTE: ONE PREDICATE DISABLES ALL THREE PROTECTIONS. Verified by direct reading 2026-09-07, after the verification seat refused the brief. *** I wrote that I was least sure of step 3 -- whether `src_x' is masked the way the destination `x' is, saying that if it were, the chain dies there. It is not, and the masking is CONDITIONAL on the very mode that disables the other two guards: if (src_is_linear) src_x += step_x; <- NO MASK else src_x = (src_x + dx) & 0x7ff; <- masked **So `src_is_linear' simultaneously (a) removes the coordinate mask here, (b) skips the `x < 0' guard in `horrible_getputpixel' via `if (!linear && (x < 0 ...))', and (c) routes to `case 4', whose `tile_nr' bound is `>= 32' only.** That is not three independent oversights lining up -- it is ONE predicate switching off three protections at once, which is a much better description of the defect than my step list. **THE REMAINING LINKS, each read at its own line:** :715 int32_t step_x = 0; SIGNED :719 step_x = d->de_reg[CRIME_DE_XFER_STEP_X ...]; straight from a guest register :724 src_is_linear = ((src_mode & 0x00001c00) >> 10) > 3; guest-controlled via src_mode :757 uint16_t saved_src_x = src_x; so the row STARTS non-negative :912 if (src_is_linear) src_x += step_x; unmasked, per above **MINIMAL REACHABILITY, which the earlier note did not state:** each row restarts at `saved_src_x' (a `uint16_t', hence >= 0), the GET uses the CURRENT `src_x', and the increment happens after. So with `saved_src_x = 0' and `step_x = -1', **the SECOND pixel of the rectangle already uses `src_x = -1'** -- a two-pixel-wide rectangle suffices. No large geometry, no wraparound, no exotic value. **STATUS: every link is now verified by reading.** What remains unestablished is unchanged and stated before: no witness has been run; [[sgitexindex]]'s overlapping TEX writes affect WHICH values land in `re_tex[110..111]'; and no real driver is known to drive a negative step. *** WITHDRAWN 2026-09-07. THE FINDING IS FALSE. `tile_nr' IS UNSIGNED, AND THE DECLARATION IS THREE LINES ABOVE THE CODE I QUOTED. *** :204 int tile_nr_x = x / tilewidth_in_pixels; :205 int tile_nr_y = y >> 7; :207 unsigned int tile_nr = tile_nr_y * 16 + tile_nr_x; <- UNSIGNED ... case 4: tile_nr = x >> 12; <- converts to unsigned on assignment if (tile_nr >= 32) return; <- 4294967295 >= 32 is TRUE. IT RETURNS. x = -1 -> x >> 12 = -1 -> as unsigned = 4294967295 -> >= 32 -> REJECTED x = -8192 -> x >> 12 = -2 -> as unsigned = 4294967294 -> >= 32 -> REJECTED **The guard I called `upper bound only' is a COMPLETE bound**, because the conversion folds every negative value into the rejected range. There is no out-of-bounds read, no guest-chosen tile pointer, and no write primitive. Refuted by the codex seat (regress/artifacts/sgilinearnegidx/codex_siblings_20260907.txt). *** HOW BADLY I GOT THIS WRONG, RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE THE PROCESS FAILURE IS THE ONLY THING OF VALUE LEFT IN THIS ROW. *** * I filed it HIGH, then ESCALATED it to a guest-chosen physical write address. * I wrote *"every link is now verified by reading"* -- and had verified the link I DOUBTED (whether `src_x' is masked) while never checking the TYPE of the index variable, which is the most basic property of an index and the one that decides the whole question. * I ran an `offsetof' to avoid trusting hand arithmetic on the struct layout. **That measurement is correct and it was aimed at the wrong link.** Rigour on one step does not transfer to the step you did not question. * **THE DECLARATION WAS ON MY SCREEN.** I printed lines 184-215 of this function earlier in the same session while checking the mode decode; `unsigned int tile_nr' is at 207, inside that range. I read past it because I was looking for the mode fields. * It is in commit `15633bb`'s MESSAGE as a headline claim, which cannot be edited. **That message is wrong** and this row is the correction a reader must reach. **WHAT SURVIVES:** the `offsetof' result (`re_tex` ends at 1760, `re_linear_a` begins at 1760, zero padding) is a true measurement, preserved at `regress/artifacts/sgilinearnegidx/offcheck.c'. It is about a path nothing can reach, so it supports no finding. *** AND THE REFUSAL COST ME THE REFUTATION FOR HOURS, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST ARGUMENT YET ABOUT §C5. *** I asked the seat to attack this chain link by link. **That brief was REFUSED for being chain-shaped.** The same seat, asked the same subject WITHOUT the chain -- *which array indexes are bounded on one side only?* -- answered in one line: *"the stated case-4 underflow is absent in this fork: `tile_nr' is unsigned."* **The refusal did not stop a bad question; it delayed a correct answer**, and in the interval I escalated a false finding, wrote it into a commit, and reported it as the session's most severe result. *The lesson is not that seats are unreliable. I built this chain, I verified the parts I doubted, and I was wrong about the part I never questioned. The seat that could have caught it earlier was refused for the SHAPE of my question rather than its content.* **WHAT THE SAME AUDIT DID FIND, and it is not this row's defect:** *"There are missing checks on complete write SPANS in TLB_A/B/C and LINEAR_A/B, whose safety depends on caller alignment."* A span check is a different question from an index bound -- the index can be in range while the multi-byte write starting there runs past the end. **Filed separately as [[sgirespanchk]] rather than folded in here**, because a withdrawn row is the worst possible place to hide a live one.closed

(a) The stated mechanism is guest-unreachable: exhausting the 2^20 budget needs a timer above 65 * 2^20 = 68,157,440 Hz, and the only two footbridge machines are cats 50,000,000 Hz and netwinder 63,750,000 Hz -- BOTH BELOW THE CAP. Not one footbridge timer can reach the ceiling, let alone four. (b) The conclusion IS reachable by a different route, and *** THE PROPOSED FIX MAKES THAT ROUTE WORSE. *** Four netwinder timers at load=1 deliver 4 x 980,769 = 3.92M iterations per signal WITHOUT EVER TOUCHING THE CAP -- 8.5-11.1 ms of 15.38 ms (55-72%), inside the rejected band. A global 2^20 budget would bound that to ~15-19%, but only by throttling four fully-delivered timers to 26% and giving them permanently-growing debt. It converts expensive-but-correct into cheap-and-lagging. capN and capgap do NOT merge -- they point in OPPOSITE directions. capgap widens the reject; capN narrows the budget. Assessment (initial problem)✓2026-08-16 — CONFIRMED — dev_sh4.c:191's sh4_timer_tick() calls fatal() then exit(1) from inside the SIGALRM handler; _exit() is the safe one. pcc_timer_tick() reaches interrupt work from the same handler. Also worth grouping here: timer_stop() does not block SIGALRM while disarming and replacing the disposition (harmless today -- it delays one message by one stop), and timer_init() never clears timer_catchup_hit. All PRE-EXISTING; named because R4's comment 'NOTHING IS PRINTED HERE, in a signal handler' was being read as a claim about the handler rather than about timer.c, and that comment is now corrected. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260815_202720/✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — DROP as a round -- argued both ways, then MEASURED. FOR: UB in a signal handler; exit() runs atexit and _IO_cleanup, taking stdio locks the interrupted main thread may hold; a hang is a strictly worse failure shape than an exit. AGAINST, measured: the seat built the exact two calls and fired them from a 65 Hz SIGALRM (timer.c's own rate) into a main thread saturated with stdio, then into one saturated with malloc/free carrying an ALLOCATING atexit handler: CONTROL (main thread) exit rc=1, message intact SIGALRM, stdio 10/10 exited rc=1, message intact, 0/10 hung SIGALRM, malloc 12/12 exited rc=1, atexit ran, 0/12 hung GXemul registers exactly ONE atexit handler (fix_console, emul.c:913), so the realistic exit path is short. A negative result on one glibc -- but it is the platform this project builds and gates on, and 22 trials produced zero difference. *** AND THE OTHER HALF DOES NOT RESCUE THE ROW. *** The 'a legal guest write kills the host' reframing looked like a missed #223 instance until the seat COUNTED: grep -c 'exit(1)' src/devices/*.c finds 50 FILES, and dev_sh4.c carries no #223 tag at all. This is not one path a completed sweep missed (the wdcflood shape); it is one member of a large untouched class, and picking it because a timer row happened to notice it is the wrong selection criterion. The class is real and is tracked as [[hlen]]/[[devexit]]/[[sh4bcr]]. Result DIFF_M8INVREAD_FAIL, 27 rows / 9 failures (E3 E4 E9b F1 F2 F4 G1 G8 G9). THE REASONING ERROR IS MINE AND I PROPAGATED IT: I recorded that the detector 'observes the CALLBACK, never the resulting STATE, so a mutant reaching invalidation by any other route is invisible.' FALSE. The spy is a TWO-DIRECTIONAL presence oracle -- rows assert zero purges where none is owed AND non-zero where one IS owed, and the second group reddens the instant the callback stops being called. There is no in-file mutant satisfying 'purge achieved, spy silent, rows green', because THE CALLBACK IS THE MECHANISM. The seat's own negative control is why this is believable: its first mutant silently no-op'd (python3 in git-bash is the Microsoft Store stub) and the harness printed a clean 27/0 PASS. A cmp against the pristine copy caught it and that run was discarded. Rule 4 -- 'did it fail for the reason under test' -- earning its keep again. — evidence: diff_m8invread.c mutant D1, built and run·······

The 5 SAPR writes per boot happen at pmap.c:1310 with the PATC empty. *** THAT IS ALSO POSITIVE EVIDENCE ABOUT THE HARDWARE CONTRACT: *** a driver that flushes explicitly and reasons about WHICH TLB needs it only makes sense if the 88200 does NOT auto-flush on an APR write. FIVE SEPARATE ROUNDS. *** agy: 'split pitflip, pitlatch, pitlsb and isaorder into separate candidate rounds'. glm: 'none merge under the one-fix-design test'. deepseek: 'no merges'. minimax sequenced them rather than combining. **This OVERRULES the measure seat's own suggestion that pitflip was 'the natural companion' to i8253zero** -- it argued same-device and same-semantic-class (counter-load byte routing), and the panel applied the remaining prongs and said no. WHAT IS FIRST -- pitlatch, 3 to 1: pitlatch deepseek, glm, minimax. glm's clause is the decisive one: 'a real guest reaches it in microtime()'. That is this project's ordering rule applied exactly -- severity and reachability, never rung, never vote -- and pitlatch is the only one of the five demonstrated to be on a path a shipped guest actually takes (_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/i386/isa/clock.c:207-209). i8253zero agy alone, as a standalone fix round. MINIMAX GAVE THE MOST REASONED SEQUENCE and it is worth keeping: pitlatch, then pitflip, then **i8253zero THIRD 'once pitflip closes its door'** -- because pitflip is what MANUFACTURES count 0 from a guest that never asks for it, so fixing pitflip removes i8253zero's main reachability route and lowers its rank. That is a dependency between rounds, not a merge. It kills 25 of 33 rows on the pre-fix build and kills six real mutants. That is categorically unlike #446's detector, which a 217-byte comment-only file passed and which was therefore replaced in-round. THE FOUR HOLES, and they are a PRODUCT rather than a list: H1 state is read back at INSTANCE 0 ONLY. V17/V18 read RCR1, V19/V20 channel 0, V21 TCR0. V11/V12 walk the other instances but only COUNT diagnostic lines. H2 state is read back on a FIRST offence only, EXCEPT at RCR1. V18 exists for exactly this shape -- its own comment cites #443's brace slip -- and the sibling row was never added at TCR or DMATCR. H3 the guard masks are pinned only FROM BELOW. V28 proves the six bits are IN the mask; nothing proves any other bit is OUT. H4 width x instance is a PRODUCT and the census covers only the DIAGONAL -- three widths at instance 0, one width everywhere else. THE ESCAPES, all measured on built binaries: M20 `| TCR_UNIE` added to TCR_UNIMPLEMENTED -- ONE IDENTIFIER. Fix: TCR0=0x0022 reads back 0x22 with a clock line at 520833.328125 Hz. M20: reads back 0x00000000, NO clock line. TCR_UNIE is modelled (`d->tcr[i] & TCR_UNIE` in sh4_timer_tick), so the guest can NEVER enable the timer interrupt. [H3] M20b `| TCR_TPSC0` -- same shape; makes TPSC_P16 and TPSC_P256 unusable. [H3] M25 `| SH_RCR1_CF` -- fix writes RCR1 0x80, reads back 0x80, 0 diagnostics; mutant reads back 0x01, STILL 0 diagnostics. Fully silent. [H3] Mdma DMATCR guard narrowed `~0x00ffffff` -> `~0x04ffffff`, ONE NIBBLE. Bit 26 is then stored, and *** sh4_dmac_transfer consumes dmac_tcr[] & 0x1fffffff, FIVE BITS WIDER than the guard rejects ***, so bits 24-28 give a silently wrong transfer count. [H3] M23 TCR stores the rejected value when timer_nr != 0. Fix: TCR1 reads 0x0002. Mutant: 0x0204. [H1] M24 DMATCR stores it when dma_channel != 0. Fix: 0x10. Mutant: 0xabcdef. [H1] Mbrk TCR `break;` -> `if (timer_nr == 0) break;` -- timers 1 and 2 then fall into `idata & 3` and install pclock/4, the exact naive-fix bug V22 was written for, on the two instances it does not watch. [H1] M21 DMATCR stores on a REPEAT offence. Fix: 0x10. Mutant: 0x123456. Both rejects carry bit 24, so the second is not 'fresh'. [H2] M22 TCR stores on a repeat offence. Fix: 0x0002. Mutant: 0x0004. [H2] M33 `if (timer_nr == 2 && len == 4) exit(1);` -- *** GUEST-REACHABLE HOST DEATH. *** A mov.l to TCR2 gives alive=False. It SURVIVES at len 2, the only width V11 issues, which is precisely why it scores full marks. [H4] *** THE FIX CHANGED H3's FAILURE MODE FROM LOUD TO SILENT, and that is the finding inside the finding. *** Pre-#447 a widened mask meant exit(1) on a legal write -- unmissable. Post-#447 it means a silently refused write. The round improved the failure and made its own blind spot worse in the same edit. A THIRD SEAT ADDED THE QUANTIFIER-COLLAPSE QUESTION, and was honest that it could not confirm it: V28 writes all six unimplemented TCR bits AS A UNION (0x02dc). Delete one bit from the mask and the union write still trips on the other five, so V28 stays green while a SINGLETON write of the deleted bit reaches the prescaler and the store. UNSETTLED -- it needs the fourteen mask-minus-one-bit mutants run: TCR 0x0004/0x0008/0x0010/0x0040/0x0080/0x0200 and each DMATCR high-byte bit, each written alone. NOTE H3-from-above and the singleton sweep are DIFFERENT TESTS and both are wanted: one requires a MODELLED bit to be ACCEPTED, the other requires each unimplemented bit to be REJECTED ALONE. A mask is pinned only when both hold, and they fail to different mutants. THE FIXES THE SEATS RECOMMENDED, each small: extend the TCR and DMATCR read-back rows to a NON-ZERO instance (H1); add a read-back after a REPEATED same-bit reject at TCR and DMATCR (H2); add rows writing a MODELLED bit-set and asserting it is ACCEPTED, with the clock line as the second witness (H3); make V11 issue len 4 as well as len 2 (H4). *** AND ONE PROCESS NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE ROWS: THE PROBE REFUSED TO PASS IN A HALF-EDITED STATE. *** An attempt at this work died mid-edit having bumped EXPECT_ROWS to 43 and registered three new opcodes, without writing the rows. The probe reported 31/33 FAIL through TWO INDEPENDENT ROWS -- V31 caught the row-count intent, V30 caught the opcode intent (mismatches for 2151, 2161, 4000, disassembler None). The identity-row discipline worked on its own author, and the tree was restored to a verified 33/33 rather than left broken. — evidence: opus5 + grok + codex, panel_20260821_171837, mutants built and scored·······

mb89352haltmb89352halt An unimplemented SCSI command stops the emulated CPU rather than refusing the commandmb89352halt An unimplemented SCSI command stops the emulated CPU rather than refusing the command — witness: none -- folded into [[b120]], which is the same omission at the same site. Not an independent finding. — note: *** DROPPED 2026-08-27 AS A DUPLICATE I FILED MYSELF. It is [[b120]]'s mb89352 face, not a separate defect -- and my own b120 record already lists it as one of that row's four outcomes. *** **The halt fires BECAUSE of b120**: the shared dispatcher's `default:` arm (`diskimage_scsicmd.c:1380-1388`) leaves `status` / `status_len` unset and returns 1; mb89352 then enters `PH_STAT` and hits `if (d->transfer_bufpos(0) >= len(0))` at `dev_mb89352.c:173`, which sets `cpu->running = 0`. **So fixing b120 to return CHECK CONDITION with sense (`status_len >= 1`) makes that read succeed and REMOVES THE HALT.** One fix site, one semantic class -- there is nothing left for a separate row to carry. *My error, and worth naming: I filed it while recording b120's own correction, in the same sitting where I wrote 'CPU halt on mb89352' as b120 outcome number four. **A finding that arrives as a by-product of another row's analysis is the easiest kind to double-file** -- it feels new because it was found separately.* **FILED SEPARATELY AND DELIBERATELY NOT HERE:** a weaker defence-in-depth item -- mb89352 should refuse gracefully rather than `cpu->running = 0` on ANY zero-length status, hardening it against any future path that leaves status empty. That is a different (and smaller) claim than this row made, and it is not b120's round. *** FILED 2026-08-27, found by an adversarial opus pass while REFUTING the mechanism of [[b120]]. It is a separate and more severe defect than the row it was found under. *** On `dev_mb89352.c`, an unimplemented SCSI command reaches the dispatcher's `default:` arm, which leaves `data_in == NULL`. The controller then sets `d->phase = PH_STAT` (`:284`). The guest's PH_STAT `DREG` read takes `p = xferp->status` (**NULL**) and `len = xferp->status_len` (**0**) (`:158-161`), with `transfer_bufpos` reset to 0 (`:429`) -- so `0 >= 0` trips the `DREG: read longer than buffer?` arm at `:173`, which emits at `VERBOSITY_ERROR` **and sets `cpu->running = 0`.** > **A guest that issues an unimplemented command to an mb89352 target STOPS THE EMULATED CPU.** That is not a refusal and not a false success -- it is a guest-drivable halt, and it ranks above [[b120]]'s false-success behaviour on harm. **Relationship to [[b120]]:** same omission, different controller. b120's fix -- populate a status buffer and return CHECK CONDITION -- **would also fix this**, because the halt is caused precisely by the absent status buffer. So this does not need an independent fix, but it DOES need its own detector row, since b120's observable (a status byte) is not this one's (the CPU still running). **Observable:** whether the emulated CPU is still running after an unimplemented opcode is issued to an mb89352 target. Binary, and it needs no status decoding. *Filed rather than fixed: the stopping rule files anything that is not a measured false pass or a wrong record against shipped material, and this is a newly found defect, not a defect in what shipped today.* dropped

The program gen_dashboard.py makes this page from pipeline/ledger.json. Do not change this page manually. If a cell does not have a ledger entry, the cell is a defect. A packet-fed seat examines the argument only. Its vote about the contents of the repository is not equal to the vote of a seat that reads files (PIPELINE.md, Section 1). An ✕ cell can be the most important cell in its row: the ✕ in the Research phase of #419 changed the design. Rule for closed rows (owner, 2026-08-15): a closed row does not need new tests when the flagship seat (Fable) examined the final change and its evidence. That examination fills the Final review cell of the closed row. Regression phase (owner, 2026-08-15): only the flagship seat reviews the regression tests, and the reviews are BATCHED TO SUNDAY NIGHT, after the full battery, which now runs Sunday at 18:00 so that its evidence covers the rounds the review examines. The other eight cells in a Regression line are NOT REQUIRED, and a Regression line that is empty on a round finished after Saturday is WAITING FOR THE SUNDAY BATCH, not missing. So a line of dots there shows a rule, not a gap. The first three phases still need all nine seats, per round, before that round proceeds.
